It was no more than a few minutes before all present saw how the man’s hand began to open despite his struggle to keep it closed. The man had begun to tighten his fingers around the coin as strongly as he could, endeavouring to keep it closed but he failed. His hand continued to open slowly but surely, as if there were some great, unseen force exerting its strong and steady pressure.

Nevertheless, the man did not give up. He continued to resist, trying to keep his hand tightly closed. But, alas! Despite his very best efforts the matter was no longer under his control. The guests were astonished by what they had just seen, but the victim was the most bewildered of all. He knew that he had spared no effort in trying to stop his hand from opening, but all of his exertions had come to nothing, and his hand was forced open as if by a powerful unseen being. At last, he yielded to the fait accompli. The nefarious magician then stretched out his hand, took the lira and put it in his pocket as his mouth salivated at the prospect of all that he might gain from this gathering.

It was clear to see that he had won the first round, and on this day he planned to earn a lot of money through his mischievous magic and cunning artifice.

It was theft of a new kind but with a license from the audience: it was theft that had been agreed upon by the participants!

Now, it was the turn of the second challenger, but would he change his mind after seeing the previous result? He was the richest man in Damascus at that time and had many factories in various foreign countries like Turkey, Italy, France and Switzerland, so a single golden lira was as nothing to him.

He took the coin out of his pocket, put it in his fist and closed it tightly, proudly convinced that because of his impressive, muscular physique he would prove to be more than a match for the magician. He exerted every bit of his strength and tightened his hand until the knuckles turned white, the veins protruded on the back of his hand, and his muscles swelled.

As before, the magician approached the man, staring at his closed fist, and started his strange gesticulations and recitation of mystical mutterings.

Yet again, the closed hand began to open little by little as if by some force that could not be seen, but that surely did exist. This hidden force was opening the hand and overcoming the strong clenched grip of its owner. The man tightened his hand even further, calling up every last bit of his energy so that he might defeat the invisible power which was forcing his hand to open.

His face became red and his temperature certainly rose due to the great pressure he was exerting. But he couldn’t maintain it and began to tire without getting any result from his labours. So, he, too, failed and his hand opened up, clearly showing the golden lira lying on his palm.

The audacious magician then took the second lira and put it in his pocket with his lips curled into the semblance of a smile that was filled with guile. His eyes were as dark as a moonless night and were sending sharp, stabbing glances around the room. Now! Who would he choose as his next victim?

Mohammad Amin was keeping a very watchful eye on the situation. He was well aware of the secret behind the magician’s tricks, due to his deep belief in God. He realised that the magician had no power except over those people who were far from observing God’s Word, and therefore deserved to be outwitted. If only those men had truly turned to God and sought His Protection, the consorts of the devil would have fled the scene without affecting their spirits. They would not have been able to disable them by making them lose control of the power and strength of their own bodies, nor would they have been capable of enabling the devil’s brother, the magician, to take the golden coins from their hands, their very own hands which were no longer under their control.

Before the third man could put his hand in his pocket and get caught up in the wiles of this artful thief, as had happened with his friends, and before the magician could continue his fraudulent round of all those present, Mohammad Amin acted. He was far from happy to let that nefarious magician carry on as this was an act that would be disapproved of by anyone who had a free conscience. He turned towards the magician and said to him, ‘Come on! I accept your challenge. Come here! I want a turn to face up to you.’

The magician then left the person whose turn it was and made his way towards Mohammad Amin, swaggering proudly in front of all those present. The magician did not doubt for a single moment that he would repeat his success as he thought that there were no true believers in existence at that time.

He stood in front of Mohammad Amin who addressed him, saying: ‘I accept your challenge on one condition: if you can open my hand and take the lira, I will give you ten more liras in addition to that one, but if you cannot, I want you to stop what you’re doing, as this magic causes you nothing but further spiritual destruction.’

‘Do you agree?’

With full confidence, the magician accepted, as his insatiable greed for the eleven golden liras had blinded his heart to all else. He could think of nothing except for the great profit he would make that day, for he knew that it would usually take many months to collect such a sum through his quackery.

General Saleem, Mohammad Amin’s brother, was surprised at what his brother offered the magician. He had seen what had happened with the two men who were duped before him, so he thought that his brother would definitely lose eleven golden liras instead of only one.

So, why did he decide to get caught up in this game?

What for? What was wrong with him?

Trying to dissuade his brother from this course of action, he nudged him lightly and secretly expressed his advice to him with a certain look, as if he had said, ‘Stop! What’s the matter with you? Why would you want to throw away eleven golden liras?’

Salah al-Din, Mohammad Amin’s son, who was still sitting between his father and his uncle, noticed his uncle’s gestures of admonishment towards his father and his attempts to turn him away from this challenge.

Yet Amin paid no attention to his brother, and he took out his lira.

Failing to deter his brother General Saleem paused in his efforts and remained quiet and still, and then began to watch as his brother placed the lira on the palm of his hand and closed his fist over it as the other men had done… but the difference was that he exerted no particular force.

The magician drew close and stood facing him, and then started his attack with his motions and murmurs.

How strange… nothing happened!

The hand before him was still closed in the normal way and clearly not too tightly yet all the while the magician was still murmuring and making different signs with his hands. The magician persisted for quite some time, but still nothing changed. He tried and tried, murmuring, gesticulating, and making more and different motions with his hands… but it was all in vain!

Indeed, nothing had changed! Although about twenty minutes had passed, the magician did not despair. He did his utmost until eventually he became tired and frustrated at his lack of success. The magician had used all his so-called knowledge and skills but, this time he did not succeed!

What the boy Salah al-Din saw, and still remembers until this day, was that the magician was sweating with the great effort, and his disgusting, stinking sweat glistened all over his face, and then began to drip from his loathsome chin… drop by stinking drop.

Suddenly, the magician’s shifty gaze went towards the window and then to the door and flickered back and forth between them as if he was calling for outside help or support!

Whose help was he seeking?

Who was he calling upon for support?

At this point his behaviour became very odd indeed: he began to mutter some strange and obscure words in a most confused fashion, and his movements became erratic. It seemed as if fear had filled his heart and he was totally overcome by it.

But M. A. Sheikho remained in front of him, his hand still closed gently around the golden lira, a gentle smile playing on his lips. He sat there, full of calm satisfaction: his face bright and shining and displaying complete confidence that he had thwarted the sorcerer.

The situation had become unbearable for the magician, so he seemed to erupt and began to shout in a most irregular voice as if he had entered a struggle to the death. He started yelling at Mohammad Amin, ‘You, Bey! A secret power must be helping you!’

‘It is none but Al’lah!’ he replied in a voice more forceful and distinct than the magician’s, that struck him and all those present as if it were the sound of rumbling thunder.

‘I hold the Name of Al’lah!’

Those words rattled around the room and echoed from the walls… the ensuing silence was profound and mingled with the astonishment and stupefaction, which had overcome all those present. Yet there was also a strange and unusual feeling of delighted relief and happiness.

Actually, the magician had failed and what an outstanding failure it was!

He was overcome with angry emotions: he was agitated, hot and bothered, enraged; and what had he gained?… nothing but two liras and total stress.

Yes, he had definitely lost that round!

When he heard the words of Mohammad Amin – which had blasted his ears and uncovered his depravity and deceit – he uttered not a single word more. Then he walked out of the place, leaving it with his spirit debased, dragging behind him the remnants of his failure and huge defeat. He was reeling, his steps faltering, his head bowed in shame. But a certain thought was growing in his mind: ‘That man seems to have a strange secret. He really is a true believer.’ And that thought remained uppermost in his mind for quite some time!

Sometime later, a similar gathering took place in a wonderful park in a suburb of Damascus: at Abu Shafeek Park on al-Rabwa hill. Again, many rich and important men were invited to attend the celebration, and once more our virtuous man M. A. Sheikho was one of those present.

So it was that when the magician arrived there to practise his quackery and sorcery, he was surprised to see our compassionate scholar, and so his villainy and duplicity were immediately defeated in the face of the truth. He was exasperated as he realised he would not be able to perform his tricks and magic that day, so he adopted a humble attitude when he saw Mohammad Amin.

In a begging and lowly manner he approached him and in a pleading voice said, ‘Oh Bey! Please, for the sake of your beloved Al’lah! Please… Let me work… Let me earn my livelihood today… oh Bey! Look at all the guests, one by one: do you see a single iota of goodness in any one of them? All of them are far from God, and the devil is their companion… please, leave me alone so I can earn my living.’ It was clear that the magician wanted him to leave the place so that he would be able to control the men there with his magic.

However, Mohammad Amin paid him no attention at all, and as he looked at those present, he felt that all of them wanted the magician to stay. They wanted to laugh, to have fun and to enjoy his magical machinations. He said to himself, ‘Since they all want the magician to perform, I’ll leave them to it… it’s their own business.’

Thereafter, whenever the magician came across our righteous, compassionate officer he knew that this meant failure for him, so either he walked away from him or approached him humbly, grovelling and begging that he should be allowed to earn his dubious living.

In his wisdom Mohammad Amin left the magician and his audience alone as religion should never be used to force anyone against their will.

chapters.title: Part Five
chapters.html:
The Dignity of a Believing Officer

He had no other choice but to act as he did; his wisdom prompted him to demonstrate such a reaction in order to stave off the dreadful situation and put an end to the farce instigated by the arrogant Turkish officer.

A blanket of silence and an awful feeling of terror fell throughout the whole of government house, for all the officers and staff were thunderstruck at what they had just heard. They stood perfectly still, as if frozen to the spot, and gaped in amazement, hardly able to believe what had just taken place!

‘Is it possible?’ they all asked themselves, ‘did this really happen? Oh... how dare he?’ Yes, indeed! In the middle of the presidential palace, in the actual presence of not only a crowd of Turkish officers, but also the two most important men in the country: the governor-general and the commander-in-chief who were both in the building... the Arab officer, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, caring nothing for any one of them, brought out his revolver and shot in the direction of a Turkish officer!

Everyone who saw the event and those who heard the shooting were overcome by a sense of awe and terror when faced with this shocking situation. As for the officer whom Mohammad Amin had aimed at, when he saw the revolver directed towards him the words of mockery stopped inside his mouth which was agape due to its owner’s stupefaction. This quickly turned into dreadful dismay as the sound of shooting reverberated in his ears. He felt his heart fall to his boots as the bullet flashed past his ear; with the shock of this his power faded and his arrogance vanished, while his heart palpitated strongly and irregularly as though it would become detached from his body.

Truly, this incident was a great deterrent for him: after this lesson his spirit would never again dare to suggest that he should involve himself in troubles with the Arab officer Aslan, not even with so much as a single derogatory word. For he found him to be a man who cared for nothing, not even death, if anything should offend his dignity and pride.

This astonishing event took place when the eminent scholar was still an officer working in the government house in Damascus. There, all the officers, senior or junior, had the greatest respect for this reputable officer because of his humanity, his distinguished character and high sense of honour they sensed emanating from him, in addition to the success of his great feats, the likes of which they knew they were incapable of achieving. The awe-inspiring demeanour of our officer caused them to avoid showing or practicing any breach of God’s Orders in his presence.

We shall relate, dear reader, what caused this awful incident on that particular day. A group of officers were standing in the foyer of the building having a conversation, and from time to time they burst into raucous laughter.

They were engaged in their vulgar, sexual jokes when one of them noticed Aslan, the Arab officer, coming towards them. He hastily turned to the Turkish officer standing beside him who was still uttering shameful words, ‘Hush! Be careful, don’t say any more now.’

The Turkish officer looked at his friend and saw that his face had turned deathly pale, so he turned to see who or what had caused his friend’s confusion.

In the meantime, Officer Sheikho was still walking towards the main door of the building and approaching the crowd of officers. The Turkish officer looked at him and realised that he was an officer equal to him in rank, so he turned back to his friend and asked in amazement, ‘What’s wrong with you? I thought you were warning me of the commander-in-chief! Are you cautioning me about an officer equal to me in rank?’

‘He is a sheikh (a religious scholar),’ answered the first officer who could hardly utter his words for he could see how close Aslan was to them and could easily hear them.

A bellow of laughter issued from the haughty, conceited Turkish officer followed by a particularly rude comment full of scorn as he looked at the Arab officer and mocked him, ‘Sh... sh..sh... eikh... Ha... ha... ha...! Sh..sh... shei... kh..kh!’

But no sooner had he finished saying this than the sound of a shot rang out, sounding as loud as a cannon-shot in the large hall of the government house as it resounded like a clap of thunder on the ears of the uncouth, aggressive officer. Although the bullet zoomed past his ear and did not scathe him, he felt as though it had hit him and exploded in his head, so he fell to the floor with his eyes bulging, and trembling from head to toe with fear and alarm.

The bullet went straight through a wooden wall and continued on its path to pass between two clerks without touching them and eventually it settled in the outer wall of the hall!

Silence prevailed throughout the entire building, for everybody had either witnessed the event or heard the thunderous sound, and they stood speechless and motionless, their hearts fluttering, totally overcome by a state of shock.

Aslan, our high-minded officer, continued unflinchingly on his way, caring for nothing, until he left the hall and came to the outer square of the government house. He left them all behind, lost in a state of shock, the brazen officer still lying flat on the floor, senseless and seized by violent fear.

The governor-general was in his office with the commander-in-chief when he heard the shot so, naturally, he became alarmed and jumped to his feet. He sent the commander-in-chief to inquire about the matter. The chief commandant dashed out of the room like a bolt of lightning and, overwhelmed with anxiety, he asked the officers in the hall who had fire a gun. Their faces blushed with embarrassment as the brother officers reluctantly told their commander that it was Aslan. Without waiting for any further details about the incident, the commandant turned back to the office he had come from and spoke directly to the governor-general, the ruler of the country.

‘Your Honour! All is well. Some mischievous children tossed fireworks into the hall, but the gendarmes have thrown them out.’

When the governor knew that it was only children playing, he calmed down and regained his composure. Fortunately, the commander-in-chief did not ask for any further explanation of the event nor did he instigate further inquiries as to what had moved the Arab officer to commit such a grave, lawless act inside the inviolable house of government. This is because his friendly relations with Aslan, his firm trust in the wisdom of this honest officer and the magnificent measures he consistently took in the problems and difficulties that faced him in all his duties, made the commander-in-chief have absolute faith that there must have been a good reason and motive behind Aslan’s behaviour and that he had definitely acted in the most correct and appropriate way.

The commander did not tell the governor that there really had been a shooting, nor did he even approach the Arab officer involved. He allowed the serious event to pass and be forgotten as if nothing had happened.

Truly, the commander had such faith in our officer that the event of the shooting, despite its gravity, seemed a frivolous matter when compared to the many glorious performances of this humane officer.

It was Al’lah’s Will to defend the faith and dignity of this humane officer and to maintain him as an honourable, reverend master at the height of Godly Glory.

Thus, through the devilment of the Turkish officer who had dared to belittle Officer Sheikho, He raised him above all the Turkish officers, a matter which made them deem him a man to be reckoned with even more than before. They were afraid to misbehave with him, even in jest, due to their appreciation of his awe-inspiring personality and high prestige that was imprinted in their hearts.

As for that flippant, ill-mannered officer, he received due payment for his insolence, and thereafter he never dared to mention the name of our righteous officer or even look at his noble face.

This was the proper outcome, for glory belongs only to God, to His Envoy ﴿139﴾

and to all true believers.

chapters.title: His Enemies Confessed to His Excellence
chapters.html:
When Mohammad Amin Sheikho, the security officer, held the post of section manager in al- Zabadani, he girded his loins and prepared to work hard to overcome the troubles and strife which afflicted his country. This caused him no difficulty, as he was accustomed to tackling these matters in a positive and straightforward manner: by chasing criminals and arresting them until eventually the whole region capitulated to his justice.

In this way, the security situation was stabilised and order restored once again. Peace spread throughout the region and again people were able to go out of their houses safely and untroubled, after they had spent a long time being afraid and concerned. They had feared for their lives because of the criminal elements that prevailed in that area and the villages around it. But now, due to the brave deeds of Officer Sheikho, they were able to leave the safety of their houses in order to go to work and tend their orchards, with smiles on their faces.

Indeed, this officer spared no effort and sacrificed a lot of time along with his soldiers – who were, in fact, repentant criminals – in order to establish peace and security all over this region.

The people of the region fully realised all this and saw the results with their own eyes, for there was now a great difference in the security of the region between the period preceding Officer Sheikho taking up this post and the period that followed it. This is particularly significant when we know that the Ottoman State had failed to control the region of which we write, as it was adjacent to Lebanon. This gave the criminals the opportunity to flee into Lebanon where they could be protected by the international Law of the Protectorate which prevented the Ottoman authorities from having any power inside the Protectorate for any reason whatsoever.

To show the excellence of his deeds, dear reader, we should point out that after only one year of Officer Sheikho holding the post of regional manager, fresh produce and other goods were flowing freely in to the market once again, and the normal daily activities of buying and selling were safely resumed.

It had been many days since the commander had last visited this region in order to inspect the situation. There existed a firm relationship between this commander and Mohammad Amin: a relationship of love and appreciation which gave the humane officer a special and distinguished position in the eyes of the commander. In fact, it was a position that was higher than that of all the other officers because of his great achievements and unique successes.

This close relationship meant that they would often visit one another, especially when Mohammad Amin held a post away from the government house in the city of Damascus, where the commander worked.

It had been some time since the last meeting between the commander and the officer when Mohammad Amin decided to visit the commander and, as usual, he wanted to take a gift with him, but what should it be? He decided to take two baskets of apples, for the apples of this region are the finest in the world.

The following morning he rushed off to Damascus taking with him a large quantity of these delicious apples and, upon his arrival, he went straight to the commander’s house with a porter carrying the two baskets.

The exemplary master knocked gently at the door and waited patiently. After a few moments, the door was opened to reveal the commander and what a shock he received! He had not expected such a visitor on this day and at this time! He stared at the face of the benevolent master, and after some moments of silence, he barely managed to stutter a few words.

‘Ah... welcome... welcome Aslan! May Allah’s curse be on the driver... he dared to put a bottle of wine in the car, so I accidentally spilt it on my clothes... they’re completely stained with the wine... wait for me Aslan while I change them... may Allah’s curse be on the driver.’

Officer Mohammad Amin was astonished at the commander’s behaviour and his manner of talking... he wondered, ‘What’s the matter with him? And why is he talking in such a feeble, hesitant way? His words seem to be those of a man who was afraid and ashamed... what a strange thing!’

He had never known his commander to speak like this before.

The commander stopped talking and began to move backwards wanting to go and change his clothes, then Aslan addressed him with a look of astonishment on his face. ‘But sir... Commander... I wanted to offer you this,’ he said, pointing at the two baskets of apples.

‘All right... all right Aslan... thanks... thank you... put it here inside.’ the commander replied, speaking more quickly now.

Then he drew back leaving the honest officer standing there in a state of astonishment... wondering to himself but finding no logical reason, ‘Why did the commander behave like that? Why does he appear to be so confused and afraid?’

It really was very strange: the commander of the Ottoman army in all the al-Sham countries was shaking and extremely confused at the sight of one of his officers!

Later, and still in such a state, he returned to his guests, a group of officers who were gathered in a room of his house. They too were worried at the sight and of him, and his sorry state which was obvious from his face and in his movements. Then they immediately jumped up as though they had been stung for they thought it was a very serious matter. ‘Is it possible that the governor of al-Sham is coming now? Or what could it be?’

Every one of them made his own analysis of the situation of their leader, as they had never seen him in such a state before. They knew him, but always as a man of strong character and incomparable equanimity and bravery. But now, what was wrong with him? And who or what might have caused this situation?

The following day, an important Turkish officer visited Officer Mohammad Amin and said to him, ‘Aslan! The commander is certainly afraid of you!’

‘What? He is afraid of me! But why?’ said Officer Mohammad Amin.

He told Officer Mohammad Amin what had happened on the previous day and the reason for the commander’s strange state, then the conversation that was held between the commander and his officers after he had appeared totally confused, as if he had met the Grand Vizier or even the Ottoman Sultan when they were displeased with him.

One of the visiting officers said, ‘What’s the matter sir... what’s the matter?’

The commander replied in his confused tone, ‘Aslan... it’s Aslan.’

When the officers heard this word, their wish to hear the answer that was tinged with fear, instantly turned to extreme astonishment, to the extent that many of them asked at the same moment, ‘What’s the problem with him?’

The commander answered, ‘Can’t you see how drunk we are... the smell of wine has spread throughout the house.’ Some of them answered, ‘Oh commander! Let it be... what’s the problem... as he’s one of the officers under your authority?’ The commander replied, ‘That’s true... but he is noble Aslan... a man of the highest morals... he is an honourable man... no... no... he isn’t like us at all... we are vile, but he is pure and chaste.’

With that, all the officers remained silent and bowed their heads; each one of them remembering what he had seen or heard about officer Aslan, that venerable, humane man. Then they agreed that what they had heard from the commander was, indeed, the very truth. It is true that Aslan was an officer just as they were, but he was not actually like them at all. Although they held a higher military rank than his, he soared far above them in the skies of purity and chastity, and was far superior to them in morals and deeds. He was, in fact, a most honourable officer with sublime principles.

At that moment, Officer Mohammad Amin knew the reason for what he had witnessed the previous day, and the mystery that had baffled him all during the night was solved.

Thus, the possessor of high morals and sublime principles is always a master wherever he goes, and due to his uprightness he is respected by all people. This is because his Almighty Lord has clothed him in the garment of dignity and reverence for he has controlled his spirit and mastered it. Therefore, all the people around him, whether friends or enemies, can testify to his noble morals.

The People of Quraysh knew God’s Envoy Mohammad (cpth ﴿140﴾

before the Mission as: the true, the honest, possessor of great morals due to all that they had witnessed of his uprightness and noble manners. Then Al’lah the Almighty addressed them indicating his high spiritual state, with the noble verse, “Your companion has never been misled, nor has he deviated [from the uprightness].” ﴿141﴾

For it was true that they had never seen him deviate from the course of virtue and rightness, neither before the Mission nor after it. God’s Envoy (cpth) had never shaken hands with a woman or glanced at her illicitly, nor had he prostrated himself before an idol. If this had not been the truth, they would have said, ‘The Qur’an has not been revealed to him, for he has gone astray.’

Similarly, our venerable scholar, Mohammad Amin, adopted Al’lah’s Path and followed His Guidance truthfully and ethically: thus, he attained all the true knowledge from Al’lah.

This is the answer to whoever asks the following, ‘From where did he get his knowledge? And why was it revealed to him personally and not to another one of the religious scholars?’

chapters.title: The Officer, a Repentant Criminal and a Chicken Coop
chapters.html:
When Officer Mohammad Amin Sheikho assumed the leadership of the police station in the districts of al-Midan and al-Shaghour his daring deeds certainly equalled those he had previously carried out in the regions of al-Salhiyeh and al-Akrad. He became the chief topic of conversation of the criminals of these two quarters since he had destroyed their evil ways. On the one hand he saved people from the wrongdoing and evil actions of these criminals, and on the other he released the spirits of these criminals from the wrongful intentions settled therein, which would cause them to lose forever their eternal life, yet to come, as they would forfeit the donation which God had prepared for them because of the crimes they committed against humanity during their mortal lives.

In fact, there is a certain type of men who, in their distorted point of view, think that true manhood belongs only to them and that all other men are mere lesser specimens of manhood. This was the belief of many men during the time of our officer. They were deceived by the appearance of their huge bodies and taut muscles, not to mention their gruff voices and overbearing manner of speaking, by which they thought they displayed heroism and bravado before ordinary, law-abiding people.

They were so proud of their long twirled moustaches, to the extent that they might spend a considerable period of time standing vainly before a mirror, waxing and twirling them, as proud as peacocks at what was reflected back at them. Such moustaches were considered the measure of manhood in their society. They considered that they, and they alone, were the “real” men at that time while all other men were lesser mortals and of no value. To kill somebody did not matter much according to the “Law of the Jungle” they adopted. They were concerned only with themselves, and considered that all other men had been put on this earth to be destroyed or humiliated and humbled at their hands, and according to their whim. It was quite clear that their behaviour was no better than that of brutal wild animals, and lacked any sense of humanity.

Such were the appalling principles of the criminals of the towns before Officer Mohammad Amin Sheikho took up the reins of security in many regions, for it was his wisdom, genius and courage which would stamp out the injustice perpetrated by these culprits and help them regain their sense of rationality.

The story we are about to relate tells of one of these transgressors: he was one of the strongest and most arrogant of all the criminal leaders.

Nevertheless, he did not lack sound thinking, for having seen that many of his like had repented to God at the hands of our awe-inspiring officer, he decided to repent after he thought of the line he had followed all his life, and the horrible end that was awaiting him.

He thought and thought until he realised that death would be his inevitable destination, as it would be for all mankind, so how would he meet his Provider? He was aware of his crimes and evil deeds; so what would his situation be before God when He saw how he had hurt His servants, killed some and stole from others? This sound logic led him to take a positive decision, to change the course of his life and to repent faithfully to God. He determined to turn his back on all kinds of wickedness and shameful deeds, to refrain from his disobedience to God and his practising whatever is forbidden. He made up his mind to return to God in repentance, just as many of his friends had done, and follow the right path. There and then, he carried out his decision and started a new stage of his life, marked by straightness and obedience.

The amazing deeds of the bold officer, Mohammad Amin, were the talk of the people of both quarters, al-Midan and al- Shaghour. Even the comrades of this repentant criminal often told of the schemes and exemplary punishments the officer employed for chasing and arresting them. Indeed he always managed to curtail the progress of their criminality and curb them with his fearlessness. And so, because of the heroic deeds of our officer this repentant criminal had heard about him, but since he had never met him or even seen him accidentally, he set about imagining various pictures of the officer’s appearance, ‘He’s a tall, strong, brawny man, endowed with a huge, muscular body... and surely he has a thick, black moustache with curled ends covering much of his face.’ This was the vision he had of the great officer, for such features were the marks of manhood and courage amongst this type of man. It was grossly exaggerated, as he imagined him to be much bigger and broader and taller than any one of his own criminal acquaintances.

One day, it happened that the repentant man was sitting on a chair at the door of a wheat store in al-Midan quarter, chatting with the owner of the store, a wheat merchant, when the conversation turned to the head of the local police station: how he chastised all criminals and defeated them, to the extent that they were afraid of him and took to their heels whenever they saw him. The merchant mentioned many incidents when the officer had pursued the criminals in the al- Midan and al-Shaghour quarters.

This was the subject of their conversation when Officer Sheikho, the man they were talking about, crossed the street before them, his willowy stature clothed in his smart khaki uniform. He advanced briskly, so fleet of foot that one might say he appeared to be flying. The merchant saw him and pointing in his direction, he said to the repentant criminal, ‘Look! That’s him, the head of the police station, Officer Sheikho.’

With great curiosity, the repentant man turned to have a look at the superman whom he had imagined to be huge and powerful. But... how strange! He did not see the coarsefeatured man he expected to see according to his own, colourful imagination, and to what he had heard about the officer and his overwhelming success when chasing the former leader’s criminal friends!

Very strange indeed!

The officer was not endowed with a gigantic body and taut muscles nor did he have a thick moustache, long and curled at the ends; he was not a strutting, mighty man who had bared his brown, powerful arms and stomped around causing the earth to shake beneath his feet! The former criminal failed to find any semblance of the physical shape he had imagined. Instead, he saw a young, handsome man, like a shining moon encircled with glory, walking with graceful, but vigorous steps! How far removed was the fact from the fiction!

‘I’m so confused!’ he thought. ‘Could this really be the man who overpowers culprits, causes them sleepless nights and instills horror in their hearts? Is this the officer that controlled them all and caused them so much trouble, who shredded their hopes with his iron fist and formidable character?’

With that, the tradition of his criminal ignorance, the seeds of which were still implanted within him, crept once again into his mind to reveal itself through his words and actions. So, being clearly annoyed because of the unexpected sight he had just seen, he said in a loud voice, ‘Is this the man whose very name has instilled terror in the hearts of tough men? Shame on you, men of al-Midan! Shame on you, ha... ha... powerful men! Is this person whose appearance is as soft as that of a woman, the officer who caused you so much trouble that you’re afraid even to whisper his name? Again, I say shame on all of you!’

But Godly Will refused to allow this repentant criminal to continue with this wrongful judgement, so It gave him the experience of a practical lesson to help him regain his sense of reason and make him understand that courage should not be judged according to physical shape and size, but is born in the hearts of men who have an unwavering belief in God that leads them to love justice and assist it. And on the other hand, God holds victory in His Hands and He grants it to those who follow His Straight Path and seek truthfully to establish what is right and true.

So, in the evening of the day when the repentant criminal had met our officer for the first time, he also met a criminal from his old gang, who went by the name of Abu al-Lail. He greeted him, ‘Hello,’ said Abu al-Lail, ‘How are you, man? Welcome... welcome... master of all strong men! Where have you been, man? We haven’t seen you for a long time. We’ve really missed you; all the men have been asking about you. They’re longing to see your handsome face. Don’t you miss your friends and hanker after the good old days? Don’t you remember how great they were? By God, we miss you so much.’ The repentant criminal replied to his friend, ‘Oh Abu al-Lail! I’ve left behind my old wrongful path and don’t have any more inclination for it. For how much longer shall I continue to disobey my Lord and hurt all those around me? No... I’ve had enough... it was no way to live, I want to enjoy a safe and peaceful life.’

‘As you like my friend, it’s your own life and you’re free to choose the path you want to follow. But don’t forget us, my friend; let’s see you from time to time. And today I’m inviting you to come to an evening entertainment with our friends, just for them to see you and have a chat... you don’t have to drink if you don’t want to; but it will make us happy just to have your company.’

‘But...’ the repentant man replied, ‘how can I sit with you while you drink wine, and break God’s Orders?’

‘What’s wrong in that my friend? We’ll be the ones drinking, not you. You only have to sit with us so we can enjoy each other’s company. We just want to see you because the men have really missed you.’

And so, his friend insisted on the invitation and made him promise to share their merry-making that night. And so it was that with these friendly words, the repentant criminal weakened and surrendered to his friend; he agreed to join the men but only on condition that he would not practise any forbidden acts with them.

Later that day, after the evening prayer, the two friends met and headed towards the place where they would all meet up to spend their night according to their whims and fancies.

They went into an Arabian-style house with a large courtyard surrounded by many rooms, with a fountain in the centre. The owner of the house had given it over to illicit purposes. Those who frequented the establishment wanted to enjoy drinking wine, and amuse themselves just as they liked. And for obvious reasons they had to hide within its enclosing walls so as to be out of sight of the police, as such gatherings were unlawful during the time of Ottoman rule. In this way, this kind of people could enjoy their boisterous entertainment without being held accountable.

When the two friends entered the brothel there was a crowd of their fellow criminals inside, and so, having been surprised at the arrival of their old friend, they rushed towards the newcomer to give him a hearty welcome. They embraced him one after another and showered him with friendly words and happy smiles that soon made him forget his repentance. He lost no time in rejoining their group and becoming one of them once again, laughing along with them, enjoying the raucous banter that appealed to them, and enjoying the same things they took pleasure in.

The alcohol had not yet been offered to them, for some were still arranging the bottles and cups on tables in a special room, together with mixed nuts and other tidbits, so that when the songstress began to sing songs to inspire fornication and inflame forbidden desires their pleasure and enjoyment would be complete.

The conversation went back and forth and moved from one senseless topic to yet another even more degraded and insignificant, and from time to time, noisy bursts of raucous laughter rang out throughout the house: the barbarous, irresponsible scene had clearly divorced itself from all sense of humanity. They laughed and sang and then broke out in spontaneous yells and shouts as if they had lost their minds. They were entirely immersed in their debauchery... To complete their enjoyment they were waiting only to clink their wineglasses and drink a toast to each other and to delight their ears with the music and songs of a harlot that would inflame their desires.

This was the atmosphere inside that house when suddenly someone let out a loud cry... in a voice that seemed to tremble with fear, as it broke through that inhuman festival. Instantly, absolute silence descended over the whole house and all heads turned towards the source of the sound to find out what was wrong. The person who had cried out had come out of the room where the drinks and tidbits were being prepared when he saw that the security forces had climbed the walls of the house and were settled down in the courtyard. There and then, a thunderous, dreadful voice resounded throughout the whole house, making hearts tremble and implanting a strange horror in the spirits of all who were there, which caused them to lose their heads.

It was him, Aslan ﴿142﴾

, the awe-inspiring officer who had arrived like a bolt from the blue with a squad of policemen. And wasting no time they attacked the place like a cyclone or a destructive thunderbolt.

What a peerless terrifying appearance this officer had! What singular courage! What incomparable resolve he displayed that never acknowledged the possibility of failure! His voice tore down the mountains of disbelief and infringements of God’s Orders settled in the hearts of those criminals and thereby paralysed their powers and their daring to practise wrongdoing and fornication. They all heard the booming cry, which shook the walls of the house, and they recognised its owner: it was him, the head of the police station, in person. He was actually inside the house.

As soon as they realised this, their hearts leapt into their mouths and all the strength fled from their bodies. They had certainly not expected to face such a compromising situation, for they had taken every precaution to be out of sight so that no one might know anything about their clandestine gathering. But unfortunately, their secret was out and they would certainly receive a severe punishment.

The bold officer kept on railing at their cowardly evil conduct, filling their hearts with trembling fear, and utterly disrupting their gathering. Some of them cowered in front of him while others tried to run away and rushed off like startled wild asses, each one trying desperately to save himself. Still the brave officer, along with his men, leapt towards them and many were arrested while just a few managed to escape.

Now let us focus our attention on the repentant criminal, the subject of our story, who had turned away from repentance and turned instead back to the pleasures he had enjoyed formerly with his old friends. When he heard the thunderous voice of our officer rumbling throughout the house he felt as though it had pervaded every molecule of his body and he was struck by such overwhelming terror that his limbs began to quiver. He could not control his tremors nor could he understand what had come over him. A strange feeling of terrifying and awesome fear had seemed to shackle his limbs causing them to lose their strength until they felt completely crushed. Truly, at that moment he felt that he could not put up the least physical resistance, not even to a little child. He had never previously, in all his life, experienced such a terrible situation, ‘Where have my manliness and strength disappeared to? I don’t understand what’s happening to me!’ he said to himself. His rough appearance was of no use to him for he had become like a panic-stricken rabbit.

But what about his impressive, long, twirled moustache?

What about his bulging muscles and powerful body? They were of no use to him either!

With great difficulty, and deathly pale, he gathered his strength and went upstairs to the roof where he looked around to find a safe hiding place... somewhere he could avoid hearing the booming threats and menaces of the courageous officer, the commandant of this patrol. But there was no place for him to take shelter except in a chicken coop situated at a corner of the roof; having no other option he sneaked inside, crouched down and hoped to be rescued from the lion’s ferocious attack.

Many hours passed while the brawny man hid in the coop, his body trembling from head to toe, his heart beating rapidly as his chest clearly moved up and down in rhythm with its beating. Although the dauntless officer and his men had left the house, having driven with them a group of the criminals in shackles ready to be thrown into prison, the criminal in question remained inside the coop for many more hours even though he realised that the danger had passed and he could come out safely. His teeth were chattering as if he was in the midst of a bitterly cold snow storm. He could not get over the extreme, strange terror that struck him forcibly the moment he heard that impressive, formidable voice of our officer. Finally, the criminal decided to move out of his hiding place, and as he did so his movements still displayed signs of the fear that had overcome him.

He ran towards his home and entered while signs of dumbfounding shock were still evident on his face and, in fact, throughout his entire body. He threw himself on the bed, but since he was terrified he could not possibly sleep. He could not forget the events he had recently experienced and was still wondering about the secret behind that voice which caused the earth to shake under his feet. He had spent a long life in crime and wrongdoing, how many times had he been in difficult situations and faced being killed, but, throughout it all he had never felt even the smallest degree of the fear he felt when hearing the thunderous shouts of Officer Sheikho.

He realised that this officer’s character was not to be sniffed at and surely he was a man to be reckoned with! So, his criminal fellows had every right to have a thousand apprehensions about this officer and to talk about him with fear and trepidation. No doubt, the Almighty had dressed him with an awe-inspiring appearance that caused them many sleepless nights and made them think a many, many times before daring to do any wrong.

The following morning, when the people who were employed had gone to their place of work and started their jobs, the repentant criminal set off in a hurry, heading towards the police station intending to meet our brave officer. He decided to apologise to him for mocking him the day before, when he was in the wheat store, and to tell him what had happened to him that same evening.

He entered Officer Amin Sheikho’s office at the police station, and looked at our man with eyes full of reverence and admiration. He greeted the officer, who replied with his customary smile and kindness. Our officer invited the repentant man to have a seat then called for his janitor to bring a cup of coffee for the visitor.

‘How can I help you, brother?’ the venerable officer asked his guest.

The repentant criminal replied, ‘Sir, I have something to tell you.’

‘Yes, go ahead... tell me whatever you want.’

The repentant man began to speak and related his story to the officer from the beginning up to the event that he had experienced the day before his visit:

‘Oh sir, I was a criminal and it never troubled me to commit any crime, either great or small, but thanks be to God for I have returned to Him in repentance and regained my sense of reason. But, sir, yesterday I said bad things against you, and to speak frankly, sir, I even spat on the earth damning the men of al-Midan quarter... how they claim to be courageous and fear a man like you; I beg your pardon, sir, for my stupid judgement about your appearance. When I said this sir, you did not see me, for at that moment you walked past without noticing me. But, sir, one of my old friends, a former brother in crime, had invited me to join in their revelry with them that evening and insisted on taking me with him to their secret party. He said that he wanted me to go because the men would be happy to see me for they had missed me so much, and I was no longer obliged to drink with them or share them with in practising what is forbidden. That’s how he convinced me to go there with him. But, sir, we had hardly finished saying hello and reminiscing over the times we used to spend together when suddenly you, accompanied by your men, broke into the house we were in. Then, sir, I heard your terrible voice thundering throughout the house. Truly, sir, I was overcome by a feeling of such terror the like of which I had never known before in my entire life. I would never forget the awful moments I experienced when I heard your voice which then threw me into a complete daze!

‘I climbed the stairs to the roof but don’t know how I managed to do it for I felt petrified with fear, and there I hid myself in a chicken coop so as to be out of your reach and sight. Yes, sir, I confess that I was so afraid of you that I even hid inside a dirty chicken coop!

‘By God, sir, even after you and your men left it was many hours until I was able to control my fear and feel safe, and still I found it difficult to come out of my hiding place and head towards my home.

‘It was only then, sir, that I understood why evil men repent and turn to God at your hands. And only then did I excuse the strong men of al-Midan who fear you and avoid meeting you. How could they not do that when your roaring voice is like a cry of truth that paralyses wrongdoers, causes their guilty hearts to shake and thus puts an end to their evil ways! How could they not do that when your awe-inspiring appearance at the moment of attack and confrontation razes the mountains of criminality down to the ground.

So, I take back all that I said against you, sir, and I hope that you may forgive me.’

When the repentant man finished his frank speech, our officer opened the register lying on the table before him, which included a list of the names of the criminals of the town. He looked inside until he found the name of the criminal before him, and then said to him ‘Yes... your name is actually included on the list of repentant criminals.’

But there and then, the gentle tone of the officer’s voice changed completely to one of firmness and censure just like a rational, tender-hearted father, speaking to his son, concerned about his future, while the repentant man stared at him, dumbstruck and with his mouth gaping wide. Our officer continued with his words of admonishment, saying, ‘Why did you agree to see them again and to spend the evening with them after you had decided to repent and turn to God? Is this acceptable? How did you agree to go with him even if he insisted and swore at you to do so? Why did you give in to him and comply with his mean and dirty request? Don’t you know that when meeting with these men it is natural for you to yearn for your past and turn your back on repentance causing you to lose your life here and in the other abode? Beware of doing such a thing even one more time; you should give praise to God that He saved you from their wily ways and that the matter ended peacefully. You should promise your Lord that you will never do this again.’

The man was so affected by the noble officer’s compassionate words of admonition that tears of sorrow and relief coursed down his cheeks, for he fully regretted what he had done. And so, he finally left the police station, but not before he promised his Lord that he would not associate with evil companions any more after the terrible situation he had recently experienced and after the conversation he had just had with the merciful officer. He thanked his Provider for His Care for him and was extremely grateful for the advice of the fearless, wise and humane officer Mohammad Amin Sheikho.

The lesson we learn from this story is that true faith is obtained when one is truly repentant, and this can be accomplished by keeping away from forbidden actions and from those who practise them. For even though a man may refrain from committing wrongful deeds, if he keeps company with evil people he will certainly return to his old ways.

For it was said, “Tell me who your companions are and I will tell you who you are.”

chapters.title: Danger Overcome on the Al - Qaboon Highway
chapters.html:
Danger Overcome on the Al-Qaboon Highway

The Ottoman Empire lost its former strength and glory and became like a sick old man compared with the European States. This period of weakness began towards the end of Turkish rule in the Arab countries where criminality and depravity prevailed and disorder spread over all areas. This came about as a result of the Ottoman Empire giving up following the Orders of Almighty Al’lah.

For a certain time during that period, Officer Mohammad Amin held the post of regional manager in Barzeh, which was far from Damascus.

That entire area was covered by forest, and all the trees which grew closely together for many kilometres, were tall and abundant, rather like those in a tropical forest which made the region a safe haven for criminals and some highway robbers who lived there.

It was Friday when Officer Mohammad Amin left the regional management office heading for his house in Damascus where he had decided to spend his weekend and seize the opportunity to deal with some personal matters. But no sooner had he arrived at his house, than something quite unexpected happened to him! He was afflicted with a severe fever that made him stay in his bed, unable to leave it without great difficulty. His temperature was very high (about 40° C), causing him to sweat profusely. He was also overcome by an extreme headache, backache and a sore throat.

While lying in his bed in such a painful state, various worrying thoughts came to his mind, ‘If I don’t go to work, they will certainly say that I’m a coward and afraid to face up to the current serious security situation. They will think that l came away from the section and left the gendarme to face a dangerous situation while I slackened off to enjoy the safety and security of my home.... I’m sure that’s what they will say about me... but, oh my God! This terrible fever has overcome me and forced me to keep to my bed... so how can I possibly go to work?’

It was an extremely difficult position for any brave man to be faced with, and especially for our noble officer, for he truly preferred death to being accused of cowardice and facing defeat... he would have preferred that the ground might open up and swallow him rather than be accused falsely of cowardice and weakness. Then he continued discussing his critical position, ‘No... no... I don’t want any false stories to be circulated about me... I shall get up now and go to my work.’

The serious breaches of security on the road to Barzeh – especially during those troubled times – would certainly expose travellers to attacks by criminals or other hooligans who would seize the opportunity during the time of political confusion and lack of security to carry out violent attacks and robberies. So, despite his illness, Officer Sheikho decided to go to the section at whatever cost to himself, for refused to let any of the leaders mention the word “coward” in regard to him for he was the so-called Aslan ﴿143﴾

... and known for his unparalleled bravery.

After taking this decision, he called out to his mother in his weak and weary voice, ‘Oh mother! Would you bring me my military uniform!’

She replied in a voice full of sympathy and compassion, ‘What! What do you say my dear son... your military uniform? But you’re in such a bad state! You have a fever and cannot get up... you are soaked by your own sweat... Oh my son! May Al’lah be pleased with you... stay in your bed until you recover, by Al’lah’s Will, then you can go if you want to.’

But he begged her, ‘Please bring it mother... if you won’t... I’ll do it myself... bring it to me and get yourself ready to go with me... tell my wife too.’

His mother gave in for she realised just how determined he was: she knew that when he decided to do something, nothing could make him change his mind. So, she brought the uniform to him, and helped him to put it on, and when he was ready, they went downstairs and out to the street where a horse-drawn cab was waiting for him.

He could hardly walk, and had to lean heavily on his mother and wife until he reached the cab. It was drawn by a pair of horses and had a door at the back with an adjustable hood that covered it and separated them from the driver who sat in his seat in the front. When they had all got into the cab, Aslan called out to the driver, ‘Let’s go to Barzeh... driver.’

The driver was amazed and terrified, and thought to himself, ‘Does anyone dare to go to Barzeh in these dangerous times when no man can be sure of coming back alive?’ and he said stuttering, ‘To... to Bar... to Barzeh sir? To Barzeh?’

Thereupon, Aslan shouted at him, ‘Let’s go!’

He turned as pale as a corpse and his lips moved without uttering a single sound. He had no choice but to drive off in the cab, all the while thinking that the end of his life would come sooner rather than later!

The cab set off at top speed along the road which was covered by a canopy of the tall leafy trees that shut out the sunshine, while the suffering officer laid his head on his mother’s knee and stretched out his legs towards his wife, then he closed his eyes and could not even try to open them because of the severe fever and pains which he was suffering.

The cab was dashing along, its wheels bouncing noisily over the stones with the cab swaying from side to side while the patient was groaning softly due to his great pain... a most unusual situation, however ill he felt.

As for his poor mother, she bent over him, her eyes full of mercy and sympathy, feeling his suffering and sharing his pain.

The journey continued in this way until they reached Tora Bridge, the little bridge, about six meters long, that crossed the Yazid River, a branch of the Barada. And right there is where something serious happened.

While Officer Mohammad Amin was still suffering from the severe fever, lying in the same position, he felt drops of water falling on his hot, flushed face. He opened his eyes and saw his mother’s tears running down her face. He felt that the cab was stopping, so he asked, ‘What’s the matter, Mother? Why are you crying?’

She was barely able to speak, and with a deep sigh she said, ‘We’ll certainly be disgraced... we’ll all be killed... they are highwaymen.’

No sooner had she finished speaking than he leaped up like a lion ready to face grave danger! With a single kick, he broke the door off the cab and followed this by leaping out to face one of the highway robbers pointing his gun toward the cab. Without a moment’s hesitation, he punched the criminal’s face with all his might. With this unexpected ferocious attack, the robber felt as if a thunder bolt had smashed into his head and he fell to the ground, unconscious, with his pistol beside him.

The brave officer then turned to the front of the cab and found the second robber had fled with his pistol after he had seen what had happened to his crony.

The robber could never have expected this outcome! How had it happened?... and all within just a few seconds! He was terrified so he ran off wanting nothing more than saving himself after shooting at the driver who, trembling with fear, raised his hands up to surrender.

But that brave officer did not let the criminal go, and he ran after him at amazing speed until he grabbed him. He beat him and took the gun from him, then he dragged him to the cab where his crony was lying on the ground unconscious. He tied them together to the back of the cab, and then went back to lying down with his head on his mother’s knee and his legs stretched out towards his wife; whereupon he began groaning again because of the severe pain he was still suffering, with glistening drops of sweat dripping from his noble forehead.

The danger that had surrounded them suddenly disappeared, and the feeling that they were surely about to die left his mother and wife along with it.

When the two highway robbers had stopped the cab, and one of them had fired his gun at the driver, and the other one at the travellers, the wife thought that they would surely be killed as she knew that her poor husband was unable to do so much as stand up. She had never expected or even imagined that her husband might do such a deed or show such great ability.

‘How could he instantly overcome illness and weakness and rush with such strength that I had never seen the like of before! He looked like a powerful, leaping lion and was able to arrest two armed men while he was unarmed and had a high fever! How was he able to do that? And what bravery had possessed this man! What high aspiration and wonderful willpower had burst in his spirit to make the impossible possible, turn weakness into strength, and with a single outburst, defend the truth. What determination he had shown before which all difficulties break down and duplicity is destroyed and wiped out!’

That was what Mohammad Amin’s wife thought to herself.

That wonderful sight made her prostrate herself before her husband, showing her true appreciation as she had never seen him react like that before. She had heard a lot about his fearless, manly deeds, his courage, and his capabilities, but now she witnessed him in action... she witnessed the reality of his deeds.

When they arrived at the police station, he put the two arrested men in a cell until the following day, by which time when he was feeling somewhat better. He sent for the robbers to investigate their case, and he found that it was only dire need that had forced them to follow such a bad, criminal road; for each of them had a family and could barely provide food to keep his children alive since he had no job to earn his livelihood legally.

At that time, with the demise of the Ottoman Empire, disorder and anarchy controlled the country and unemployment was rife; many jobs in all fields were lost, and men were unable to provide even basic necessities for their families.

Because of the difficult circumstances these men had suffered, which forced them to do such wrong inhumane deeds, Officer Mohammad Amin forgave them and released them after giving them sufficient money to support their families for many months.

Thus, his conduct always displayed his great mercy and compassion. Before punishing the robber or wrongdoer you must investigate his situation. If he steals due to force of necessaity, help him. But if he robs again though he is no longer in need, this act shall be seen as arising from a spiritual defect and then you have the right, no, the obligation to arrest and punish him in order to uproot the affliction and evil from his spirit.

Many days later, after he heard of Aslan’s illness and spectacular deed on the dangerous road to Barzeh, the commander visited him. He had also heard of the strange, remarkable story of the arrest of the highway robbers, and totally astonished he addressed the officer, ‘Aslan! How did you dare to take such a risk under such serious circumstances? You know... if I were you I would never have gone!’

‘Oh sir... Commander! I want you to swear by God that if I had not gone, that you would not say that I was a coward.’ Aslan replied.

‘Yes... by God I would,’ the Commander said.

Then he remained silent preoccupied with thoughts of the officer’s amazing courage and willpower, and respect for this exalted, honourable spirit.

What a great risk! And truly all people should be like him and place their trust in God.

chapters.title: Obsequious Behaviour Is not Tolerated
chapters.html:
Dear reader, the story we are about to relate may be a practical interpretation of the reality of the noble verse, “Honour belongs to Al’lah and His Envoys, and to the believers.” ﴿144﴾

You might also find other relevant points and glean useful lessons from it.

The events of this story took place in Barzeh, in the region of Ghoutah, the verdant and fertile oasis of Damascus, at the time when our noble man, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, held the post of regional manager there.

This region was notable for its wide open spaces and vast areas of arable land. Some of it was forested, while other parts were planted with various kinds of grain, greenery and vegetables. The region was in a sorry state before our magnanimous officer took up his post there. Due to the condition of the area, a feudatory held power over the people; he greatly exploited them but they were powerless to do anything about their situation. He deprived them of the fruits of their labour and the wages for their work, which meant that the farmer and his family might go to bed hungry after a long day spent labouring in the fields.

The feudatory of whom we write had amassed great wealth by bribing previous managers and their gendarmes to encourage them to shut their eyes to his depriving the people of their rights and seizing their land. This enabled him to go to extremes in his oppression: he broke all laws, with nothing and no one to deter him, and no man to stand up to his tyranny. But, would he persist in this oppression? And would matters continue in the same way as that overlord expected once our honest officer Aslan took up his post? For this unscrupulous man had dealt with many regional managers before our officer arrived, and his business was always facilitated by them because of the large bribes with which he bought their passive compliance and encouraged them to close their eyes to his wrongdoing.

Therefore, when Officer Mohammad Amin took up his post, the overlord attached no importance to the matter, and as he had always done with past regional managers, he immediately went to see him, to sweet-talk him and grovel before him, offering his services and assistance, and showing his false admiration for the new officer in order to earn his favour; just as he had done with previous managers.

The meeting proceeded in the usual manner and Officer Mohammad Amin spoke to the feudatory and thanked him for his sentiments and kind offer, but he was fully aware of what lay behind that obsequiousness. It was for the personal benefits he sought to achieve by denying the rights of others and asking our officer to ignore the unlawful acts that he had no intention of giving up.

But, dear reader, would he achieve his evil aims?

Certainly, the overlord believed that nothing would change as he was confident that with large sums of money, he could buy the officer’s acquiescence in his ruthless aims.

When Officer Mohammad Amin set out to introduce reform and bring about change throughout the entire agricultural area of that region, he faced many difficulties but, as always, he overcame them. And after only a few days of the officer’s reformative actions the feudatory was shocked by an incident he certainly had not expected! For the new manager stood in the way of his exploitation and oppression of the local people. He realised immediately the gravity of his position, so he rushed off to see the new manager to grovel once again and flatter him with his soft words, offering his services and assistance in any way possible. And he did not stop there, for he realised that this approach had not been successful the first time, so he brought with him some precious gifts, even though he was known to be an extremely stingy man. But in fact, he found a reaction which he did not expect, for the regional manager adamantly, but politely, refused all the presents and gifts.

The disappointed feudatory left the section office, but day after day he tried to approach the honest officer cringing before him and asking him to overlook his unlawful actions.

In fact, the truth that was settled within the spirit of this upright, honest officer made the feudatory’s aims impossible to achieve. His evil actions were no longer possible because of the existence of the honest master, Mohammad Amin, who dispelled oppression and reinstated the rights of the people.

As for the overlord, he did not stop in his efforts to get close to the officer and continued to show his great love and admiration; many times he sought to bring the officer to his house for a banquet, but he never succeeded.

Thus, he got no support for his wrongdoing from that noble master, and so he came to hate him, but he was as sly as a fox, for he cleverly hid his hatred and showed nothing but love and obsequious tactics, trying to earn the officer’s satisfaction and compliance.

That was how the matter progressed until this honest officer moved to another section, and the day of his departure would never be forgotten by the feudatory. For him it was a day of great happiness, for the man who had stood firmly in the way of his oppression and tyranny had left, so he could return to his unlawful acts as there was no longer anyone to call him to account.

One day, while that upright man, Mohammad Amin, was sitting in his house, there was a knock at the door. He opened it to find one of his acquaintances there, a person he did not know very well. The visitor greeted Mohammad Amin who welcomed him amicably and received him in a hospitable way.

Inside the house, the guest soon stated the reason for his visit. ‘Abu Fathi... you selfless man! I want you to help me through your knowledge... I want to buy some arable land in the region of al-Ghoutah where you used to work. I’m sure you had many acquaintances there, and you can help me to achieve my aim through them. Would you do me a favour and help me with this?’

Mohammad Amin replied, ‘Yes, certainly... by Al’lah’s Will I’ll do my best to help with what you want.’

The guest smiled, and his increasing optimism was displayed on his face, as he said, ‘This is exactly what I expected from you... you have never changed... rather you grow more kind and generous, and your essence becomes even purer and more brilliant. Thank you very much... may Al’lah reward your goodness.’

Half an hour passed in pleasant and agreeable conversation, then the guest left in cheerful high spirits after the two men had made an appointment to discuss the results of Mohammad Amin’s enquiries.

Our righteous man recalled the days that he had served in that section, then he remembered that despicable overlord, and his bootlicking and attempted bribery, so he decided to visit him the next day.

In the morning, before setting off to the area which was not far away, he sat for a while to think about the journey, for it might need some planning, especially as he had heard a lot about the feudatory’s extreme miserliness, from people of the region. Therefore, our officer immediately decided to go to the market and buy one kilo of fresh meat, then he ordered it to be grilled and added some vegetables. He folded it in a piece of flatbread and wrapped it; then he headed off to the Barzeh section where he had once occupied the post of regional manager.

Driven by the intention of carrying out the kind deed which the acquaintance had asked him to do, his forthcoming journey filled him with great pleasure.

Mounting his unique white horse, he passed through the orchards of al-Ghoutah and its lush orange groves, enjoying its cool soft breezes that carried the aromas of various fruits and the sweet fragrance of roses and flowers. When he reached the countryside he was in a state of great joy and spiritual relief as he headed for the house of the feudatory.

When the local people saw him, they longed for his return and for the time when fairness prevailed. No one he met in the lanes of the countryside passed him without smiling and raising a hand in greeting, saying, ‘Welcome sir... welcome... come in please!’

As for Officer Aslan, he returned their greetings in the best way, with a constant smile on his noble countenance, and kind and gentle words for all of them.

When he arrived at the overlord’s house, still mounted on his white horse, he approached the door, then stretched out his leg and gave a powerful kick at the door!

After a few moments the door was opened to reveal the overlord in person...and what a great surprise he received for it was the former regional manager himself who had banged at the door! It was not a pleasant surprise, in fact it was such a shock that it brought a frown to his face and his countenance darkened!

The venerable officer greeted him and the feudatory returned his greeting; then Mohammad Amin asked him if he had any arable land for sale, or knew someone who wanted to sell a piece of land in the region.

The overlord held such hateful feelings towards our officer that his face paled at the very sight of him; and completely lacking in any kind of chivalry or respect he replied in a very rough manner, ‘No... I don’t have any land for sale, and I don’t know anyone who wants to sell land.’

And instantly he retreated and shut the door without uttering another word, contrary to his past manner, when his friendly honeyed phrases full of hypocrisy had flowed from his tongue and he had greatly exaggerated in showing false respect and high praise for Officer Sheikho. But now, he did not invite the officer to enter the house... or even utter a single word... he simply shut the door.

Mohammad Amin had never received such treatment from him when he held his post as a regional manager of the district, but he knew him well and understand all that he had heard about the man’s miserliness, stinginess and lack of chivalry, so he left and set off to look for a piece of land of the requested specifications until he found it.

He then returned to the feudatory and kicked at the door once again while still mounted on his horse. The miserable man opened the door and this time it was only his head that appeared around the edge of the door as he asked, ‘What do you want?’

Officer Aslan replied, ‘Hey you... listen to me... whoever knocks at the door with his foot... does not stretch out his hand to ask for help. Thank God that I have not dismounted my horse, and my actions were correct when I did not allow you to encroach upon anyone’s rights; nor did I eat any food with which you tried to tempt me. Know that he who stretches his leg, does not offer his hand.’

Then he took out the wrapped food and opened it to display the grilled meat and he addressed the feudatory, ‘I’m sure you won’t offer me anything more delicious than this meat... I don’t need you, nor do I need your welcome or invitation to have food. I thank God that I have never once been deceived by you.’

He turned his horse forcefully, showing great disdain for the deeds and character of the overlord, and hurried off to a pleasantly cool and shady place where there flowed a creek of sparkling water. He sat there and spread open the package of meat and ate happily and cheerfully. When he was sated, he went to the bank of the creek and drank from its fresh cold water, then he praised God most highly for His Graces and for enabling him to distinguish between good and evil, for he had expected the treatment that he received from the feudatory and had never been deceived by him either now or in the past. He knew well that his previous kind treatment and his bootlicking and offering of presents, services, and invitations to banquets – which were always met by our officer’s refusal – were only to serve the overlord’s personal interests and base purposes which he might attain through the executive power of our honourable officer, Aslan. But now that Mohammad Amin had moved to another region, that shameful man had no further use for him, therefore he was neither welcomed nor received hospitably as a guest. The despicable man used to welcome only those guests whom he thought could further his personal interests, but to welcome and receive them for mere humane or friendly purposes would be a loss in his sight.

Officer Mohammad Amin had left that region happily thanking God that he had upset the obsequious overlord but had not displeased Al’lah, for he had never complied with that contemptible man in any of his wrongdoing or oppression.

Such was the glorious course of Mohammad Amin Sheikho, for by his words and deeds he aimed only to satisfy Al’lah: Glory to His Splendour.

chapters.title: Superior Intelligence Resolves a Difficult Situation
chapters.html:
There came a time when the Ottomans changed and lowered their moral standards: they abandoned Al’lah’s Book (the Holy Qur’an) and replaced It with temporal laws devised by man. So it pleased Al’lah to cause them to be removed from the countries they had governed, as their staying there was giving rise to actual and moral destruction. After they withdrew from our country (al-Sham, Greater Syria) and because of the collapse of the Ottoman Empire, Mohammad Amin Sheikho no longer held his rank as an officer in the security services. He had been a manager of the castle and its prisons, and it was his responsibility to maintain security and uphold the law against criminals and corruption. And so he became an ordinary citizen like any other, and no longer held any official rank, nor did he have any other employment.

One day, while he was walking along a street in Damascus on his way to buy some household requirements, he chanced across one of the malevolent criminals he had come up against as an officer. So, the criminal was quick to grab his chance to hurt the dignity of the man who had pursued him relentlessly, punished him, and even put him in jail.

As soon as the criminal recognised him, his vicious tongue knew no limits in expressing his delinquency and baseness. He was yelling all manner of vile threats to that pure humane man, Mohammad Amin, and muttering to himself, ‘Your days are numbered! You’re nothing now... your time of glory is over... you’re not an officer now!’

That hardened criminal would not care even if it came to a fight as his enemy was no longer an officer, and was now just an ordinary citizen with no particular power over him.
