Mohammad Amin heard the words and knew exactly which criminal it was, but he hurried to the market followed by the foul-mouthed man till he disappeared into the crowd.

He could have attacked the criminal and thrown him to the ground with just one punch as he had done once with their boss “Hamu Jamu”, (the leader of the criminal gangs), because not only did he excel in the arts of fighting, but he possessed great courage and feared none but Al’lah.

But he realised that if he followed that course of action he would end up in jail along with the criminal, degrading himself by being sentenced to prison and being thrown in with all sorts of felons, drug addicts, thieves and other such people.

Therefore he thought, ‘I’ll bide my time... I won’t beat or punish him now... every problem has a solution, and this one, by Al’lah’s Will, will surely be solved.’

Having completed his purchases Mohammad Amin hurried back to his home, where he sat alone, in a pensive state of mind, analysing the matter from all sides with the aim of finding a solution. He thought, ‘I’ll be exposed repeatedly to such situations as I was today... as there are a lot of criminals who were caught and punished when I was an officer... they will flourish now and try to take revenge, or even kill me.’

He mulled over the matter, again and again, till he reached a solution but he kept it to himself. With newfound vigour, and the strength of a lion, he left the house again, whereupon he happened to meet one of the truly hardened criminals. He rushed up to him, smiling broadly and greeted him as a long lost friend. The criminal was taken totally by surprise and looked at him in utter astonishment. Then he respectably saluted him wondering what on earth was going on. ‘Hello, sir!’ he said, as he was still accustomed to greeting this man politely and, too, because of the formidable character of this august former officer which was imprinted on his mind... the very same officer who had constantly pursued and punished them.

His astonishment increased even further when Mr. Mohammad Amin said to him, ‘Where have all you men got to? I miss you... I’d be so happy to live near you. I’m tired of living with all that “garbage” (as the criminals referred to ordinary people, so he spoke to him in their own “language”).’ He added, ‘I’ll be miserable unless I see you men more often, and I’d be honoured if you and some of your friends would come to eat with me tomorrow. I want you to invite the real men, the toughest criminals... not those who have only killed one or two people and claimed that they’re real men... no, I want the heroes that have killed at least five, and I want the bravest ones, like you.’

Initially taken aback, the gang leader was then overwhelmed with delight at the invitation to eat with the former officer.

The criminal answered, ‘Yes, sir! At your command!’ for as he heard the words ‘eat with me’ he knew that the food would be excellent and their reception friendly and hospitable. Then he continued, ‘Tomorrow sir, I’ll come to you with three or four of the toughest men that I’m sure you will admire.’ Mohammad Amin, the sagacious man, replied, ‘What did you say?... three or four men? No... no.’ The criminal asked him, ‘So, how many tough men shall I bring, sir?’ Mohammad Amin replied, ‘Fifteen or more... twenty. Tomorrow I want you to honour me with twenty courageous men as dear esteemed guests, for I truly miss being in the company of brave, daring men.’

The criminal dashed off, delighted to carry the good news to many of the top criminals that they were invited for an excellent meal with their honourable, faithful “friend”. And so, it was that he gathered together twenty of the most hardened criminals of the city.

At home, Mohammad Amin had ordered to be prepared for them two whole sheep stuffed with rice and delicacies cooked by expert chefs, as well as a variety of other tasty foods and excellent fruits and mixed nuts. He had all of the food placed on a raised dais in the shady courtyard of his house. He also brought them eight sets of playing cards and then, finally, he placed his tall chair behind a little table in an elevated spot close to a wall, and sat with his narghile ﴿145﴾

, which had been specially prepared for the occasion. He remained there, relaxed and at ease, to await the arrival of twenty of the biggest criminals, who had accepted his invitation with great pleasure. As soon as they knocked at the door, he opened it and received them hospitably, saying, ‘Welcome to you, brave men, my home is your home! I miss you so much... and I hope you will all stay very much a part of my life.’ These friendly words served to whet their appetite for the delicious food to come, as there were so many good things to look forward to: roasted, stuffed sheep... fruits... and spending time in enjoyment and pleasure, and all of that at no cost to them. They were more than happy when they sat to eat and could hardly believe the extent of the banquet. They feasted their eyes and ate their fill till they were fully satiated, while Mohammad Amin remained seated on his chair, smoking his narghile.

Once they had eaten their fill, some of them started to wash up all the utensils and dishes, and put them back in place in the kitchen, they also cleaned the kitchen and rinsed the floor ﴿146﴾

, and then they returned to sit in the courtyard to play cards, feeling happy and replete, to drink strong Arabic coffee. They relaxed like this till the sun was beginning to set, when the criminal who was the guest of honour said to them that they should go and leave their master to relax.

So, they all stood up and took their leave of him. Then, their kind host, Mohammad Amin, said to them, ‘Listen men! I really enjoy being in your company, so I’m inviting any of you who have nothing better to do to come and spend the evening relaxing and having fun; I don’t like to be alone and I want a few bold men to keep me company... my life is boring without you men around.’

‘At your command, sir!’ they said, and left the house.

In this way, it became the habit for them to pass most nights at Mohammad Amin’s home playing cards and drinking coffee.

One day, Mohammad Amin went out on the road on a matter of business, in the company of his entourage of fifteen strong, tough men: some on his right and the others on his left. He stood amongst them like the moon surrounded by its halo, or the lion with its cubs. They all yielded to him and were at his beck and call. Previously he had held his position of authority as the officer in charge of many policemen and he now held the reins of power through another, different group of men; and so he established justice and security in the country at a time when it was passing through harsh conditions due to many political and security twists and turns. This was the time shortly after the exit of Turkey from Syria and it became occupied by the French.

This was a time when peace and stability faltered and confusion reigned.

In fact, the residents of the neighbourhood began to regard him as the master and commander of his escorts, the leading criminals, and one day their neighbour expressed her astonishment to his wife, saying, ‘Your husband has really confused us! We knew him once as a religious man, highly respected by sheikhs, but now we find him as the commander of a band of criminals... so, is he a religious man or the leader of a group of bold men?’

One day, as usual, Mohammad Amin was out with his entourage of criminals, and came across the criminal who had insulted him on the street. Mohammad Amin pounced upon him as quick as lightning, leaving his men behind. Lightly and swiftly, he cuffed the criminal twice saying, ‘Why did you abuse me?’

Hastily the criminal pulled back and loaded his gun directing it towards our quick-witted man but, what a surprise! Within a few moments Mohammad Amin saw him being hurled up above the heads of his entourage and then thrown to the ground, where they assaulted and disarmed him. Showing no mercy, they hauled him off the ground and dragged him to the bank of the Yazid River, (a tributary of the Barada), pulling out their knives to kill him and cast him in the river, as if killing a man was a normal, everyday matter.

Suddenly aware of their intentions Mohammad Amin cried out, ‘No... no... men! I don’t want you to stain your knives with his tainted blood... leave him, it isn’t worth dirtying your knives on his filthy body!’

Our man was not only courageous, but also intelligent and quick-thinking. He did not want them to kill the criminal, for he believed killing should be avoided whenever possible, so he spoke to them using the words and kind of language they were accustomed to hearing.

As soon as the order was given they let him go and pulled him to his feet, but every last one of them was quite bemused at the order not to kill him... while the reprieved culprit stood trembling like a straw in a strong wind, unable to believe that he was still alive.

Then, Mohammad Amin continued, ‘I want all of you men to spread the word of what has happened here today. Tell all bold men that this man’s blood has been shed in vain and let those of you who are here tell all those who are not. So, anyone who sees him anywhere in this country, after this day, should kill him immediately as this will be considered a lawful action.’

The culprit could not believe his luck! He was still alive even though a band of hardened criminals led by a former police officer had been about to kill him. But he did not stop to question why.

Then, not wanting to tempt fate he deserted the state of Syria and never came back.

chapters.title: The False Penitent Will Never Succeed
chapters.html:
A certain hardened criminal repented, turned his back on his former life of crime and started to attend the mosque in a particular area of Damascus. He took his place behind the imam every day at all the appointed times of prayer for forty consecutive days. He got up for the dawn-prayer and would even enter the mosque before the imam himself.

The imam was astonished at the radical change that had come over the man and his sincere repentance, for it is wellknown among the sheikhs that: ‘If man perseveres in praying at collective prayers (at the mosque) for forty days, he is then considered to be one of the believers’ and... ‘if you see the man frequent the mosque, then testify to his belief.’

What great contrition he showed! That desperate bandit repented from his life of crime... he stopped killing and robbing, and despoiling all in his path in order to turn to a life of rectitude and prayer. No-one, not even the most righteous of young men could have displayed greater sincerity than he did. This youth seemed to have turned to a path of true repentance and great integrity so that he compared most favourably with the best of other youths in the neighbourhood.

The sheikh (imam) had noticed all of his newfound qualities of character, so he expressed his great admiration and encouragement, telling him how pleased he was with him for this remorse and subsequent attendance at all prayer services every day.

What is more important is that no sooner had the forty days passed than the repentant youth went to the house of his sheikh where he received an especially warm welcome as the sheikh was so heartened that this was a man who had foresworn his former life of crime and wrongdoing, and now turned to the sheikh for guidance.

On entering the house, he wasted no time at all and immediately made a proposal of marriage to the sheikh’s daughter: not only had he rejected his life of crime and turned to devout prayer, he also wanted to be a son-in-law of the sheikh!

The sheikh was so pleased with his request and accepted the proposal without any delay, wanting to consolidate the relationship between them so that he would be encouraged to continue on his path of repentance and not be tempted to return to his former life of crime.

Surely by this alliance, he would not stray from his path of repentance and would continue to worship Al’lah, his Provider for his wife-to-be was the daughter of the sheikh, and so his father-in-law was the imam himself.

But...! This youth, who appeared to have turned away from his life of crime and shown true repentance, was actually planning a despicable deed! As the proverb says, “I kept praying until I got my request, and when I got it, I stopped praying.”

The sheikh’s daughter was a captivating beauty, and the description of her allure had been circulated on the tongues of some ignorant women in the neighbourhood until it reached the ears of this sly fox; devilish thoughts came to his mind and, slowly but surely, he began to formulate his malicious intention... and so he resorted to his dishonest show of “repentance” in order to achieve his purpose.

And it was not long until he showed his true colours! Once the sheikh’s daughter became his wife and went to live in his home, he took off his mask of righteousness. His real intention behind the façade of repentance was unveiled... and within a few days of the marriage he brought home a group of criminals who were every bit as odious as him. Bottles of wine were brought out and his evil purpose was revealed: he wanted to trade in his wife’s honour and earn money from her. He wanted to use his wife as a prostitute! This was shocking to any right minded person!

He went in to her room and told her about the men who were coming, which she found quite strange. Then when he added that he wanted her to entertain them she thought she was going crazy... What? Surely she must have misunderstood him! Is that really what he wanted from her? She could not believe what she heard!

How dreadful! She was a pure, chaste woman who had been brought up and educated in the ways of purity and uprightness at the hands of a virtuous upright man.

It was a severe shock, but fortunately she was clever enough not to react; she knew that if her husband got any idea that she was appalled at his suggestion he would quickly set out to destroy her.

She told him to wait a moment, pretending that she wanted to use the bathroom and he told her to be quick as his friends were waiting for her. As soon as he had joined them she ran to her room... grabbed a cloak to cover herself and fled from the house, barely able to see her way because of her fear and the terrible shock she had just received. And thank God that she had the presence of mind to act so quickly! She arrived at her family’s house and could hardly believe that she had managed to escape from that beast and his evil intentions. Her father was most surprised to see her in such a distressed state as she tried to relate the details of the incident to him despite her floods of tears.

He was soon in a state of shock! How could he have been taken in by this man?

He was frustrated because his usual impeccable judgement had been proved to be completely flawed. The imam had thought the young man to be truly repentant, a man who had turned to worshiping his Provider, and so he had lost no time in giving that poor girl, his daughter, in marriage to him so that he might continue on his path towards true closeness to his Provider. But he was shocked to find him a sly and malevolent man.

As he became aware of the full truth of the matter he grew even more aggrieved and said to his daughter in a sad voice, with his eyes brimming with tears, ‘Forgive me my daughter... forgive me... may Al’lah punish him... may Al’lah take revenge for us.’

As for the criminal, there was no one to hold him back. He wondered why she was taking so long to come back to the room and he called her but there was no answer. Then the truth dawned... she had outwitted him and run back to her family!

He was furious but thought that she could not escape from his grasp, so he went to his father-in-law’s house and began to pound at the door. They knew it was him and were afraid as there was no man in the house to defend them except her father, the poor aged sheikh.

They did not open the door... and they even locked the door of the room for extra security, then the criminal – who would stop at nothing – raised his voice so that all the neighbours heard his shouts, ‘I want my wife... I want my wife back... I’m telling you... send my wife back to me otherwise you’ll be sorry.’ He repeated this appalling behaviour every day, filling the entire neighbourhood with his hollering,, and even more so if he met the old man accidentally in the street.

‘God help my father-in-law!’ he would call out, and use every foul and dirty word to describe the gentle old man. He cared nothing for the reputation of the family but continued to shout obscenities in the street in the hearing of all the passers-by. He threatened the sheikh... he threatened his own wife... using the foulest language! He terrorised the entire family so they could no longer go about their daily lives and they became embittered by his undeserved cruelty.

And the poor sheikh trembled with fear and helplessness because he knew of no way to escape from the man’s malevolent onslaught.

Some people advised the sheikh to complain to the authorities: he did so but it was no use! Certain intermediaries intervened in this case and reported it to the French high commissioner in Syria, but no help was forthcoming, for it is well known that “nothing good can be expected from someone who does not pray.”

Word came back from the high commissioner that as the malevolent husband had not broken into the house or caused any physical harm to the occupants he could not be punished. This was the law and no action could be taken against him.

But surely his daily verbal onslaught outside the sheikh’s house and his intentions for the sheikh’s innocent daughter should be considered a crime in itself! Eventually, due to continuous representation about this case the high commissioner banished the man to Lebanon for just one month which was all that could be done under French law.

The month went by and the damned offender returned. Unfortunately the month in Lebanon had not helped him to mend his ways, and he went back to shouting strings of obscenities outside the sheikh’s house growing ever more insistent and stubborn, even more wicked and ugly than before the banishment. Daily he went to holler for the return of his wife, issuing all manner of menacing threats if the imam did not comply with his demands.

The family lived under a permanent cloud of anxiety and terror, expecting that one day the husband might climb the wall, sneak into the house, and kidnap his reluctant wife. The sheikh would be powerless to stop him even though he knew that his daughter would be carried off to be violated and used to entertain the man’s low-life companions.

Days passed and still the criminal continued to act in this manner that made the family’s life unbearable hell whereas they used to be so happy. It was a hopeless situation as no one had the power or authority to stop him. Feeling utterly helpless, with nowhere to turn for help, the sheikh could no longer eat or drink, and sat alone out of sight of his family, crying and begging God to save them from this evil, despicable man, ‘Oh God... I’ve become terribly grieved and it is You Who relieves... oh God... I’m powerless and You are powerful... would You please turn this wicked man away from us... drive him away please... and relieve us of his evil in whatever way You wish.’ This poor sheikh went through a long period of harsh cruelty during which he lost at least half of his weight because he was unable to eat. After much suffering one of his friends finally took steps to help him. He had heard of the excellent reputation of Mohammad Amin Sheikho and his great success in crushing crime and punishing criminals, so he made it his business to speak to him about the matter of the sheikh and his daughter. Mohammad Amin reassured him with his heart-warming words, ‘Leave the matter to me... and give good news to the sheikh that certainly the problem will be solved with God’s Will... I shall ensure that this devil divorces her willingly... or unwillingly...!’ Then he invited the sheikh – the wife’s father – with two of his sheikh brethrens to lunch the next day.

The sheikh could barely believe what he had heard and said to himself, ‘Is it possible...? Will he really be able to persuade that cursed villain to divorce her when the French high commissioner failed to do so?’

As for Mohammad Amin, as soon as the sheikh’s friend had left, he chose two of his most powerful and courageous men from his band of reformed criminals... for he knew the wrong doer (the sheikh’s son-in-law) since he had been an officer in the army... but this criminal was not among his men at the present time as he had not committed as many serious crimes as Amin’s close criminal circle.

He said to the two men, ‘Tomorrow, I want you to invite the sheikh’s son-in-law to lunch at my house... tell him about my invitation and bring him with you... is it understood?’

Then he revealed to them his plan to entrap the criminal who was causing the family so much grief. The two men answered, ‘Yes, sir... whatever you say!’

Next day, Mohammad Amin held a splendid banquet where he offered the most magnificent and delicious food and fruits. At lunch time the sheikh duly arrived with two other sheikhs of his acquaintance and Mohammad Amin welcomed them hospitably and showed them the respect due to their status.

After a short time, the criminal, the subject of this tale, arrived, and as soon as he entered the room and saw his fatherin- law, he stood at the door, ready to leave. Immediately he said, ‘I won’t divorce my wife... I won’t...!’

Mohammad Amin said to him, ‘This is disgraceful... did I ask you a question for you to speak like that? I simply invited you to my house.’

But the wicked criminal took no notice of what he had heard, and he continued, ‘I won’t divorce... I won’t... otherwise, why is he here?’ and he pointed at his father-in law.

Our man replied to him in a way that would accept no argument, ‘Did you hear me? Have I asked you to divorce your wife so that you say such things?’

‘No,’ he replied.

Mohammad Amin said, ‘So why did you raise the subject? He is a man who has respect for other men... go into the room and sit down.’ Thereupon, he kept silent, entered the room and sat down, still insisting that he would not divorce his wife.

He soon composed himself and when Mohammad Amin felt that he had calmed down, he got up and sat beside him and then started to talk with him about divorcing his wife, but unfortunately... he was rock-like in his obstinacy and persistent in his hypocrisy... fully determined not to divorce her.

Mohammad Amin then tried to tempt him by offering him money... but he refused. There was still to be no escape for that poor chaste woman.

By then, becoming increasingly annoyed he said to him firmly, ‘So... you refuse to divorce!’

The wicked criminal replied, ‘That’s right... I will not divorce her!’

He was about to learn that his time had run out!

Then Mohammad Amin decided to take action and gave a simple pre-arranged signal to the two men from his criminal band. No sooner had they received that signal than they pounced upon the husband and grabbed his arm forcefully, then they grasped him by the shoulders. He tried to resist but he could no longer move as they were stronger and braver than him and he knew that he had to give in. Defiantly the criminal said, ‘Go on... kill me... I still won’t divorce her... so let a crime be committed in your own house... oh Bey!’

He replied, ‘No, I will not kill you... why should I bring shame on my home?’ He then ordered his two men, ‘Strip him... here... in front of the guests!’ The significance of this act is that in the criminals’ code, the most disgraceful thing that can happen is to be undressed before others, whereas to murder someone is of very little consequence.

When the criminal heard our man’s order he lost his mind, his inflexibility and tyranny were crushed, and he was overcome and extremely humbled, then he shouted, ‘Oh sir... please... I seek refuge with you... I seek refuge in your honour sir...’

Mohammad Amin replied, ‘You have no honour... you vile individual!’ The two criminals set about stripping him, then he shouted as if the world was closing in on him, ‘Sir, please... I’ll divorce her... she is divorced... she is divorced... she is divorced...’

At that moment Mohammad Amin called out to the three sheikhs who were watching these events unfold. They sat as though in a state of complete shock... that was because when they heard the order to undress the criminal they all shouted, ‘No... no...’ and the wife’s father cried out, ‘I don’t want him to divorce her... let him go... I don’t want him to divorce...!’

So, with these words from the sheikhs it seemed as though he would be frustrated in the clever plan he had thought up. But despite their strong objection he shouted to his two men, ‘When you’ve finished with him do the same with those three,’ and he pointed at the sheikhs.

The three sheikhs looked at Mohammad Amin in great dismay, then they saw his face... he looked as fierce as a lion and deadly serious; they were sure of what they had heard but were so confused that they no longer had any idea of what was going on.

But as the criminal repeated three times that he divorced his wife, and added that the divorce was irrevocable, Mohammad Amin wanted to make sure the three bewildered sheikhs heard the oath of divorce, so he shouted at them after shaking them with his hand in order to help them to recover their wits and said to them, ‘Listen... listen to what he’s saying.’ And when they became aware that he was speaking, he said to the husband, ‘Repeat the oath of divorce once more.’ Then the criminal said, not believing that he would escape from the situation, ‘My wife is divorced... divorced... divorced... I have divorced her once and forever.’ And by that, he rejected his wife, and all of them were witness to his words.

After that, Mohammad Amin – whose very appearance could evoke terror in the hearts of even the most powerful of men – addressed the two criminals from his band, ‘Listen to me... let it be known to all villains that killing this dog is to be considered a lawful action from this moment on... and anyone who catches sight of him should kill him immediately. Release this vile creature!’

He fled the state of al-Sham and never returned, which probably saved his life.

Then the other two criminals left after they had eaten lunch and taken leave of their master. Mohammad Amin addressed the three sheikhs, ‘Did you believe that I would allow my men to carry out my order? It was no more than a trick to make him agree to divorce... by God I would not have allowed such a matter even if the woman were my own daughter, but this malicious criminal and his likes do not understand unless you speak to them in their own rough language... and even if he had refused to divorce his wife, I still would not have let such a thing happen at all... and then I would have made a different plan in order to force him to divorce her... but all that you have seen and heard was just a ploy to save this poor woman from the claws of this monster. At least I succeeded whereas the French high commissioner failed.’

Thereupon, and after they heard his words, the three sheikhs felt ashamed of their initial reaction, and they looked at this merciful, humane thinker with their eyes full of admiration and appreciation. Then they left Mohammad Amin’s house, full of praise for him, and the father of the young woman did not know how to thank this merciful man and reciprocate his favour.

So, he asked God to reward him in whatever way he deserved. And surely, this is the best of all things!

chapters.title: The Minister of War Yusuf Al - ’Azma and the Battle of Maysalun
chapters.html:
The Minister of War Yusuf Al-’Azma and the Battle of Maysalun

We should open this account with a little background history of that time when the Ottoman Empire came to its end. The League of Nations came into being after the end of World War One: its task was to ensure that war never broke out again. After the turmoil caused by the Versailles Treaty of 1918, many looked to the League to bring stability to the world. So, when the Ottoman Empire came to an end and had to relinquish its authority over al-Sham and other countries, an alternative authority was put in place to help those countries through the transition. The Arab countries which had recently separated from the Ottoman Empire were considered to be underdeveloped and reactionary and should be placed under a mandate in order to assist in their process of civilisation and progress.

At a meeting of the Allied Powers in the Italian town of San Remo a decision was taken under article 22 of the covenant of the League of Nations to give France the Mandate for Syria and Lebanon.

At that time, the king of Syria was Faisal ibn Sharif al- Hussein who informed Britain of his government’s absolute rejection of the decisions of the San Remo talks. On 14th July in that same year, France was informed of the decision of King Faisal and his government which prompted them to send their interlocutors, General Gouraud and General Allenby to enforce the decisions taken in San Remo. Hence Gouraud sent a warning to King Faisal accusing him of hampering the progress of the French forces by preventing them from using the Riyaq-Aleppo railway line and he gave him four days grace to comply with the following terms:

Hand over control of the Riyaq-Aleppo railway line to the French.

Cancel conscription and disband the armed forces.

Accept the paper currency issued by France as the legal currency.

Accept the French Mandate upon Syria.

Under the circumstances, the Syrian government was compelled to accept these terms and informed the French commissioner in Syria of their acceptance for this to be transmitted to General Gouraud in Beirut. However, the French had taken it upon themselves to disconnect the telephone lines between Damascus and Beirut in the border area of Serghaya in order to delay the Syrian government’s approval from reaching General Gouraud. Hence, believing the Syrians to be at fault General Gouraud ordered his forces to march towards Damascus and Aleppo because of the Syrian government’s apparent negligence. So, the forces which presented in the north were ordered to move towards Aleppo and those which were in Shtora were to march towards Damascus. This occurred on July 23rd.

Meanwhile, and before this news reached the Syrian government, they had actually set in motion the execution of the articles of Gouraud’s caution, since King Faisal had no choice. Given the difficult circumstances of the country and its inability to defend itself against a state as powerful as France, Syria’s acquiescence was inevitable.

At that time Yusuf al-’Azma was the minister of war. When he was informed of General Gouraud’s military advance to occupy Syria he issued a command that the disbanding of the army should be halted immediately and the soldiers who had been demobilized should be re-called. He then gathered a force around him, armed them, and took the decision to proceed towards Maysalun in order to confront General Gouraud.

Through his military experience, minister Yusuf al-’Azma was certain that the remainder of the army and a few young volunteers would not be able to stop the French military advance or repel it, so he might well leave, never to return; that’s why he entrusted his only daughter Laila to a noble Damascene family, by the name of al-Husari. He committed her to Mr. Sati’ al-Husari’s care, saying to him, ‘I am leaving my beloved daughter Laila entrusted to your care.’ As soon as he placed his beloved child under the custody of Mr. al-Husari he went to the Royal Palace to ask permission of King Faisal to advance on Maysalun; this was granted. Then, Yusuf Bey, the minister, met with the retired officer Mr. Mohammad al-Taghlibi, who accompanied him to visit the venerable scholar Mr. Mohammad Amin Sheikho before leaving for Maysalun.

In the house of the noble master, they were welcomed most hospitably. Then, the three men sat discussing the subject of the French military advance and the decision of the minister of war, Yusuf al-’Azma.

The noble master could do nothing except advise him saying, ‘Oh, Yusuf Bey! The weak are helpless in the face of the mighty! You will face an army that is strong, welltrained, highly disciplined and fully armed, which is surely beyond your capacity. As you know, the region of Maysalun is exposed from all directions and your going there means a risk in the full sense of the word, and will lead you and all the men entrusted to you to inevitable death... I advise you not to go. You would do better to wait for the French here, on the outskirts of Damascus. Surely, you know, Yusuf Bey, that their only viable approach to Damascus is the al-Rabwa corridor where they have no way but through a narrow passage which runs between two mountains, so, when their first tank arrives at the town of al-Rabwa, the last one would just be reaching the beginning of the al-Rabwa corridor and so all of their army would be enclosed within the passage. If we position ourselves above them at the top of the mountains on either side we could pound them with rocks from above, and halt them in their tracks, trapped in the narrow pass. Then, we can roll down huge rocks at the beginning of the corridor from the Dummar side of the pass and they will be trapped in the valley unable to advance or retreat. Our men could then continue to heap rocks and stones on them and open fire too. They would be defenceless as their supply lines will be cut off, but we, on the other hand, will still be able to get reinforcements of men and equipment without being subjected to the danger of their fire.’

The minister of war, Yusuf al-’Azma, replied, ‘But Bey, what will future generations have to say about us? They will surely say that the citizens of Damascus are such cowards that they put up no defence and waited till the French army entered the city.’

The venerable master Mohammad Amin replied, ‘Oh, Yusuf, Bey! This matter is of far greater importance than any amount of talk or historical precedent... it concerns the souls under our charge, and leading them there will be a clear military error which will definitely result in failure and death. The sound military logic in this situation calls for our forces to wait for them at the al-Rabwa corridor and be fully prepared to encircle them from above: preparing piles of rocks as I have said, and setting up the sites and arsenal of the fighters. And what’s more, with this strategy we can ensure our supply lines.’

But, the minister of war refused to accept this sound military logic, so he replied, ‘Oh Bey! I know perfectly well that our victory will be impossible and death will be the fate of most of my troops... yet, we have to confront them so that the future generation cannot accuse us of cowardice or say that we failed to go out to face our enemy but waited till they were at the gates of our city... yes, we have to go... otherwise history will record that General Gouraud met with no resistance till he arrived in Damascus.’

Hence, the marks of sadness appeared clearly on the features of the noble master whose heart is full of mercy, so, he sighed deeply and then related the story of Abdul- Mottalib, the grandfather of our master, Mohammad (cpth), and his uncle Abu Talib. ‘Yusuf Bey,’ he said, ‘Please listen to this story: when Abraha al-Habashi arrived in Mecca he went to Abu Talib, after he had confiscated the camels of Abdul-Mottalib. The latter went to meet him, and when Abraha received him, Abdul-Mottalib accused him, saying, “You have seized my camels and I want them back.” Abraha said, “I thought you had come to dissuade me from entering Mecca to defend it!” Abdul-Mottalib replied, “As for al- Ka’ba, it has a Provider Who defends it.” Then, Abdul- Mottalib took his camels, stood on a hill and said, “Oh, Provider! I’ve guarded my own possessions, so, would You protect Your Holy House?”

‘Therefore, you have to behave according to military prudence and keep your men here so we can ask for their help, and not go blindly towards an inescapable fate.’

But, alas! In spite of all this advice based upon wisdom and relevant opinion, the minister of war did not agree with the noble master, so he took leave of him and went ahead with his men to Maysalun where he and most of his men were martyred. The few who survived barely managed to escape through the mountains.

Thus, Gouraud and his forces were able to enter Damascus with relatively little opposition and he went to the shrine of Salah al-Deen al-Ayubi, the leader of the Battle of Hattin which had been fought many years before, and the liberator of renowned Jerusalem, and there, he addressed the shrine saying, ‘Rise... oh Salah al-Deen...! We are here again... we have succeeded in occupying Syria!’

Many years passed after this sorry incident which caused great heartbreak for the Syrian people. Then, a German General came to General Abdullah Atfah who accompanied him to visit the venerable master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, and there General Atfah spoke with him about the story of the Battle of Maysalun: the arrival of the French army in Syria, and about the plan which the noble master had put forward, and through which the course of history surely would have been altered.

When the German general had listened to the full details of the ingenious plan that had been proposed by Mohammad Amin he expressed his extreme admiration, then he praised him saying, ‘Yes... exactly the apposite of what happened and certainly the perfect tactic! Waiting for the invading army in al-Rabwa would have been the right stratagem, and it would then have been impossible for an exhausted army coming from Lebanon to occupy Syria.’

chapters.title: The Tale of a Good Butcher and a Bad Butcher
chapters.html:
One day, a butcher from the al-Midan district went off to see Mr. Mohammad Amin in the district of al-Muhajireen on Mount Qasiyun to rent a shop from him. This was a shop that Mohammad Amin had inherited, along with other property, from his father.

An argument had taken place between this butcher and the inhabitants of al-Midan that prompted him to leave his neighborhood and move to al-Muhajireen.

This butcher started to practise his trade in an open and honest manner. He supplied his shop with only the best carcasses: fattened young sheep with excellent, tender meat, and he allowed the clients choose the cut of meat they wanted, and let them choose which part of the carcass they would like their meat from. It was usual for a customer to want the choicest cut of meat which this butcher sold him at the low price of the inferior cuts.

Even a child would be treated in the same fair way if he came to buy meat for his family.

As a result, this butcher became widely-known throughout the district and every day people would form a long, orderly queue before his shop, each one waiting his turn irrespective of their personal level in society. So, a typical scenario would be of a senior officer standing in line behind a child, or a simple workman.

Consequently, he sold many carcasses each day, and with the high turnover his income was good though the profit was small.

As for the leftover meat which was not fit for human consumption, and the suet, he sold it wholesale to the farmers who came to collect it every afternoon.

One day our man, Mohammad Amin, saw that a large group of men had arrived from al-Midan and stood in front of his shop greeting their former butcher and praising him loudly. They had come to appease him and take him with them after apologizing and soothing him for their previous unseemly behaviour. He was happy to go along with this genial crowd, so some of them set about collecting up the tools of the butcher’s trade from the shop. Another group hoisted him on to their shoulders to take him back to their district... but the butcher shouted at them, saying, ‘Wait a minute... I need to pay the rent to the shop owner.’ One of them answered, ‘Don’t worry... I’ll pay him whatever he asks.’

There and then, he headed for the shop owner, Mohammad Amin, asked him how much rent was due, and settled the amount in full.

And so, they went back to their own district with their comrade carried high on their shoulders, clearly happy to be taking this excellent tradesman, a man of the highest moral standing, back with them.

Some days later, another butcher came to rent the shop from Mohammad Amin. He was completely different from the first one: he was dishonest, he brought only the lowest quality of carcasses to his shop; and if a child or a young girl came to him, he would give them the worst piece of meat he had and as a result, during the entire day he would sell only half of the single carcass he had brought. His dishonesty and the poor quality of his meat gradually led to people avoiding him and going elsewhere to buy what they needed.

That was what our man Mohammad Amin, the owner of the shop, had noticed and as he was accustomed to doing from the goodness of his heart, he wanted to advise the butcher so that he might deal honestly with the clients and provide them with good quality, tender meat. He explained that the customers would be satisfied and buy greater quantities of meat, and in turn he, the butcher, would gain greater financial profit.

It was the sensible thing to do!

He said to the butcher, ‘Oh, brother, I see that your business isn’t going very well, so I thought I should mention to you that another butcher occupied this shop before you... he brought only the best carcasses and best quality of meat. For his honesty and fair treatment of his customers, Al’lah made him very successful; all his carcasses were sold within a few hours. It’s true that his profit on each carcass was quite low because of his very reasonable prices but since he sold a lot of meat every day his overall profit was very good. I suggest that you should do as he did: bring only the best kinds of meat, treat all of the customers fairly and make no distinction between them! After all... the money of a rich man has the same value as that of a workman!’

The following day, as our man was on his way to his place of work, he looked at the shop and noticed that the butcher had brought a carcass of good quality meat, so he said to himself, ‘Thank God... he listened to my advice and acted on it.’

But a great surprise was waiting for Mohammad Amin, for when he left his work to go home, he passed by the same shop and found the carcass still hanging as he had seen it in the morning... still whole and not a single chunk of meat cut from it. At the same time, the butcher was wringing his hands in despair and raging against the man who had advised him.

Mohammad Amin tried to pass without being noticed by the cheating butcher but he could not go far as the butcher’s shop was beside the door of our officer’s house and he was waiting for him impatiently!

No sooner had he seen Mohammad Amin than he intercepted him and blamed him for what had happened to him after he had acted on his advice! ‘Look at the bad luck you have brought me!’ he said in a quavering voice, showing his anger and vexation.

Thereupon, Al’lah inspired Mohammad Amin to put his hand on the butcher’s head and to say, ‘Swear by God and His Envoy to tell the truth... didn’t you say to yourself, “If I make a good profit I’ll continue to do business in the correct way but if not, I’ll go back to my old ways and bring bad carcasses and cheat the customers.”?’

At that moment, the butcher was flabbergasted that the officer had seemingly read his thoughts. ‘How odd!’ he said to himself. So, he asked him, ‘Who told you that? And how could you know even though I didn’t voice my thoughts to anyone?’

Then, our man answered him saying, ‘Go away... you want to test your Provider; the Almighty should never be tested... He should be obeyed and then, only then, you will have good results.’

Having said this, Mohammad Amin went into his house thinking about the matter of this stubborn butcher who would not be able to sell any meat, and what a great loss he would incur as a result!

After having his meal and taking a rest, he felt a certain pity for him and went back to the shop and said, ‘Load your carcass onto a mule and follow me.’

Our man took the butcher around to some of his acquaintances who had restaurants and at Mohammad Amin’s request each one of them bought a part of the carcass so that the butcher regained his original financial outlay; at least he managed to avoid what would have been certain loss, because if the carcass had remained in his shop, it would inevitably rot since there were no refrigerators to keep food fresh at that time.

Next day, as our man was on the way to his place of work he passed by the butcher’s shop as usual. Immediately it became clear that some men will never learn the error of their ways! He saw that the butcher had returned to his previous habit of bringing an inferior quality of meat... and his customers – who had similar bad characters – continued to buy from him, “Impure men attract impure men, and pure men attract men of purity.”

Really, the vicious spirits insisted on manifesting their malice, and in the words of the proverb, “Like will always attract like.”

chapters.title: The French Woman Learns the Reason for the Veil
chapters.html:
In the Holy Qur’an God says, “Oh Prophet, tell your wives, your daughters, and the wives of true believers to draw their outer garments over their bodies [when outdoors], so they should not be known and not molested. And Al’lah is All-Forgiving, All-Merciful.” ﴿147﴾

This is the Godly Law and divine Legislation which our master, Mohammad (cpth), and all the Prophets and Envoys (cptt) who came before him brought to mankind.

This Law leads to happiness which is the Purpose of this Merciful and Tender Provider Who wants all His creatures to enjoy happiness in this world and in the world to come.

But alas! Repulsive and devilish desires have made people neglect these Laws. They did not stop to think! They believed that their licentiousness way of life would bring them happiness.

As for the man who is aware of the secret and the wisdom of these Godly Laws and knows that people can be pleased only when applying them, it is recognised that he has true love for his Provider.

The closer and more loving a man is towards God, the more understanding and knowledge of the Godly Purpose behind His Statute he will acquire.

In order to clarify this, here is a story of an actual event relating to a woman’s veil:

A meeting was held between the eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho and a certain person of a high social and cultural class. The man had gained a doctorate at a time when there were no schools and the majority of people were illiterate; education for those of a higher social rank would be through tutoring. The meeting concerned some details for the inauguration of Prince Abdul-majeed Haidar, a king of Greater Syria at the time of the French mandate, ﴿148﴾

who had been approved by the French government to rule the country.

On the following day at the time that had been previously arranged, the eminent scholar, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, went to that man’s house and knocked at the door. When he realised that a woman had opened the door to him, he turned his back on her. The woman was French and the wife of the doctor, and being unable to speak Arabic she was obliged to ask her daughter to explain that her husband would be ten minutes late because of an important meeting with General Sarrail, the French resident in Syria. So, he continued down the steps and waited in the street near the house.

The doctor apologized for being late and our man answered, ‘To be just ten minutes late is not considered late at all!’

Then, they entered the house together and sat in the salon. Before they began to discuss their business matters, the doctor’s wife and their daughter came to join them at the meeting. Mohammad Amin looked at her husband who knew full well that he was not in the habit of sitting with the fairer, gentle sex. The husband looked at his wife then lowered his head and did not utter a word because he saw that his wife’s face showed her intense anger.

She began to speak in French, with her daughter translating her words into Arabic, ‘I believed in your impeccable reputation, your international renown in Lebanon. I valued you highly. Now I see that the opposite is true.’

He was obliged to reply through her daughter, ‘Please tell your mother that she is a fool.’

When she heard these abrupt words, she became agitated and stood up crying out, ‘I’m a fool, am I?’

But one should remember, that it is well known that the French have always been hot tempered.

He told her, ‘Of course you are. Anyone who gives two completely contradictory opinions about a man whom he does not know nor has ever met, is surely a fool. Have you ever met me or even seen me before, that you can form these two diverse judgments?’

She replied, ‘No; but why didn’t you come into the house when I invited you? Am I not beautiful? My husband knows that I am a charming Parisian woman! Have you heard somewhere that I’m not an honest woman so that you did not want to come in? Here is my husband, ask him if he has found anything dishonest about me during my life with him.’

Our man replied, ‘I am a Muslim. One of the basic principles in our unquestionable jurisprudence is that men keep to their own world and women keep to theirs. They do not cross over... the social intermingling of men and women is forbidden.’

She then said to him, in a most derogatory fashion, ‘You Muslims have exaggerated so much. The Jews are older than you are. The Christians are more powerful than you are too. Where did you get this idea of the veil from?’

‘Is it a matter of age and power, or of logic, proof and righteousness?’ our man asked.

She said, ‘Truly it’s a matter of evidence and proof.’

Clearly giving the matter some thought, Mohammad Amin set out his reply with all seriousness, ‘So, let me show the reason why Islam decrees that a woman should be veiled in the presence of men. When I spend my time talking and working with men, the harsher sex, all day long, and then I come back home from work, the only woman I see is my wife and for me she is the most beautiful woman in the world. My love for her increases... the bonds between us become stronger. This is very important for the stability and emotional development of my children within the family. When we sit together, it does not matter how honest you and I are, and you certainly have charms and excellent characteristics that possibly make you more appealing than my wife. I may succumb to your charms because I am a human being. When I return home, the comparison will begin unconsciously between what I saw and liked of those attributes which I do not find in my own wife; then I’ll feel sorry for myself and my own bad fortune, and think that my situation isn’t fair. I’ll ask myself why this particular woman became my wife and not another with greater charms or beauty! She does not possess the same elegant beauty and charm as other women, nor is she as articulate, or her voice as musical; she isn’t as attractive as other women, nor does she have the same lightness of soul... and I could mention even more. If these superior qualities are presented to me they will likely lessen my love for my wife and make me feel dissatisfied. Antagonism and aversion will replace our previous feelings of love and intimacy. When my wife is nice to me in her usual gentle way saying ‘Oh my darling’, it will sound like a bullet blasting my ears, because the feeling in my heart would have changed.

“God has not given a man two hearts” ﴿149﴾

; so my love for her will change as the spirit naturally tends towards the most beautiful, the most charming, the most attractive and the finest. Then, altercations will prevail instead of cooperation, and injustice instead of justice. My wife may put up with my bad treatment once or twice, but her patience will soon come to an end. She will question herself about the secret of this seemingly spontaneous reversal, which is causing me to treat her in that way despite the fact that she continues to do her duty towards me and my children to the best of her ability. She will rebel and treat me in the same fashion, and therein would lie the downfall of our marriage. There would be tension in our relations. Quarrels would begin for the silliest reason and tempers would flare. Because of this change, life would become an unbearable hell with divorce being the only solution. And it wouldn’t be just the two of us who reap the result of divorce, but it would be reflected upon the children. Instantly they would lose their guardian, the person who teaches them right from wrong; instead they would be influenced by the misbehaviour of their friends in the street, the place where they might well learn the arts of vice and crime.

‘What’s more, my family and hers would become involved in the quarrel too. This breakdown would extend further still and have a very bad effect on the community. Due to the mingling of both sexes, and of women removing the veil, the community becomes disconnected and it could easily be destroyed. This would be the result of our mixing together; despite the fact that both you and I are honest people.

‘This is from the man’s point of view. But in relation to the woman, and through her meeting with a strange man, she will like some characteristics in him such as the way he talks, how he treats her, his outward appearance, his rank, etc. She may not find these qualities in her husband. With the passing of time her dissatisfaction with her husband will grow, leading to antagonism towards her husband and the beginning of disputes and quarrels.’

Then, Mohammad Amin looked at her and said, ‘If you find good qualities in me... wouldn’t you like these qualities to be available in your husband?’

She replied that she would like her husband to be the best man in the world.

He continued, ‘Therefore, the absence of these qualities in your husband would belittle him in your eyes, and his value would decrease in your view. The only reason this might happen is if you mix with men other than your husband. This mingling would invariably lead you to like certain qualities in other men, which are not found in your husband, and the result would be feelings of disgust and repulsion instead of love and enjoyment. Thus, happiness is lost.’

When she heard this logical discussion as a positive scientific analysis of a practical situation, she looked at her daughter and said, ‘I want you to follow in the footsteps of this man: become a Muslim like him, but not like your father.’

Her husband, who had remained silent during this conversation, bowed his head in shame because she was aware of his behavioural practices that contradicted the spirit of Islam.

After that the great eminent scholar took his leave of the family and went home.

A few days later, the husband of the French woman came to tell the honest master that his wife wanted to meet him again for she had found in him true, meaningful and logical words. He also intimated that she might have the true desire to embrace Islam if she could meet him again.

Mohammad Amin apologised to her husband saying, ‘I felt obliged to meet her the first time so as to reply to her accusation of fanaticism within Islam regarding the use of the veil and other matters. Now I do not want to go to meet her of my own free will. The first time I saw her it was through necessity and not by desire, but the second time would be to meet her through my own conscious decision and I may desire her... I am a human being, my brother... thus I would bring ruin on myself and this is not acceptable. If she wants to embrace Islam, that is her choice, and should be made of her own free will.’

Less than a month later, the doctor returned to the home of Mohammad Amin accompanied by his French wife who was dressed in long clothes concealing her body, and with her hair covered. The eminent scholar opened the door for them although he was not expecting their visit. He welcomed them and invited them to enter his house. When they were seated comfortably in the salon she told him that she had seen the Prophet Mohammad (cpth) in her sleep, shining so brightly in his grandeur and beauty that all had to avert their gaze: she had been shown the heavenly delights of the sacred worlds and her spirit experienced a beautiful paradise. She then came to loathe her base desires and wanted nothing other than to reach that state of transcendence. She added, ‘Since I had that great vision, I began to live a life of fulfillment and enjoyment whereby my emotional pain was changed into complete happiness.

And I’m still living that vision; for this reason I decided to declare my conversion to Islam at your hands.’ And there and then, she embraced Islam.

This true story occurred during the French Mandate over Syria.

Then he added, ‘Once you embrace Islam you have to cover your face in public in order to continue your life of heightened spirituality, for we do not accept the feminine charm that is harmful to man.’

She answered, ‘In all honesty I don’t feel that I can do it yet because all my life I have been used to having my face uncovered. So, I find it difficult to apply all of the instructions at the same time.’

She asked him to be patient with her a little and eventually she would accomplish that too in accordance with God’s Will, and for her love of His Envoy (cpth).

The political troubles that stormed Damascus at that time prevented them meeting again, but he was reassured of her truthfulness. He was certain that she would accomplish everything by God’s Will.

chapters.title: Defending the Sheikh against a Murderous Mob
chapters.html:
Mohammad Amin Sheikho, the great humane man, was devoted to a certain venerable sheikh who was regarded by all with the highest esteem. One day, the sheikh wanted to refurbish a room inside the courtyard of Abu al-Nour Mosque in the Kurdish region on the banks of the River Yazeed: a tributary of the River Barada.

The engineers advised him that refurbishing the room would be impossible unless the river could be diverted temporarily for a few hours while the work was carried out. So, having decided to go ahead with the project the sheikh had the river diverted for just two hours, during which time the work should be completed.

Yet many envious and evil men soon spread rumours among the owners of the local fields, farmers and the inhabitants of the region that Amin Kiftaro, the sheikh, had arranged for the river to be diverted for the use and benefit of his own followers, thus cutting off the supply from the majority of people who relied on this water for their orchards and fields. This malicious story quickly spread widely among the farmers like fire in a haystack. When it reached their ears they did not stop to think, or ask questions, but rushed around like mad men, calling on each other to attack and kill the sheikh and to return the river to its original course.

They came from all directions carrying pickaxes, sticks and such like, in order to attack the sheikh who was innocent of any wrongdoing. Hundreds of men and youths gathered in a great crowd, their numbers swelling to become an overwhelming popular uprising as they approached the sheikh’s house. They surged forwards aiming to storm and burn the sheikh’s house, and kill him along with any of his followers who might defend him.

When he saw the crowd approaching in the distance, the sheikh became afraid for his life and was certain that he was about to die: there was no way out for him, or anyone to rescue him. The rabble were beyond wanting to hear the truth about the diverting of “their” water and were hellbent on their mission, and he knew that he had no chance of stopping them. So, he simply surrendered to the unruly mob and what would surely be his impending death, accompanied by four of his loving, faithful disciples who resolved heart and soul to stand alongside him and meet their end too, so that he should not face it alone.

In the meanwhile, during the last few minutes before the mob would reach them, the dreadful news reached our compassionate man, Mohammad Amin, while he was coming along the same road, ‘Your sheikh has just been killed!’ he was told.

No sooner had he heard those shocking words which had come like a bolt from the blue, than he was stirred into immediate action, like a predatory lion, and dashed quickly, roaring and snarling, ‘I’m still alive, while my sheikh has been killed... that should never have happened!’

He covered the distance in no time at all and when he reached them, he saw the men and youths running towards their prey yelling deafening, hostile threats. Over and over they chanted, ‘Cut off our livelihood and we’ll cut off your head! We want the soul of the man who’s deprived us of our water,’ as they drew closer to his house.

As good fortune would have it they arrived there at the same moment as Mohammad Amin Sheikho who turned to face the murderous throng. Just then, a sound like the roar of righteousness burst from him: a thunderous sound fell on their ears as though a bomb had burst above their heads, stopping them in their tracks.

This wide man began to heap insults upon them, describing their malicious characters, and did not let up till their hearts sank, their resolve weakened, and their fury abated; and when he pounced upon them slashing left and right with his stick, they were filled with horror and dread and scattered in every direction, intent on escaping this terrible man. Now fearing for their lives many of them tripped and fell, their feet unable to bear them, and they felt as if death were about to overcome them.

Those hundreds of once brave men soon became terrorstricken cowards and ran to hide wherever they could, behind trees and the water wheels alongside the river: they could not run fast enough from their attacker’s terrible wrath and thunderous voice, which filled their hearts with absolute fear. And yet, he continued chasing them like a raging lion, while they failed to understand why they were overwhelmed with such feelings of terror which was causing them to scatter in every direction.

When the sheikh saw this man dashing towards the throng and shouting at them he felt a sense of overwhelming relief as he realised that the threat of death at the hands of this terrible throng had been averted. As the horde scattered in every direction the sheikh sent two of his disciples to summon him.

Mohammad Amin entered his sheikh’s house, still in such a state of extreme rage that he was like an erupting volcano; his uproar did not subside for at least an hour, and his look of fury could have reduced a towering mountain to dust. There, his sheikh addressed him saying, ‘By the Almighty God, when I saw you coming in that frenzied attack, I was more afraid of your appearance than I was of my impending death. So, I had to take my eyes off you, as I had never seen such fury or awe-inspiring actions.

‘So! What is this great secret power encompassed in the voice which Al’lah granted you? ‘What is that cloak of grandeur and veneration that Al’lah has bestowed so lavishly upon you? ‘What is this great courage which excels that of all others? ‘May God preserve and reward you for every act of goodness, as He alone can reward you, not I!’

chapters.title: The Governor of the Castle Ensures Stability within its Walls
chapters.html:
When Officer Mohammad Amin Sheikho was named as governor of Damascus Castle and its central prison, he became an object of envy for all the other officers that worked there; for every one of them aspired to that prominent position. Because of their jealousy of him, some plotted together secretly to hatch a shocking scheme whereby they sought to have him dishonourably discharged.

Within days of taking up his new position Mohammad Amin was quick to see the deceit and disloyalty in their eyes, so he knew that sooner or later he would face many problems and that he had to deal with them by careful thought and intelligent planning. He felt that they were already conspiring against him and frequently asked himself what it might be. So, an air of suspense and vigilance infiltrated every corner of the castle.

Officer Mohammad Amin looked around him surreptitiously, constantly scrutinizing and studying all the officers and gendarmes in the castle, yet he found none that he could trust and depend on, except for one simple, kind-hearted policeman. This man was his aide who had been transferred with him to work alongside him in the castle.

When Officer Sheikho sent for this policeman to come to his office, he responded happily and immediately reported to his superior; indeed he was in such a rush to respond to the command that the cobblestones of the path resounded to the footfall of his heavy boots.

‘Yes, sir!’ He saluted and greeted his commander eagerly and with an air of great pride.

‘Welcome Abu Mohammad!’ our officer responded kindly to his greeting, ‘Come in and have a seat... take a rest.’

He sat with his face expressing his great pleasure because of his true love and appreciation of his leader, the brave officer.

Officer Mohammad Amin smiled, and then said to him, ‘Listen to me, Abu Mohammad. I want you to spread the word throughout the citadel... among the gendarmes, the officers and prisoners... that the new director of the castle is an autocratic and tyrannical officer. Tell them that he used to be the commandant of the commandos, and that’s the reason the French government have assigned him to this position. They wanted to use him to enforce discipline and suffering on the Syrian prisoners. I want you to tell them that he’s not in the least bit like any other officer and that he has an iron fist that will kill anyone he strikes.’

Abu Mohammad’s eyes widened in wonder at what his commander had just said. His features expressed both astonishment and disapproval of what he had heard, so he said, ‘God forbid! How can I say such things about you sir, when your character is far above such autocratic and vicious qualities? What you’re saying is a lie... there’s no truth in it! You are the epitome of noble morality, compassion and virility: you are really a gallant and honourable gentleman.’

‘Oh, you faithful man!’ our officer replied, ‘I’m asking you to say exactly the opposite, and the more you exaggerate in describing me as a cruel, hard-hearted man, just as I’ve told you, the more you will help me tomorrow.’

Abu Mohammad complied with the order of his commanding officer without questioning him any further, and despite his amazement and confusion. He did not understand why Officer Sheikho wanted this false story about him to be circulated yet, by his commandant’s very look and the tone of his voice, he sensed the seriousness of the matter and that the desired outcome depended on his success in achieving the orders of his master. Still confused about the matter he nevertheless accepted to do as he had been asked.

Abu Mohammad began to spread the false character profile, as instructed, among the officers, gendarmes and the prisoners, throughout the castle and its prison. Thus everybody there heard of the apparent violence and cruelty of the governor and that he was a man to be reckoned with and should be regarded with awe.

Since our officer was always extremely earnest and had gained the reputation of being as predatory as a lion, the rumour quickly spread and was believed by many, but by no means all, who heard it.

Despite that ingenious arrangement of Mohammad Amin, there were still some inside the castle who persisted in their erroneous ways and evil intentions. They made an arrangement with their cronies to create some disruption inside the castle and the prison so as to disturb the usual state of controlled order, and spread chaos and confusion. Such a situation would make it appear that he was incompetent to hold such a high position and to be a leader of so many men.

So, if their plot were to succeed, the French government would then be obliged to remove him from his prominent position of authority. That was the aim of these treacherous officers and was exactly what our officer had anticipated and was prepared for.

It was not long before several policemen burst through the door of the commandant’s office, their faces ashen as they gasped out, ‘Sir... sir, a prisoner in dungeon number 20, which is used for those sentenced to death, has stabbed another prisoner. He was given a dagger secretly by a corrupt gendarme, and now he’s standing there threatening and menacing anyone who tries to approach him.’

Our officer gave them the order to arrest him but they replied, ‘Sir, he may stab us if we approach him; so, can we shoot him and be done with it?’

Our officer realised immediately just what was going on! They wanted him to give the order for them to kill the criminal so it would seem that he was incapable of controlling the prisoners, and he would then be responsible for the murder of a prisoner. So, he was right in his initial suspicions about them; for what he had expected was in the process of becoming a reality.

He had told Abu Mohammad to spread a rumour about his cruelty and violence around the castle only as an initial arrangement. If this step failed to stop the deceit and the conspiracy, it would be just the first basic stage of a plan to prevent disorder, and impose order upon everybody in the castle and its prison indefinitely.

Actually, the first precautions which he took did not inhibit those envious officers from implementing such actions. They had used one of their followers amongst the gendarmes to give the criminal a knife which he used to stab another prisoner. The injured man fell down bloodstained in the middle of the dungeon; the other prisoners were shocked and drew back towards the walls in fear for their lives, for they did not know who his next victim might be. Then the killer stood over the blood-stained prisoner, looking at him, laughing hysterically, and clearly relishing the sight of the blood and the groans of the dying man. The other prisoners in the dungeon were not part of the plot, and did not realise that the criminal had been given the dagger and instructed to commit the crime, so that the director of the castle would fall into a trap.

Officer Sheikho had been expecting the news and was not in the least bit surprised, so he tackled the situation immediately with firmness and resolve. He dismissed the gendarmes angrily, and then he looked at Abu Mohammad conveying by his look that he would deal harshly with those who sought to disturb order and undermine his authority.

He said to him, ‘Abu Mohammad! You trusty and loyal man! I want you to go straight to the dungeon and to tell that criminal that the prison commander wants to see him right now.’

‘But that’s impossible! How can you do that sir? Surely, he’ll refuse! He’s such a hardened criminal that he doesn’t care about your orders.’

‘Don’t worry, you loyal man! Just give him my message... I’m sure that he’ll refuse, so wait there for exactly five minutes. And remember, don’t leave there until I come to join you.’

Abu Mohammad saluted his commandant and hurried away to carry out the order. He brought out a large key from his waistband with which he opened the ancient iron lock. The heavy door squeaked as it was opened and from there he called out to the brutal criminal in a booming voice, ‘Hey, you! The warden has ordered you to come to his office at once.’

When the prisoner heard what Abu Mohammad said, he started to laugh as though he were demented. Then he said to him haughtily, ‘He wants me to go to him... me! Go to him! What a joke! Does he really think that I’d do that? How stupid!’

Then he began to swear at the warden in the foulest language which demonstrated nothing other than his contemptible behaviour and unbounded ignominy.

Abu Mohammad stood speechless beside the door, waiting for his commandant as he had been ordered to do. He was furious with the criminal but he controlled himself. The prisoners wondered what was wrong with him! It was not usual for a policeman to listen to that kind of abuse and take no action. But the prisoners had no idea that Abu Mohammad was simply obeying orders and they continued to look at him while he remained on the spot for the five minutes that the commandant had stipulated. They thought that out of fear of his commander’s reaction if he failed to obey the order, he did not move from his place.

Five long minutes passed before they heard the firm footfall of our proud officer resounding on the stone floors. He was drawn up to his full height and entered the cell with sparkling eyes, a sword and two revolvers hanging from his belt. He halted before all the prisoners, and stood there as solid as a rock. His appearance was truly awe-inspiring. Then, like a clap of thunder his voice reverberated off the solid stone walls and addressed the gendarme, Abu Mohammad, ‘Woe betide you! Didn’t I tell you to fetch that cowardly dog to me at once? How dare you disobey my order?’

Then, as quick as lightning, he slapped him so forcefully that he landed face down on the ground two metres away with bloodstained lips.

It was such a terrible shock for Abu Mohammad that it left him speechless and stunned... unable to move. He remained where he was, lying on the floor, stupefied more by the emotional shock than the physical one. He could not believe what had happened... one moment he was carrying out the commandant’s order... and the next moment that same commandant that he held in such high esteem, had knocked him to the ground for no apparent reason.

Silence prevailed; astonishment and surprise could be seen on the face of every man present, both prisoners and gendarmes alike! The warden’s action was shocking! The common military tradition of that time considered the public denigration of a gendarme as an atrocity for whatever reason it was carried out; how would they then regard this beating of the gendarme by his commanding officer?

All present then understood the reality of what they had heard of his character and became sure of its truth when they witnessed that unexpected event.

‘If Abu Mohammad, the gendarme, had been treated in that way simply because of his delay in carrying out orders, although it was not his fault, what would be the punishment of a prisoner in the castle – who deserves to be punished – if he disobeyed orders? So, what we heard about his tyranny and cruelty is true. His strike leads to the grave and none can escape from him when disobeying orders. He does not care for laws or traditions. Definitely, the government has given him a free hand. Really, he seems to be the cruellest of commandants; so God help anyone who disobeys his order.’

These were the thoughts running through the minds of all the prisoners who had witnessed this event. At that moment, a terrible silence spread over the place because of the enormity of the event which had left everyone dumbfounded. All of them were totally shocked at what they had seen, and overwhelmed by alarm and fear.

All the while Mohammad Amin was not looking directly at the criminal, but he could see him from the corner of his eye and was aware of his every movement.

Again, his voice resounded around the dungeon like a thunderclap, as he ordered the prisoners to leave the cell.

They were trembling and all obeyed without hesitation, starting to file out one by one.

In the meantime, some of the criminal’s cronies gave a sign to him to drop the dagger and to mingle among the rank and file of the prisoners to save himself from our aweinspiring officer. Yet nothing escaped the keen eyesight and acuity of Officer Sheikho, who was covertly following the villain’s every movement, before and after he threw down the dagger. The criminal managed to mingle among the crowd until his turn came to file out. As soon as he had taken a couple of steps past Mohammad Amin, our officer fell into line behind him like his shadow, then in a flash he stretched his leg forward and hooked it in front of the criminal’s legs; their momentum carried them forward so they were now locked together. At the same time, his hand landed firmly in the middle of the criminal’s back... and crash... he was lying full length on the floor.

‘Oh God! Is this human strength? It’s more like superhuman power,’ the prisoners said to one another in astonishment. ‘Oh God! What a brave man!’ they said secretly to themselves.

They had not noticed the officer’s legs interlocking with those of the criminal, causing him to fall flat on his face. They thought it was only that terrible blow which had caused the criminal to fall so heavily. Then, our officer set about beating and kicking him until he had beaten him senseless. There, he called upon the scheming gendarmes and ordered them to drag the criminal by his legs and throw him into solitary confinement.

Fear and alarm spread throughout the castle after details of the incident circulated, and everybody there became panic-stricken. They all knew for certain that anybody falling foul of the strong arm of the new director would surely be destroyed.

Officer Mohammad Amin did not stop there! In his determination to restore his authority he took further steps and visited every cell in the prison. Some of those cells were large enough to hold almost a hundred prisoners. There, the officer of imposing stature began to pace and roar throughout the large space. He removed his badges, then rolled up his sleeves and turned towards the crowded prisoners with a determined face like a lion on the prowl. ‘Come on, men,’ he said, ‘let’s forget about military regulations! It’s well known that most prisoners are honest heroes (although he knew that was not true!). Now, I’m taking off my badge so we can romp together, man to man, in sportsmanship. I promise that if any one of you can withstand just one blow of my arm without falling over, I’ll give that man a privilege over all the other prisoners. I will let him move freely wherever he wants around the castle all day long; I’ll also shower him with hospitality and gifts. So, is there anyone here that wants to accept the challenge?’

Everybody heard that tempting challenge, but they were all cowed by what they had seen and heard. Not a single one of them dared to accept Officer Sheikho’s challenge, for his stature and vehemence had really terrorized and shocked them. So, through his exceptional wisdom and mastery his plan stopped the plot in its tracks! After that event, everybody in the castle, officers, gendarmes and prisoners, submitted to him. Security and order prevailed and Mohammad Amin ensured that they remained in constant awe of him.

But what about Abu Mohammad?

When our officer finished quelling the problem in the prison, he sent for him to come to his office.

Poor Abu Mohammad! He came into the office in a terrible state. He was so sad and broken-hearted that he was barely able to speak, but thoughts were flying around his mind, ‘I can’t believe what happened!
