He found this extremely odd, and wondered, ‘Why are children laughing and playing in the courtyard at such an hour of the night? And how did they get in when the outer door is closed and locked?! Really, this is a very strange state of affairs!’

So, he approached them and asked their names, at which point, the three children stopped, but still held each others’ hands, and then continued to jump up and down in a lively, carefree way.

Then, the oldest one said, ‘I’m Kberoon.’

‘I’m Azgar,’ said the middle one.

‘And I’m Zgeroon,’ the youngest said.

As soon as the third child finished speaking our master, who was still puzzled at the situation, uttered the word “Al’lah”, a word that came from a man who, through his heart’s eye, constantly bore witness to his Provider, and suddenly, the three children changed into columns of smoke, leaving no trace behind them.

And then it became quite clear that there was no Um Fathi attending to the laundry, no oil burner, and not even the slightest sound or whisper. There was nothing but absolute silence, and no sign that anything unusual had just taken place on that very spot.

The virtuous master was most concerned about his wife Um Fathi, so he rushed upstairs, barefoot, to check on her. He headed straight for her bedroom, where he found her deep in her slumbers. In fact she had been sleeping soundly from the moment +she had laid her head on her pillow and was still fast asleep. In fact it appeared that she had not turned over or even moved because of the enormous effort she had exerted and the fatigue she felt from her work the day before. It was obvious that she was totally unaware of what had happened.

Later, when she woke up a few minutes before sunrise, her husband asked her calmly, not wanting to disturb or worry her, ‘Did you get up last night, Um Fathi?’

‘No!’ she answered, ‘I felt absolutely nothing, from the time I put my head on my pillow until I woke up to pray just before sunrise.’

Nevertheless, Abu Fathi continued to hide this event from his wife for six years so that she should not become afraid, due to any whispers or disturbing ideas that may have come into her mind.

After that night, no more events of that kind occurred in their home ever again, and the haunted house turned into a house that was haunted only by the family’s happiness which spread joy throughout, and which flowed constantly from the spirit of that noble man.

So, we learn that, when somebody rightfully resorts to God and truly seeks refuge in Him, when they yield and apply His Orders, and when they become truly upright, all evils and offences will be driven away from them as they will be protected and strengthened by the encompassing fence of their true belief.

In this way, God will protect them as long as they stay within His Bounds and constantly seek refuge in Him.

So, those that follow the right path will perform real communication with God, and then the divine states, enlightenment and witnessing will enter their spirits and uplift them towards God, where they will become cured of their defects and diseases. Then no man or creature will have power over them, as they will have become clean and pure.

That is the state of anyone who truly believes in God, for He says, “No power has he [Satan] over believers who put their trust in their Provider. He has power only over those who befriend him and those who serve other gods besides Al’lah.” ﴿194﴾

Truly, there is a great lesson here for those who wish to learn.

chapters.title: A Vow Should Never Be Broken
chapters.html:
One day our man, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, was sitting having a conversation with one of his friends, when his friend asked him if he remembered a certain mutual friend.

‘Yes, I do; what’s the matter with him?’

‘Poor man! He got married many years ago, but he still does not have any children. He prays to God persistently to grant him a child. But it seems that God’s Will has deemed it fit to leave him childless. Although medical tests have confirmed that he is sterile he has not lost hope. You find him constantly asking God to fulfill his wish: he particularly wants a son.’

This was how Mohammad Amin heard the story of his barren friend who was, as he remembered from the past, frugal to the point of being stingy.

Just a few days later, our benevolent man met the childless man by chance, and as he looked at him he recalled his problem. As for the man, who was fully aware of the highly moral character of Mohammad Amin, his love of God and his strict adherence to His Commands, when he saw him he immediately rushed towards him begging him, ‘Oh Bey! Oh Bey! You are close to God and God listens to your prayers. So, please, I beg you… ask Him for my sake… ask Him to give me a male child. Oh Bey, please… I want a son to occupy my time and fill my heart. And perhaps he will help me when I grow old.’ As he was speaking his eyes filled with tears. Our compassionate man answered him in a kind and gentle tone, ‘Dear brother! If you want God to fulfill your wish, then make a promise to Him and you will find that He will grant your request.’

‘Really,’ the man asked eagerly, ‘is it truly that easy? If my greatest wish can be achieved by a promise, then before you I vow to God that if He favours me with a baby boy I will offer up a sheep… not just any sheep… it will be a fattened sheep.’

And so it was not long before God fulfilled his wish. His wife became pregnant within a few days, and day by day, her pregnancy became clear to see. The husband felt as though he were in the seventh heaven and spent the rest of the nine months almost boiling with impatience whilst eagerly awaiting the birth of his child.

For many years he had been yearning for a little boy, and before long his hopes would be realised: there were no words to describe the happiness he felt as he counted down the days.

At the end of the pregnancy, the wife gave birth to a healthy, handsome boy… indeed, some would say a beautiful cherub that infatuated the hearts of all who saw him. The parents were overwhelmed with joy at seeing their wish fulfilled after such a long time of yearning and deprivation. The baby became the sole focus of his parents’ attention as their every waking moment was taken up with giving him endless care and attention.

But what about the promise? It seemed that the father had forgotten it as soon as he saw his beautiful baby… or should we say he pretended to have forgotten it. So, he failed to offer up a fattened sheep, or even a scrawny chick! Miserable miser! Whenever he looked at his son and saw him growing day by day, he became ever more loving and attached to him. Alas! He had become immersed in the favour and forgotten Who had granted it. He neglected his promise to God and failed to give thanks to his Provider.

The highly esteemed master, Mohammad Amin, heard of God’s Gift to that niggardly man, and he met him once again by chance… although as one might realise, this meeting was purely by God’s Will.

Our man congratulated him on his newborn son and thought to remind him of his vow, so he said, ‘What about your promise, my friend? Have you sacrificed a fattened sheep?’

‘No, no… not yet,’ the miser answered, ‘but of course I will certainly do it… yes, yes indeed… but not now. I will have the boy circumcised first then I will arrange the sacrifice… yes… yes, after his circumcision!’

The baby was circumcised and still the father failed to keep his pledge to God. For him to sacrifice a fattened sheep would be a great financial loss even though he was rich. So he chose, quite simply, to forget all about it.

Not long afterwards God created another chance for the new father to meet our compassionate man who reminded him for the second time, ‘I expect that by now you must have fulfilled your vow and slaughtered the sheep, am I right?’

Whereupon the man replied, ‘Oh Bey! Does God really need my sacrifice? Of course, He doesn’t. He doesn’t need any sacrifices at all. He can feed all the poor in the world if He wishes. So, He has no need of me or my offering.’

Our man became deeply disturbed on hearing his words, so he said to him, ‘What are you saying? Do you think that a breach of promise is an insignificant matter? I can tell you that it’s most serious in the Eyes of Al’lah. How can you back out of your commitment and go back on your promise? Listen to me, man! I warn you, if you don’t sacrifice a sheep, by God, within fifteen days and not a day more, you will lose your son. He will die. You have made a vow to God, and this is not something to treat lightly.’

When Mohammad Amin uttered these words he was boiling with rage.

The man heard the force of his words which nevertheless hid great mercy and fear for him, yet, unfortunately, he failed to understand the gravity behind them. In fact, he paid them no heed whatsoever, and he mumbled something under his breath while backing away. He thought to himself, ‘Would God truly deprive me of the light of my life just because of a single sheep? No… no, I don’t think so… my son is in the best of health and a very bonny baby.’

Weeks passed while the child continued to flourish and become more beautiful and active with every passing day. Indeed, the boy could be compared to the moon as it waxed day by day: Glory to the Great Creator.

Then, on the fifteenth day the sun rose in all its splendid glory and was reaching its zenith as midday approached! The baby was still lively and blooming, smiling at his father and mother who took turns to hold him in their arms, and breathe in that sweet, milky smell that is particular to babies. They were enraptured! But suddenly the child’s face turned pale and an alarming change came over it.

‘Oh God! There’s something wrong with him… it seems serious… what is it?… what’s happening to him?’ his parents gasped.

The baby’s face had lost its healthy glow and now appeared to have a yellowish tinge, indicating that he may be close to death, and his cries were pitiful as though he was suffering unbearable pain! The parents stood helpless before their child. They were looking at him bewildered and confused by this alarming sight.

They sent for the doctor, but just minutes before he arrived, the baby breathed his last while cradled in his father’s arms. The father moved him gently in an effort to revive him… then he shook him, but it was in vain for the baby did not respond. His bewitching eyes were still wide open but his chest was still: there was no sign of life.

A long, loud lament issued from the father expressing the bitter pain he was feeling at that moment, ‘He’s dead! He’s dead!’ And he burst into tears. Then he remembered! He remembered the words of his noble friend. He remembered his admonition and advice. As his mind thought back over the events before his son’s death he found that it was exactly fifteen days from the day he had met his noble friend until the day his child died!

He dashed out of his home and began staggering right and left like a drunkard. He did not know where to go or what to do. Poor man! He had brought this pain upon himself. His feet led him inadvertently in the direction of some of his friends who stopped him and tried to calm him down. But he could only repeat the same words over and over again, ‘By God, he’s a Prophet! By God, he’s a Prophet! He predicted the exact time of my boy’s death. He told me that he would die after fifteen days, and his Prophecy has come true!’

As for our gracious man, Mohammad Amin, when he was asked about his Prophecy, he said, ‘By God, when I uttered those words I did not know what I was saying. It happened as I said it would… though I knew nothing about it.’

chapters.title: Talking with the Dead
chapters.html:
Steadily and inexorably the Day of Reckoning is approaching the appointed hour when all of mankind will be called to account. With every passing day, hour and second he is drawing closer to the moment of death and the afterlife to come. And yet he pays no attention to this!

Nobody can know when they will die; nobody can be sure that they will still be alive tomorrow.

Oh Mankind! Do you not think you should prepare yourself for this one inescapable fact: your inevitable death?

You will die and be interred in your grave, and then the angels will come and question you. What will your answer be? Are you making good preparations for this difficult moment? What provisions are you making for this journey?

The Envoy of God (cpth) said, “Death is the best preacher.”

Everybody surely has experienced the death of a relative or friend. In our daily lives we are accustomed to seeing one another, spending pleasant time in each other’s company, and then suddenly, often without warning, one of us moves on to the next life. This is a life so different from our present earthly life and lasts from the world of the grave until the final world. The train of this person’s life has reached the final station where it will stop and they are called to alight. And so, they descend from this train of life, leaving behind all those inside.

At this moment, they will come to understand that the journey of life is too short and the relationships they thought firm and unbreakable are now over. This is the act of death: it puts an end to all earthly pleasures and breaks up company and lovers. All the joys and pleasures of this life are nothing but a mirage in a desert: people think there is water but, alas, a mirage is nothing, and “nothing” does not quench thirst. And then the fires of anguish, distress and regret are inflamed in the spirit.

Those who spend their life in debauchery will come to know the reality of their base desires at the time of death, and then they will wail, calling for help, ‘Oh Lord, send us back so that we can perform good deeds in the world we have left behind.’ Truly, their sorrow and remorse for their negligence of God’s Recommendations and for their loss of closeness to the charitable Benefactor will be beyond description. They will repeatedly ask to be sent back to life in order to do good deeds. But, in fact, they are liars, for even if God responds to their call, they will again fail to do good deeds and will never change their wrongful ways. The Almighty originally sent them to this world for this purpose but they neglected to do this and foundered in the morass of their earthly pleasures.

In the pre-material world they neglected to keep their promise to God that they would never turn away from Him; however, God gave them another chance when He sent them to this world. But, alas, despite the miracles with which God filled this universe, and the warnings sent with His Envoys, they take no notice of them and never study them. And so, they are sure to fail again.

So, why do they call for a third chance?

They will never repent to God, and that is why they will never again be sent back to this world. They will remain in the grave, living in darkness, desolate and terrified. For such people, it will be the time for regret and pain, and an even greater terror awaits them on the Day of Resurrection.

In the Holy Qur’an, the Almighty says, “Give out of what We have provided for you, before death comes to one of you, and they say, ‘My Lord, if You would only reprieve me for a little while, I would donate to charity and become one of the righteous.’ ” ﴿195﴾

From time to time, and according to the depth of their affection for the deceased, people go to the graveyard to visit the dead who have left them. They stand at their gravesides and read the al-Fatiha Fortress for their souls. We greet them, and they hear our greeting and answer it. They hear us and even talk to us, but we, the living, as long as we are not illuminated by God’s Light, are unable to hear them.

The visit serves as a warning of impending death for our spirits. We, ourselves, are reminded of the moment of our certain departure from this world, the moment when we will leave behind all the adornment and vanities of this world and be removed either to live in eternal joy or to undergo a series of bitter treatments in order to heal our sick spirits.

For the spirit does not die, it only has a taste of death when the angel of death draws the soul from the physical body. Then the body becomes cold and no longer of any use to the spirit. Therefore the spirit, which is the essential element of man and his immaterial, conscious self, leaves the body and follows the soul. By leaving the body, the spirit experiences death as it departs from the present world, where it was enclosed within a body, and goes to the middle world where it becomes exposed, unrestricted by its body. There, the angels will show it all the deeds and actions it performed during its worldly life, as every last one will have been written on its pages. If they were good the spirit will enjoy a good condition, crowned with light, soaring up to the Lord of Light, and living at the highest degrees of happiness and joy. But if the deeds of a spirit were bad and evil it will suffer deep sorrow for its negligence. It will be confined to its long, dark prison in the grave, suffering loneliness and agony, unable to escape from this dreadful fate.

We often stop to wonder: what are the conditions of our deceased family and friends? Are they living in beautiful Gardens, happy and honoured? Or what?

Our great Envoy Mohammad (cpth) said, “By He Whose Hand controls Mohammad’s spirit there is no home after this world except Gardens or Fire.”

Who can know the state of the dead? Do you know anything about this? I do not think so. Then who does know? Indeed, it is only those who are illuminated by God’s Light, those whose heart’s eye is opened to show them realities and truths who know about this. And it was said, “Those endowed with knowledge of God have heart’s eyes that see what the eyewitnesses cannot see.”

Those people have certain knowledge; they look with their heart’s eye and keep close company with no one but Prophets and true men. This group is not found guilty. Their spirits are free, not shackled by sin or shameful deeds, rather they soar up to the highest heaven. This is because they have true love for their Provider and are faithful to their guide, the Envoy of God (cpth). They live and act under his light (cpth), the light of the shining lamp. It is they who can bring back the spirits of the dead. With their opened heart’s eye they witness the state of their dead acquaintances, by the light of the Envoy (cpth). Thus, we understand that their knowledge depends on certainty and reality, not on doubt and assumption.

However, this situation is not destined for them, alone. In fact, every human being is capable of attaining the same high rank as they have. But this requires them to follow the straight path and avoid whatever is forbidden, and to seize opportunities to perform noble deeds and commendable acts.

The Envoy’s cousin, Ali (God honoured him) said, ‘By God, when the veil is removed (meaning: when he dies), I will not become more certain than I am now.’ While still in this worldly life he gained true knowledge about what comes after death, and so he witnessed the in-between world and the world to come. This is what is meant by believing in the other world. When a human attains this sort of knowledge they will be able to talk to the dead with whom they were acquainted during their lifetime. But the ability to talk to all the dead in general, indicates a high degree of piety and Godliness that is known to none except Al’lah and His noble Envoys (cpth).

Our merciful man, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, took care of his mother until he led her to true belief; and because she was so attached to her pious son, she drank from him the love for Al’lah and His Envoy (cpth), until she became a pure and pious woman.

Through his humane and clever handling of his mother and his honouring her, the noble master was able to drive her heart towards God and help her to enter His Presence while she was still in this world. And so, she lived in this high state until she departed this earthly life, in a state of happiness.

After her death, the virtuous master consistently visited his mother in the graveyard to remind himself of the day of his own death and to teach it that it must not pursue any worldly purpose but seek only to attain God’s Satisfaction.

This is a distinguished quality of a true believer; whatever high rank they may rise to, they keep in mind that they, too, will die.

Our master, Ali, reached a high degree of piety, however, he continued to visit cemeteries to keep death in his mind until he was called Abu Turab. ﴿196﴾

Our man, Mohammad Amin, was deeply affected by his mother’s death and so he took the opportunity and began to teach his spirit and give it practical lessons about death. He would leave home every evening after performing the evening prayer and climb Mount Qasiyun where the cemetery of God’s Prophet, Dhi al-Kifl was located (and is until this day). He used to walk up the mountain heading toward his mother’s grave where he would spend the whole night until day-break.

He had already asked the gravedigger to prepare a grave for him next to his mother’s; and so he spent the time there by lying in his own grave and reflecting on God and death.

He maintained this habit for fully six months and did not miss passing even a single night at the graveyard all during this time.

By such conduct, he practised one of the ways which lead to firm belief in the life to come. For thinking of death results in believing in the Afterworld which allows man to become aware of the events of the world in-between and the other world. Through this belief, the spirit will flow to the other abode and live there. This is an example of what is meant by realisation of the spirit; it means to experience things through the spirit before they actually occur.

A few years before his mother’s death, our noble man noticed that the house they lived in needed some repairs and restoration of its wooden doors and window frames. At that time he was an officer and a faithful follower of Sheikh Amin Kuftaro.

So, he talked with a carpenter who was, incidentally, one of his brothers in the circle, about the repairs he needed to carry out in his house.

This carpenter was a naive and good-hearted man; and because he loved our master so much he soon agreed to undertake the work by himself; and for many successive days the carpenter worked hard and with great skill in the house of our eminent man. He used to go there in the morning and did not leave until the afternoon. While working, he often heard the voice of Mohammad Amin’s old mother, sometimes when she was speaking with her son, or other times when she might call to him from her room or the kitchen. Then her beloved son would answer her without delay. Because the carpenter frequently heard the voice of the old mother he soon became very familiar with it.

Then, a few months later, the exemplary mother left this earthly life and her faithful son devoted himself to visiting her every night at the cemetery so as to chasten his spirit by lying in his own grave. For six long months, the venerable master continued to spend the night in the graveyard, lying in his grave beside that of his mother.

One day, the carpenter missed the company of his virtuous friend, Officer Mohammad Amin. He yearned for his noble character and great integrity and remembered how he had guided him to their honest sheikh, Amin Kuftaro. So, he decided to visit him at home, but failed to find him there. Some neighbours told him that they had seen his friend on the road leading to the graveyard, and so he set off in that direction.

By this time, dusk had fallen and darkness enveloped everything around him, for electricity had not yet reached our country. All alone, the carpenter walked along the road until the way began to climb upwards in the mountainous area, and signs of habitation were soon left behind. The place was desolate; and with every step the carpenter took towards his destination he felt his heartbeats grow stronger and quicker until he began to tremble all over in terror. As he approached the graveyard, he felt intense fear creeping throughout his body until it controlled all his movements. To try to overcome this state he began to mumble and murmur, making different sounds to dissipate the solitude, and calm down and put the exhausting thoughts out of his mind. And yet all his efforts came to nothing! It seemed that the night had truly drawn a heavy cover over everything around him so he could see nothing but waves of darkness which served only to heighten his feelings of loneliness and terror for his thoughts were dwelling on the place he was heading towards.

However, his eagerness to see the magnanimous benefactor was able to overcome such irrational and unwarranted fears. The path to the graveyard seemed so long. He walked and walked until he finally reached its outer boundary where he caught sight of the gravedigger. ‘Have you seen Abu Fathi?’ the carpenter asked him eagerly as if something of great importance had happened.

This prompted the gravedigger to reveal the secret conduct of the virtuous man which was known to no-one but him, and so he replied, ‘He’s up there, lying in the grave he has prepared for himself beside his mother’s.’ The carpenter set out to climb higher still, to the top of the mountain, and all during the ascent he kept calling out for his friend in a loud but trembling voice in the hope that he might hear him reply and his own fears be banished.

In fact, the distress that took up his entire spirit had cleared all the other troubles that usually occupied it, and with no interest in anything else in the world. His thoughts were fully focused on one single matter: to see Abu Fathi, so that his own gloominess and fears might disappear. Along the path, completely deserted except for the many graves, and in an atmosphere of dreadful silence, broken only by the sound of the cinchona trees rustling in the gentle breeze, the carpenter continued to climb while calling, ‘Abu Fathi… Abu Fathi’, hoping to hear him answer at any moment.

The august master heard the call while lying in the tomb and he recognised the carpenter’s voice. He wondered, ‘What could have brought him to this place at such a time? Why is he calling me? There must be a very serious matter that has caused him to come looking for me!’ There and then, he stood up and stepped out of his grave and answered him, ‘Here I am. Come on, keep climbing.’

The words of the noble master brought a great sense of relief and peace to the carpenter’s heart for they eradicated his anguish and despondency and revitalized him. He felt a renewed sense of energy and vitality so he continued his ascent with faster, more nimble steps, with his heart reaching out to Abu Fathi.

Finally, he reached the upper area of the cemetery where the mother’s grave was located and there he found the noble master standing beside it and looking at in his direction. The carpenter heaved a deep sigh of relief at seeing his friend and then greeted him warmly. After acknowledging the greeting, Mohammad Amin asked him, ‘Is there anything wrong? I hope that it’s good news that has brought you to me in such a place and at such a time.’

The carpenter was still breathing heavily because of his exhausting efforts and the horrible moments he experienced on the way to see his friend; and his reply, when it came, was with a quivering voice…, ‘It is only because of my longing to see your noble face… I missed you so much.’

And the noble master said to him, ‘Okay, my friend, I’ll come with you in a little while but only after I recite the al-Fatiha Fortress for my mother’s soul and take my leave of her.’

Mohammad Amin turned towards his mother’s grave and raising his hands he began to recite the Opening Fortress (al-Fatiha Surah), while the poor carpenter stood beside him reciting the same Fortress in a trembling voice.

When the noble master finished, he bade farewell to his mother in a loud voice, saying, ‘Al-Salamu alaiki, my mother.’ Everything was quite normal until the moment when an affectionate and merciful voice reached the ears of the carpenter that confused him and almost caused him to faint. It was the mother’s voice, the voice of hajja Um Saleem herself. He was certain that he had not made a mistake for he knew her voice very well. He heard her reply to her son, ‘Wa alaika al-Salam wa rahmatullahi wa barakatu, my son.’

‘Oh my God! What is this? I can’t believe what I hear with my own ears! How odd! It’s her voice, her very own voice! I still remember it exactly. It became imprinted in my memory all during the time I worked in their house; only a few months ago I used to hear her calling to her son every day. But how does she talk to her son when she’s dead? This is incredible… but it just happened! How did it happen? How?’

The situation was so bewildering that the carpenter became absentminded and could no longer control himself. He said, ‘Am I still alive… in this world? Or could I…?’

Immediately, he was overwhelmed by a feeling of deep foreboding causing him to stand motionless, eyes and mouth wide open, trying to grasp the matter and comprehend the truth of what he had just heard. The woman had died six months ago; but now, when her son greeted her she answered him! It was the very same voice he had heard when she was still alive! Suddenly, shaken out of his stupor, he took to his heels, and began to run as fast as possible, as if a malevolent ghost was trying to catch him and kill him. He fell down, rolling over soil and stones among the tombs, as the old mother’s reply repeatedly sounded in his ears. He quickly scrambled to his feet and continued on his downward path, going faster and faster.

His body was covered in cuts and bruises but he felt nothing, for his entire attention was focused on one thing; to reach the house of his uncle-in-law, Sheikh Amin Kuftaro.

He ran out the cemetery with the dust and soil covering his clothes as if he had faced a violent desert sandstorm. He kept on running as fast as he could until he reached the sheikh’s house where he entered his face pale and covered with dust.

When the venerable sheikh saw his son-in-law in such a state he stopped talking to his guests and turned his attention to the younger man and asked, ‘What has come over you, son? What’s the matter?’

Puffing and panting, and in a tremulous voice, the carpenter replied to his sheikh, ‘Oh sir… oh sir… It is Abu Fathi… Abu Fathi, sir… ‘

Sheikh Amin Kuftaro said, ‘What’s wrong with him? Come on, son, tell me, quickly.’

‘Oh sir, he talks to the dead and they answer him!’

The news astounded the sheikh, so he said, ‘What are you saying, son? Do you understand what you’re saying?’

‘By God, sir, I’m telling you the truth. I went to see him at his mother’s grave, and before leaving, he said goodbye to her and she answered him. I heard her with my own ears. It was her voice, I know it very well and I was not mistaken.’

Sheikh Amin found himself in a compromising situation in front of those present; so, to avoid this he said to the alarmed carpenter, ‘Oh, son, I think you’re not well today.

Perhaps your night visit to the cemetery has exhausted and terrified you. I think that you should go home to get some rest. And I advise you never to visit the graveyard during the hours of darkness again.’ Then the respected sheikh sent two of his disciples to look for Mohammad Amin and bring him to the meeting. When the two men went out to the street they found the august master already coming towards the sheikh’s home. Entering the house, our compassionate man joined the meeting, his face glowing as though crowned with an unearthly light that created pleasure in his heart. He greeted his sheikh who thanked God for his arrival and spoke to him directly, saying, ‘Come on, my son. Come and listen to what my son-in-law has said about you. He claimed that when you took your leave of your mother in her grave she answered you, and he insisted that he heard her voice with his own ears.’

The sheikh’s purpose in informing Mohammad Amin of what the carpenter had said was to let his guests hear a denial of this incredible event. He did not want them to think that his teaching was ill-founded and based on imagination. The good-hearted sheikh was sure that the noble master would answer in the negative and deny the event; yet Mohammad Amin’s reply was quite the opposite! Not for a single moment did the sheikh think that what they had heard was the truth, and had actually happened. Mohammad Amin said to his sheikh, ‘If my mother’s answer to my words had such an impact on him, then just think what a terrible state he would have been in if he had waited until I took my leave of all the dead in the graveyard, and they all replied!’

Sheikh Amin was completely flabbergasted at the words of the noble master. He was confused for he was certain that Mohammad Amin was a truthful man, and he knew well about his firm faith in God. However, not for a single moment did he imagine that this man might have reached such a high degree of belief and piety, a degree at which a human could address the dead and hear their response!

With a look full of reverence and admiration for this pure, godly human being, Sheikh Amin looked at Mohammad Amin, appreciating his great love for his Provider and his faithfulness to Him, a matter which uplifted him and led him to this supreme dignity at a time when many people drew away from God and ignored His Book.

So, he said to him, ‘May God bless you, my son! May God increase your honour, my son. Indeed, you are a blessing that God has granted to us. What high standing you have with Him! I have not reached this level, my son, I mean, the level which enables a human being to talk to the dead and hear their reply! Tell me, son, for how long have you been visiting your mother in the graveyard?’

‘For six months, venerable Sheikh!’ the noble master replied.

‘What! For six full months you have been visiting your mother in her grave to delight her with the mention of God! For six full months you have been spending every night in the graveyard! That is enough, my son. You have achieved what Imam al-Gazali did. Tell me, son, why did you do it?’

‘I wanted to refine my spirit, sir.’ Mohammad Amin replied.

On hearing this, all those present looked at the noble master with the greatest admiration and respect. They wondered how, despite the bad times they were living in, there was still a man with such noble merits and at such a high degree of illumination by God’s Light, a degree known only to Al’lah and His Envoy (cpth).

But this might bring a further question to one’s mind: how could the terrified carpenter hear the reply of Mohammad Amin’s mother to her son’s greeting?

In fact, the carpenter had been so overwhelmed with fear that his spirit was completely clear of all thought of any other concerns he might have. He was wholly engrossed with just one thing: to see our exemplary human being, Mohammad Amin, and keep him company. The fact that the carpenter’s heart was fully directed towards the noble master allowed the carpenter to live in a state of heart bond and spiritual connection with him.

And since the noble master was talking to his mother and listening to her words spiritually, the carpenter was able to hear the same words with his own spirit and not with his ears as he thought.

This is an indisputable fact. When a spirit is released from its love for this world, it will be able to see realities by the Light of God. This “seeing” will be associated with the senses of sight, touch, taste, smell and hearing: for the spirit is the conscious self of man. In this world it is confined to the body, so it is aware of its surroundings through the five senses. It sees with the eye, hears with the ears, smells with the nose, feels and touches with the skin, and tastes with the tongue, which is also used in speech to express ideas and thoughts.

But when the spirit is freed from its body and becomes illuminated by God’s Light, it will see, smell, hear, speak, and feel and perceive everything by itself: and this is obtained only by God’s Light.

This is referred to in the Holy Qur’an when our Master Shu’aib (pth ﴿197﴾

talked to his people after their destruction. God says, “Thereupon an earthquake seized them; by the next morning they were lying prostrate and dead in their dwellings. It was as if those who had denied Shu’aib had never lived there: it was those who had denied Shu’aib who were the losers. Shu’aib left them, saying, ‘I conveyed to you, my people, the Message of my Lord and gave you sincere advice. How can I grieve for a people persistent in unbelief?’ ” ﴿198﴾

The same approach was followed by the master of creation Mohammad (cpth) when he addressed the unbelievers who had been killed in the Battle of Badr. He (cpth) stood before their corpses at the end of the battle and addressed them, saying, “You, people of Qulaib! Have you found the Promise of your Provider to be true? The noble companions asked him, ‘Can these dead people hear you, Oh Envoy of God?’ He (cpth) replied, ‘Their hearing is even sharper than yours.’” ﴿199﴾

Truly, in the character of our noble human being, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, we realise the truthfulness of the saying of the great Envoy (cpth), “All that is good flows from me, and from my followers till the Day of Resurrection.”

chapters.title: The Bus Conductor Is Caught Out
chapters.html:
Mohammad Amin was living in the al-Muhajireen area on Qasiyun Mountain which overlooked Damascus and its lush, verdant hills. It was situated many kilometers from the city, so he occasionally had to use the public bus as the means to go there and back.

One day, as he was accustomed to do when going home, he got in the bus going to the district where he lived. Al’lah had planned that after it began to move Mohammad Amin would see one of his comrades who was also on the bus. He greeted him, exchanged a few pleasantries, and asked after his family and business matters; everything was as normal.

In the meanwhile, the bus conductor passed by them asking for the fare. With good grace, Mohammad Amin paid for three passengers: himself, his child whom he had taken with him to help him in some affairs, and the friend. He took no notice of what the conductor did after he issued the three tickets.

When they arrived at the stop they needed he and his son headed for their home.

With that, the youngster stopped him saying, ‘Oh, Dad! Why did you pay for your friend’s ticket?’

He replied, ‘I paid because he’s my friend!’

The youngster added, ‘But the conductor took the fare from him too!’

Carefully, Mohammad Amin asked him, ‘Are you sure?’

‘Yes Dad, he issued an adult’s full-price, green ticket.’

Mohammad Amin immediately decided to follow the bus to catch up with the cheating conductor, but it had vanished along the road, so he accompanied his son home and then waited for the arrival of the next bus in order to board it and head off in the same direction as the first one, to the terminus, but the two buses were going in opposite directions: the one carrying the cunning conductor was returning to the city from the end of the line, and the other one carrying Mohammad Amin was travelling towards the end of the line, so he could not catch the conductor. He paid for a ticket to go to the terminus, then he came back by bus and paid another fare to return again to the city, where he found the tramway in the city centre, al-Marjah, which was the starting point for the buses.

He stepped onto the bus looking for the conductor, and when he saw him he grabbed hold of his collar with both hands aiming to hit him. The conductor was overcome by fear and began to beg his forgiveness, saying how sorry he was for what he had done. Mohammad Amin then addressed him saying, ‘Listen to me, you thief! Why did you do that? How dare you take the fare from my friend after I paid it for him?’

His prompt action enabled him to catch up with the conductor and admonish him; through his customary shrewd prudence he pointed out the error of the conductor’s ways when he scolded and chastened him. He also took back the money for the extra fare paid by his friend, then he returned home on yet another bus. And so, altogether, he paid the price of a third ticket for his journey home.

This pursuit actually cost him three times the sum he got back from the conductor. Clearly his purpose had not been about the money at all, yet the decisive factor and aim were to stop deception for, as is well known, no-one could ever fool him. He refused to be defrauded by the conductor whatever the personal cost was to himself.

“I am not a cheat, nor can anyone cheat me.” ﴿200﴾

Moreover, if he left the conductor to persist in breaching people’s rights, his misdemeanours would increase and he would eventually go to extremes and become a force for evil: he would become used to stealing and ill-gotten gains until it became second nature to him. What is more, whatever has been acquired illegally had better be treated by fire, so he should be dealt with by the harshest measures, out of love for him, and to protect him for his own good.

Through his wise behaviour and beneficent deeds, this merciful man, Mohammad Amin, made an example of the conductor and provided a lesson that would deter others; the conductor would be guided towards the right way, so his spirit would never entice him to go too far and steal again after this humiliating lesson, scandal and public degradation.

But let us ask: what would the results of that transgression have been, had Mohammad Amin not acted with him in such a way? And what would happen eventually to the conductor, the perpetrator of that deed, and anyone who followed his example if they were never punished, or had their lie exposed, and received a severe warning? What if this unforgettable lesson had not been given to society?

Truly, if we were to be cowardly and fail to prevent wrongdoing in order to curry favour it would generate misery, pillage, robbery, mutual hatred and discord in this world which would lead to hell-fire in the Hereafter.

Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth) said, “Let him who sees an abominable act correct it by his actions, yet if he cannot do that, then it should be by his words, and if he is unable to do that, then it should be in his heart: but that would be the weakest faith.”

chapters.title: The Distinctive Man
chapters.html:
There were many invitation cards sent that day, to invite a number of guests, prominent in al-Sham, to a stately banquet to be held in honour of Dr Abdul- Kadir al-Zahra’, who was held in high esteem in Syria. Dr Abdul-Kadir also held the military rank of brigadier general at that time. Amongst these eminent guests, there was a certain man, distinguished by his handsomeness and reverence that bore the scent of the musk of purity, veneration, perfection and splendour.

The banquet was to be held in one of the parks of western Ghoutah where the weather was pleasant and clear. The cool, fresh breezes evoked joy and gladness in the heart; and to add to the pleasure of such a perfect day, close to the park there were abundant springs and rivers of glittering, flowing water whose gentle murmuring blended with the chirruping of the birds to compose a unique, magnificent piece of music created by the Hand of Al’lah, the Most Kind, the Almighty.

The crowd of guests arrived, to find a big table prepared for them in the garden of the park, in the verdant shade of the trees and close to the babbling waters. And though the sun was high in the sky on that particular day, its heat was soft and gentle, causing no discomfort at all.

Generally, at that time, the western Ghoutah area of Damascus was distinguished by its pleasant, temperate weather even on hot summer days, compared with other parts of the county. This was due to the abundance of fresh water and trees in the region, which influenced its weather and resulted in constant coolness and temperate conditions.

The guests were smiling happily, and their bursts of laughter expressed their joy and high spirits. Every one of them wore the stateliest suit he owned, in order to present the most elegant appearance.

The natural fresh fragrances of roses and various other flowers mingled with the pleasant Parisian perfumes of the notables and were diffused all around by the gentle breeze. As for their voices, sometimes they were loud and sometimes low, and at other moments they might fall silent.

But one particular man, the subject of our story, a man distinguished by his solemnity, elegance and good looks, left the other notables behind, and walked with his light solemn steps towards the flowing water. The guests noticed this but knew nothing about the reason for his action.

There, on the bank of the river, under one of the wide spreading trees, he took off his shoes and removing his jacket he hung it on a sturdy branch of the tree, having first asked the servant to bring him a prayer carpet. He turned towards the flowing water and baring his strong forearms he bent towards the water to perform briskly the ritual ablution, and then got up to pray in the shade of the tree. He had decided to recite the noon prayer before he sat to eat with the other guests, for it was time for prayer and if he did not pray at once, the conversation might last a long time; it might then be too late to pray before the call signalling the afternoon prayer.

The assembled guests saw him and immediately understood why he had retired from the group, and so did Dr Abdul-Kadir al-Zahra’, in whose honour the banquet was being held.

After some time, the solemn master returned from praying to sit tranquilly with the crowd by the big table where various small groups were conversing quietly amongst themselves; but all of them noticed the venerable master when he came back to join them.

Thereupon, Dr. Abdul-Kadir al-Zahra’ said, complimenting the attendees, ‘Dear brethren! Prayer is not everything in our religion… it is not the only support, nor is it the basis. The most important thing is to have a pure, good heart and to treat people kindly.’ Dr. Abdul-Kadir al-Zahra’ had spoken these words as a courtesy to his fellow guests, so that they should not feel ashamed before the honourable master, as they were far from performing such a Godly duty as prayer.

When the solemn master heard those words, he interrupted the doctor, a man of high prestige, not in selfdefence, as he was the only one who prayed, but to support the truth and to clarify Al’lah’s sublime Purpose beyond prayer; for He did not charge us with it vainly, with no a fruit to be attained. The Almighty’s Bidding to establish it is not simply an order to worship, devoid of wisdom or great purpose, but it is directly derived from the Majesty and Lofty Wisdom of the Almighty.

He said in a loud voice, heard clearly by all the attendees, caring nothing about any courtesies or formalities, for he cared only for Al’lah’s Satisfaction, and the glorifying of His Orders and High Statutes, ‘Oh doctor… oh doctor! A doctor does not graduate from a stable.’

A wave of shock and a deep silence fell over the guests like the silence that follows a rumbling earthquake. What… doctor… stable…! Oh… how terrible! But the brigadier general could find no reply.

By his words the great master, Mohammad Amin, meant that had a doctor not studied at universities, he would not have been a doctor, nor would he have received that distinguished certificate and notable position in society. So how can a man become good-hearted and well-intentioned if he does not communicate through prayer with Al’lah, the Source of all goodness, virtue, charity and perfection?

He continued, ‘The Almighty has not futilely ordered us to pray, for prayer, in its reality, is the close communication of the spirit with the Creator, and true prayer is like the highest school of all the schools of heart purity, in which the spirit is refined and polished. If man does not enter that school, he will not be pure of heart and noble of manners – which is what you meant by your speech – and he will not perform good deeds. And if that happens, it will surely be to achieve doubtful aims hidden within his spirit. How can he be a pure and good human being when his heart turns away from Al’lah? He does not communicate with his Provider to attain that mark with which He tints the prayers who communicate with Him; and who has a better mark than Al’lah?

‘The master of the creatures, the Envoy Mohammad (cpth), the most honourable man and possessor of the highest and noblest manners, was able to attain that rank when he surpassed all mankind in communicating with God in a true heart communication.

‘Prayer, in its reality, is the link between the spirit and the Great Creator, and its close connection with the Light of its Provider. It produces countless effects in the spirit of the prayer, which are greater than anything that can be expressed by the spoken or written word. It changes man’s morals and turns him into a man unlike any other man.

‘I shall illustrate this to your honour, by means of an example: if we say that chemistry converts stone into clear corundum, or coal into shining diamond, and copper into pure gold, know that this is nothing but a symbol and a sign. This is because true prayer, and true prayer alone, is that which alters the hard, cruel heart – that resembles stone in its thickness and density – to become like corundum in purity and clarity, and transforms the dark heart to become like a brilliant, glittering diamond. It changes all of man’s qualities and substitutes them with high character. Such is the Making of Al’lah Who disposes of all things in the perfect order.

‘Neither gold nor jewels are more valuable to the communicant human than what his heart (spirit) acquires of high morals, and gains of perfect qualities.

‘Our example for this are the noble companions who were the most unlearned of people, but when they established the way of true prayer, they became the best of people who were raised up for mankind, enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong and believing in God: as a result they raised the esteem of Arabs above that of all other nations.’

In the beginning, when the venerable master Mohammad Amin interrupted the doctor’s speech, all the attendees were amazed, and they paid great attention to the solemn master. A strange silence and great stillness prevailed in the place, except for that wonderful, solemn voice which captivated all minds.

All the guests listened carefully to his words, and admired them greatly because the astounding realities revealed to them and the high logic that they had not heard before, bewildered the mind. Mohammad Amin continued his speech saying, ‘Prayer is the true chemistry that changes man’s morals from one state to another, and the noble companions are true witnesses and examples of this. If you really communicate with God… with true communication… you shall have a light in your heart (spirit) which will be for you the strongest proof. You will then sense it in your very depth and realise the great change that has occurred in your character, that it has become pure and noble, with no impurities to blemish it. There will be no stinginess, no cowardice or envy, nor any other qualities that are unfit to describe man’s character.

There will be only purity, chastity, courage, generosity, nobility, sublimity, chivalry and honour.

‘And the more man advances in his prayer, and the strength of his communication with his Provider is consolidated, the more he will proceed in the fields of perfection; and I tell you that God’s Favour is limitless and endless.’

Mohammad Amin continued his constructive talk and superior guidance supported by factual examples in the form of stories, and all those present were surprised, captivated and content with that. He explained to them how to attain such true prayer and showed them the way that each man should follow in order to reach that level of prayer, and communicate truly with Al’lah. This was the way of our master, Abraham, that is, to think thoroughly about God’s Creation and the signs of the universe.

All the attendees listened to Mohammad Amin with a strange intensity, and the one who listened and understood his words most deeply was the brigadier general himself.

In his self, he dwindled before what he had heard of the sublime logic which revealed to him facts he had not known before, or ever expected to find. He discovered that Al’lah’s Orders are all of great purpose and they are not merely Orders about how to worship, yet they are all full of sublime wisdom, not known by most people in this temporary material world.

Suddenly, that eerie silence was interrupted by the voice of the host asking the guests to make their way to the table, for the food had been served and was waiting for them.

Among the guests, there was a beautiful and fascinating woman dressed in seductive Parisian clothing, and she had been the focus of attention prior to the speech of the virtuous master, Mohammad Amin. She was the wife of a well known, wealthy Syrian man who held a doctorate from France.

She was truly a woman of great beauty. She noticed the scholar’s modesty, and how he avoided looking at her. She also noticed his unparalleled boldness and heard his wonderful logic; all this was in addition to his handsomeness, singular sublimity and perfection. It was clear that she admired him greatly and so tried many times to attract his attention by her seductive gestures, but she failed. He took no notice of her existence at all for he was fully absorbed in correcting the doctor’s courtesy to his fellow guests, and clarifying Al’lah’s sublime Purpose in ordering us to pray.

At the dinner table, and by Godly Arrangement, the chairs of the venerable master and the doctor were side by side, and since the invitation was in honour of the doctor (the brigadier general) he was offered the best kinds of food and his plates were filled with the most delicious food, including various kinds of cooked meat, chicken and fish.

The guests began to partake of the delicious food and the virtuous master started to eat from the plate before him. As for Dr. Abdul-Kadir, he seemed very content and he greatly admired Mohammad Amin, so he said to the attendees, ‘Oh brethren! By God, all that this virtuous master has uttered is true. Though, initially, I was upset by his words, by God… by God… all that he has said is true and within the realm of contestable and blameless logic. I have previous knowledge of this honourable master, and I vouch that he fears no one and pays no attention to any accuser when defending the truth.’

Dr Abdul-Kadir continued to speak, thanking Mohammad Amin and praising him, and all during the meal he took tasty morsels of the excellent meat on his own plate and put it on the plate of the solemn master in order to honour him.

As for Mohammad Amin, he addressed him with words that were both extremely kind and warm, and so he had no choice but to eat what the doctor offered and adjured him to eat, wanting to placate the good doctor, since he felt obliged to make his speech in reply to the doctor’s courteous words. Meanwhile, the doctor’s great interest in the venerable master had not gone unnoticed by the other guests.

When they finished the meal, the virtuous master was sated and felt heavy and lethargic because of the great amount of rich food he had eaten.

After dinner, the host suggested that the doctor and the other guests should go to the al-Fijah Spring, to the source itself, as it was close by, and they all welcomed the suggestion.

The guests mingled and took a number of cabs to accommodate all of them. But that charming high class woman with her coquettish ways did not lose hope and was still trying to attract the attention of the virtuous master. He, however, did not look at her even once, which left her even more determined to achieve her goal.

She was truly infatuated by him and by his boldness and wonderful words: the way he could attract the minds of all the guests and turn their attention away from her. She therefore seized the opportunity and followed him directly to the same cab he entered, and took a seat very close to his.

The cab set off slowly, then accelerated towards the spring crossing the charming Barada valley with its captivating landscape, attractive sights and pleasant weather.

Her Parisian perfume pervaded the entire cab; all the passengers, except one, had their eyes fixed on her fascinating beauty and were unable to stop looking at her. But as for that chaste honourable master, once she mounted the cab and sat beside him, he, unaware of her existence, turned his back to her, choosing to face the window to observe the passing beauty of nature. She had failed to entice him yet again!!! She had hoped for just one glance from him…so that he would see her outstanding beauty that attracted the admiration of all men… except his! But his eyes did not swerve for a single moment, intentionally or otherwise! She could not believe what she had seen… but it was a fact.

This is the effect of true prayer on the heart. Its honour, sublimity, purity and chastity embellishes man just as the sun embellishes the infinite sky.

Half an hour passed as he maintained his position, while she was beside him and about to flare up with rage… she found him to be like a great mountain deep-rooted in chastity and honour… so how could she ever achieve her wish?

Many years later it happened that Al’lah willed that the beautiful woman should meet the wife of Mohammad Amin. when she knew her to be the wife of that virtuous master of whom she had never met the like before, she remembered the episode in all its detail, and related the entire episode to his wife: how he had captivated the hearts of all the guests with his high, logical words, and how she tried many times to draw his attention, but she had not succeeded in eliciting even a single glance from him. She also related how she sat beside him in the cab, but he turned his back on her. She continued, saying, ‘May Al’lah bless you with this chaste, honourable husband of high morals and noble character… in my life I have never seen a man of such high morals and sperior qualities. All of the other attendees were vile, they did not stop looking at me, but he alone was chaste and honourable.’

And so, let us return to the story: the passengers dismounted near the spring, and headed for the main entrance where the watchman stood to welcome them, but he apologized that he could not let them enter without informing the director of the al-Fijah Spring water department in Damascus. He phoned him and when the director knew of the arrival of those notables, possessors of high positions led by the brigadier general Dr Abdul-Kadir al-Zahra’, he said to him, ‘Woe unto you! Let them enter immediately, for my post and yours are in their hands. No one is allowed to enter except those dignitaries, especially the brigadier general.’

The watchman rushed off to attend to them with all humility, and there, through the sparkling, flowing, deep water, the bed of the spring appeared as if it was no more than a metre below the surface because of the extreme purity of the water, granted by the Hand of the Great God: one of His great Gifts to the people of al-Sham so that they might thank Him for the graces with which He endowed them.

The watchman set about distributing cups of water to all the attendees so that they might drink and enjoy fresh water from its source. The virtuous master drank many cups even though he still felt a heaviness in his stomach after the sumptuous meal, but the strange thing was that a few minutes after drinking the pure spring water, he felt a lightness, for the heaviness in his stomach had been dispersed.

That carbonated mineral water, drawn fresh from the spring, has an instant digestive effect which is gradually lost as the reaction of the beneficial gases dissipates.

After that, Mohammad Amin felt that he had regained his appetite and could eat once again if food was offered to him, as did all the other attendees.

So, dear reader, you see how great is Al’lah’s Mercy to mankind! He sent them cold, fresh water from the most remote parts of the world: the two icy polar regions, and offered them sweet water free from germs or harmful matter.

Thus, whoever seeks to satisfy the Creator by any deed, even though this act may displease people, Al’lah will be pleased with him. What is more, He will ensure that those people are also pleased with the person who performed that deed.

This is the real life, a life of honour and sublimity to God; otherwise, it is worth nothing.

chapters.title: The Quarrel between the Leaders of Two Districts Is Resolved
chapters.html:
God says, “If two parties among the believers have a quarrel, you should make peace between them.” ﴿201﴾

It was common for each district of Damascus to have a community leader to advise its residents on every matter, however great or small. This community leader should be characterised by his bravery, honour, knowledge and wisdom, amongst other such attributes appropriate to this position.

At that time, the merchants and notable people of the district were accustomed to meet at the coffee house to exchange opinions, advice, or simply to chat with one another in the evening.

One day, the boss of al-Salhiyeh quarter and his peer of the Sheikh Muhyiddin quarter were in a particular coffee house which they both used to frequent. They maintained good and friendly relations with each other, and each one had his entourage of companions who used to accompany him wherever he went.

But unfortunately, a quarrel flared up between them in the coffee house and the dispute intensified to the degree that both sides were issuing threats: the situation had become quite menacing.

The devil inflamed the intensity of the quarrel between them and inflated the arrogance and obstinacy in their minds so that neither of them would give in. The discord and dispute went beyond words to the point that it became violent. Both leaders were prepared for it as they were known for their inflexible attitudes; and as for the escorts of the two bosses, they were prepared to spring into action but could not intercede unless their bosses told them to do so.

The conflict and scuffle became more intense until one man stabbed the other… a severe thrust that resulted in him falling to the ground where he lay motionless, bleeding heavily. The moment that the perpetrator saw his opponent lying wounded on the floor, he took to his heels with his escort before he could be attacked by the men of the fallen boss intent on taken revenge for their injured leader, who had been rushed to the hospital. Here, for the reader to gain a full picture of the potential severity of the situation, it is important to state that each boss had more than 1500 men at his personal command, and should the problem escalate there was the potential for much bloodshed between the two groups.

The news of the incident soon became known and it was widely spread across Damascus that the two strong men had quarrelled and one of them was in a critical condition. Consequently, fear and terror spread throughout the community, the signs of which were to be seen clearly on people’s faces for they expected the situation to escalate and lead to a very unfavourable outcome. And yet, the only action which they took was to indulge in senseless talk which made the matter escalate to the extent that the two districts began to prepare themselves actively and took up arms for the awful, imminent fight.

As soon as the news reached him, Mohammad Amin rushed to the hospital to take precautions to avert the grave disaster before it could flare up between the two districts. The followers of the stabbed boss had put out the alert and called in more men and arms to attack the other district in order to avenge their boss. They were waiting to see if he would live or die; but in any case, whatever his fate, they had resolved to fight and take their revenge to restore the prestige of their stabbed leader.

Mohammad Amin, intent on avoiding terrible bloodshed, had gone to the hospital where he adhered to the injured boss as though he were his shadow, and began to take care of him. He surrounded him with sympathy by day and by night, like a tender mother, attending to his every need. He also made every effort to draw the doctors’ attention to the man, so that they would take the greatest care of him and offer him all the treatment he needed. Most of the man’s followers, and his family, noticed what was happening and appreciated our man’s favour and compassion. So, too, did the boss when he regained consciousness and was well enough to be aware of our man’s great kindness and support; he kept it in mind that Mohammad Amin insisted on keeping him company and never left his side even for a moment.

Within just a few days, the boss seemed well on the road to recovery and the doctors declared that he was now out of danger, so he was allowed to leave the hospital after the lifethreatening injury that had caused a lasting scar on his neck.

On the day that he left the hospital, no one knew anything about the plans and arrangements which this boss had decided on in order to take his revenge on his opponent, but Mohammad Amin forestalled him and put a stop to the “devil’s whispers” saying, ‘You’re my guest today!’ The boss was surprised at this but he could not refuse the invitation after the great care and extreme kindness so generously shown to him by Mohammad Amin when he was in dire need of both care and protection. So, the boss accepted the invitation gratefully and, as he felt indebted to our man, he accompanied him to his house. Yet the two districts were still on a state of full alert and readiness for the expected encounter as soon as their boss gave the word.

In his home, Mohammad Amin prepared all that was fitting for his guest, the head of a district, then he praised him, conversed with him and soothed him till he forgot about the recent shocking incident; and this outcome was entirely due to the cheerful and tender nature of our humane man.

In the interim, Mohammad Amin sent his eldest son, Fathi, to invite the other boss to his home but told Fathi not to tell him anything except, ‘My father has invited you to our house.’

Immediately, the youngster went off to summon the boss who was in hiding for fear that he might be killed. He had disappeared since the incident of the stabbing and no one knew of his whereabouts except our merciful man, his own family, and his loyal escort.

When the man who had carried out the stabbing arrived, Mohammad Amin welcomed him with due respect, and after he indulged and reassured him they proceeded to the room where his antagonist was sitting.

As soon as he entered the room he found himself face to face with his adversary. He stopped still, one might say rooted to the spot… his eyes wide open in wonder… unable to believe what he saw before him! Was it true, or was he dreaming? He shook his head, but quickly realised it was the truth, and that his antagonist was really in front of him. It was such a great surprise that it would never have entered anyone’s mind!

It was just as much of a shock to the other man already sitting there and they stared at each other in grave silence, like buzzards contemplating their prey. All the while, Mohammad Amin was watching them closely, his eyes full of compassion and mercy.

Meanwhile, the stabbed boss did not know what came over him. He was suddenly overwhelmed with intense feelings of goodwill, tolerance and mercy; all the spite and hatred were torn from his spirit, and his heart became calm. He found his heart aspiring to peace but did not know the source of all this growing tranquility.

At this point, he stood up and turned to Mohammad Amin saying, ‘Is this what you want, Bey?’ And suddenly he opened his hands towards his antagonist in a manner of conciliation, and approached him smiling. So the other boss, although truly amazed, responded to him in a like manner. They shook hands and embraced each other. It was truly a miracle that everything was back to normal between the two leaders ﴿202﴾

by virtue of this kind and generous man, Mohammad Amin Sheikho. Every long-held grudge and sense of bad feeling between them vanished and was replaced by rapport and friendliness. They opened their hearts to each other as if there had never been any quarrel!

After Mohammad Amin had finished entertaining them in the most generous and hospitable manner, he suggested that the process of reconciliation should be completed publicly for everyone to witness that all feelings of animosity between the two chiefs had now gone. He then walked out of the house between them, and all three were chatting and laughing in the most natural and friendly manner. Everyone outside saw this amazing sight! The impossible had happened! And they began to wonder if they were actually dreaming.

How strange and unusual! But how had this happened?

Everybody had been expecting a big fight to break out at any time. The threat of death had been hovering over thousands of anxious potential victims, but beyond all expectations the opposite had occurred! The three men continued walking towards the house of the boss who had been stabbed, where they entered the reception room. His family and supporters were waiting for him fully expecting to receive the order to avenge their boss for the knife attack, and they were fully prepared to shed blood!

But here he is in the company of his opponent and not a sign of enmity could be discerned between them: clearly everything is back to normal! Needless to say, everyone was startled, and absolute silence spread throughout the room. They sat for a while, and gradually everybody realised that the dispute between them had truly ended due to the intercession of the wise and generous man who arrived with them.

Life then returned to normal after the entire local population had been on full alert and fraught with alarm all during that period.

Mohammad Amin then escorted both chiefs to the other quarter to complete the process for the peaceful settlement of the dispute. They entered the guest house of the other chief and gathered there with his escort for all to witness the miraculous ending of the trouble and the amicable settling of the dispute. The dark pall and the potentially great danger which had befallen them since the quarrel had now come to an end in the most unexpected way: with the ending of the conflict life returned to its previous state of tranquil and peaceful normality. Thus, Mohammad Amin stopped the trouble and saved the inhabitants of the two districts from a terrible blood-bath, which would probably have been worse than anything seen in any of the counties of Damascus before, and he saved them from an awful aftermath which might have lasted for many years.

Truly, it was a wonder of wonders that life became peaceful once again without the shedding of a single drop of blood and thereby avoiding the horrible confrontation which would have occurred if Al’lah had not shown His Mercy to them at the hands of Mohammad Amin, the benevolent man whose prudence managed to save both sides from a potentially disastrous situation.

May Al’lah reward him with the best possible recompense for the people of Damascus.

chapters.title: The Prime Minister
chapters.html:
He had heard about transcendence and glory and that some soared up until they reached the sun, then the sun raised them higher still and acquainted them with Al’lah, the Only One, the Irresistible, so that they witnessed His Supreme Attributes.

The man of whom we speak was swayed by appearances, so he set about building a tall tower, placing stone upon stone, wishing to reach the sun so he could be lifted to the heavens. He sought glory and believed that he could obtain it by money or stones or gold. He wanted to achieve eminence but he did not believe it would come to him by giving up his worldly desires and abstaining from whatever was prohibited, and performing good and charitable deeds in their stead.

‘How can I become prestigious if I am not rich? Does belief or trouble provide me with power? And what about people? Will they respect me if I don’t have millions of liras? I believe in God’s Existence and I really do want to recognise Him, so I’m going to ascend the tower which I have built by myself and by my own wealth so that I may reach heaven.’

But, “That Home of the Hereafter We shall give to those who do not intend high-handedness or mischief on earth: and the end is the best for those who are illuminated by Al’lah’s Light.” ﴿203﴾

He set about emulating windmills, constantly moving, thinking that he would gain something. He did not realise that it is the wind that keeps windmills turning and he was following nothing but a will-o’-the-wisp.

Suddenly, he found himself beginning to sink into spiritual darkness. The lowly life unmasked its brutal reality before him, having previously been hidden behind a cheap, materialistic cover.

Today, for him, there is neither daylight nor lamp. The dream has disappeared as if in a puff of smoke, the money has become useless, the yearning is over, and he will never again be able to sit upon the minister’s chair.

All that awaits him now is a narrow place under the soil waiting to receive his mortal remains, whereupon it will be covered by stones, leaving him alone without light or air, and far removed from the people he sought to impress.

Why do people not learn lessons from death even though they see how it never fails to take away their friends and loved ones? The Prophet (cpth) told us a truth well known to him when he said, “Death is the best preacher.”

In fact, if we fail to think of death and not prepare ourselves for it, if we do not bear in mind that that day will certainly come and that every spirit will definitely taste death, it means that we have nothing good within our spirits. There is no good in a nation that fails to remember its dead.

One finds, these days, that most people do not like to hear about death; furthermore, when they are obliged to attend the funeral of a relative or friend they stay only for a few minutes, then as soon as the corpse is laid in the ground they endeavour to beat one another in their hurry to leave the graveyard, and give a deep sigh of relief once they are outside. As for the poor dead person, he remains alone, soon forgotten, and far from their hearts. There is nothing around him save darkness and loneliness, and it is no wonder, for the person who fails to recognise his Provider and to be near to Him, will find no companion and no provision in the Hereafter.

In this account, we are going to read about a man who supposedly lived a comfortable life, for he enjoyed all the pleasures and delights of this world and did his utmost to become prime minister. This dream stayed in his mind for many years, and since he insisted on achieving his goals and the desire to succeed fully occupied his spirit to the point that it reached its very core and penetrated to every last shunning molecule, God helped him to achieve it.

Had Al’lah the Almighty not fulfilled this man’s wordly desire, its germs would have engulfed his spirit and destroyed it completely. He would not have been able to forget it or to return to his Provider. But when the spirit achieves its purpose, the germ of that desire will gather in one place, which partially frees the field of the spirit. After that, the Almighty sends adversity and disease to that intractable man so that he may make use of them and turn towards his Lord. If he does so, Godly light will flow into his spirit and purify it, but if he does not, the germ of desire will remain attached to his spirit, gathered on one side. It will remain so until the moment of death where the torment of the grave or the flaming Fire on Doomsday will be a means for the purification of the spirit.

The man we are talking about had achieved his dream, but it was the last thing he enjoyed, for it was not long after that he was overcome by a serious illness as the ultimate warning from God before he departed from this life and his mortal body passed away.

Mohammad Amin Sheikho and the former prime minister were old friends, their friendship having sprung up when both were officers in the Turkish army. Thoughts of his friend came suddenly to mind, so quite unaware of why that should be, Mohammad Amin found himself walking towards his friend’s palace.

But on arrival he sensed that there was an air of misery and heartache prevailing over the palace. He saw the staff endeavouring to wear masks of happiness although they were clearly distressed. He failed to understand why he felt both annoyed and anguished when he entered that magnificent building. He greeted the doorkeepers and asked about his friend; they replied that he was crippled and bedridden in a room on the ground floor.

He was most surprised at this fact, not because His Excellency was ill, but because the owner of all that glory and wealth was sleeping on the ground floor which is normally reserved for the servants’ quarters! A servant led our man to his friend’s room, but even before he reached it, he could smell a bad odour emanating both from the room and from its occupier.

Oh my God! What misery!

Ah! Alas for men who have lost the two abodes, those of heaven and earth!

‘Eh, it’s you, my friend! Welcome!’ whispered the prime minister from his bed, as our man entered the room and saluted him. His voice seemed muffled, as though concealing strong feelings of embarrassment and contrition. He remained silent for a few minutes so as to control himself but he failed and began to cry copious amounts of tears: it seemed that every tear was like a firebrand that fell to his heart and caused it to bleed.

‘Oh my friend! If only I had listened to you when you spoke to me about death and the ugliness of this life! But I was just like a foolhardy child distracted by his toys, and here I am now on the verge of death.’

Mohammad Amin remembered that this man had taken a new, young wife. But this merciless woman had turned her back on him when he fell ill and became paralysed, whereupon she put him in that shabby room, employing a nurse to look after him. If she had not been afraid that people would blame her and have no respect for her, she would certainly have discarded him like a piece of old furniture.

She then indulged herself in all the luxuries of an extremely comfortable life and set about spending her husband’s wealth for her own enjoyment and amusement, along with his young sons, and all within the sight and hearing of her bed-ridden husband.

Mohammad Amin could hear sounds of merriment and dancing coming from a room on the upper floor. They were immersed in their own burning desires and blatantly disregarding all principles and feelings of others. They gave no consideration to that poor man who was crying and calling for his beloved wife, begging her to come to his room. She, however, did not care a scrap for her old bedridden husband who still thought of himself as a young man, nor did she give any thought to his condition. Moreover, she came down to express her aversion to him. She stood arms akimbo at the door of the room, gyrating her body, dressed in a shameful, dirty dress suitable only for a harlot, and from there she said to him, ‘Leave me alone!
