In your condition, what do you want from a lady? Have you got anything to entice me that may make me kindly disposed towards you? Here’s the nurse, if you need anything, you can ask her.’

She uttered those harsh words with such scorn as if she was talking to a sick servant or animal. She even expressed her loathing and lack of care with a dismissive movement of the palm of her hand as if she wanted to push him away from her, saying, ‘This is unbecoming of the lady’s prestige; you have nothing that appeals to this lady.’

The husband burst into tears, his heart broken, while she turned her back on him and headed off towards her den to continue the shameful practices which suited her inferior rank.

It was God’s Will which caused her to ignore her husband’s call, except during the visit of his friend Mohammad Amin! If that sick man had been of sound mind and had applied proper judgement, he would have made a conscious decision to escape from his terrible predicament, but failing to do this he continued to slip towards the lamentable end he eventually reached. But despite all that happened and despite the unfortunate circumstances he was living in, his heart was still attached to his young wife and he was constantly searching for her sympathy and care. He did not realise that she was the cause of his sickness, and that his suffering grew much greater because of his yearning for her. If only he could forget her and turn away from her and turn instead towards the Almighty God, he would have a chance to escape, and Al’lah would help him to be healed of all his diseases and cleansed of all his bodily and spiritual attachments.

Alas! There are many men who are like that prime minister. They come into this world knowing nothing and spend their entire lives in error then they feel as if they had never been given any assistance or provision. They fail to acquaint their spirits with the Almighty Al’lah.

After shedding copious amounts of tears, the premier became silent once again, his eyes focused on some point in the distance but saw nothing, and he began to think over his past actions in this world. He saw his evil deeds surrounding him and seeming to encircle his neck like heavy chains.

He was unable to sleep; but if he did manage to sleep for a moment or two, he soon woke up terror-stricken as if he had seen a ghost or witnessed a huge explosion. In his dreams he twisted and turned, trying to run away and forget, but there was no escape… the body had become incapable and the spirit was shackled by its own deeds and its distance from its Creator.

The memories began to gather in his mind leading him to reminisce about bygone times…

He had gone one day, by himself, to visit Mohammad Amin in his home. He knew the standing of our man in people’s hearts for he knew that after he had retired he dedicated himself whole-heartedly to teaching the truth and guiding people to Al’lah; so his circle of followers was a wide group of men who learned from him and appreciated him very highly.

Yet that was not the premier’s purpose when he went there. It was not his appreciation of, nor his love for, the people of truth, nor was it his search for the truth which drove him to that visit. He went there for personal gain and a request that was far removed from the interests and tendencies of Mohammad Amin. He wanted to use the position and popularity of our man for his own advantage.

At that time, he was standing for a seat in the country’s parliament, so to succeed and qualify for premiership he needed a majority vote.

‘So that’s why you have come here,’ our man said, ‘you want me to recommend you to my company so that they vote for you. Okay my friend! Do not worry, it’s a simple thing. By God’s Will, I will do as you ask.’

In return, the candidate offered his unstinting ability to carry out any request that our man might make should he become premier.

When it was the time for the lesson and all of Mohammad Amin’s followers were present in the assembly hall, he took his place in the hall and in the hearts of those present, as was usual, for him to offer them his guidance. Then he spoke to them about the candidate’s visit and his request. But he added, ‘It is not for us to expose a person’s faults or mention his bad qualities and manners except in two cases: firstly, in the case of engagement and marriage, for it concerns the fate of a woman honoured by God who has been deluded. Secondly: in the case of the presidency, as is our case now, for it does a disservice to the common good of the nation and the future of this country.

Accordingly, I declare to you that this man is a man with a past and he should not win the election. He is known to be a drinker, a liar and a sinner…’

He told them the facts about a particular aspect of the candidate’s shameful character and disgraceful manners, then he left them free to form their own opinions and come to their own decisions; but knowing these men as he did, he was sure that none of them would vote in favour of the candidate.

And he was right! Not one of them voted for this candidate since they took the pure and virtuous man, Mohammad Amin, as the best possible example for themselves.

Mohammad Amin recalled many memories while he was sitting beside the ailing premier, talking to him gently, surrounding him with love, tenderness and care. He wished he could find the way to his heart so that he might guide him to the way out of his terrible predicament, but unfortunately the man was totally preoccupied by thoughts of his wife and unable to forget her.

He remembered the day when an ostentatious limousine stopped before his house, then two men wearing expensive clothes got out, headed towards his house and knocked on the door. When he opened the door, they both bowed before him in a most courteous and civil manner then they told him that their master, the new prime minister, wanted Mohammad Amin to attend a reception being held to congratulate him on the occasion of his success and appointment to the high position.

Politely, our man asked them the name of the new prime minister who wanted him to attend this occasion. And he was most surprised when he heard who it was!

It was none other than his old friend who had visited him to ask for his help!

‘But how did he win?’ he asked.

‘He got the majority vote over all the other candidates, so the appointment was rightfully his.’

Our man bowed his head for a short while, thinking of what he had just heard; then he asked the two men to excuse him and he went to his room.

He had never cared for such positions for himself, or even attached any importance to these matters, so he was not surprised that one of his acquaintances had been appointed to a position of such high standing. However, what made him wonder, was how a man of such low manners was able to win!

He looked at the situation with his heart’s eye: then he looked further, and yet further still to encompass the greater picture, and he saw nations in decline having lost their defining characteristics, and nations moving towards the abyss until there was only a hair’s breadth between them and destruction, especially at that time when the Second World War was causing widespread devastation.

Truly, “Time is like its people and its people are as you see” and “As you are, so will be your ruler”. To elaborate on this, one could say that the events that occur during any period in time reflect the nature of the people: if they are bad they will be faced with disasters, and the opposite is true if they are good. Similarly, God will entrust good people to a good and benevolent ruler.

Our man put on an elegant white tie that reflected his appearance of the utmost magnificence and splendour, then he went out and got into the limousine, escorted by the two men, and was driven to the presidential palace.

The car passed through the wide, imposing portal of the palace heading for the splendid reception hall which was surrounded by a vast, luxuriant and well-arranged garden.

As the car came to a halt, one of the two men got out quickly, and showing great respect, he opened the rear door to let the noble guest alight.

Mohammad Amin got out of the limousine then ascended the steps of the palace accompanied by the two men, and walked towards the grand reception hall. The large doors stood open showing the hall crowded with guests who had come from all cities of the republic to congratulate the fortunate man who had risen to that high position and deserved to be the prime minister.

As for His Excellency, he was seated at the front of the room, talking freely in a grandiose manner and smoking his big wooden pipe, while all eyes were focused on him. But as soon as he saw our noble man step into the room displaying his customary matchless dignity and reverence, he rushed towards him and received him with a hearty welcome and led him to sit beside him, all the while repeating how happy and grateful he was that Mohammad Amin had accepted his invitation. He introduced him to the other guests and told them about the great favour that Mohammad Amin had shown towards him and his important role in the premier’s success.

The prime minister’s overwhelming reception of Mohammad Amin attracted the interest of all the other guests and caused them to turn towards our man with great respect and reverence. Those who were present to offer their congratulations began to wonder and ask one another about the man who exuded such a powerful personality. Why should he be the focus of the premier’s attention?

Mohammad Amin’s sole purpose in attending the reception was to admonish the people there. They heeded his words, and so his aim was achieved!

Such were the memories occupying Mohammad Amin’s mind while he was looking at the prime minister and comparing them with the sight he now saw before him: the prime minister lying in his bed, weak and humble, near to death. It brought to mind the sorry sight when, on the same illustrious occasion, the premier ran away from the hall, escaping from the mention of death in order not to let it muddy his joy.

This happened when the premier was recounting to his guests an incident that occurred as he was passing through Istanbul when he was a young man…

‘One day,’ he said, ‘I saw a tall, slender woman, strutting as she made her way along the streets of the city. She was going from one boutique to another to do some shopping.

So, I followed her until she turned into a narrow lane where nobody would see us.’

At that time, all women were supposed to be completely veiled when away from their homes. Every Moslem woman was obliged to cover herself from head to toe, and the law was strictly applied in the Turkish state whose success and superiority in the past was based on its strict abidance by the laws of the religions that adhered to God’s Statutes.

‘Then, I began to whistle softly to her,’ the prime minister continued, ‘so that I might attract her heart, and actually she turned towards me and uncovered her face! But what a great shock I got! That evil woman thought that she could draw my admiration and captivate my heart, so she unveiled her face, laughed, and said to me, “Have I caught your fancy?”

‘She was a negress with a wide mouth and thick red lips; and compared to the darkness of her skin, her teeth seemed snow-white.… then she poked out her red tongue in a seductive manner. When I saw her face, my desire vanished and I felt myself about to black out, so I spat on the ground and shouted at her, “Shame on you, you black woman! I have wasted two and a half hours of my time chasing you and you’re a negress.”’

He regretted the time he had wasted in following her, panting, priding himself on how clever he was.

But the truth is that he was a blind-hearted man. He distinguished between a black and a white person even though Islam makes no distinction between them except according to their level of piety and devotion to God.

This bad story appealed to those present so they began to laugh loudly, knowing nothing about how sordid it truly was.

There was only one man among them who could perceive the depth of the matter and because of his tender heart he could not remain silent. So, he seized the opportunity and raised his hand to stop the farce. He began to talk seriously, using forceful and effective words to show the ugliness of this world.

It was Mohammad Amin who said, ‘Such is this worldly life, my friend. We live in it seeking its material goods, ornaments and pleasures. We even compete with one another wishing to have the greatest share of wealth and enjoyment. We may sell out our principles and compassion for its sake, and give up our pledges and honour just to get a plaything that attracted our hearts and minds. But suddenly death knocks at our doors and snatches us one after the other, and then we will come face to face with a bitter and painful fact.

‘We shall then see that we have missed all that is of importance.

‘There will be no friends, no money, and not even any desires. There will be only a dark deed that follows us and clings to us like a shadow.

‘People are sleeping; when they die they will wake up.’

‘What? What do you say? Death?’… the premier said fearfully. ‘Please, my friend, please do not mention this word before me at this gathering. I do not want to hear it and I hope that you will not mention it ever again. I think I’ll faint if I hear any reference to death.’

Then he put the palm of his hand on the mouth of the honest man, Mohammad Amin, trying to prevent him from warning of death and the Day of Resurrection, yet our man removed it and continued his speech. When the premier failed to change the subject of Mohammad Amin’s speech, he could do nothing but run away from the hall leaving all the guests there; at that moment he cared nothing about the prestige of his new portfolio, while Mohammad Amin continued with his admonitions and illustration.

Since the premier was an old man his body had taken on the appearance of a large jar with a short neck and round puffy belly, so the sight of him running away was very amusing: in order not to hear about death he inadvertently made a comic spectacle of himself, which made all the guests laugh at him.

What a wonder! Did that premier think that he would live forever? Did he think that he could escape from death? Or perhaps he imagined that the day of death was as far from him as a star from the earth! The Almighty God says, “Wherever you are, death will find you, even if you are hiding in tall, fortified towers!” ﴿204﴾

So, after the storm of laughter and disparagement quietened down, Mohammad Amin returned to his speech about death, and they were all then prepared to listen to him carefully, and were affected deeply by his ensuing words.

Their spirits turned fully towards him because of the solemnity and dignity they felt emanating from him, especially when he did not respond to the prime minister who wanted him to change the subject into one that was pleasant for him.

How can he remain silent when he is fully aware of the consequences of following those desires and material things? How can he keep silent when he knows well that those who adopt a life of ease and pleasure are moving towards a dead end where darkness surrounds them and fills their spirits with rancour and delusion?

He cannot leave them to go astray without trying to help them and guide them towards the right path which would offer them peace and safety, and secure for them honour and bliss during their lifetime, and then after their death. He is not the one who refrains from doing good, nor does he lag in seeking God’s Satisfaction and serving His creatures.

Now let us return to His Excellency, the premier, so as to recognise his mental condition after he left the hall. We will see him regretting his behaviour which had caused him to lose some of his prestige and eminence. He thought about what had happened and saw the fault clear before his eyes. He found that his actions were foolish and imprudent, therefore he decided to return in order to apologise to his friend and to his guests.

So, he screwed up his courage and displayed firmness and dignity as he boldly entered the hall in order to regain the respect of those present. He sat in his chair then apologized to the noble guest, Mohammad Amin. He explained to him in the presence of all the other guests that he ran out without thinking because he feared death, and the mere mention of it upset him. He was so afraid that he felt goose flesh on his arms and his heart would beat rapidly whenever he had to drive by the graveyard and saw the myrtle which was usually placed on the graves. He would then spend the entire day in a bad mood and unable to sleep a wink all during the night.

‘There is nothing except my life here on this earth so I want to enjoy it to the full. I do not care about what may come after death, in fact I do not think that I will be resurrected. But what kind of fate shall I face if there is to be an account? I don’t want to think of that.’

And now is the end! The prime minister became incapable of enjoying any pleasure, and here he is lying on his bed like a mosquito that has sucked a surfeit of blood. The worldly life has turned its bright face away from him, only to replace it with the other face which is terrible and dark. Today all his deeds, all his possessions, even all his children are of no use to him.

It was not long until the physical body came to the end of its earthly purpose and the soul returned to its Creator, after a death struggle that lasted many days. Then, he came face to face with the truth,

‘Where am I? Who am I? How did I get here?’ His spirit seems strange and so does his body… the place is dark and horrible. There is no friend, nor lover, nor child nor wife, nor any other relative.

There are only chains and sins and deeds that cross the mind and fragment. Today, there is no escape: there is only a judgement of everlasting imprisonment with hard labour that he brought upon himself.

Mohammad Amin had stayed beside him for some time, trying faithfully to help him. He did all that he could in order not to let him depart this life in such a state.

He wished that he could touch the premier’s heart or draw his attention to him, his compassionate friend. He stayed there waiting, perhaps his eyes might meet with his or his heart turn away from its past, and then the premier’s escape would be possible. But alas, even the eyelids had surrendered to his shame, and there, on the forehead, the stain indicating the past and the present was drawn.

Thus, the last cord between the premier and life has been cut and the last glimmer of light has been extinguished. The foundations of that tower which he built on sand when he indulged in the hope of glory and immortality have cracked and its pillars have sunk down to the depths: its walls are now surrounded with darkness and the flames of hellfire. Now nothing will serve him: neither hope nor repentance; and nothing will bring him back: neither wealth nor servants.

God says, “The blind and the seeing are not alike: nor are the depths of darkness and the light; nor are the chilly shade and the genial heat; nor are the living and the dead. Al’lah makes him to hear who wills; but you cannot make those to hear who are indulged in whims.” ﴿205﴾

But in fact, the real death is the death of the spirit when it turns away from its Maker. It is not only the soul leaving the body, for life is but the life of the spirit: all of its deeds are attached to it and all gains return to it, and the results of the direction it takes will reflect on its surface. So, he who turns towards the Creator, the Living One Who does not die, and the Light which does not cease, his spirit will stay alive, overwhelmed by the lights and enjoying forever the Gardens of the Peerless Compassionate One.

chapters.title: The Magician and the Needle
chapters.html:
On the hills of Damascus lies a town that the Hand of Godly Potency has endowed with captivating beauty and all the most wondrous, beguiling charms and allure of nature.

It truly seduces the heart and fills the eye with its splendour. The weather is pleasant and clement, and the houses are surrounded by orchards, thickets, gardens, flowers and trees bearing luscious ripe fruits waiting to be plucked.

Such is the exquisite Artistry of Al’lah, Who has perfected everything. A playful breeze wafts gently around the branches, causing the leaves to quiver with the joy and passion and refreshment that come from the diffusion of the refreshing air. As night falls, all becomes enveloped in its soft, velvety darkness and a gentle silence spreads over the land.

At one time, an Arab-style house stood here, in the midst of farmland and orchards, and a gentle, welcoming light glowed constantly from its windows. Although this was the light of a solitary, simple lamp, nonetheless it contained a kind of tranquillity, a heart’s ease, and a strange spiritual purity, to welcome all who came to the house.

Inside this house, in one of the rooms in particular, an unusual calmness prevailed. It was infused with a purity and sublimity that never failed to overwhelm those who were present.

A charming, melodious voice could be heard sounding a tune, beautifying the stillness and sending forth an aura of purity and delicacy that was carried on the air. A number of visitors sat there listening with rapt attention. They had come to see their beloved eminent leader, and to hear his sublime interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, with which they were fully preoccupied, and which filled their hearts with bliss. These were the disciples of the great guide, Mohammad Amin Sheikho. One of these disciples had brought some guests with him, who had insisted that they must be taken to see this virtuous master whose noble qualities and profound words were the talk of people everywhere. So, it was that when Mohammad Amin had finished speaking, one of those guests – who had been affected by an event that had happened many times before his very eyes – said,

‘Oh, sir! I wish to talk to you about al-Gawi whom people regard as one of the people of God. He has a kind of supernatural power which enables him to know secret things. Oh, sir! What he does is, he asks one of his attendants to remove anything he likes from the room, even if it is as small as a needle, and to go and hide it out of sight, wherever he wants, without telling anyone where he has put it. Then, after he returns, al-Gawi goes out and in no more than a few minutes he comes back holding the very thing that was hidden! He is easily able to discover the hiding place and bring the item back, even if it has been buried in the earth. What a strange ability this al-Gawi has! Don’t you agree, sir? He has become widely known, and the news of the supernatural powers he displays has spread by word of mouth. So, sir, what’s your opinion about such exploits as these? And what position does he have himself? Surely somebody who does such things can be regarded as one of God’s people. Don’t you think so?’

With a gentle smile, the great guide answered him, ‘No, my son, he is not as you say. He is nothing but one of the devils’ people. He performs such actions by means of the devils with whom he has aligned himself. You could also say that he is now nothing but a tool for them. They use him to help them to achieve their aims and use their wicked cunning to work with simple-minded people.’

As a look of astonishment spread over his face, the same guest said, ‘So he’s really full of deceit… as cunning as a fox! And he claims that nobody can do such things without being one of God’s people and, what’s more, must hold a special rank with Him.’

The righteous master said, ‘My son! If his claims were true, the Envoy (cpth) or any of his noble companions would then be more deserving than him of having such supernatural powers.

‘Have you ever heard of the Envoy (cpth) doing such things? Is there any mention of the companions performing such deeds?

‘Listen, my son! Islam is a religion that depends on sound logic and a righteous mind. It is based on acclaimed facts and it is far removed from such foolish wonders. When the noble companions continued the advance of Islam and conquered many countries, they encouraged people’s hearts and minds to adopt this religion through their rationality, high logic and deep wisdom. They inspired people to cling to God’s Book and yearn to assimilate the religion in the same way that they yearn to smell the fragrance of the sweetest perfume. Through this religion they were able to clarify God’s Justice, Wisdom, Patience, Compassion and Grandeur to all of creation until all hearts prostrated themselves before His Majesty and His other Supreme Attributes.

‘As for miracles, they ceased after the age of our master Jesus (pth), for they served no real purpose.

‘In fact, people can gain no true belief unless they themselves seek to ascertain the Existence of God, and His Greatness and Kindness and all His other Attributes. They should ascertain this through their own process of thought and rationality, and by reflecting on God’s cosmic Signs, such as the sun, the moon and the stars.

‘Should men be impressed by a seeming miracle the effects will be short-lived and soon vanish; then people’s spirits will turn again to their depraved desires, and to oppression and aggression.

‘Consider the people of our master Saleh (pth)! Did they gain any advantage from the miracle of the she-camel? Certainly not! ﴿206﴾

‘They even deprived her of her young, which made them incur God’s Wrath. And there are many other examples, for God says, “Nothing prevents Us from giving signs, except that the ancients did not believe them. To Thamud, We gave the she-camel as a visible sign, yet they oppressed themselves with it.” ﴿207﴾

‘Anyhow, my son, you can bring this al-Gawi here and I shall demonstrate to you his lying and duplicity, as well as his worthlessness.’

A date was duly set for a meeting between al-Gawi and the great guide Mohammad Amin Sheikho. The meeting was to take place in the presence of the questioner, along with some of his companions who believed that they had witnessed great wonders and remarkable actions performed by al-Gawi.

On the appointed day, the meeting was held before a number of the disciples of Mohammad Amin, who welcomed his guests cordially.

However, when al-Gawi entered the place, he began to cast furtive glances at the great leader, looks that were both questioning and full of anxiety, and then cast his eyes down towards the floor. He continued to repeat this rather odd behaviour until they were ready to begin.

When everyone had taken their seat, the great guide, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, began the discussion by saying,

‘So, what have you decided?’ The questioner answered, saying, ‘Sir! This is al-Gawi. He has come to show us some of his strange marvels.’

‘Good! Then let him do whatever he likes,’ said Mohammad Amin.

The look on al-Gawi’s face was still rather strange, and added to this there had now appeared an expression of fear.

What a strange case this was! At first his face had carried a look of conceit and disdain, but at this moment signs of humility and inertia began to appear. He remained, as he was, silent for some time. His face paled but his eyes still seemed to be trying to focus on the great guide in a desultory and hostile way, but strangely they continually failed to do so.

By contrast, the face of the great guide was clear and radiant, His piercing gaze dispersed the darkness, just as the rays of the sun pierced the dense clouds. He seemed to be surrounded by signs of brilliance, dignity and beauty, as if he was bathing in the Light of his Provider, living in a constant state of passionate absorption in His Presence. A smile could be seen on his lips, expressing his faith in the Provider of the people.

Suddenly, al-Gawi broke his silence, saying, ‘Today I am unable to practise my work in the normal way because I feel worried and absent-minded, so I cannot show you my wonders unless the object is hidden by a female.’

Those present found this to be a very strange request. They were accustomed to seeing him perform these actions without specifying whether the person hiding the object was male or female. So what was wrong with him?! Why did he dare to make this odd request in front of the great guide?!

The dignified master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, then rose from his seat and went to his wife’s room. He entered, and said to her, ‘Um Fathi! I want you to take a needle and go to the end of our orchard. Go to the mulberry tree and hide the needle beneath it. Bury it in the soil, but do not forget to pinpoint its exact location with a marker, such as a piece of granite or white flint, so that I can find it later on.’

She said, ‘Yes, of course. I’ll go at once to do as you ask.’

Mohammad Amin continued, ‘But I want you to keep reciting the following Fortresses (Surahs) as you walk there and back: Oblivious Humankind, Oblivious Jinn-kind (al- Nas), All That’s Coming to Appearance (al-Falaq), Sincerity (al-Ikhlas), and the Opening (al-Fatiha).’

‘I’ll do exactly as you say.’

She took a needle from her room and went up to the orchard while her husband stood waiting for her to return.

She reached the far end of the farm and chose the tree under which she would hide the needle. Then she put a medium-sized piece of granite over the hiding place. According to her husband’s directions, she kept reciting the Qur’anic Fortresses until she returned to the house, where she found him waiting for her.

‘I have done as you asked,’ she said, and then told him where she had hidden the needle and described the marker under which he could find it.

‘Very good! God bless you!’ the kindly master said.

He returned to the room where his guests were waiting, and addressed al-Gawi saying, ‘Come on, al-Gawi! We have done as you asked.

Al-Gawi stood up and then went out to the orchard, followed by the rest of the group. He walked among the trees, and then stopped as if undecided which direction he should take. Those present found that his actions up to this point were not in line with what they knew about him previously.

It was not long before al-Gawi turned to them and said, ‘She hasn’t hidden anything.’

The master replied, ‘Come with me! I will show you where she has hidden a needle,’ and they all followed him to the hiding place. He stooped to the ground and removed the white flint, and then dug at the soil lightly with his finger until the needle appeared clearly to the eyes of those present.

Mohammad Amin picked it up, and turned towards the sorcerer saying, ‘So, what do you have to say about this?’

‘Let her do it again.’ said al-Gawi, ‘but this time, I want you to stay in the room with us until she returns.’

The venerable master smiled and said, ‘As you like. Let us go back to the house.’

Once again, they all entered the room except Mohammad Amin who went to ask his wife to hide the needle again, but in a different place that they both agreed on, and then he entered the room and stayed with the group. Despite this, al- Gawi was fated to face failure yet again.

They repeated the exercise a third time at al-Gawi’s request, but he fared no better than on the two previous occasions.

Thus, al-Gawi realised that if he had truly possessed hidden knowledge, he would not have failed to find the hidden object.

Therefore, he could only confess his failure, and so became humbled in the view of all those present. He had lost his prestige in their eyes, and especially in the view of the questioner, who had previously been greatly impressed by him to the extent that he had thought him one of God’s people. However, in reality, he was nothing but a magician, as the faithful guide Mohammad Amin Sheikho had said all along.

A magician can never thrive in the presence of a true believer that seeks power and refuge in his Provider and keeps Him wholeheartedly in his mind, as in the case of the great guide Mohammad Amin Sheikho. This is because the magician’s devilish consorts will be unable to approach a true believer, as light and fire cannot come together. When angels come, devils run away! God says, “He it is Who keeps communication with you, as do His angels, so that He may bring you out from the depths of darkness into light.” ﴿208﴾

One must always keep in mind that magicians can never have power over believers who have been illuminated by Al’lah’s Light.

chapters.title: A Wealthy Man Suffers for His Sin
chapters.html:
Once, the owner of al-Khuja Market in Damascus invited the elite of the religious scholars to a banquet. When they arrived, the generous young man welcomed them and received them with perfect hospitality. The table was prepared and many dishes of sumptious food were brought in; once his esteemed guests were seated he asked them to start eating, but they replied that they would not do so unless he shared it with them. The host excused himself saying that he could not eat normal food like them for his nourishment was restricted to liquids only. They insisted on his eating with them even if it was only one small morsel, but again he excused himself and explained to them that his reaction might disturb them if he were to eat solid food.

Because of their insistence he felt obliged to have a single mouthful, so he tried to chew the food and then to swallow it but he was unable to do so. His face became red and mottled and his voice quavered so that he seemed to be suffocating. He fell down, his body lying on the ground and jerking as he gasped for breath: it seemed that he was about to die.

Within half an hour, the young man had recovered completely and there was nothing to show for the unpleasant episode save the pallor of his face.

When the guests witnessed the plight of their host they were most upset and lost their appetite for the food set before them. Among those present was our venerable scholar, Mohammad Amin, who took the matter most seriously. He thought, ‘As far as I know, this young man is good-hearted, well-mannered and religious. He is charitable and is always prepared to do a favour. So, why did God, the Just, the Compassionate, send him this dire affliction? Definitely, he must have done something wrong for, “No disaster befalls you unless you have caused a disaster twice as great.” ﴿209﴾

Far be it from God to be unjust.’

When the young man recovered, he insisted that his guests should relax and eat their meal which, one must add, was delicious and extremely generous. So, when his guests had finished eating they thanked him for his kind hospitality and generosity, then they took their leave of him and left the house.

Apart from their initial reaction, not one of them cared for the awful affliction of the young man except Mohammad Amin who kept thinking of what had happened, and the reason why he was unable to eat solid food. He truly wanted to know what he had done to deserve such a punishment. For the noble verse plainly serves, “What does Al’lah gain by punishing you if you are grateful and you are a believer?” ﴿210﴾

Therefore, he befriended the young man for a long time during which he frequently tested his character and true nature. Every time he found him to be both honest and upright, so he became even more interested to discover the reason behind the problem; but it seemed that the young man’s secret was too deeply buried. He kept it to himself and did not disclose it; nevertheless, our man kept him company and did not desert him.

It took twelve years for the young man to be sure of the honesty and trustworthiness of our merciful man, and only then did he unburden himself and disclose his secret. He said to Mohammad Amin, ‘I want to tell you the reason for my affliction: my father was the owner of all the shops in al-Khuja Market. Although he was extremely wealthy, he was also very tightfisted, insomuch that he used to feed us nothing but bread. We begged him many times to provide for us those things that all fathers provide for their children but he refused, and in fact he became even stingier. He was ill-mannered and treated us badly. Our life became unbearable because of his evil nature. All my family, the old and the young alike, turned to God praying that He would save us from the hardship of living with him. One day, he suddenly fell quite ill and became bedridden, so the physicians decided to perform surgery on him. In fact, the surgeon decided to perform the operation at our house and had all the necessary equipment sent there. At a critical stage during the operation the doctor needed a particular instrument, but I had hidden it. He looked everywhere for it and shouted at us, but it was in vain.

During that time my father took his last breath and died.’

On hearing this, our great scholar understood the full implications of this serious matter and finally realised the reasons for the young man’s affliction, after twelve long years of research and investigation. He perceived that the Almighty God had rightly deprived him of his father’s estate because of this particular action.

Following this event, the man repented of the crime he had committed against his father. If he had borne his father with patience, his father would have left this earthly life even if the doctor had not been missing one of his instruments, for a man will die at his appointed time. It is not necessary for anyone to force this issue by killing him.

The virtuous scholar, Mohammad Amin, always had great faith in his Provider. He was certain that He is Just and Merciful towards all of His creatures, so He directs to man nothing but good and whatever helps him to save his spirit in this earthly world before he departs to the other world; thus any affliction that befalls a man is as a result of his own behaviour or wrongdoing. The law of justice is in effect amongst all creatures, for God says, “We did them no wrong, but they were accustomed to doing wrong to themselves.” ﴿211﴾

Our man became even more assured of the Fairness of God’s Actions when He sent a distressing affliction to the young man’s body so as to cure his spirit and to make him serve as a lesson for everybody that lusts after money and, in doing so, does away with his own sense of humanity.

However low and ignominious a man may be, his human value is higher in the Eyes of his Provider than anything that exists in this worldly life. So, when you strive against your errant brother, let your reason be simply to help him return to the right path and uplift him, and not be for the purpose of acquiring his money, or for any other vain ambition. And one should keep in mind that Al’lah helps him who helps his brother with benevolence and compassion.

The young man eventually became full of remorse because of what he had done to his father for the sake of money, and so he decided to adopt the ways of righteousness and obedience, and spent his father’s wealth in dispensing favours, helping the needy and helpless, and treating the people of religion, and its scholars, with great hospitality. No doubt, Al’lah the Almighty accepted his repentance because of his ensuing noble conduct, but as punishment for his spirit in this world He did not let him, personally, enjoy his father’s wealth.

Far be it from Al’lah, the Just, the Compassionate, to direct evil towards any one of His servants unless that is what His servant deserves.

“And nor is your Lord ever the least bit Unjust to His servants.” ﴿212﴾

chapters.title: The Young Housemaid
chapters.html:
Damascus, the aromatic garden, has always been a great source of inspiration for poets. They wrote and sang of the fresh sparkling waters of its river, of its pleasant climate, fresh, gentle breeze and its beautiful nature. Such was its beauty that they called it Al’lah’s Paradise on earth.

Our story took place many decades ago when the Bedouins who lived in its semi-desert region passed through difficult circumstances due to a year without rain; unfortunately, the ensuing drought brought about great poverty and some of them resorted to stealing.

During those years, Mohammad Amin Sheikho used to lease a house and its surrounding orchard in a rural area, and every summer he would leave Damascus with his family, and head for this pleasant summer home away from the hustle and bustle of the city. He used to spend the entire summer there relaxing with his family and enjoy eating fresh fruits directly from the trees of the orchard.

Qud’ssaya, is the name of this wondrous suburb and is the setting for this story…

Dear reader, let us spend a few hours with Mohammad Amin Sheikho in his lush orchard, where the many trees display an abundance of ripe fruits; the gentle breeze rustles the leaves, we become aware that it is the Justice of God that rules everything, and we sense the faithfulness of our man and his great care to attain God’s Satisfaction – (Glory to His Names).

It was a little before noon and Mohammad Amin was sitting on his wooden chair in front of the house, relaxing and enjoying the warm sunshine, hoping that it may relieve the stomach-ache which was troubling him. While immersed in his thoughts, he heard a low sound, so he turned towards the direction it came from and listened carefully. Within a few moments, a Bedouin woman appeared. She was tiptoeing towards the middle of the orchard seemingly intent on stealing some fruit because she was hungry. However, she failed to notice the owner of the field, Mohammad Amin, sitting by the house and she was startled when our virtuous man called out, ‘Hey, you, what are you doing there?’ When she heard his voice, she turned round and immediately ran off like a frightened rabbit leaving the orchard behind her.

When she was out of sight he remained silent for a while thinking about her circumstances. He thought to himself, ‘Perhaps she is hungry and has no other recourse and so her spirit is out of control. I think that the drought in the desert has caused the lack of food and is what has prompted her to steal fruit from the orchard.’ Wasting no time, he got to his feet and hurried towards the oven in the orchard on which there was a cooking pot filled with stuffed marrow. He took a piece of traditional flat bread from the kneading trough and folded several pieces of stuffed marrow inside it.

A little girl, about seven years old, stood a short distance away watching what her master was doing. Her parents had asked the honourable guide, Mohammad Amin, to employ her as a simple housemaid, and at the same time they wanted her to get a good spiritual education at his hands because of what they had heard about his impeccable noble character.

‘Come here… good girl… quickly,…’ Mohammad Amin called to her. She hurried forward and stopped before him.

He stretched out his hand holding the food and gave it to her saying, ‘A Bedouin woman has just gone that way; come on… good girl! Take this food and follow her. Hurry up and give it to her before she has the chance to leave.’

She took the food and ran in the direction which her master pointed to. She was soon back and smiling happily as she walked towards him.

‘Did you find her?’

‘Yes, I did, sir.’

‘Did you give her the food?’

‘Yes, she took it and quickly put all of the stuffed marrow inside the flat bread and folded it up, then began to eat it greedily like this…’

The child was standing before our noble man, demonstrating how the woman devoured the food… opening her mouth to bite the sandwich just as a ravenous beast might do… biting off mouthfuls of food, swallowing, and tossing its head.

Through the scene that the little girl was enacting, he understood just how hungry that poor Bedouin woman must be; and he thought, ‘How sad! She’s trembling with hunger! Perhaps the food I sent her isn’t enough.’ He rushed back to the oven and took two pieces of flat bread; he wrapped it around many pieces of stuffed marrow then he gave the food to the little girl saying, ‘Off you go! Take it to her as quickly as possible.’

She held it fast and ran quickly back to where she had left the Bedouin woman devouring the food. She gave the second meal to the woman, who took it and began to scoff it in the same voracious manner. This was what the little maid recounted to her master when he asked her whether she had found the woman or not, ‘Yes, I did,’ the girl answered, ‘and she ate it like this…’ again she imitated the woman’s manner of eating, shaking her head, demonstrating the woman’s great hunger.

Our man pondered the woman’s situation. He was concerned that she might have small children who would surely be as hungry as she was. He said to himself, ‘I think that she’s no longer hungry; but what about her children? What about the coming days?’ and he turned towards the little girl saying to her, ‘Come on, little one! Follow her quickly before she leaves the orchard otherwise we won’t be able to find her; and when you do find her tell her to stay where she is. Hurry up… good girl!’

The little maid set off once again to follow the Bedouin woman while our noble master hurried off to the house where he picked up ten Syrian pounds, ﴿213﴾

a substantial amount of money in those days. He thought, ‘This amount will provide food for her and her family for about two months or more.’ Then he returned to his seat in the orchard where he sat waiting for the little girl to return.

A long time passed, but the little maid had still not returned! Mohammad Amin was becoming most concerned that the poor woman might leave without getting the money and her family would stay hungry. Time passed as he sat in the orchard, his concern for the plight of the Bedouin woman growing by the minute, when eventually he saw the little girl ambling along in the distance, stopping to look at flowers or other distractions, chewing gum and blowing bubbles, seemingly without a care in the world.

He called her to hurry, ‘Where’s the woman?’ he asked, ‘did you stop her?’ ‘No,’ she replied in a cold, casual manner, ‘I didn’t.’

When he heard this, he was furious because of her coolness and indolence, so he cursed her father. ﴿214﴾

When the little girl heard him swearing about her father, she bowed her head, stopped chewing her gum, and her lower lip began to tremble. She was heartbroken. As for the noble master, he called his three sons to come to him at once; and barely a few minutes had passed before they were all standing in front of him awaiting his order. He put his hand into his pocket and brought out two notes, each one with a value of ten Syrian pounds. He gave one to the eldest son, Fathi, and one to the other two. He pointed towards the two roads leading to town and said to them, ‘You, Salah and Walid, go along this way; and you, Fathi, follow that one. When you find this Bedouin woman (and here he described her) give her the ten pounds then come back home quickly. Have you understood?’

‘Yes father, we’ll do as you ask,’ the three sons replied and darted off to carry out the task.

No more than fifteen minutes had passed when the three sons came back one after another, having found the woman and given her the money. They related to their father how she had taken the note and begun to touch it as if she couldn’t believe her eyes… she wanted to be sure that it was real and not a dream… she had become oblivious to everything around her. As soon as she was able to believe her good fortune she rushed off to her family overcome with relief and happiness.

When Mohammad Amin heard this he was so pleased and his heart felt at ease. But after a few minutes, he felt the pains of colic and diarrhea worsening, so he held his stomach and ran quickly towards the water closet, when suddenly a low-hanging branch struck his forehead. The impact was extremely painful, yet the griping pains in his stomach were rapidly become much more intense, so he ignored the pain of the blow and hurried towards the water closet as fast as possible.

But once there, and having found relief from the pains in his stomach, he began to wonder why he should have been struck by the branch, saying, ‘Oh my God! What have I done wrong? I fed the poor woman twice, and what’s more, I gave her enough money to provide food for her and her family for at least two months. So, why did the branch hit me?’

No sooner had he spoken these heartfelt words than he heard a call coming from within his heart, ‘What about that poor child? Why did you swear about her father and hurt her feelings? It’s true that you gave that poor woman enough food to satisfy her hunger, and it’s also true that you gave her enough money to provide for her family’s needs for two months or more. You will be rewarded for this, but what about that little girl, why did you break her heart?’ He replied secretly to the question, ‘Yes, I did that for the poor woman’, yet the voice answered, ‘The favour you have done for that woman will bring you the reward you are worthy of, but the act you have done towards the little girl brought you punishment.’

At that moment all became clear; he understood why the branch had struck his forehead. He washed his hands, and without further delay he went towards the little girl who had not moved, and spoke to her kindly, ‘Are you sad? Are you upset?’ (it is a characteristic of the Bedouins that they take to heart any swearword against their father). At this the little girl bowed her head down showing she was very sad and deeply affected by his words. Then Mohammad Amin said to her, ‘Now you can ask me for whatever you want and I will fulfil all of your wishes.’

As soon as she heard his words she felt happy and joyful.

Smiling again, she raised her head, and quickly listed her wishes, ‘A dress, a golden bracelet, and a pair of shoes.’

Immediately, Mohammad Amin called his son-in-law who soon answered him saying, ‘Yes, uncle, what can I do for you?’

‘I want you to go into Damascus at once to buy the following items for this girl: a dress, a golden bracelet and a pair of shoes. Off you go and take her with you.’

Being loath to go just then, the son-in-law answered, ‘But sir, it’s afternoon now, people usually go for a stroll at this time of the day… it’s the time to relax and enjoy oneself… and as the proverb says, “Go shopping in the morning, not in the evening.” So, tomorrow I will go and buy whatever she wants.’

‘No! Go right now,’ said Mohammad Amin, who was not only the younger man’s father-in-law but also his guide and teacher in religion. When the younger man saw his father-inlaw’s insistence on the matter, he unwillingly responded to his request and went to Damascus with the little girl where he bought for her a dress, a golden bracelet and a pair of shoes.

So, dear reader, take this story to heart and see what an important lesson one can learn from it! It is a true event that presents to us a clear example of how Godly Justice manifests itself in this universe among all of His creatures. It tells us that Al’lah never accepts oppression of any one of His creatures. He is displeased when somebody is wronged whilst favour and charity are being rendered to the poor or needy.

God is in every spot on this earth and if a man wrongs any single creature, anywhere, all his obeisance and worship will not prevent him from receiving the punishment he deserves for this wrongdoing. That is because Al’lah is Merciful to all His creatures.

So you, too, be merciful to them, and will also receive His Satisfaction. As for the charity you give dear reader, Al’lah will repay it to you in full, for there is a reward for every good deed and a punishment for every bad one. The maxim says, “Do as you would be done by.”

Whomsoever you may deal with, young or old, powerless man or weak woman, and whomsoever may be under your patronage and has less power than you have: beware not to oppress them or to wrong them, otherwise Al’lah will certainly empower against you someone who is stronger than you. So, “Judge not, that you be not judged.”

And praise be to God, at the beginning and at the end.

chapters.title: Do not Steal and It Will Be Given
chapters.html:
It was a moonless night, and darkness prevailed. Silence had spread its wings across the land… and the suspicion of lurking monsters created a kind of wonder.

The setting for this story is one of the farms in west Ghoutah (al-Hamah) where Mohammad Amin had leased an apple orchard in which was situated a beautiful rural house where he would spend the warm summer months.

At midnight, when total silence prevailed, our guide, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, sat contemplating the events of the day, thinking them over and planning his programme and arrangements for the following day as he had always been accustomed to do… until, eventually, sleep began to steal over him.

Suddenly, this tranquility was interrupted by the soft sounds of vague movements like the sound of dry leaves being rustled by a gentle breeze. It seemed that the sounds were coming from the farm so he listened attentively and the sounds became clearer.

He tiptoed into the orchard, where he moved lightly between the trees and followed the direction of the sound, and when he drew close to its source, he saw two ghostly shapes – their features hidden by the darkness – engrossed in picking the apples and putting them into a big sack that they held between them.

Giving no sign of his presence, Mohammad Amin returned to his house moving as lightly as the breeze, and picked up his pistol, which was always kept under his pillow; he quickly loaded it, and went back to where he had seen the thieves. He approached them stealthily and when they were in range he stopped and aimed his pistol at them with the customary accuracy and skill for which he was renowned, and then he fired. The bullet passed between them, and with the stillness of the night and deadly quiet of the universe the sound was magnified and they thought it was a cannonball; they were terrified and rushed off leaving everything behind them as if they were frightened donkeys fleeing from a fierce wild animal. They ran hard and fast, striding out so that their heels almost kicked their backsides. Then Mohammad Amin fired another bullet which just missed their heads, and they ran all the faster in their rush to escape.

When they reached the fence, the first one jumped over to the slope beyond but then lost his balance and slid all the way down it and, scrambling to his feet, he ran away. And when the second one jumped, his foot became caught in the struts of the fence, but his weight propelled him forwards, and he rolled down the slope unable to believe that he might escape; unfortunately for him every time his abdomen bumped on the ground, and because of the fear that the bullets had provoked in him, he released noxious body odours, which amused the spirit of Mohammad Amin, so he laughed out loud. He was delighted that he had provoked great fear in the hearts of the good-for nothings who would steal from him.

Then suddenly… Oh!… How terrible!

A glittering blade appeared above our man’s head… he thought that there was a third man with them whom he had failed to notice… so he bent down sharply and briskly jumped about one and a half metres backwards, and landed sitting on the ground… and the blade fell in the exact place he had just been standing: this movement was a tactic he had adopted when chasing after criminals and punishing them. And then, in the twinkling of an eye he grabbed his pistol and pointed it at the person he thought was attacking him, and at the precise moment that his hand squeezed the trigger, he saw the long hair of a woman on someone he thought to be a man; so in less than the blink of an eye he pointed the muzzle upwards and the bullet missed its mark with only a split second to spare… then he cried out, ‘Um Fathi!’

It was, indeed, his own wife; she was thunderstruck when she heard his voice and her legs buckled beneath her, for the supposed intruder was none other than her husband!

When she heard the sound of the first shot, she thought that criminals had already attacked her husband, so she hurried in the darkness to the farming implements leaning against the wall beside the orchard gate and grabbed an axe. She had then rushed towards the sound of the firing and brought the axe down towards the supposed intruder’s head, but he eluded the blow with that amazing leap.

What a moment! Whenever anyone thought about it his spirit trembled, praising God and thanking Him, and his heart would submit to Him for the extreme Mercy and great Care which He, the Almighty, deals to those who are truly obedient to Him. God saved both Mohammad Amin and his wife at precisely the same moment for His Care had intervened at exactly the right time… how Great You are my God – how Great You are! And how Great Your Power is!

After sunrise the following morning, Mohammad Amin found a huge sack half-filled with apples and another empty one at the spot where the incident had taken place. The tree from which the two robbers had been picking apples bore the finest and largest fruits and were the best in the orchard, indicating that the thieves had prior knowledge of the place before attempting to steal the fruit.

The following morning, the local mayor passed by the orchard of our great scholar and after greeting one another he said, ‘What’s the matter, Oh Bey? Yesterday we heard the sound of shooting coming from your house… what happened?’

Our man looked at him… it was quite clear from the expression on the mayor’s face that he knew the thieves, for the village was small and had few inhabitants, so it was obvious that they knew who might do such deeds… besides, some of them looked on such actions as a kind of rite of manhood and they prided themselves on recounting it to those who were of similar character and frequented the coffeehouses.

God says, “Nor did they forbid one another the iniquities which they committed: evil indeed were the deeds which they did.” ﴿215﴾

Our honest man turned to the mayor and said, ‘Yes… two men tried to steal apples from my orchard but they managed to escape under cover of darkness, otherwise I would have ended their wicked lives.’

The mayor was astonished and asked, ‘Would you kill two men for a few apples?’

Mohammad Amin replied strongly, bravely and firmly,

‘Yes… I’d kill them for stealing even one apple.’

The mayor felt a sense of awe and a strange reverence spread into his spirit such as one might feel when confronting a lion. He read indisputable signs of strength and determination in the character of the courageous man standing before him; thereafter this is what deterred him and the people of the village from committing such unlawful acts.

And, in fact, no-one dared even to approach the orchard after that event.

With this single act Mohammad Amin gave us a practical lesson on how to weed out an alarming social disease that might otherwise destroy the pillars of the community and degrade mankind. His mercy extended to the thieves themselves for he turned them away from the evil enclosed within their spirits. This, then, is something which reflects on the entire community, so that safety, peace and cordiality can prevail over all the land and criminals can turn to fruitful, honest work if they always find that there is someone who will stand up to them and deter them.

Some time later, this humane man offered more than half the fruit of the orchard as gifts to the mayor and people of the village for them to eat lawfully.

chapters.title: The Magician Is Thwarted in His Plans
chapters.html:
In a large room, a number of men sat gathered in a circle, listening to a soothing and pleasant discourse. Their faces displayed expressions of great pleasure and enjoyment, so one might think they appeared to have left behind this world and all its troubles and strife.

At the front of the room, sat a broad-shouldered man with a very pale face, but with rosy cheeks that served only to enhance his beauty. His charming green eyes shone with allure and liveliness. He appeared to have been encompassed by a great Godly Solemnity, and displayed signs of exceptional fortitude crowned with signs of compassion. His assembly was very open and untroubled and was enhanced by his imposing speech. He was reciting interpretations of the Holy Qur’an that were overwhelming the hearts of his disciples and uplifting them to endless, sublime paradises. At the end of the lesson, and after performing their prayers to God, the audience went one by one to address their guide, then respectfully began to take their leave of him. A few of them were still there when two of them approached him and one began to talk as the other nodded in agreement. The two men had recently joined this circle of the great guide. The man said, ‘Oh, sir! There is a man whose character we do not know very well at all. We suspect that he is one of the true men of Al’lah who have supernatural powers, although he is not Arab.’

He peered at them, saying, ‘Who is he? What do you mean?’ The new disciple said, ‘Oh, sir!

This news is being passed around by word of mouth. People are talking constantly about a foreigner that has come to Damascus and established himself in the main square of al-Marjah. He has opened a shop there and has started receiving people who ask him questions about many things. It is said that he can give you the answer to anything you may wish to ask him about.

‘The odd thing, sir, is that he asks his visitors, whoever they are, to keep their questions secret, and not tell anyone what they are. He then takes out a white piece of paper, which is totally blank, folds it and places it inside a book lying on the table before the visitor. Then he excuses himself and goes to his private room for a few minutes. After that he comes out and retrieving the piece of paper he opens it to disclose that there is now written the question or wish that is hidden inside his visitor’s spirit, as well as the reply to the query. All of that costs one golden lira, sir!’

The eminent guide, Mohammad Amin Sheikho said, ‘What? What are you saying, my son?! He is nothing more than a human devil who is dealing with evil djinns.’

The speaker replied, backed up by his companion, ‘But his deeds are really amazing and strange. Sir! Do you know that, once, a man who had decided to drill a well in the region he came from, went into this shop. He kept his idea to himself and spoke of it to no-one. So, when the foreigner drew out the paper, his answer appeared on it, written in beautiful Arabic script. It stated, “Drill deeply, and you shall succeed”.’

The other man added, ‘Yes, sir! We have seen this with our very own eyes! But what a disappointment the advice turned out to be! Although the man dug deeply and burdened himself with huge expenses, eventually the digger reached bedrock, and not a single drop of water trickled out!’

The first man then added, ‘Another man came to him, keeping secret his wish to travel to a foreign country to engage in trade there. He wanted to know whether or not he would prosper in this course of action. So, when the foreigner drew out the paper, he found a clear reply written there that said, “Travel, and you shall prosper!” – and there are many other men, sir, who have come seeking answers to their questions. What’s more, if the person who came to him was not Arab, but of a different nationality, he would find the paper written in his own language, and that is the wonder of wonders! By God, this person surely has a strange, secret gift – doesn’t he, sir?!’

Mohammad Amin laughed and said, ‘Haven’t I already told you, my sons, that all of his deeds are achieved by means of devils? And he is a human devil. He performs such deeds with the help of the blind associates of the djinn who help the likes of him. Haven’t you heard of Al’lah’s Saying in His Holy Qur’an, “And that there were men of mankind sought the help of men of djinn, but they added them nothing other than more strain.” ﴿216﴾

‘Indeed my sons, his actions are those of a magician who will never prosper whatever he does. There is nothing unusual about him, because he has withdrawn from Al’lah and his heart has turned away from Him. He has shunned his Creator to the extent that he, himself, has willingly become a devil, adhered to the devils of the djinn. They have used him to serve their evil purposes of harming creation and turning the beings of creation away from Al’lah. With such deeds he aspires only to two things: one of them is money; the second, that is worse, is to make people turn away from their love and appreciation of God, so as to make them glorify him instead. He makes them turn their spirits towards him, and admire his deeds; but meanwhile he is far from Al’lah and his spirit is in torment. Through his distance from God and through people’s directing themselves towards him – appreciating his deeds and apparent wonders – he enables devils to creep into them. As a result, these people are at risk of having spiritual and psychic diseases inflicted upon them, and so they withdraw from their Provider and mistrust Him.

‘That is, they hold serious doubts about Him just like this sorcerer does. Thus, they forfeit everything, and their spirits fall into darkness and turn away from Al’lah. This is what he seeks, which is the same thing that is sought by the failure, Satan, and is his ultimate purpose. Because of his envy and the grudges he bears, the loser always tries to bring others down along with him.

‘Through the story of our master Adam (pth) and the original Satan, we can glean a warning and a lesson so that we become well aware of his enmity. Then we can avoid being deceived by Satan. It shows that the one you are speaking about is none other than an enchanter who transmits what is concealed by humanity by means of his own and others’ maleficent djinn associates; that is, by means of the devils.

‘Had man resorted to his Provider and fully sought refuge in Him, this sorcerer would not have been able to deceive you into thinking him to be one of Al’lah’s righteous men.

‘So do not be deceived by this trickery, my sons. The sign of God’s true men is that they draw our attention, our thoughts and appreciation to our Creator, the One Who is Gracious and Obliging for all creation: it is He Who provides food, drink, and life. They direct our spirits towards Him through thinking of creation and of the Almighty’s Miracles, such as the sun, the moon, the stars, clouds, rain, plants and trees, and all of the countless other gifts with which He supports us. Then they appreciate Him as they appreciate His Benevolence to them in providing for them, and consequently, they turn to Him with feelings of love. This is their sign. They never ascribe any action to themselves at all, nor do they direct people anywhere other than towards God and His Envoy (cpth). They do not practise acts which are forbidden and in contravention of cogent thought and sound logic. These are nothing but occult matters that turn people away and alienate them from the right process of thought and sound judgement.’

With his distinguished and rational words, the noble master continued to gently admonish these two disciples who had newly attached themselves to him. At the end of his speech, he turned to the questioner and said, ‘In any case, tomorrow we shall go to see him together. What do you think of that, my sons?’

Eager and curious to know the outcome, they both said, ‘An excellent idea! Whatever you say, sir!’

The next day, the two men accompanied the great master to the supposed “master of wonders and oddities.” They reached the place where this foreigner had established himself in a large shop inside which there was a small room.

Mohammad Amin entered first, with his two followers close behind.

The sorcerer was sitting on a chair near an Arab man, undoubtedly a translator employed by the former to help him to perform his acts. The translator rose to his feet and said, ‘Welcome… come in, please.’ The foreigner glanced at the venerable master with brief, shifty glances, and then cast his eyes elsewhere as though the sight of Mohammad Amin displeased or unnerved him. He turned his attention to his translator, requesting him to ask his visitors what they wanted. When he found out that they were going to keep the subject to themselves as usual, he asked the translator to tell the master to think of something and share the thought with no-one.

The virtuous master did so, and then said to the translator, ‘I have thought of something… I’m ready.’ And then he placed a golden lira on the table. The enchanter brought out a white sheet of paper and took care to show the spectators that it was completely blank. Then, he folded it in the middle and put it inside a book that was on the table near them. He quickly entered his small room and shut the door behind him. As usual, only a few minutes passed before he came out, but now there was something rather strange about him! He had gone into the room in a very sprightly manner, but when he came out he appeared to be stressed and exhausted, contrary to his usual manner.

He took the folded paper from the book which had remained in place on the table and when he unfolded it, the colour of his face took on a greyish tinge. The paper was still white and blank, which was totally different from the usual situation after he emerged from his room.

The two questioners looked at the paper and saw that there was nothing written there, and their surprise was clearly visible on their faces. They turned their gaze towards the dull-faced man, regarding him with a questioning look, and not knowing what to think. But when they looked at their eminent guide, they noticed that a dignified expression of confidence and tranquility had appeared on his face. He was standing there as normal, displaying his usual proud posture.

As for the translator, he was looking about himself hesitantly, sometimes at the foreigner and sometimes at Mohammad Amin. The foreigner remained silent for a short time and continued to look steadily at the blank page, nervously biting at his lower lip. He seemed to be rather confused. A few minutes passed… silence prevailed. The only interaction between them consisted of mutual, questioning glances which expressed nothing but an enigma, as it emanated from the language of the spirit. Suddenly, the foreigner turned and spoke to the translator who, in turn, addressed Mohammad Amin, saying,

‘You did not think of a secret question!’

Mohammad Amin said with a smile, ‘Tell him that I did!’

Then, the man returned the sheet of paper to its place, just as it was, then turned and rapidly went back into his small room. The great guide turned to his two disciples, talking to them in a sublime and noble fashion about Al’lah’s Majesty which fully attract people’s hearts. A quarter of an hour passed, which made the translator look at his watch in astonishment, as he had not been accustomed to such delays from this “master of marvels” in the past. This was the first time he had stayed in his room for such a long time in order to disclose a secret. After about twenty minutes, the sorcerer came out of the room looking sweaty and exhausted. He was frowning and sullen, as if he had just been weeping over his bad luck on that unfortunate day. He approached the group with heavy steps, and stood with his head bowed before our dignified master, and unfolded the paper. Once again, the paper was spotless… and blank! The translator and the two disciples looked at it with an air of amazement, with many questions seemingly written on their faces. As for the foreigner, the misery on his face appeared to be aggravated and he became gloomier still. He turned to the imperturbable master – whose face was still bright, luminous and clear – and he said to Mohammad Amin through his translator,

‘No! No! You definitely did not think of a secret question.’

The generous master said to the translator, ‘Tell him that yes, I did.’

The foreigner replied through the translator, ‘If he has really done so, let him secretly and privately tell you what he has thought of, out of my earshot. Also tell him that you will stay close to him and will not come near me.’

When the noble master was told of this request, he smiled and said, ‘As he likes!’ and then crossed to the translator in two short steps, and the latter drew close to Mohammad Amin who whispered to him what he had intended as his secret question, saying, ‘I want him to inform me about Mohammad ibn Abdullah: communication with Al’lah and peace are through him.’

During this exchange, the “master of wonders” was standing away from them, but was minutely scrutinizing them with his black eyes and closely observing the situation. After the information had been passed on, he signalled to the translator, asking if he had been told the secret thought. The latter indicated that he had. The enchanter then returned to his room and shut the door. He stayed there even longer than the previous time, in fact nearly half an hour had passed before he reappeared. Then, when at last he came out, he looked almost as though he had been given a severe beating, to the point that he appeared weak and extremely listless. He was sweating and staggering around, as if unable to bear the weight of his own body. When he opened the folded sheet, he found that it was just the same as it had been. Nothing had changed… it was still white and blank! He remained silent a little longer, thinking about the problem of his failure that day, and then he seemed to realise the cause. He knew that, in the words of the saying, there were still some “sentinels who had never been neglectful of foxes”. Truly, he was most surprised and deeply shocked by this fact. His expectations had been smashed. He had been thinking that this country no longer believed in the true faith, and that, therefore, he would meet no barrier in spreading his corruption. But unfortunately for him, he had been frustrated in his aim.

The virtuous master turned and said to the translator, ‘Tell him that his devil can never approach our pure and honourable Prophet, Master Mohammad (cpth). If he had tried to do that, he would have been burned by his Godly Light.’ After remaining speechless for a while, the sorcerer turned to his audience and told his translator to inform those present that his usual ability and spiritual status were not functioning that day, but if they were to return the next day, they would have their questions answered. Here, Mohammad Amin smiled and said to his two companions, ‘You will not find him here tomorrow, for he will certainly abscond.’ Then he took back his golden lira and put it in his pocket. By the following day, the magician had fled from Syria and gone back to his own country, disappointed and despondent. He had been planning to resume his tour throughout all the provinces of the country of Syria, from Homs to Hama to Aleppo, but had been thwarted in this dishonest ambition by Mohammad Amin Sheikho.

chapters.title: Almsgiving Can Work Miracles
chapters.html:
It’s neither a far-fetched tale, nor a myth! The following tells of a true incident.

A story told truthfully and honestly, without exaggeration or imagination, serves as a lesson for all, and has no aim other than spreading goodwill, love and guidance by Al’lah’s Will.

The Grandeur of God and His great Love for mankind is the main theme of what we are about to relate.

Al’lah’s Mercy upon His servants entails that He never lets them indulge and wallow in the mire of their cheap worldly desires believing that pleasure and comfort are to be found only in this lowly world and its temporary pleasures. So, the Almighty brings upon us whatever is necessary to caution us against the outcome of our own evil deeds which will be as a raging storm rooting us out from this world whether we wish it or not, and will then cast us into the abyss. Undoubtedly, the Almighty showered us with a multitude of gifts when He created the earth and all that it contains: its seas, mountains and rivers, the sky and its planets and celestial bodies; and besides all that, He gave us the ability to hear and see, and the mind to live and enjoy all this, on one condition: that is that we should adore no-one and nothing and thus forget the Creator! Truly, this lowly world was not created simply for man’s pleasure, but was called into being as a means by which man should be led to Al’lah.

Then, he who discerns the cause of his own trouble, which is certainly incumbent upon his deeds, must know that it is inflicted because of Al’lah’s Mercy, so, he praises, thanks, and turns to Him in repentance and prays humbly for relief and the end of his suffering and pain. The Almighty says, addressing His noble Envoy Mohammad (cpth), “When My servants ask you about Me, I am indeed close to them. I respond to the prayer of every supplicant when he calls on me, but let them first, willingly, respond to My Call, and believe in Me: that they may walk in the right way.” ﴿217﴾

As soon as man repents his past sins, God will certainly comfort him and cure him of whatever ails him: thus, He will open a channel through which he can become acquainted with Al’lah’s Perfections and Supreme Attributes.

As long as man is sincere and truthful in wanting to be reinstated on his proper path and then remains loyal to the pledge he made to Al’lah that he should renounce his aggression and remain close to his Provider, Al’lah will surely help him, and turn his affliction into good health and his distress into well-being. Yet, if our turning back to Him proves to be of a merely temporary nature, whereby our personal benefit comes to predominate over our love for Al’lah and a true desire to return to Him and obey His Orders, then our affliction shall be like a curse upon us, and our distress shall be like fire upon our hearts. Should this be the case, Al’lah would never remove His Temptations from us and we shall remain lost and confused in darkness until our time of death, when it would cast us into further and deeper suffering. God says, “The day that the wrong-doer gnaws at his own hands, he will say, ‘Oh! I wish that I had taken a straight path with the Envoy.” ﴿218﴾

This story carries important messages for whoever seeks redemption: by learning from its lesson, and becoming enlightened, it gives us the greatest proof of God’s Assertion of His grand Omnipotence and wise Will when He afflicts us with relatively slight hardship, disease and torture, in order to spare us the terrible evil of the greatest torture that we will suffer if we persist in our infidelity and rejection of the sources of His Light and Purity.

Saleem Bey was a man of noble Arabic (Hashimi) origin and was born in Damascus to a wealthy high-bred family. It was God’s Will that this man should have a brother, our humane master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho! The two brothers lived and grew up together in the same home. Their father died and God determined, according to the wishes of the elder brother, Saleem, that he would travel to Turkey, where he settled in the city of Istanbul.

Eventually, he married the daughter of the then foreign minister of the Ottoman Empire. Of course, this wife was suitable for him and his prestigious political and social position, as he held the rank of general in one of the Turkish military divisions.

Through his rank and, later, his commercial undertakings, Saleem Bey was able to amass great wealth thinking that it would give him security against humiliation and changing times. As he thought then, and as most people still think today, money can solve any problem.
