As the years passed, Saleem became ever more materialistic and attached to money and possessions, but as we shall learn, something unexpected occurred!

He became ill! A debilitating illness crept into his joints and his limbs began to weaken and lose their ability to move or to feel. Soon, he became almost paralysed throughout one side of his body, a condition known as hemiplegia, and this intensified to such an extent that it seemed as though he might become bedridden, and, no doubt, human nature being what it is, he might soon have been forgotten by all except his close loved ones.

It was then that Saleem knew his health had deteriorated to a critical level, so he sent for many doctors, but it was in vain, as they all held a unanimous opinion on the outcome!

‘So, you don’t have any remedy for me! You can’t even stop this accursed disease from spreading throughout my body?’

‘Unfortunately, no! We have no medicine for this affliction and we can only suppose that your days are numbered. You may have no more than fifteen days and during this time you may become paralysed and confined to bed. May Al’lah preserve you and lessen your pain.’

At this moment, the patient sank down to the lowest depths of sorrow and despair… and lay in his bed with many thoughts running through his mind.

‘I have spent my life looking for fortune, and when I got it, it was never truly mine nor did I make good use of it… and here I am about to depart this world and leave it all behind! Oh, my brother! Where are you now? Something in my heart is calling me to you! I must tell you that I’m ill… I must write to you. I wish I could travel and return to the land of my forefathers… to my mother, my history… my childhood… to you, my dear brother in Damascus…

‘I want nothing more from this inferior world for it offers false promises! And as for money… it should be incinerated and thrown into the depths of the sea… I don’t want it if it can’t help me. I have desperate feelings of loss and homesickness, loneliness, and a yearning for the past… so many memories following one after the other before my very eyes… I cannot sleep for my eyes will not close, fearing death, my unknown fate, and that the darkness of the grave will suffocate me!

‘Oh my Provider! How can I escape from all that? My God! I admit my weakness and undeniable need for You, so, will You please release me?’

His conscience was in turmoil, although those around him did not notice. And he realised how much he needed to see his brother and the urgency of writing to him, informing him of his illness, and asking for his advice respecting his assets and making arrangements for who should inherit them. ‘How much should I bequeath to whom? Who should inherit my personal property?… I know that I’m not long for this world.’

The telegram carrying the sad news was sent without delay and when Mohammad Amin read it and learnt of Saleem’s illness, he was deeply saddened by his brother’s predicament; he realised too that his brother was showing great repentance for past deeds and his life which had been spent as though on a train carrying him from one stop to another in this world, until he suddenly found himself reaching the final station and his inevitable departure from the train, leaving behind the family, the money, and all the memories, to go to an unknown world in which only those who have been illuminated by Al’lah’s Light will live happily.

However, our man always hoped for the best outcome, and he had great confidence in God. He was sure of Al’lah’s Omnipotence to cure and restore his brother’s health and grant him a happy and healthy life on condition that he should understand that the real reason for his present distress was Al’lah’s Compassion, for He says, “It is possible that you dislike a thing though it is good for you.” ﴿219﴾

This was a final great chance to change his ways and habits and spend his fortune as God decreed and which would cause him to draw closer to His Presence, and ensure that he would become enlightened by His Light.

‘There’s no time to waste! Every passing day will be against the interests of my dear brother. I must reply immediately.’ So, he sent him a telegram calling upon that which is more important than money, inheritance and bequests, and his answer contained the following, ‘In the Name of God, the All-Compassionate, the All- Merciful.

Dear brother Saleem, may Al’lah preserve you.

‘I’ve received your letter, in which I’ve read many things.

I’ve read of your longing for your home and family, your sorrow and regret, and all of your inner confusion.

‘I know that you are in a bad way but I want you to be totally confident that Al’lah is Merciful and Fair, and He is Omnipotent in all matters. Wouldn’t He Who first created you and provided abundantly for you be able to cure and rebuild you again? Surely, as it is He Who inflicts all disease, He alone can lift it. But this will depend on you and the decision must be yours.

‘I recommend one important thing to you, which will be your way to escape from this predicament and draw near to Al’lah! It’s almsgiving, my dear brother, purely and simply!

‘Since that is our great Messenger’s advice for us, it is good advice for you too. And all who read this account.

‘Our noble Envoy said, “Help your patients to be cured by almsgiving.”

‘You have to give alms, Saleem! For this will ensure your retreat from ill health and achievement of happiness both here and in the hereafter; by Al’lah’s Will, you’ll recover your health and resume your journey through this life by Al’lah’s Light and Care, if you really wish to, and all that is up to your own free will and determination, of course. I call your attention to an important point, that is: the donation must be in proportion to the financial resources of the almsgiver. I know that you have a large, valuable plot of land in the centre of Istanbul, and I advise you to build a large complex there consisting of a basement, stores and offices, and above these there should be flats, in three sizes and designed as follows:

One bedroom, living room, and facilities, to suit a man who is debilitated, for instance.

Two bedrooms, living room and facilities for a medium sized family.

Three bedrooms, living room, and facilities for a big family.

You should then rent out the basement, the stores and all the offices except one: this you retain and employ a manager to control the entire property from there, and give him the responsibility for calculating the revenues of the project. This income should then be distributed on a regular basis amongst those whom you house in these flats, and to other poor families, orphans and needy, helpless people according to each one’s needs, so they have the means to live at a basic level.’

He ended his telegram full of hope and prayer to God that it may be well received by Saleem, and that he might reply positively, and apply this advice promptly, after establishing a true and meaningful undertaking between himself and his Provider.

Saleem’s condition worsened and his sorrowful sighs increased, tearing into the depths of his heart and bringing him nothing but further sadness, pain, and hopelessness. But when our man’s telegram arrived it caused a flash of hope to light up inside him, which he had not dreamed of.

He perceived a gleam of hope rising from it, so he clung to it. And yet he lingered a little, wondering, ‘Alms? I’ve never heard of a thing called “Alms” that can cure an incurable disease like mine! I don’t care about the land, I no longer aspire to money or possessions, but if medicine has been unable to cure or help me, how will almsgiving restore my health? Oh, my Provider! Is this true?’

While he was in that state of pondering and contemplation, he dozed and dreamed that his brother came and greeted him. Mohammad Amin sat beside him talking to him and showing him great sympathy; he interrupted his loneliness and answered the questions that came to his mind. He explained to him the wisdom concealed within almsgiving and the Greatness of God, and His Potency and Mercy, as he clarified to him the reason for all disease, and the only remedy for every disease whatever it may be.

‘Yes, dear brother, it is almsgiving and nothing else. It is the only way that can bring you closer to God. By giving alms the spirit becomes sure that Al’lah is pleased with it due to the good deed it has rendered; therefore, it does not hesitate to draw near to Him, and by its nearness and ascension towards its Creator, it becomes cured of all ailments and imperfections which have attached themselves to it in this world; and when the spirit regains its health, its cure will be reflected in the body which is like a mirror that reflects the state of the human spirit.

‘Dear Saleem! Al’lah is Near and He is always ready to answer your request, but we should be believers and observe His Orders when asking Him for favours; remain close to Him and be grateful for His Benefits for He is Al’lah, the Peerless, the Owner of all perfection Who hears all and answers all. He is the Truth and the best Disposer of affairs. If we surrender to Him and put our trust in Him, He will arrange all that we need, for He owns and controls everything. So, turn to Him wholeheartedly, dear brother! Pray to Him and ask Him for whatever you want, then place in His Hands any offering that you like, so that He may bring you near to Him and overwhelm you: begin with when you were a single drop of semen that was formed in a man’s body by a mixture of many different kinds of food and fruit, and then turned into an embryo inside your mother’s belly. Ask yourself, who put you in her belly? Who created you and then provided everything for you until you became such a wonderful creation? Who guided you to her breasts which contained delicious, nutritious milk in quantities that were appropriate to your age? Contemplate the phases you have passed through: how you turned from a child to a youth and then to a grown man! Think of all of that: think of the sun and the moon, the heaven, the day and the night! Who created all of that?

‘It is Him, my brother! It is Al’lah.’

At that point, Saleem awoke as though from a long dream with tears flowing from his eyes. And as came to his senses after experiencing this vision and reading the words of his brother, he pondered upon both of them. He sensed the truth of his words, and believed what he said. He was overjoyed to see his brother and to hear such wise words from him. He felt as if something new had been created inside his spirit; and indeed it had: it was a great love for Al’lah and His Prophet which he had never known before.

Without further delay, he called his two sons, ‘Come on, my sons! I want you to send for the civil engineers and the contractors; we need those who are experts in complex buildings… I must recover; I must start out as I mean to carry on! I do not want to die in such a state.’

He was truly enthusiastic and sincere, and far be it from God to close the doors of His Mercy before anyone that prays to Him in distress, since he sacrifices what he likes for His Sake. The noble saying denotes, “No man may become a believer unless he sacrifices something that he likes.”

Indeed, he carried out his brother’s recommendation to the letter. He fully understood the juncture he had just passed through in his life, and the gravity of the coming stage which would require faithfulness, firm decisions and persistence. He knew he had to be resolute in his commitment to the construction of a considerable building on his valuable land to provide homes and income for needy and helpless people. He would offer this as a deed dedicated to God, alone, so that he might become cured of his physical and spiritual diseases which came as a result of his love for this lowly world and which had worsened because of his remoteness from God.

Having fulfilled his brother’s advice, he began to monitor himself and await the results; but in this he was not alone for Mohammad Amin was with his brother wholeheartedly, anxious, and about to lose his patience.

‘Oh my God!’ General Saleem soliloquized, ‘Could this truly happen? Will God actually cure me of this affliction which His Wisdom inflicted upon me? I really feel better; I feel that there is something flowing in my veins: something that has touched my senses and is inspiring me to stand, to walk and to return; but to where? ‘Shall I return to the same old way of life that I followed?

Shall I return to the primrose path, the life of ease and pleasure, that I was following and that might end in calamity? Shall I return to my negligent ways? To my oppression and ungratefulness? Shall I forget Al’lah once again? Shall I deny His Favour and Charity? May I return once again to my disregard and indifference? What good will my health and wellbeing bring me then?

‘No! By God I do not want to regain my health… not at all! I do not even wish for it if it enables me to go back to my old way: a cold and dark path on which every step would drive me further towards that terrible abode which I will have chosen by my own free will, and by my work and shunning; only then will I witness the truth, and the selfreproach will begin, “Oh my God! How did I come to be here? Was I deaf? Was I blind to let my feet carry me here?” At that time, I would find no shelter except a flaming fire which will be a treatment for my spirit to be cured from its defects and low diseases!

‘No! No!… And no again! Oh my God! I ask for Your Pardon! Please God, forgive me! Oh God, please, I’m a servant standing at Your Doors, wishing to obtain Your Mercy and Love. Oh God! My spirit has become filled with love for this world, so please, would You cleanse it by Your pure Water and Light?

‘Oh my Provider! I beg You to answer my call and not reject me. Oh my Lord! I promise that I will perform the communication with You through Your Prophet as long as I live, and I shall ensure that my wife puts on a veil.’

Indeed, it was not long before he felt himself growing gradually better, and with this he became more truthful and persisted in his truthfulness. He invoked God for many long nights; he cried and asked for His Forgiveness, as he offered up what he liked to become nearer to God so that He might accept him and forgive him.

And so he would pass the spiritual test; he could seize his final opportunity before the doors of his life were shut, when leaves would fall to the ground as the soul will have gone up to heaven and the body will have decomposed under the ground. At that moment, unless he repented, the spirit would be wandering and full of regret; it would have no place to settle, neither on earth nor in the sky.

It would live forever in the depths of darkness, loneliness and fear. There, its laments would ring out, breaking the silence, shaking the pillars and waking the dead who will say, ‘Oh our Lord! Send us back so that we may perform the communication with You and prostrate ourselves to You.’ But how far! How far it would be! For by then, our years will have been spent and death will have overtaken us.

As for Saleem, he considered all that he wanted to save himself from, the woes and evils of that day, so he prepared himself and cast off all the shackles from his spirit. So, his lifeblood began to flow, his nerves were revived, bones regained their strength, and his heart beat with joy… and finally, the smile on his face expressed his overwhelming happiness. There were, too, fervent expressions of pleasure; and the bright rays of the sun heralded a new morning, while beautiful spring flowers bloomed after a long winter, adding to the feeling of joy. Indeed, the Grand God overwhelmed Saleem with His Compassion, Tenderness and great Care as He bestowed pleasure and bliss upon him and planted the seeds of virtue and goodness in his spirit, in addition to a great desire to escape a regrettable end. All combined to reflect on his body which soon recovered and became full of life. His happiness was complete when he was able to go on foot to the land on which the charitable project would be constructed; here he laid the foundation stone for the building which would give shelter to tens of needy and helpless people and ensure an easy life for them so that they might forget the times of hunger and need.

He regained his health and went on to live his new life as the Almighty wanted him to live. But of course, he would not forget his brother’s favour and the important role he had played in his recovery from diseases that had inflicted his spirit even before his body. He would not stop performing the communication with God, and, too, he would ask his modern wife to veil her face and wear religious clothes; happy that her husband had been restored to good health she complied willingly.

As for our man, Mohammad Amin, the great happiness he felt could not be matched either on earth or in heaven, especially when he saw a picture of his brother which was enclosed with a letter sent by Saleem where he wrote about what had happened to him: the trials and tribulations he had passed through, until he was ultimately restored to health.

Saleem explained that, ‘The commemorative picture was taken while I was laying the foundation stone by myself’… and it is still kept in the house of Mohammad Amin, (May God grant him more sublimation and nearness to His Honour).

In fact, Saleem rendered an exceptional deed when he sacrificed something that was dear to him to prove his truthfulness in wishing to gain God’s Satisfaction and Forgiveness, and to regain his physical and spiritual health, although he was quite sure that Al’lah has no need of us. On the contrary, we are in need of Him, for as it states in the Holy Qur’an, the Almighty says, “Whatever of good you give benefits your own spirits.” ﴿220﴾

The giving of alms is not to give money for Al’lah to add to His Treasures, but it is an expression of our truthfulness and our faith so that if we then follow the straight path with no deviation we will certainly believe that there is no god except Al’lah, for this statement means that there is no doer and no steerer except Al’lah and He is the sole Owner of power and Possessor of all. So, if you are honest and truthful in your intention and your direction towards God, He will fulfill your call and improve your situation.

After recovering from that affliction, Saleem Bey lived for more than fifteen years.

He watched over the construction of the large building and over the allocation of the homes it contained among the poor people and securing their financial assistance. During those years, he was very active, enjoyed excellent good health, and lived a far happier life than he had ever lived before.

chapters.title: A Miraculous Feat of Strength
chapters.html:
The Almighty God says in the Holy Qur’an, “They give preference to others, even though they are in need themselves.” ﴿221﴾

The heat of the midday sun had gradually lessened during the afternoon; it was now early evening and a welcome breeze had sprung up. The great master – who was about sixty years old at the time – was still in his room on the upper floor of the house where he had spent a relaxing, contemplative afternoon. His room adjoined a corridor which led to the main door of his Arab-style house. Um Fathi, his wife, had begun to clean the passage when suddenly she heard a knock at the door.

She called out to her husband, ‘Abu Fathi, there’s someone knocking at the door!’

The august master stood up and went to open the main door, while his wife remained standing nearby behind the door of the guest room. He stood at the door looking at the visitor, and realised it was someone he had ever seen before.

The man standing there before him addressed Mohammad Amin hesitantly, as though certain matters weighed heavily on his mind… but it was his impoverished condition and obvious dire need which had compelled him to ask for help. As the wise master looked at the man God revealed to him, within an instant, the true extent of his need and suffering: the profound misery and despondency which arise from poverty and lack of income was displayed clearly on the stranger’s face.

The Almighty says, “You will recognise them by the obvious signs: they do not trouble people by begging from them.” ﴿222﴾

Those people deserve to receive all possible assistance. The light of this master’s heart and his nearness to Al’lah granted him the vision to be fully aware of the reality, so we are given a warning from the Tradition of the Prophet, “Be cautious of the believer’s insight, as he sees by God’s Light.”

Mohammad Amin hurried to help the man in his time of need and raise him out of his state of deprivation and penury, but there was no help to be found in his pocket as there were only a few coins: this amount could never satisfy Mohammad Amin’s customary levels of kindness and generosity. Furthermore, it would do little to alter the obvious desperate condition of the pauper standing before him, or even allay his hunger temporarily. An idea came to him, so he emptied his pocket of every last coin and gave the money to the wretched man standing before him, saying in a gentle voice laced with extreme mercy and kindness, ‘Please take this money and go to bring a pack animal here to my house, while I bring a sack of wheat to help feed your family to prevent them from starving to death.’

The desperate man accepted the money gladly: the master’s gentle words were like water to a thirsty, wilted plant and he seemed rejuvenated as he grabbed the coins and rushed away from the house. His helplessness and weakness had suddenly turned into strength and vigour and he hurried away to return with a donkey to carry the promised sack of wheat.

In as much as Mohammad Amin’s words were soothing and comforting to the heart of that wretched man they came as a hard shock to his wife!

She could hear her husband’s words as she was close by tending to the garden and watering the plants and flowers. She could not believe her ears! She stood dumbfounded, unable to concentrate on the task at hand, and even stopped breathing for a few moments, as she remembered what effort had gone into cleaning the wheat. It had taken her three whole days of exhausting, back-breaking toil to clean that sack of wheat which weighed nearly 120 kilograms. For not only did it need cleaning but it then had to be spread out to dry in the courtyard, and afterwards she had put it with her own hands into this large sack to be ready for grinding. And now, with a mere knock at the door, it would be given away and all her hard work would have been in vain.

‘Oh, please,’ she thought, ‘let him take whatever he wants but not this sack of wheat… No! I have worked so hard… I’ve given my heart and soul to the task of preparing it… I’ve sweated like a labourer for three whole days.’ A few moments passed as she pondered this predicament, then she snapped out of her reverie and thought about what should happen now.

With great determination, she rushed down to the ground floor where the sack of wheat was lying in the store room. A few moments later, Mohammad Amin entered the room heading for the sack of wheat. When she saw him her suspicions were confirmed and she was overcome with fury which had settled deep in her heart, and expressed itself in her strong reaction to his decision which had affected her so strongly. She was determined to stand her ground beside the sack of wheat and face up to her husband displaying her tough, steely will. Then, she said in a tone of voice that registered her strong disapproval of his actions, ‘Abu Fathi take anything you want for him except that sack of wheat!! Upon my blood… upon my soul…’ She was so upset that it seemed she would not allow this sack to leave the house even if she sacrificed her life for it. Yet when the humane, merciful and generous master saw her determination and objection to his carrying out this good deed, his innate sense of goodness became aroused to the point that he was even more determined to carry out his good deed; he cared for nothing around him, and would not be thwarted by any emotion however intense it might be.

He was more determined than ever to carry out the humane deed of releasing that miserable man from his poverty and deprivation which would ensure God’s Satisfaction with him, Mohammad Amin. So, he lost no more time and dashed off immediately to put his thoughts into action.

But how was he going to pick up this heavy weight? He bent over the sack, put both arms around it, and undeterred by the enormous weight he stood up with new found strength, denoting the compassion, generosity, zeal, and love for rendering good and magnificent deeds, that were enfolded within his spirit.

He drew up to his full height hugging the large, weighty sack close to his chest. But what was this? It is virtually impossible for any man, however strong he might be, to carry such a load in this way: normally it would have to be carried on a man’s back.

Incredible! This man was almost sixty years old and he was hoisting a 120 kilogram sack of wheat, a feat that even the strongest champions would find difficult to achieve.

What kind of steady will and extreme resolution prevailed over this man’s superhuman physical state, giving it the strength to carry out this heroic performance? The picture was quite remarkable, but true!

That amazing sight had really startled and overwhelmed his wife so her determination was swallowed up in an instant, as a drop of water is consumed by the sea, thus weakening her intention and scattering her determination in every direction. She knew for certain that there was no way to deter her husband: the deed would be done even if it cost her blood… soul… life… for how could she stand firm before the unleashed forces of a stormy sea?

Mohammad Amin was rushing forwards carrying a sack which weighed 120 kilograms, and if she tried to stop him she would surely be knocked down and crushed to death under the combined weight of the sack of flour and her husband. So, she retreated slowly and stood with her back against the wall… amazed, astounded, and silent… she realised that her outburst had served no purpose, so she calmed down. Still hugging the weighty sack, Mohammad Amin went up the first three steps, then walked a few paces on the landing before climbing ten more steps till he reached the open door of the house.

He staggered out to the road where he put the sack down in front of the door, as the beggar appeared approaching the house, followed by a drover leading his donkey; when he arrived they both lifted the sack on to the back of the animal, making sure that it was properly balanced. The pauper then departed after offering heartfelt words of thanks and saying goodbye to the kindest, most open-handed man he had ever met during his life. The generous, pure master returned to his room feeling extremely happy after carrying out that heroic performance in applying Al’lah’s Command, and not giving way to the discontent that had been expressed by his wife. Al’lah’s Satisfaction and the importance of charity had been uppermost in his mind. He was amazed that he had been able to lift up the immensely heavy sack with relative ease and climb thirteen steps carrying such a weight!!

Sometime after this incident, when money became available, Mohammad Amin bought another sack of wheat to replace the one that had been given away, and fortunately for Um Fathi this wheat had already been cleaned and dried.

Mohammad Amin went to lift it as he had lifted the previous sack but failed to lift it off the floor… in fact he could not move it at all!

With what kind of love for good, and zeal for attaining God’s Satisfaction, had his pure and honest spirit been endowed to enable him to achieve that incredible feat?

Truly this super power is the fruit of the truthfulness and desire of Mohammad Amin’s spirit to achieve the Approval of Al’lah the Great, Who says, “The righteous will surely drink from a cup mixed with overwhelming delight. A spring from which Al’lah’s servants will drink their fill, causing it to gush forth abundantly. They fulfil the vow; and they fear a Day of widespread woes. They willingly give food, for the love of Him, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive,” and when they do this they say to themselves, “We feed you only for the Sake of God; we seek neither recompense nor thanks from you.” ﴿223﴾

Truly, that faithful man enriched the earth with deeds of glory and sublimity, the veracity of which has been proved by his miraculous performances.

In his presence blessings always prevailed!

chapters.title: The Wisdom behind the Marriage Contract
chapters.html:
A venerable manner with a proud, defensive posture of pride which he displayed in defence of Al’lah’s Law and Wisdom: such were his disposition and principles which demonstrated his great zeal and support for his belief and which he employed to fend off the accusations aimed at contesting God’s predominant Religion.

The true guide, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, was born in the al-Ward section in the Sarouja quarter in Damascus. He lived there until he was eighteen years old when he moved to another section in al-Muhajireen quarter which stands on the slope of Mount Qasiyun in Damascus. When he left the al- Ward section he left behind the imprint of so many wonderful memories and a great number of friends and loved ones. Days, months and years followed in quick succession until forty years had passed during which he assumed the mission of guidance as his heart’s eye was opened and his spirit was illuminated by God’s Light, so that he became an eternal eminent scholar whom Al’lah endowed with great knowledge and wisdom. Therefore, a great circle of people assembled around him and he invited them to Al’lah with certainty, showing them the way of believing in God and how to communicate with Him, the Almighty.

As already mentioned, when he left Sarouja quarter (al- Ward section), he left behind many dear friends, amongst whom was Abu al-Yeser Abdeen. In the old neighborhood a strong, long-lasting friendship had developed between them. This friend was one of the important men of religion and a medical professor in his time. He was appointed to the post of General Mufti of Syria, apart from holding the post of medical professor.

Student physicians could not graduate unless they passed the final examination which he, himself, set for them. It is an extremely exacting exam, unlike any other. He asked the questions, and if anyone answered his question wrongly, the professor did not allow him to pass the exam as the souls of people are entrusted to their hands. Therefore, the aspiring physicians should be astute in medical matters and worthy of assuming this serious position and great responsibility.

So, as we see, this man carried the burden of the two weighty tasks simultaneously: he read a lot of religious books and was extremely interested in this field. As a young man, he regularly attended the sessions of sheikhs (religious scholars) and followed their lessons; when he grew up he, too, became a sheikh and studied the religion assiduously until eventually he assumed the post of General Mufti of Syria.

One day, our venerable scholar went to his old house, and whilst there he was happy to visit his old friend, Abu al-Yeser Abdeen. When he entered the professor’s house he found some medical students questioning him about religious matters, ‘Professor… Islam made marriage conditional upon a certain regulation and without this contract no marriage can be finalised and consummated: in fact, Islam considers such marriage as fornication, so what is the actual function of this contract? And what purpose does this written marriage contract serve in Islam? If the man and woman love and desire one other and each of them wants the other to be his or her partner, why do they need a written contract? And is it of such importance that marriage is considered adultery without it? It is nothing more than a piece of paper… and how can a piece of paper have any bearing on the subject?’

Professor Abu al-Yesser was astonished at these strange questions and, clearly agitated, he said, ‘No… no… it’s not allowed… it’s forbidden… it’s apostasy… what are you saying? Of course it’s necessary, my sons… yes… yes… this document is necessary, otherwise it will be adultery and not a legalised marriage.’

When they heard his reply they persisted with their question as he had avoided answering it or refuting it with evidence. They repeated, ‘But if they truly love one another… what purpose will the document serve? We think that Islam is upholding a useless regulation.’

The good sheikh became even more upset and zealous in defence of his religion, and he cried loudly, ‘No… no… I don’t want to hear any more talk of disbelief and banned topics… without this contract marriage is prohibited… the devil has taken control of you today and cloaked you in the garment of disbelief… he’s imposed his own wrongful ideas upon you… I ask Al’lah’s Forgiveness… I ask Al’lah’s Forgiveness… there is no might or power except by God.’

But unfortunately, his outburst served only to increase the students’ laughter and jibes, and they repeated their questions, concluding, ‘It’s simply a piece of paper which means nothing and serves no purpose!’ Then they burst out laughing, as they directed their looks and words of mockery at the professor… ‘Tell us: should it be a special type of paper? Or is there a secret contained within it?’

The hapless but honourable sheikh became more and more angry and no longer knew what to do but heap abuse upon them in a vain attempt to stop the farce.

In their view, they saw that there was no wisdom nor any use in that Godly Legislation; the head of all the sheikhs stood before them but even he was unable to answer them, so, receiving no conclusive reply, they persisted in repeating their question in the hearing of the good sheikh, using sarcastic words, and mocking Islam and its laws because they considered it out of line with this advanced age. They insisted that there is no wisdom behind its laws, nor any benefits folded within its legislation… it is nothing more than a set of worthless principles and of no relevance in this mighty civilisation and the worldly sciences which depend on logic and proof.

Those thoughts settled in their minds and prevented their hearts from discerning the truth, especially when they found no-one to stand up to them and refute their thoughts with logic, and cogent evidence.

Therefore, they accused Islam of futility and ineffectiveness. If they really wanted to know the truth, they would have asked their question politely and would not be uncouth and disrespectful to the good sheikh when they knew that he had no compelling explanation. But they were determined to accuse Islam of inadequacy and shortcomings, and that it promoted superstitions and fanaticism with its useless precepts.

But Al’lah refused to let them continue to stray in their darkness and wrong themselves, so He directed the venerable scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho to go to them.

He went to the home of his old friend and neighbour to greet him, and there he found him broken-hearted because of the shocking way the young men had spoken to him. They had questioned him in a derogatory manner, aiming to enrage him, but the good man answered within the limits of his knowledge which failed to satisfy them or stop their mockery. Mohammad Amin saw what was happening and heard the on-going talk: as always, his heart was inflamed with his zeal and love for Islam, and being outraged at finding his friend in such a state, he went to his defence. He said to him, ‘Excuse me! Would you please let me answer their question?’

‘Of course… willingly!’ replied the good sheikh.

The group of young physicians turned towards him, and when they saw his air of gravity and peerless awe, a strange feeling crept into their spirits, stopping their laughter and mockery in their tracks, and they turned to listen to him attentively.

The eminent guide seemed genuinely interested in speaking to them: there was great truthfulness glowing in his eyes revealed by his great passion for Islam and Al’lah. This supreme affection and delicate sensitivity were accompanied by boundless mercy for that misguided group of young men who were in great need of guidance to help them out of the depths to which they had sunk. Mohammad Amin’s reasoning was that if they saw the sublime facts of the Islamic religion they might turn to it, abide by its laws, and be saved from unsparing punishment.

The virtuous guide said, ‘Let us suppose that the young man became fond of the beautiful young woman and they fell in love… let us then suppose that we refused this document and they practised love without it, and had children. Then, what would happen if the infatuated man died suddenly? Who would support his sons and daughters and that sad broken-hearted woman after her lover had departed this life having deflowered her and abandoned her without insurance, leaving her poverty-stricken, humiliated and debased? What about the fate of the fatherless children? Undoubtedly, the inheritors and the family of the departed young man would come and cast them out to be ruined since they are illegitimate and their father had passed away, leaving his “widow” and progeny to the evils of fending for themselves.

‘Of course, the heirs – for example, his brother, sister, father, mother and other relatives – would come to seize, legitimately, everything the young family had in the way of furniture, belongings, food, drink and residence, saying to them, “The inheritance should be for the rightful family and you will get nothing!”

‘So, my brothers, now do you understand the purpose of the contract of marriage, which you describe as “merely a piece of paper”, for it makes a virtuous wife from a dissolute woman, and respectable, legitimate sons instead of criminals who would show enmity towards the cruel society. So, could anyone swindle them out of their father’s bequest or render them homeless to live in poverty? Moreover, due to this paper, would his partner-in-life be considered as an uninhibited adulteress or an honourable wife? In the unmarried state, who would accept her with her sons and daughters to be a heavy burden and shameful mark of disgrace? Where is her inheritance? And how would she spend the rest of her life? Would it be in prostitution after her youth had wilted? What a hard and bitter life she would face! Yet who, in fact, would have been responsible for such a situation?

‘That said, let us return to this paper you have ridiculed. You are wrong! This is the Law of the Merciful God!’

The scholar resumed, ‘So, wouldn’t we, ourselves, have destroyed the first link of society, which is the family, and consequently destroyed society in its entirety had we followed this deficient point of view that “they loved one another”? Now, don’t you see that this contract will provide lasting evidence to ensure the rights of the wife and the children and make sure of a secure life for them? What do you think? Should we still dispense with it?’

Faced with this superior logic and intelligent rebuttal, and Godly Aid for our enlightened guide, they bowed to the great wisdom behind Al’lah’s Law and Order, admitting and confessing the truth and necessity of this legislation, they said, ‘In fact, we thought the religion to be just madness, but the reality seems to be different.’

The scholar, Mohammad Amin, went on showing them that Islam is a religion based on facts and valuable principles, and its precepts are not at all futile, for it contains nothing but truth, and that each Godly Command and heavenly legislation includes deep wisdom and leads to happiness here and in the Hereafter for one and all. Indeed, the Almighty wants nothing but happiness and no misery for His creatures in this world and in the Afterlife, and that is why He sent His Envoy (cpth) for all people, thus revealing the sublimity of His Sharia and the grandeur of His Guidance and the deep wisdom enfolded within every one of His Orders, and the goodness gained by applying them.

One of the Envoy’s (cpth) instructions about marriage that has been handed down, without interruption, throughout Islam, is that the male relatives, friends and neighbours of both the bride and groom should gather together to witness the marriage on the day it took place; they should be offered a banquet of fine foods, including the most delicious sorts of savoury food and exquisite sweets, so the day would be a lasting memory. Then, should the husband ever try to deny his wife or his children during his lifetime, these witnesses would be able to attest to the truth of the marriage: so, too, if the inheritors denied the wife and children after his death.

Similarly, at the same time the women would be gathered at the bride’s home around a luxurious banquet so as to witness the occasion, for the word would be spread, “That man has married this woman and she is now his wife.” So, most of the inhabitants of the quarter, the kinsfolk and the friends of the bride and groom would be well acquainted with that fact.

Nowadays, the civil court is the norm, replacing the sheikhs, and this is where the contract of marriage is drawn up and entered into.

chapters.title: Part Eight
chapters.html:
The Faithful Mentor and the Lost Judge

He never uttered a single word unless it was ethical and enlightening, which demonstrated his sharp insight, cogent mind and sound process of thought.

He was imbued with a deep-rooted, profound sense of humanity and a discerning sense for the truth.

These are but a few of the many sacrosanct qualities embedded within him because of his great love for the Almighty, the Origin of sanctity; and this is why his words were like sacred gems enhancing the spirits of those who sought all that is right and true. These words were received in accordance with the listener’s status, and touched whatever occupied his spirit so that he could find the reality which was evident within them. He spoke whenever necessary and always in a manner which was appropriate for the listeners’ spirits so as to bring them nothing but goodness and happiness, both here and in the Hereafter.

His piercing insight and knowledge gave the effective cure for illness garnered from his sublime wisdom so that disease might be eliminated and replaced with sound health and happiness. Thus, the advice of this faithful mentor always resulted in benefits and happiness for his listeners in this world and in the Afterlife.

Everyone who came into his presence recognised his peerless realism and piercing insight by God’s Light. His unparalleled recommendations ensured deliverance and success and, by contrast, those who disagreed with his advice were deprived of these benefits and blessings and ultimately regretted their decision.

This was the humane scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho.

The following event reveals an example of his Godly advice:

A certain hapless judge stood wringing his hands together… saying, ‘Oh… if only I had listened to your advice, Abu Fathi.’ Then, he began to relate what had happened to him in the hearing of several men, repeating yet again, ‘If only I had followed your advice, Abu Fathi!’

So, what is the story of this judge? What was the advice which he ignored and then regretted doing so?

It was during the 1940s, when the salaries given to state employees far exceeded imagination, and those who were employed were extremely fortunate, whether they were employed in a low position or a high one: a gendarme or an officer, as all their salaries were considered to be enormous. Their income was not simply a consistent trickle, but could be described rather as a continuously streaming river. The lowliest official received a monthly salary from which, within a year, he could save enough money to buy a sizeable house and a car; in addition to which all members of the family would enjoy the high life.

At that time, when the luxurious life for people in general and public servants in particular had eased off somewhat, the Ministry of Justice declared that it needed to appoint judges in its official courts.

The judge of whom we write was an acquaintance of the eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (Abu Fathi), and was one of those applicants who held the certificate of law. The list of names of the persons to be appointed was issued after a while and his name was among them. Needless to say, he was extremely pleased when he became a prominent official, a judge who would earn a large salary which was many times greater than that of an ordinary employee.

He completed the formal assignment papers as fast as he could, and took up his position a few days later; when he received his first salary, he realised that it was quite considerable. He then calculated his monthly needs and found that the amount he needed came to no more than a tenth of that huge salary. Then, an idea struck him whereby he thought that he could draw nearer to the state authorities by presenting himself as an honest and upright human being; so he sought to appear concerned for the state’s public interest, a caretaker of its budget, and honest and righteous in his employment.

He talked to Mohammad Amin saying, ‘Oh, Abu Fathi! As you know I became a judge, receiving a monthly salary that is so large that I need only one-tenth of it to live in comfort. I wondered what I should do with the remaining nine-tenths, and then I had the good idea of returning it to the state treasury, as it is rightfully theirs. So, I decided to write a formal letter to the authorities in the prime minister’s office and ask them to lower my wage to just one-tenth of the current amount.’

The august scholar understood the judge’s reasoning, which was that he cared to show himself as the very soul of honesty and fairness in the eyes of those in authority, but he advised him, saying, ‘Don’t ever do that. They have willingly given you this salary, and it is your right, yet if you find it is in excess of your needs, donate it as charity to paupers and others who are in need.’

The judge replied, ‘But, as I have told you, Abu Fathi, my salary is so large, and I have no right to anything beyond my basic needs, so in fact it belongs to the state, as nine- tenths of my salary is above what I need and I shall return it to the treasury.’

At this point, the candid admonisher repeated his advice and caution to the judge, ‘As I have told you my brother, give the excess as a handout to the poor and needy. You know there are a lot of destitute families in dire need, so if you spend the surplus amount on them you will have eased their embarrassment and saved them from poverty, deprivation and misery by securing for them the essential necessities of life. Through that you will improve their condition and bring them happiness: thereby you will draw nearer to Al’lah because of your noble deed. So, all of their happiness and liberation from the ties of poverty and deprivation will reflect on your worldly life by giving you happiness, joy, and true closeness to Al’lah, the Almighty… and furthermore, you will gain Paradises of bliss in the Hereafter. Be sure, my brother, that all creatures are Al’lah’s servants, and the more one offers them benefits the closer they will be to Him. Al’lah has opened the gateway of Paradise before you, so do not refuse to enter it. Seek Al’lah’s Satisfaction and He will surely be pleased with you and make many people pleased with you too.’

The judge heard the scholar’s true utterance denoting his sublime logic. Those peerless words encompassed great goodness in this life and in the life to come. He thought for a while, then he realised he could not refute these words and the truth and love for humanity and for Al’lah’s Satisfaction that they denoted. Yet, he felt that they did not conform to his wish to present himself as an honest, upright and zealous man before the people… and certainly not before Al’lah, the Almighty. This was his personal, unbending point of view!

Therefore, he did not abide by these Godly gems and divine advice, thinking that his success in this world would not be realised unless he continued on his intended path, so, he decided to carry out his plan. At the earliest opportunity he sent a letter to the authorities in the prime minister’s office stating that he wished to reduce his monthly salary to one-tenth of what he was receiving. He stated, as he had previously said to Mohammad Amin, that it far exceeded his needs and one-tenth of the amount would be sufficient, therefore he felt that he had no right to retain the extra money. He explained that his conscience and deep sense of patriotism dictated that he should return it to the treasury since it rightfully belonged to the state and not to him.

This odd and unprecedented communication was received by the senior personnel in the prime minister’s office. Really, it was such a strange letter, the likes of which had never been seen before! So, those concerned held a meeting to discuss the matter, and after spending some time in discussion and deliberation they found the judge’s communication to be illogical and certainly open to doubt, thus giving rise to many questions about the judge’s abilities, the state of his mind, and the soundness of his reasoning.

Finally, they reached the following conclusions, ‘Truly, this judge is not of sound mind and lacks reasonable judgement, for anyone who refuses money rightfully offered to him is not at all fit to judge others. A judge’s position is so sensitive and strongly related to the citizens’ matters and interests, and consequently to the cases that come before him, that whoever occupies this position must be of sound judicious mind and unerring thought. Accordingly, the judge in question, about whom we held this meeting, is not suited to that position; he must, therefore, be discharged from this sensitive post.’

Thus, the man was instantly dismissed from his position, lost his employment and was left without income. His actions, that he had thought to be so worthy, had gone against him, whereas he had thought that his request would serve to strengthen him in his office and raise his standing in the eyes of the authorities. He believed that by his actions all people would hear of his fairness, honour, and rectitude and that he would become the model for integrity and patriotism.

But, on the contrary, the matter brought him a most unexpected and unpleasant result. When he was informed that he had been dismissed from his position and stripped of his employment, he remembered the great guide’s advice and words of caution against his planned action, and the aim of his intention which was directed at attracting people’s satisfaction not that of Al’lah. So, the authorities became perturbed at his request and he lost the great gains which Al’lah had prepared for him and toward which the eminent scholar, Mohammad Amin, had guided him.

Then it was that he remembered the warning and admonition, and sighing deeply he said, ‘If only I had taken your advice Abu Fathi!’

He was the loser and deeply regretted his decision, but it was too late!

chapters.title: The Devil Was Thwarted and Confessed, “I have No Power over You”
chapters.html:
One day, our noble scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho returned to his home filled with a feeling of great happiness, as his love for God provided him with all that he needed, and His Satisfaction with him was his only aim and desire. Without doubt, honour is attained by rectitude.

Usually, everything was orderly and satisfactory within his household, but that day it seemed that something strange was afoot!

As soon as he entered the house he heard strange sounds and was most surprised for he was accustomed to an air of tranquillity pervading his home. What had happened?! Everything had been fine when he left, but now he was taken aback by the sounds of grief-stricken voices. He could hear women crying as if something terrible had happened. But throughout his noble life, whenever he was taken aback, our great scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho sought refuge in his Provider, the Almighty, Who relieved him and saved him from every single difficult problem.

As always, the spirit of Mohammad Amin Sheikho flowed towards the place of the event, and then continued towards the Holy Mosque. It travelled to al-Ka’ba, which is honoured throughout the world for its holiness and purity and is the holy place where God sent down lights upon His Envoy (cpth); ﴿224﴾

and these lights continue to come down because this is the location of the descent of the Godly Manifestations. Our eminent scholar put his full trust in Al’lah, without Whom there is no refuge or protection, and he commended the case to Him.

Within a few moments quietness prevailed once more in the house, and the recent fear and confusion were replaced with tranquillity: all signs of distress and suffering had disappeared… and moreover all of this happened within a single moment.

The scholar’s wife then came out of the women’s quarters and walked towards him, as she had sensed his arrival. She began to tell him about the events leading up to that point, relating the reason for the loud voices and what had happened before he arrived home. She said, ‘Some of the women of the neighbourhood came here, bringing an epileptic woman with them. She was having a seizure and thrashing around on the floor. Her limbs were in spasm, contracting and extending in a most unnatural way, and her whole body was making involuntary movements. Foam was frothing from her mouth and her eyes were bulging as though they were about to pop out of their sockets. She was struggling to breathe… it was as though she was being suffocated, or someone was trying to strangle her. Then she became very pale and the pall of death covered her face… she was struggling so hard in an attempt to escape from seemingly inevitable death. It was really a terrible sight.

‘Her state was very distressing. All of the women were sure that she was just moments away from death, and they all started shouting and crying and lamenting.

‘A few of her female relatives brought her here, hoping that God would heal her through your blessing. The people advised them to resort to you because they know about your uprightness and piety. Although they had previously taken her to many physicians, who prescribed different medicines and tranquillizers and analgesics for her, but these attempts to cure her had achieved nothing. The doctors failed to cure her because they do not have any effective medicine for such diseases. Every one of their medicines only provided temporary relief. But as soon as you entered the house, she became calm and recovered as if there had been nothing wrong.’

Mohammad Amin understood the case immediately.

He said to his wife, ‘Actually, she is possessed by evil spirits. This has been brought about by her wicked associate from djinn-kind who wants to destroy her and lead her to hellfire. But she has resorted to us, “and anyone who enters your home seeking protection from you, you should protect them.” However, this case is very easy to resolve, as Satan’s scheme is weak. The evil webs that he weaves are weak and ineffective as they have no material existence, even though he acts against those who are deserving.’

The great scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho could hear the cursed devil that had entered into the woman speaking to him.

It said, ‘I will leave her and enter you.’

The scholar answered in a loud voice, ‘And I will break your head.’ Then, he began to recite the noble fortresses, al-Falaq (All that’s coming to Appearance), al-Nas (Oblivious Humankind, Oblivious DJinn-kind), and al-Ikhlas (Sincerity), as he began to direct his mind towards God and his heart fully towards the Holy Mosque. It was not long before that obnoxious devil left the woman and the house, defeated and subdued.

Due to the timely intervention of Mohammad Amin the afflicted woman regained her health and was able to return to her normal life, for all the pain and the effects of the attack had disappeared completely. As a result of her recovery, a feeling of joy and pleasure prevailed in the house, and incomparable signs of thanks and gratitude shone from the faces of those present. They all then left the house giving thanks and praising Almighty God and asking Him to give the august scholar great rewards.

Later on that night, Mohammad Amin was lying in his bed, trying to rest. As he lay there, neither fully asleep nor fully awake, he felt, suddenly, the alarming presence of a black spirit. He heard it saying, ‘No fault! No blemish! There’s no way I can enter into you! I have never met a man like you, who is such a hopeless case for me!’ The black spirit then uttered curses at the scholar’s religion and fled, for fear of being burned by God’s Light when the scholar sought refuge in Him.

And if you ask about the reason that the Almighty God allowed the devil to curse and swear at our religion, it is because He, the Almighty God, just wanted to show Mohammad Amin the profound enmity of the devil, his disbelief, and his humiliation and ultimate defeat.

chapters.title: The Session of Truthfulness and the Voice of Reality
chapters.html:
His assembly (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) was a session of truthfulness, and his tongue was the voice of reality

The gatherings of the noble scholar, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, were scented with the essence of paradises and refreshment; they were flooded with blessedness so that true life would descend upon the faithful hearts who seek to know their Provider, and these gatherings would make their hearts fragrant, clear and tinted with shades of brilliance and purity. They would be illuminated by God’s Lights and cultivated by the jewel of His Supreme Attributes so that they will be reclaimed and refined. The low deeds they had previously insisted on would be abolished, releasing them from the chains which had confined them and prevented them from soaring into the orbit of truth and reality where the luminosity, the light, the beauty and the majesty are to be found. Here too is where the hearts of the grand Prophets and Envoys (cptt) melt when they witness the Greatest Treasure and the Origin of goodness and generosity where the sacrosanct Grants of the Almighty God, Glory to Him, are manifested.

Because of his truthfulness in guiding Al’lah’s creatures and his aspirations to bring the optimum goodness upon them, the Almighty made him a doctor for the hearts. To this end He disclosed to him the conditions of everyone who had resorted to him, with the aim of curing them and leading them towards the truth, if that is what they truly sought. Therefore Al’lah’s Light reveals to him the truthful man and the liar and shows him both the ailment and the remedy. It discloses to him the cause that drove some disciples to distance themselves from the Almighty, and where the fault might be, and the direction in which the spirits of others may scatter or incline. By Al’lah’s Light, he knows the cause which gives rise to a slackening in seeking its aim and requirement if the spirit really sought to be acquainted with Almighty Al’lah.

Thus, this venerable guide Mohammad Amin Sheikho was a healer for their hearts: it is he who saved them from their alienation from Al’lah and then invited, guided and led them to Al’lah, to the levels of closeness to Him, and to sublime paradises. That’s why the Almighty ensured that his heart’s eye was always observing them, looking by His Light at all their conditions and knowing their inclinations and inward thoughts.

And why should this not be so? For he was their spiritual doctor assigned by Almighty Al’lah to guide and help them to attain and realise the truth.

Mohammad Amin was so gentle, so merciful: his kindness towards his murids and disciples was limitless. If he wanted to refine a fault in the manner of a certain disciple, or draw attention to a particular weak point in one of them which might prevent him from persistence in adopting the way leading towards his Provider, he would do so in a sensitive manner. In order to show the murid the method and the medicine which would release him of the weakness he found in his spirit, the eminent guide would refrain from speaking out openly and frankly to the disciple about what he found inside him or pointing out his faults openly. He would, however, relate stories and lessons in which he would refer to the ailment and its appropriate remedy. Hence, and without being aware of it, this murid would receive a description of his complaint or the mistake he had made, along with the suitable cure and the necessary medicine to rid himself of the malady and reject what was making him withdraw from Al’lah which caused him to degrade his position and debase him with Al’lah, and fellow humans.

All this occurs by Al’lah’s Light, when the diagnosis for spiritual disease and the prescribed remedy were given through Al’lah’s Manifestation by His Light for this true guide and merciful, humane doctor to know the condition of his murids, and the methods for effecting a rescue, cure, and success for each one of them.

Indeed, this true master really astounded all people who sincerely sought the truth through his incontrovertible luminous science and his superb diction in guiding and directing those who had resorted to him for guidance in loving God and drawing nearer to His Presence, Glory to Him.

He had amazed all people who aimed at sublimity and attaining the heavens. Why not, since the Almighty God spoke through the master’s tongue, enabling his lofty revelation to flow in abundance.

At this particular seminar and assembly of guidance, there were more than four hundred murids from various cities and villages. They were all leaving after the sanctified lesson during which their hearts were filled with great light and measureless gratitude and praise for God Who had sent this grand blessing. Indeed, everyone of them had profited by gaining solutions to all his problems or a diagnosis for his ailments and the weak points in his spirit. Moreover, the master would have given him the medicine and an unfailing cure which would never miss the target since it had issued from the Almighty Al’lah through the tongue of this eminent true guide. All of this diagnosis and cure came through his kind stories, gentle words and actual, realistic lessons and incidents within which he explained a particular point of weakness, its causes, and the ways man can rid himself of it.

One wonders just how many questions they were concealing in their hearts, yet by the end of the lesson all questions were answered and resolved; and so it was with all doubts and uncertainty which would be replaced with lofty Godly Wisdom and the luminous certainty of shining reality. In this manner, all questions and doubts would be resolved without anyone actually voicing a question or stating his problem publicly! Even if the questions had arisen only in a person’s mind, they would be answered with cogency, logic and firm evidence by the end of the lesson.

Then the disciples would leave the session, their hearts filled with light and love for Almighty Al’lah, since everyone of them would have achieved his own aim and been made aware of the right way in proportion to his personal closeness, and his level of aspiration and desire to be acquainted with his Provider.

One would also see that in their daily life the disciples were ordered and fully followed the law learnt from their eminent master: visiting the master would have its appointed terms; and pondering on the creation of the heavens and the earth also had its own specific times, just as there are appointed times for praying. In addition, to achieve the maximum benefit, attending his assembly must have its morals and controls; and so it was with the special visits for their venerable guide which must be regulated and have particular conditions: they began at 8 a.m. and ended at 11 a.m. As for the midday period which lasts until the call announcing the afternoon prayer, none of the disciples was to disturb him because this time is specified for rest. In summer, the lesson usually started after the afternoon prayer and lasted until 10 o’clock at night; while in winter this lesson and sacred recitation began after sunset and also lasted until 10 o’clock at night.

One night, unusually, the lesson was prolonged. The venerable master had given his disciples the opportunity to ask questions within this general lesson. So, the brothers began to put questions to him and he answered all their queries and that special lesson lasted until midnight. After that they had no need to ask him anything, for they were accustomed to having the answer presented as soon as the question occurred in their minds. Moreover, each of them understood the lesson according to his closeness to his Provider, his rank and his own efforts and personal humane sacrifices. So, Al’lah’s Speech was recited and so was the scholar’s revelation and explanation of the Holy Qur’an. It was the same assembly and speech for all the disciples but the level of understanding was different for each of them depending on his status. In this way, every disciple felt that the words were directed to him personally, solving his problems and showing the way to get rid of his faults which impeded his advance and approach towards his Provider. He would then leave the assembly having fully understood the solution of his own matters through the grand truth which was revealed by Al’lah and put into words through the tongue of this venerable master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho.

When the disciples gathered the next day to recall and discuss the lesson, exchange ideas, review the thoughts presented and the recited Godly explanations, you would find each of them had grasped it and explained it differently from the others. This was so because everyone had drunk from the spring of this true Godly guide in a different state from the others, and according to his own rank, level of truthfulness, and personal problems and ailments.

It was the same lesson and the same speech, yet it treated every murid and every heart, every status and rank. This proves that it had undoubtedly issued from the Almighty God and was aimed at the simple truth for each of them individually.

In fact, all the brothers in the circle of this eminent master had witnessed and realised this description and did, in fact, live in this state, which is why it had never occurred to any of them to oppose the thoughts or the perception of another of his brothers during their discussions of the lesson.

In confirmation of this, Professor Abdul-Kadir Yahya al-Dayrani, the disciple of the eminent scholar, says, ‘If you attend the lesson of this august guide, you need not ask or enquire at all, since Al’lah Almighty unveils to him everything by what He reveals to his heart and then passes through his tongue. Therefore, during his lesson (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) the Almighty speaks through his tongue so that each disciple will hear his own personal reply and be guided to enhance himself.’

Indeed, many incidents, examples and various indications had happened to each one, individually, in his assembly and to every murid of his circle, thus verifying that this solemn master obtained his science from the Almighty Who had shown him the states of everyone that had recourse to him and drank from his true guidance. So, by the foresight granted to him by the Almighty Al’lah he was a doctor, a director and a guide for them, as his insight observed them by day and by night.

Once, Mr. Abdul-Kadir (the disciple of the honourable guide) was entrusted by his mother to sell a house she had inherited from her father. He complied with her request immediately and within a few days he had sold it and received the sale money.

Since he knew that his mother did not need this money whereas he, himself, was in dire need, he returned to her bringing the money and began to speak about his situation, yet before he could finish his explanation she interrupted him saying,

‘Oh, my dear son! Take all the money from the sale of the house and use it as you like!’

Truly, the money came at just the right time to help him to straighten out his financial problems.

What a miracle!

In the evening of the same day, this honest disciple went as usual to the lesson of his august master, and as soon as he entered the meeting room, and before he managed to take the hand of his venerable guide to greet him, a gentle smile appeared on the features of the master, who said, ‘Surely, no one loves you as your mother does.’

In another one of these incidents, this murid had eaten his lunch; he then took off his formal clothes and, being exhausted he soon fell asleep and slept for two hours, more or less. When he woke up, however, he found himself in some discomfort, and even more tired than before he took a nap.

As soon as the disciple entered the session that same day the honourable scholar, Mohammad Amin, approached those present saying, ‘It has been proved medically that it’s unhealthy to eat before sleeping.’ Surely, this was no mere coincidence!

Similar incidents and other, greater examples happened repeatedly with one or other of the murids of this truthful, august guide; therefore they asked him about nothing since they knew about his familiarity by Al’lah’s Light and his knowledge by Al’lah’s Informing and Witnessing of their states and all of their troubles. This is how he was able to explain matters to them and answer the questions which occurred in their minds. Thus, the tongue of this guide who directs people to the truth speaks only the simple truth, and his words come from the Almighty Al’lah. God says in the Holy Qur’an, “He does not speak out of his own inclination.” ﴿225﴾

Once, a consul of a certain Arab embassy visited the venerable scholar (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) to listen to his great Godly Speech. When the consul entered, the venerable master received him with his cheerful countenance which was alive with joy and vivacity, saying, ‘Welcome, Your Excellency, Mr. Ambassador!’

The consul replied, ‘Alas! How could I reach such a prestigious position… ambassador…! I’m only a consul, sir!’

The honourable master replied, ‘We’ve said it, accept it then, Excellency.’

The consul said, ‘I wish… that God responds to your statement!’

During the session, there was a wonderful, sublime and heavenly speech which so overwhelmed the consul with bliss that he did not want to leave. In fact, he would have liked to stay for a long time in this state of heart irrigation by the companionship of this venerable, true guide; but, unfortunately, it was out of his control as he had many commitments and another appointment relating to his position. So, when his visit came to an end he took leave of Mohammad Amin who bade him farewell and said that he hoped for further meetings with him. The consul then left in a happy and grateful state of mind.

When he arrived at his office a great surprise was waiting for him for he heard news which had such a great effect on him that he couldn’t contain himself for joy, and he headed back to the venerable master just half an hour after taking his leave of him. Then he arrived for the second time and knocked at the door; as soon as he entered, he happily approached the honourable master saying, ‘By God… by God, sir, you welcomed me and said, “Welcome, Your Excellency, Mr. Ambassador!” ‘

‘I have come to tell you that at the very moment the decision was issued to assign me as the ambassador for my country here in Syria, and the embassy and appropriate authorities were advised, you addressed me as “Ambassador”. The previous ambassador had been discharged and they didn’t find a substitute, so they have appointed me. Yes! When you addressed me as an ambassador the decision had already been confirmed and announced!’ How strange the matter of this venerable man is!

How great is the truth that comes from his tongue! Really, it’s the tongue of truthfulness! What can his rank and position be with the Almighty Al’lah, Glory to Him? The august master endorsed the ambassador’s new position and congratulated him wholeheartedly, saying, ‘Praise God for this favour my brother, and keep offering charitable deeds.’

chapters.title: A Terrible Accident Is Avoided by Giving Alms
chapters.html:
Come, travel with us dear reader, to experience something which you may have never thought about. Our journey will take us by road to Lebanon in the company of our esteemed guide, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, and we shall see evidence of his great wisdom and discipline.

One day, our illustrious scholar decided to travel to Lebanon on business matters. He took his son with him, and some of his followers accompanied him too.

At the taxi station, he was not to forget what he and his brethren – who were travelling under his wing – should do, so he reminded them saying, ‘By the way, my friends! Have you paid alms before travelling?’

And as he expected, they had forgotten all about it; meanwhile he put his hand into his pocket and took out one Syrian pound to pay alms for himself and his son, in addition to which, he took half a pound from each of his travelling companions and gave it as alms to a poor man at the taxi station.

All of them gave the alms willingly and eagerly except one who was reluctant to comply, and dithered in paying it, even though he was rich and from a famous family.

Thereupon, the venerable scholar, Mohammad Amin, stretched out his hand quickly and grabbed the money from the hand of his hesitant disciple and gave it to the poor man; then they all got into the car which set off from Damascus, the capital of Syria, to go to Lebanon.

On the way, all was quiet inside the car… except the gentle, pleasant words spoken by the great scholar, Mohammad Amin, including his thoughts on mercy, relief and happiness for their hearts, through which he guided his disciples who listened to him with the utmost respect and courtesy; all the while his little son sat contentedly near the window looking at the charming views of nature unfurling as the car passed through the countryside.

The car was moving at an average speed when suddenly something happened quite unexpectedly: a big lorry was approaching it at the crossroads and it seemed that an accident was inevitable. The driver desperately tried to avoid the lorry by decelerating and turning hard right, but there was no time to avert an accident… for the lorry collided heavily with the taxi on its left side.

Walid, son of Mohammad Amin Sheikho, was sitting in the back of the car on the left side, still absorbed in watching the passing scenery, and when the collision occurred, the boy flew into the air as if a hand had carried him from the left and dropped him – thank God – in his father’s lap on the right.

Fortunately, none of the brethren were harmed either, except the laggard disciple who paid the alms only when he was shamed into doing so.

And so, it was that Al’lah willed that he should know the value of almsgiving before travelling and why the noble Envoy recommended it to us with an effective practical lesson; for the man that was reluctant to pay was affected by a slight injury to his leg that confined him to his bed for a full month.

The noble Envoy (cpth) spoke truly when he said, “Hurry to pay the alms for almsgiving will ward off affliction.”

chapters.title: He Cannot Be Blamed for Telling the Truth
chapters.html:
In the Holy Qur’an the Almighty Al’lah says, “As He has already revealed to you in the Book, if you hear people denying and ridiculing God’s Revelation, do not sit with them.” ﴿226﴾

This is a Command of Al’lah, and whoever believes in Him should obey His Commands. No doubt, the true believer will show his good nature, forgiveness and tolerance when somebody behaves badly towards him personally, but if a man’s misconduct is directed towards God or His Envoy (cpth), he will become like a raging fury. For that man, there is no space for leniency nor gentle persuasion, when confronted with untruths or deception; rather, he will spring forth as a lion in order to uphold the truth, giving no thought to the price he might pay for his defensive reaction.

Every believer sets an example of personal devotion and self denial for the sake of God’s Envoy; he may sacrifice his wealth, dispense with friends and even offer up his soul when he senses any criticism of God and His Envoy. This is a distinguishing characteristic found in all people of true belief, while it is totally lacking in all hypocrites. Believing that their requirements and the arrangements of their affairs are controlled by human beings, those who have not fully understood the statement that “there is no god except Al’lah” frequently fawn over and flatter people of authority so that their worldly advantages and inferior desires may be easily fulfilled, unconcerned at losing all respect, and their demeanour being marked with obsequiousness and false humility.

Pitiful people!

They are unaware of the great remorse and pain they will inevitably suffer when the veil is removed from their heart’s eye at the time of their death, and this carnal and temporal world vanishes forever more. Only then will they come face to face with the reason for their existence and understand the sublime purpose lying behind it, and only then will they sense once again the nature of perfection which God had stamped upon their spirits. But at that time, it will be too late for them to repent and make amends for their wrongful conduct.

Out of his love for God’s servants and to avoid them experiencing such a sorrowful end, the august guide, Mohammad Amin, repeatedly admonished his followers to adopt the path that leads us to be proud of God and His Envoy and to avoid the path that may taint our hearts with lowliness and degradation. Relying on the noble verses of God’s Holy Book, he revealed to us how we should act if we ever met people who mocked God and His Envoy. His guidance was not restricted merely to his spoken words, but rather his behaviour was a practical example in support of all his teaching.

The following tells of a true incident that the noble guide experienced personally, through which he (God sanctified his secret) introduced a proof of his true and actualised guidance, and his magnificent zeal for the Grand God and His great Envoy was clearly expressed.

It is well-known by everybody all over the world that the Jews have set a clear example of loving this worldly life and wasting all the powers that a man may have in order to enjoy its abundant pleasures and vanities, instead of using their endowed faculties to recognise God and approach Him, the Almighty. And because of their insistence on expending great efforts to attain carnal enjoyments, God fulfilled their desires and placed the majority of the national wealth in their hands, thus making them the richest nation in the world.

During the lifetime of our noble guide it happened that a wealthy Jewish man, a famous merchant, came to visit some of the merchants and notables whom he knew personally, in Damascus. The men of Damascus received their visitor warmly, showing him great respect, and addressing him constantly with kind and gentle words! And how could they not express their great esteem for this man when his opulence was obviously so much greater than theirs!
