They competed with each other to arrange banquets in his honour; and how fortunate was the one who would have him as a guest at his home! This was their ill-considered view. As for His Excellency, the more the people around him humbled themselves and kowtowed to him, the more his insolence and presumptiousness grew. Sometimes he swaggered among them virtually submerged in his own pomposity and overwhelmed by his sense of pride and self-conceit, and at other times he sat nonchalantly with his legs crossed, turning up his nose at them whereby signs of contempt were clearly visible on his features.

At one particular banquet, he became increasingly full of his own self-importance and began to scoff at his acquaintances amongst the Moslem notables and merchants, their religion and beliefs in particular. And yet, despite that all the present continued to smile politely, and failed to react to his loathsome behaviour. Not a man among them had a degree of faith and fervour for their Envoy (cpth) that would spur him to roar in his face and defend the truth, so that his cursed wrong would have been destroyed and his wicked devil along with it. What gives one cause to wonder, is that their position and behaviour towards him never faltered, on the contrary it remained as it was, coloured with boundless honour and glorification and ingratiation! But their reverence for the wealth that the Jewish merchant possessed reduced them to the lowest possible degree of contemptibility when he mentioned to them, mockingly, a noble saying of the great Envoy (cpth), and then he burst out laughing, and they laughed with him!!

‘Your Envoy said,’ the rich Jew began with a derisive sneer on his lips, ‘…that tomorrow the Jew will hide himself behind the tree, but then the tree will speak to the Moslems, “Come on, Moslems! There is a Jew hiding behind me… come on, kill him”.’ He laughed and again everyone with him, that is, those who could understand his language, laughed too!

It was God’s Will that our august scholar was invited to that banquet. When he saw a large group of the guests there laughing he asked some of them, ‘What does this Jew say that makes him and you laugh so heartily?’ And they told him the reason for their laughter. He was shocked, but more than that, there was a feeling of deep sorrow that penetrated into his pure heart for the state of those sycophants around that accursed Jew. There and then, a whirlwind of unmeasured compassion was brought forth inside his free spirit that made him burst out with unique, glorious, moral power in the face of that evil man. He shouted at him in a thunderous voice, ‘You, Khawaja!’ ﴿227﴾

The Jew, who did not speak Arabic, turned towards the source of the thunderous voice to see an awe-inspiring human being with an unparalleled mien that caused him to stand staring at him, his mouth agape and limbs quivering. ‘Listen… Khawaja’, the revered master continued while his hands gesticulated in an attempt to make the Jew fully understand the meaning of what he was saying. ‘Tomorrow… the Moslem (pointing to himself)… the Jew (pointing to the Jewish merchant)… a knife (with his hands signifying that he would hold a knife)… will slay him (passing the same hand over his own neck and giving a sound like that of a knife cutting through a neck).’ The meaning was perfectly clear and was instantly imprinted on the mind of the malicious Jew. There and then, the justice that dwelt within the spirit of the pure master clashed with the injustice and wickedness within the evil spirit of the wealthy Jew and stamped it out completely.

Then the Jew perceived a rampant lion stamped on the face of the noble master that caused him to become completely dumbstruck, as an overwhelming feeling of awful terror crept into his depths making him quiver from head to toe, and convincing him he was about to breath his last.

Yet the imposing sight of the august master was also highly impressive for all of the guests at the banquet, for having heard his evil-crushing words, their hearts shook violently. But how strange! When they should have been pleased that there was still a true believer defending God and His Envoy with such peerless zealousness before that ill wisher, they were alarmed instead, and their spirits became aggravated! Their reaction denoted an obvious fact: these people were definitely on the wrong path, and clearly pleased to be there!

Worse still, they appeared to be displeased because of the august master’s reply to their friend, to the extent that a few days later some of them declared their annoyance by criticising Mohammad Amin, saying, ‘He shouldn’t have acted in that way with our friend, the Jew; his behaviour was embarrassing and his answer was sharp. Why didn’t he simply ignore the man’s words?’ They did not want the prestige of their pompous, defamatory friend to be touched; and as for the prestige of God’s Envoy, they did not care one iota if the Jew belittled it, and even took pleasure in doing so.

No wonder! For when the carnal world becomes the chief concern of men and hoarding money their main aim in this life, then one should find nothing strange in such a shameful position and reaction.

chapters.title: The Woman Money Lender
chapters.html:
The Almighty God says in His Holy Book, “Whoever looks with the Light of God, God will give them salvation and provide for them whence they do not reckon.” ﴿228﴾

And in one of His Holy Sayings, He (Glory to Him) declared, “Oh My obedient follower, be for Me as I want you to be, and then I will be for you as you want Me to be.”

This is a law and something that, in reality, happens continuously when a human being becomes connected with God’s Robe, meaning Prophet Mohammad (cpth); and abiding by His Statute they will be close to God. Thus, whatever good they ask from Him, He will definitely respond to them and fulfil their requests.

The more one is submissive to God and conforms to His sublime Legislation, the more beloved to God they will become and the more God will respond to their call.

Our humane guide, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, was extremely close to God, and because he took great care to apply His Orders and to serve His creatures many incidents occurred that showed the effectiveness of this Godly Law and gave proof of the scholar’s high standing with God.

One of these events took place at the beginning of winter when the noble guide was concerned that his new house would not be in a suitable state to receive his disciples during the coming rainy days.

He had bought the house during the summer. It was an Arab-style house in the al-Muhajireen area, including a vast courtyard where fresh air always circulated freely. A fountain was located in the middle of the courtyard, surrounded by many beds of green plants and colourful flowers and roses which spread their fragrant perfume to captivate the heart and heal the spirit: it presented a delightful picture when one observed their bright beauty which the Godly Hand had produced and formed in all its excellence.

Like all other Damascene houses, the house of the noble guide consisted of two floors: the ground floor which was inhabited during the summer season while the upper floor was used in the winter. Both floors of this new house contained many spacious, sunlit rooms providing perfect ambiance and comfort to all.

But what distinguished this house from others was that whoever went into it would feel as though they were entering a garden of Paradise. This is because of the serenity and comfort they would sense within; they might experience a state of deep pleasure, or even of bliss: the kind of feeling that could not be found in any other house.

And it was no wonder, for the Envoy of God (cpth) said, “Court of knowledge (about God) is a garden of Paradise.” Our noble guide had dedicated his house to weekly religious lectures, and this was in addition to the special gatherings where he used to meet with his close and loving disciples. This blessed house was indeed like a Ka’ba, a focal point, for all his murids and all those who honestly sought truth, rectitude and religion.

When this great master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, reached fifty years of age he turned fully to devoting himself in spirit and time to guiding people towards God: leading their spirits into His Presence under his distinguished direction and the superior knowledge God revealed to him. He helped them turn to God and His Envoy with love, through the great realities he unveiled to them concerning God’s Perfection and His Supreme Attributes, and the truthfulness and noble merits of His Envoy (cpth). By virtue of the scholar’s endeavours in creating this feeling of love for God in the hearts of his followers, their spirits were refined and became imbued with the mark of Godly Perfection.

Large groups of young men, whether educated or not, joined his circle (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) where they could acquire great intellectual and spiritual fruits from the superior lessons they received from their teacher, and enjoy happiness simply by talking about the Supreme Attributes of God, the Almighty. These lessons breathed life and beatitude into their hearts and therefore they were unable to dispense with them for they felt them necessary to their daily lives.

Days rolled by and turned into weeks and then months, and summer faded, then autumn spread its colourful cloak; that too ran its glorious course and gave place to winter which brought with it chilly weather, heavy rain and snow.

With the onset of winter, the noble scholar, Mohammad Amin, began to ponder upon the state of his new house and how it would fare in the coming rainy days, for it was the only place available to receive his followers who would be coming to drink from the fount of his heavenly knowledge. When he bought the house, it was still not plastered and the courtyard was covered with dust for it had not yet been paved. At the time, this was not a problem for him and his followers for they were still experiencing the warm, dry days of summer.

But on this particular day, thick banks of grey clouds covered the sky and veiled the sun; winds loaded with cool moisture began to blow, causing the rain to fall lightly at first. But it quickly increased and the heavens sent it in abundance.

The rainfall lasted long enough to turn the open courtyard into a large, muddy pool. The noble master came out of his room and stood beside the pool observing this new problem and wondering what he could do about it. He thought to himself, ‘Winter is here and the heavens have overwhelmed the earth with its blessings and rainwater; so, what can I do about this unpaved courtyard? I see that it will cause me some problems. Had it been only for me and my family it would not matter. But this situation will affect my disciples and the visitors who come here to learn about God!’

In fact, the problem might well affect more than three hundred people who were used to attending the lessons in person; and this number is apart from the groups who would visit him all during the week, morning and evening, to quench their thirst from his heavenly sciences. Unfortunately, the noble master was facing this problem at the same time that he was passing through financial difficulty, and so he did not have the money to solve it. He knew that the problem could easily be rectified by paving the courtyard, but this would cost a lot of money as the area in question was large, and he would have to buy the floor tiles and the materials needed for paving, also pay the delivery costs and the wages of the workers.

He had always been in the habit of keeping a sum of money to provide all the daily needs for himself and his family, and other necessities, including the alms he gave to the deserving needy. So whatever difficult circumstances he passed through, he carried all the burdens he faced easily and without any trouble, but with this new situation he felt a heavy load on his shoulders. He had to pave the courtyard as soon as possible because winter had arrived, but at the same time, he did not have the money to pay for it. So, what could he do?

He thought that he might borrow the necessary amount from his close disciples, but he realised that they were all poor and thus unable to cover the cost of the work. A feeling of anxiety began to flow into his pure heart when suddenly he heard a knock at the outer door of his house. The great guide walked steadily towards the door and opened it, and to his surprise he found an old woman standing before him although it was still early morning; the woman seemed to be strong and active even though she was advanced in years. He recognised her, for she was a famous usurer known not only to all the people in the region where she lived and, incidentally, where Officer Sheikho had once been the director of security, but many of the people of Damascus had also heard of her. She was well known for her abundant fortune, and her wide area of influence. In short, she was like a moving bank, for what she was worth was equal to, or perhaps more than, all the deposits in any bank. And now, this money lender was standing at his door holding a heavy bag. In a trembling voice she greeted the noble guide, saying, ‘Good morning, Abu Fathi.’

‘Good morning!’

‘May I come in, please?’

‘Yes, of course! Welcome, come in!’

She passed across the doorstep, still carrying the heavy bag, and then the noble master closed the door behind her. Once inside the house she put the bag down on the floor and revealed her careworn face, dripping with sweat. In a breathless voice she addressed the noble guide and began to tell her story, ‘Oh Abu Fathi! Last night I could not sleep at all. I was so afraid that burglars would burst into my home… at any moment I expected them to come over the wall… from all directions. Oh, sir! I was sure that they would steal my money and deprive me of so much of the fruit of my life’s work. I couldn’t close my eyes for even a moment. I waited, on tenterhooks, for the coming of morning, but it was needless for last night passed peacefully, but who knows what may happen tonight or any other night? So, I’ve decided to resort to your protection, sir. I can put my trust only in you, sir, for I believe in your honesty and truthfulness. I still remember your reliability and noble manners when you were the director of our region. I still remember your honourable conduct, therefore I find no-one to be more trustworthy than you, sir.

‘That is why I have brought these golden pieces for you to take care of on my behalf; in this way I will protect myself and my beloved money from the eyes of thieves and burglars. And with this I give you a full and free hand to take whatever sum of money you need and to spend any of it in whichever way you see fit. But this will be on one condition only, and that is to hand the full amount of golden liras back to me on the day I return to collect them. If you agree on this condition you can take the amount you need and I will not charge you any interest on it at all. I just want to find the full amount of money when I come back to get it. Here is the bag of gold coins, take it and protect it. Now I can go about my business with a peaceful mind. But again I remind you, when I visit you again I want to see it as I left it, with not a single penny missing. Do you agree?’

The noble master took the bag from the woman, saying, ‘As you like, but don’t you want a receipt for this money?’

‘Not at all,’ the woman answered, ‘a man like you who is entrusted with men’s souls can surely be entrusted with even the greatest amount of gold. No… No I will not take a receipt from you.’

However, the noble guide refused to keep the money in his charge without giving her a receipt which he wrote and signed with his own pen. And so, the woman said goodbye to the honourable master and left the house with a calm mind and tranquil heart. Her heavy steps expressed the exhaustion she suffered because of the previous sleepless night she had spent, worrying that thieves might break into her house and steal her bag of gold.

Glory to Him! How Great He is! He directed this woman to his obedient servant at the proper time, and did so even before Mohammad Amin prayed to Him to ask for His Help! It was only because the feeling of a heavy burden had begun to creep into his noble spirit as he thought of the new situation of his house in winter and joined it to his straitened circumstance, that the Almighty soon dispelled his worries by totally unexpected means. He sent to him a “moving bank” and placed at his disposal a sum of money, interest free, and many times greater than the sum he needed. Thus, the noble master was relieved of his worry and his features relaxed as he decided to borrow some of the woman’s money since she had willingly offered it to him. In this way, he could pave the courtyard and make some necessary improvements in the house so that the entire problem would be quickly resolved.

When the work was finished, the noble master was extremely happy for everything had been easily accomplished. He turned to God in praise for His Arrangement and Help which enabled him to continue his lofty lessons of guiding people to Him without any trouble.

Many days passed before another favour came from God to this noble guide when one of the shops which he had inherited from his late father was sold; so he took a part of the price he received for the shop, equal to the sum he had borrowed from the money of the money lender, and put it back in her bag after he changed it to golden coins.

That same evening our noble man went to bed with his heart full of immeasurable gratitude for the Almighty Al’lah (Glory to Him) Who supported him and eased the difficulties in his way, helped him to finish the work and return the money he had borrowed to the bag before the woman came back and asked for what was hers.

That night he closed his eyes, delighted and at ease, and surrendered to sleep. Then, as dawn broke the muezzin called for the dawn prayer, and so our great guide performed the communication with God and then he began to glorify the Almighty Al’lah. Suddenly he heard the echo of a voice as though coming from a distance. It reverberated around the entire quarter repeating one phrase, ‘I have missed it… I have missed it.’

‘How odd! Who could it be?’ the noble master thought to himself, ‘It’s still early morning, so who is shouting like this and in this area? Oh, God of all! I hope it’s good news.’

The quarter where he lived was known as the area where the upper class of society and the ruling element in Damascus lived and where silence and tranquillity constantly prevailed.

‘So,’ he thought, ‘who is causing this clamour and speaking in such a strange voice?’ But the answer was soon revealed when he heard loud banging on his street door followed by the same voice echoing the same words, ‘I have missed it… I have missed it.’

With this, he could guess who the source of all this noise was, so he got to his feet and quickly rushed to open the door. It was she, the money lender! She had come back to reclaim her bag of money.

Without any word of greeting she said to the noble man, in her Bedouin accent, ‘I’ve missed it… my money… my gold… I want my bag of golden liras.’

‘Okay… okay… you will have it,’ the noble master replied, ‘the gold is complete, not one lira less.’ She went into the house and the noble master entered one of the rooms and then came back holding the weighty bag and handed it to the woman.

She drank the delicious cup of coffee that had been offered to her and then said goodbye to the noble guide and left the house holding her beloved bag, not just with her hands, but seemingly with her eyes and heart too.

Behold, dear reader, the Wise Actions of the Almighty and Merciful God! Unaware of God’s Will and against her own will, the Almighty directed this money lender to relieve His beloved obedient servant of his distress and to alleviate his difficult circumstances. He sowed in her heart a feeling of alarm about the security of her gold and so pushed her to seek refuge in the noble guide and bring him, unconsciously, a release from his own anticipated troubles. He did not allow his obedient follower, the man of high intentions, to suffer straitened circumstances or to be put in any kind of tight situation.

Rather, He sent that woman at the appropriate time to solve his problem and, again at exactly the right time, He sent her back to reclaim her money after the borrowed sum had been replaced, and not a moment sooner.

If this demonstrates anything at all, it shows the great rank of this truthful guide with his Provider.

The Almighty says in His Holy Book, the Qur’an, “Every difficulty is followed with ease” ﴿229﴾

In this noble verse, Al’lah, Glory to Him, states a firm rule and effective law, “Whoever is straight in observing His Commands and Statute, He will assuredly raise his prestige and remove any difficulty that may stand in his way.”

This is true for every righteous human being. As for those whose difficulty arises in their spirits out of their care for the advantage of their brothers and sisters in humanity and for fear for their future in the Afterworld, and not out of any personal purpose, how high their spirits are and how close to God they are!

Let all humanity strive in that same way.

chapters.title: Success
chapters.html:
By Al’lah’s Wisdom, he who comes to our gathering will succeed, and he who does not will fail.’ These words fell on the ears of all those present at the assembly, so thereafter they paid even greater attention to what was being said. Indeed, it was a strange and wondrous prophecy! A prophecy to which their hearts submitted and which moved their deepest emotions. Oh, Provider! Is this true?

The meaning of that prophecy and its fulfilment assumed great importance after it had been explained by that august master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho. So, what might it foretell? And why did it seem so astonishing? In fact, it was not a story but a real prophecy confirmed by Al’lah the Almighty.

We shall speak of two friends, colleagues at university, who were like brothers in their search for religion and the truth. Their characters were similar and through their close adherence to the virtuous eminent scholar they became just like two truly loving and sacrificing brothers, exemplifying brotherhood in its full sense. The men of whom we speak were Rateb and Adel.

They frequently attended the instruction sessions of their great guide… and always left together… discussing and debating… exchanging sincere advice, fully understanding one another’s point of view. They even went on excursions together, always in each other’s company, just as they were in the university, attending lectures and lessons together as they were both students in the faculty of Arabic language at Damascus University.

On that day something really strange occurred as Rateb attended the assembly of his guide without his great friend Adel, which all those present found most unusual, as did the eminent master who was prompted to ask ‘Rateb… my son! Where is Adel?’

‘Oh, sir! He has an exam at the university tomorrow, so he couldn’t come because he needs to study!’ Rateb replied.

‘What about you, Rateb?’ asked the eminent scholar, ‘don’t you have an exam too?’

Whereupon Rateb, with an air of prudency etched clearly on his features, said nothing… he did not answer his guide’s question. Then the venerable master stated, ‘By Al’lah’s Wisdom, he who comes to us shall succeed, but he who does not, will fail!’

These words made a great impression on all those present… the scholar’s words were truly astonishing… but more than that… it was a sensational and unexpected prophecy… all the more astonishing because Adel was the epitome of an energetic, hardworking student and the idea that he might flunk his exams was difficult to imagine. All those present were well aware that Adel was the top student.

He was extremely interested in his studies, dedicating ample time to fully understanding each of his quarterly subjects; he used to read every text book carefully and with great concentration. He never skipped a single chapter or lesson, or even the smallest detail without assimilating it fully; leaving no chance for unexpected circumstances which might occur.

Because of his dedication to his studies he became widely known to everyone for his diligence and academic success.

As for Rateb who was not so interested, nor showed such serious devotion to his studies, it would not be considered odd if he should flunk his exams, whereas it seemed to be impossible for Adel to fail, and for him to do so would be extremely surprising

A short time later the results were announced and the truth of the strange, astonishing prediction by the great master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, became apparent when the final results of the exam showed Rateb’s success and Adel’s failure.

That was a clear vision of the future, including firm guidance for the hearts of the attendees, all other disciples and, indeed, all people who seek the truth and religion. Thus it was demonstrated that an assembly of this imposing master should not be set aside in favour of other worldly matters as its duration is sacrosanct and contains guidance, healing and forgiveness of all sins and wrongdoing. At his gatherings the truth will be manifested upon the heart of the true believer, since we have come to this lower life for no other reason than to attain this truth and heart’s cure, while Al’lah Almighty ensures this lower life for us, so let us make it the means to an end and not the ultimate aim.

Indeed, let the sole aim be to achieve Al’lah’s Satisfaction which will be realised through attending the assembly of sacred Godly Science, because this lower world has been designed and effected for our advantage if we really seek to gain our Provider’s Satisfaction. The Prophet (cpth) said, “Court of knowledge (about God) is a garden of Paradise.”

chapters.title: The Compassionate Man and the Little Girl
chapters.html:
A hint of his great humanity and mercifulness

The position of guidance is of such great importance for it is based on the specific appointment of Al’lah and His Messenger, and not on mere memorised sayings and lessons recited from a platform. It is far more complex and involves leading by illumination, consciousness and witnessing, affecting and attracting the hearts of those whom one guides to the realities of the verses of the Wise Qur’an and to Al’lah’s Supreme Attributes.

This form of guidance is the most profitable as it acts in two ways: by the guide’s illuminated spirituality and his words, that is, he guides them as did Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth). By his own closeness to God he draws them nearer to Him and imparts to them qualities of perfection derived from Al’lah’s Supreme Attributes; and besides which he leads them by his knowledge which is founded on witnessing the truth and reality of God.

Such was the conduct of the great, esteemed Mohammad Amin Sheikho (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah), the venerable guide who directs his disciples and followers towards the Sublime Presence of Al’lah by both his own spiritual state and great words. This kind of instruction and guidance to Al’lah is the most sublime, and it is through which he overwhelms everyone who turns of his own will towards him with a great desire of drawing near to God, so that they will have their characteristics changed and their spirits reclaimed, to be enraptured by, and bathing in the refreshing spring of Godly Perfection.

As an example of this, the disciple Abdul-Kadir al-Dayrani explained, ‘Within just one sitting with the eminent scholar all my personal traits have changed, as happened with the change of the spiritual characteristics of Pharoah’s enchanters ﴿230﴾

when they became illuminated by Al’lah’s Light through the company of our master Moses (pth), ﴿231﴾

and came to believe in Al’lah. I began to feel a flood of compassion in my heart for all creatures to the extent that once when I saw my little nephew, Hisham, playing with matches and lighting them, I gave him a little tap for I was afraid of the possible consequences if he were to repeat his dangerous game. Yet, in spite of that justified action my spirit blamed and censured me for hitting him, till I became immersed in a feeling of self-inflicted blame for what I had done, even though I had given that no thought whenever I disciplined or smacked the child before I met my dear guide. Therefore, I was happy to apologise to the child in such a way that he would understand the apology, and so that I might be released of the distressing effects of guilt and remorse. I knew that he liked to visit his grandfather’s house in Barzeh, a suburb of Damascus, so I decided to take him there. We went to the bus station, but we made a mistake and instead of getting on the bus going to Barzeh I took the one which goes to Erbeen. ﴿232﴾

At last, I turned back home with him and he was extremely pleased and happy, even though we had failed to visit his grandfather.

‘That evening, I went to visit my guide (the scholar) in his house, and no sooner had I seen him than I felt real light flowing into my spirit and a flood of mercy and compassion overwhelming my heart. Truly, through that grand master, the Almighty filled my heart with mercy and sympathy: he endowed it with the gem of Godly Perfection.

‘After that meeting, I never again hit any one of my nephews, and even so the reverence they held for me in their hearts so far excelled that which they held for their parents that the parents would threaten the boys that they would tell me if they were naughty. The mercifulness of this great guide for all creatures, which he derived from Al’lah the Almighty, was a pattern that one aspires to attain, along with the ceaseless guiding light shining from his heart, so everyone who turns with his heart towards him will have this guiding light flowing into his spirit which will be endowed with this same Supreme Compassion.

‘All during Mohammad Amin’s military service as an officer in the al-Sham gendarmerie cruel criminals and spiteful enemies tried to get rid of him by shooting at him using live bullets while he, on the other hand, faced them with the utmost mercy which flowed as calm oceans into his heart; so beside his real hand gun, he held a fake one with which he pretended to fire on them simply to frighten them. He was a man who hid his compassion and concealed his affection in order to show strength and firmness for his beloved child in a wise and beneficial manner.

‘In this way, he spent his entire military service without using a real hand gun against them even though he was holding it, so, when he eventually handed in the real one, the bullets were spoiled inside!’

The disciple Abdul-Kadir continued, asking, ‘Suppose a man has a cruel heart and lacks compassion… then, what could he possibly do to obtain it?’

As he had been disciplined by the great scholar, the reply was, ‘This kind of humanity should counteract his enticing spirit, so that he acts contrary to its own inclination, and does the opposite of what it requires him to do… for instance, if he found a dirty cat in his house and he was tempted to be cruel to the creature, he must counteract the temptation and never give in to it, so instead of rebuking or beating or getting rid of it, it would be better if he took immediate action to respect and feed the cat, and what’s more, if he could cleanse or wash it, he should do so. Let him remember and abide by the saying of Al’lah’s merciful Envoy (cpth), “Honour cats and she-cats.”

‘Furthermore, if someone talks badly about this man, and his spirit becomes inflamed with rage and he wants to pay his detractor back two-fold… here, he ought to quash his spirit’s evil whim and repay the offence with charity, such as giving a banquet and inviting him to honour and entertain him, and instead of invoking God against him, he should invoke God in his favour, wishing Him to cure his heart and rid the man of his malice and hatred, or his inhumanity. ‘So, if he adopts this great, illustrious path in contradiction of his spirit’s inclination, and opposes the call of the cursed devil, the Almighty will look into his truthfulness and change his imperfect character accordingly when His Light flows into his heart, wiping away evil from his spirit, and flooding it with His ever-flowing Mercy.

‘Thus, “Knowledge is obtained through learning, and Mercy is obtained by acting compassionately,” as Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth) said. Besides, man should seek the company of faithful, true and merciful persons, because his spirit will be affected and acquire perfection through the company of perfect men amongst whom are those the Almighty made as guides to truth for ourselves, since they had been led by Him because of the great mercy folded in their hearts and which flows outwards to encompass the whole of mankind.’ Now, let us tell our story.

There was a knock at the door… and Ahmad entered.

‘Welcome Ahmad! Come in and sit down, my son.’ With extreme mercy, tenderness and cheerfulness, issuing from his merciful heart and which appeared on his noble countenance to revive and irrigate thirsty hearts, the venerable scholar welcomed his disciple who was still young at this time. It was the first day of Bairam. ﴿233﴾

‘What’s wrong Ahmad? You look sad… what happened? Tell me my son! Do you have a problem?’

At this, the good-hearted boy gave a long, tremulous sigh, and with innocent tears streaming from his eyes, he struggled to explain the situation, saying, ‘I don’t know… what can I say…? It was such a heart-breaking sight and it has upset me deeply. On the way to your house sir, I saw a funeral procession coming out of a house in al-Jisr al-Abyad (an area of Damascus). People were walking behind the coffin followed by a little girl crying and calling her dead father saying, ‘Oh Daddy! Who will give me the gift this festival?’ And then the mourners told her to go back home.’

Ahmad continued to describe what he had seen and heard which had painfully affected his heart, while the tears of the compassionate and venerable scholar began to fall from his gentle eyes, glistening like jewels on his pure cheeks, as abundant streams of Godly Mercy flowed from his pure heart to overwhelm all who were present.

A short time had passed when Mohammad Amin said, ‘Enough… my son! You have broken my heart… for God’s Sake, please… enough! Come on… hurry up and take me to the house from which you saw the funeral leaving.’

Immediately, the scholar with the great merciful heart stood up and, accompanied by Ahmad, walked quickly till they arrived at the house.

When the merciful master knocked at the door a little girl, about six years old, came out with her older brother… she was the daughter of the man who had passed away… the very same girl who had wept so desperately for her father.

The merciful master, Mohammad Amin, looked at her with eyes full of compassion and sympathy which overflowed to soothe the child’s grief… then he took a bag of money from his pocket, and gave it to her brother, saying, ‘My son, take this… give it to your little sister and tell her that her father sent this money as a festival gift for her.’

chapters.title: He who Listens Will Hear Good Advice
chapters.html:
In the Holy Qur’an the Almighty says, “You who believe, do not push yourselves forward in the Presence of God and His Envoy but remain beneath Al’lah’s Light. Al’lah hears and knows all. You who believe, do not raise your voices above the Prophet’s, nor speak aloud when addressing him, as you do to one another, lest your good deeds be cancelled out without your perceiving it. It is those who lower their voices in the presence of God’s Envoy whose hearts Al’lah has tested and proved to receive illumination by His Light.” ﴿234﴾

These noble verses clarify that anyone who truly believes in God does not put his own point of view before that of the greatest Envoy (cpth). It is impossible for them to do that since they have realised that his words (cpth) are the Words of Al’lah (Glory to Him). As for those who do not recognise his prestige (cpth) nor the prestige of any true guide who is a successor of the Envoy (cpth), they may consider their view on some matters to be more appropriate than that of these great human beings.

The Envoy (cpth) judges according to God’s Judgement; all his decisions are inspired by God and he refers to God in all matters. Therefore, whatever case may be laid before him, his judgement will be true and his words decisive even if he does not ask for full details of every point of the case.

In one review of his memoires, Professor Abdul Kadir John, alias al-Dayrani, a disciple of the humane scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, acquainted us with an incident that took place during the lifetime of his truthful guide. He related the incident as follows:

‘My brother, Basheer, was a disciple of our great guide. He had a friend called Mahmood Abu-Sabha whose father had died. This young man was good-hearted and of a noble mind. Basheer convinced his friend of the great advantages to be gained by attending the lectures of our truthful guide, the scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho. And so, his friend joined the circle and began to attend the revered lessons, which caused my brother’s affection for him to deepen.

‘When our imposing scholar saw the newcomer at his lectures and sensed his good and noble merits he loved him and sympathised with him after he learnt of his poverty and that his father had died. A few days later, I saw our noble guide in a vision one night, saying to me, “Listen to me, Abdul Kadir, go to your brother Basheer and advise him to be a good friend to Mahmood. As for you, I want you to maintain your company and good relations with Abu Waddah.”

‘Abu Waddah was a friend of mine, endowed with the simplest and best heart of all my friends. And so, when I woke up I went to my brother’s house and told him about my dream. He listened to the advice and acted upon it, which made him draw ever closer to his poor, fatherless friend. And so was it with me. I behaved according to the directions of my teacher and maintained my firm friendship with my companion Abu Waddah. In fact, Abu Waddah and I had been friends since childhood and therefore we loved each other; but my love for him grew stronger when he began to attend the lectures of our imposing master and we became brothers in God.

‘Once, when I visited him in his house, as was our habit, his sisters passed before me unveiled. This was an abhorrent situation for me and one which I always avoid, for the socialising of males and females is a clear infringement of God’s Statutes. I had to tell him immediately how annoyed I was and said to him quite frankly, “Please, Abu Waddah, if you want our friendship and our brotherhood in God to last you must prevent your sisters from showing themselves to me.” He did indeed comply with my request; and after that I never caught sight of any of his female relatives whenever we spent time together in his home. Thus, our companionship and friendship became deep-rooted, and then when my venerable master advised me to take care of him it grew even firmer, and so it remained until he departed from this earthly life (may God have mercy upon him).

‘And now, let us return to our main story:

‘When the young man Mahmood Abu Sabha joined the national service, he went to one of the recruits’ assembly points; this particular one was situated in the al-Nabek area. A few days after his departure, my brother Basheer missed his friend and wanted to visit him in order to make sure that he was well and to see if he needed anything in this new stage of his life. And so, he decided to travel to al-Nabek to see his close friend. Mahmood Abu Shnaq, another friend of Basheer’s, and also a disciple of the eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, wished to accompany him on the visit.

‘And so, the two brothers in God met together at the agreed time and headed off to the house of our venerable guide to ask his permission for them to travel to the al-Nabek area to visit their young friend, Mahmood Abu Sabha. When Basheer arrived at the home of the venerable guide he was in his room, so he knocked as was the polite thing to do, and entered the room to ask for his master’s opinion about their planned journey and their reason for it. The revered guide looked at his disciple Basheer and then said to him, “Basheer, my son, do not go there.”

‘“Yes sir, whatever you say.” Basheer replied and then took his leave.

‘In the large room which the eminent scholar assigned for his visitors, Mahmood stood waiting patiently for his friend, and when he saw him coming out he approached him asking, “Have you told our master about our intention to travel, my friend?”

‘“Yes, I have,” Basheer replied, “but he wants us to forget it; he said that we shouldn’t go there.” Mahmood remained silent for a while, turning over the reason that made their guide disagree with their travel plans and then he said to his friend, “Oh Basheer, I think that our tender-hearted master doesn’t want us to suffer the difficulties of this visit because of his compassion for us. You know, my friend, the weather in that area is extremely cold and today it’s snowing, so there will be little traffic; it will be very difficult to find transport going there or coming back. But, I think that you should go back to his room to explain to him that if his response is based on his fear that we may face difficulties on such snowy days, tell him that we will happily put up with anything in order to visit our brother Mahmood and be sure of his well being.” Basheer was convinced by his friend’s point of view so he returned to the room of their exalted guide and put their thoughts to him. With this, Mohammad Amin told him that they should do as they wished.

‘When Basheer told his friend about their master’s reply, Abu Shnaq said, “Didn’t I tell you, my friend, that our tender-hearted guide was reluctant to agree to our journey simply because of his great concern for us? Come on, let’s leave right now so that we can find a bus going through the al-Nabek area so we can leave early, and return early too.” There and then, the two friends hurried off to the bus station in Damascus where they boarded a bus and sat beside one another.

‘Two hours later they reached al-Nabek, wherupon they got down from the bus and stood on the main road which ran all the way from Damascus to Aleppo. They stood there for more than an hour, waiting for any car that might take them to the camp which was located about two to three kilometres away from the main road. By then it was snowing heavily; a bitter chill began to penetrate into their bones and still no car passed by. They thought that the road must be impassable to traffic, so there was nothing for it but to start out for the camp on foot, shuffling along the snow covered road. It took them one and a half hours to reach their destination after a long, hard struggle against the blinding snow storm.

‘At the main gates of the military camp they told the guards standing there that they wished to visit their friend, the soldier, Mahmood Abu Sabha, and asked if they would kindly call him… and then they stood aside, waiting. After half an hour that seemed like eternity as they waited in the harsh conditions, the guard returned and told them that the soldier they wanted to meet had been stood down due to health reasons and had left the camp heading to Damascus! Although the news was quite a shock for them, it was, nevertheless, a pleasant shock.

They were happy that their good-hearted friend had been exempted from national service.

‘All of a sudden, a feeling of astonishment came over them as they remembered how their inspired guide did not want them to undertake this journey, as if he had a premonition that the only outcome would be exhaustion and a difficult situation for both of them.

‘Again, bearing chill and snowfall, they retraced their steps on the snowy road back towards Damascus, passing the turnpike on their way. And it must be said that their way back was no easier than their way forward! It took one and a half hours of trudging back along the secondary road until they reached the main road which lead to Damascus. There they stayed for a considerable period of time in very difficult weather conditions hoping for the arrival of a bus coming from Homs or Aleppo and heading towards Damascus. At last, just as they were giving up all hope, a bus arrived and they began the return journey which lasted more than two long hours!

‘In fact, the entire journey caused them nothing but disappointment and suffering and brought them no benefits at all.

‘When they reached the city, they soon headed to the house of their noble guide where they found their friend Mahmood, the ex-recruit who, after mutual hearty greetings, began to relate the story of his dismissal which had occurred by virtue of Godly Providence. On their part the two adventurers told him the story of their exhausting journey which had taken the entire day, and the long hours they had spent exposed to the bitter cold and the driving snow.

Indeed, they were very sorry that they had not heeded the advice of their honest mentor. Had they listened to his words of advice, they would have spared themselves all that suffering and exhaustion: the only “fruits” they gained from that fruitless journey.’

chapters.title: The School Director Acts upon Wise Advice
chapters.html:
Here we shall tell of yet another honourable event that occurred during the noble life of Mohammad Amin Sheikho. It demonstrates his wise guidance based upon his prodigious superior knowledge of Al’lah, as it shows the positive benefits that Al’lah bestows upon him who follows his supreme guidance.

Without prior appointment Mohammad Amin Sheikho, the venerable guide, decided to visit one of his disciples at his place of work, so he hurried off with this in mind. The disciple held the post of a director of one of the top schools in the most elite area of Damascus.

On this particular day, while he was absorbed in his work and compiling some lists, there was a knock at the door.

‘Yes… come in…’ he called out. He was most surprised to see his revered master visiting him at his office! He stood up immediately to welcome him politely, and bent to kiss the master’s hand as he uttered warm words of welcome and happiness at the unexpected visit. Mohammad Amin returned the greeting with his usual kind words.

The great master sat down while his disciple, the director, asked permission to gather the files before him and to finalise some work in which he seemed to be engrossed, for then he wanted to be able to give his full attention to honouring his master. The great guide could not fail to notice that he was preoccupied with his paperwork, and asked him, ‘Oh son! What are you so busy with?’

‘Oh sir… it is my school,’ he replied. ‘The number of pupils has exceeded the maximum permitted, so the Ministry has ordered me to compile lists of the names of all the extra pupils whom I suggest to be transferred to another school which has vacancies.’

Mohammad Amin remained silent for a little while, then he addressed his disciple asking what he proposed to do about the situation.

The director answered, ‘Oh sir! I’m sitting here preparing these lists… but I have just stopped because of your welcome arrival. I’ve selected all the lazy and disorderly pupils and compiled lists of their names. I’ve decided to keep only the polite, hardworking ones in my school… sir.’

The wise guide hardly waited for his disciple to finish speaking, and, astonished at the course of action he was taking, interrupted him saying, ‘Praise is to God Who has sent me to you at precisely the right moment before you deliver those lists to the Minister.’ The school director was astonished at the words of his guide and he immediately began to wonder if he had done something wrong, or if he should have handled the matter differently!

The wise master, Mohammad Amin, continued, ‘Oh son! Don’t you want to do a good deed by which you will receive God’s Satisfaction? Don’t you want to keep for your life to come whatever may bring you closer to Al’lah? What effort are you making for the sake of God? What will you gain if you take the easy path and retain the hardworking, studious pupils? Those you want to keep at your school are naturally diligent, so it requires relatively little effort on your part to educate them, but as for those you suggest should be transferred, they are the ones who require you to strive and make great efforts to educate, and take care of. This single act will lead you to earn much for your life in the Hereafter, but if you move them to another school, you will be deprived of the deeds that Al’lah has directed towards you so that you may gain from this experience, and for your spiritual improvement. No son! This is the wrong course of action… you would do far better to transfer the diligent pupils and keep the lazy and troublesome ones.’

When told by the Ministry to reduce the number of pupils at his school, the director had seized this as a convenient opportunity to keep the hardworking pupils and send away all those who were lazy and disruptive, and by so doing he would attain superiority over all the other schools because of the high success rate of the excellent pupils in his school: something which would bring him great acclaim and praise from the Ministry of Education. But now, with the advice that he had received from his esteemed guide, he could not ignore this guidance and he chose to abide by this instruction as the merciful guide was greatly revered not only by his disciples, but also by everyone who had ever met or befriended him. Without fail all could sense the dignity and reverence held within his heart.

He answered, ‘As you wish, sir! I’ll do as you say.’

He immediately cancelled the first lists and prepared new ones containing the names of his exceptional pupils, and gave them to an employee with instructions to deliver them to the Ministry of Education on that very day. He did this even though it went against his personal inclination. The Ministry approved the lists and the pupils were removed to another school soon afterwards. It was not long until the administration of this school recognised the standard of the new pupils they had received and compared it with that of their original pupils, then they were extremely surprised… and somewhat confused!

It was clear that the lowest achieving pupil among them was of the same high standard as the previous superior pupils at the school and even surpassed them! Those pupils were supposed to be the lazy ones of the first school that we mentioned, so how can the pupils of the lowest standard compete with their excellent pupils? Therefore, they were full of admiration for the administration of the school where those pupils had been taught previously.

If the under achieving pupils of the first school are of such a high standard and so successful, then what about its top pupils? Truly, the school administration deserved great admiration and praise for its teaching plans and the tremendous efforts expended in preparing its pupils to achieve a standard that had never been attained by any other school: and all of that is by virtue of its director who is highly qualified to control all matters, and directs his school most ably towards such excellent achievements.

Of course, this was an erroneous train of thought, for they would never believe that the superior school had sent them its excellent pupils while they retained the lazy and troublesome ones. Now the director of the second school informed the Minister of Education, who happened to be his relative, of the excellent standard of the pupils sent from the first school.

Then the Minister wrote an official letter of thanks and praise for the excellent efforts of the director of the first school. The letter contained the greatest commendation for the highest standard of teaching in the country, and it was sent out to all schools with the directive that they should follow in the steps of this school which was the first in knowledge and development.

The disciple director was greatly surprised with the superb commendation for he had certainly never expected such a result; but he was wise enough to realise that he had attained this position by his compliance with his great guide who only wanted for him the rewards of the life to come. And so, because he had followed the enlightened teaching of his guide Mohammad Amin, Al’lah granted him the rewards of both this life and the Afterlife.

Similarly, Al’lah will be pleased with any man who seeks the Satisfaction of the Great Creator, and will make human beings satisfied with him too.

So, let man’s intentions be concerned solely with receiving God’s Satisfaction, seeking through his deeds the reward of the life to come rather than that of this temporary life. Let his only purpose be to please God, then he will attain happiness in the two abodes, and the men of truth should offer good deeds in the pursuit of such high aims.

chapters.title: The Curer of the Spirit Treats the Curer of the Body
chapters.html:
The Envoy of God (cpth) said, “Communication with God is the route of ascension for believers.” The spirit that believes flows toward the venerated Ka’ba during its prayers whence it rises up to Al’lah, the Almighty, by means of the companionship of the noble spirit of God’s Envoy (cpth) which is always present in God’s Presence. This is the way that true communication is achieved with Him, the Almighty, and it rises ever higher in witnessing His Supreme Attributes. This is the reality of prayer which every true believer performs, as long as his belief is combined with strict adherence to God’s Commands.

As for those whose belief and faith are based on mere tradition and imitation, they may commit infringements and breaches of the Godly Statute, therefore their prayers will be imperfect and will produce for them nothing but sentiments and spiritual states which do not grow sufficiently to enable them to ascend to the High Presence of God and witness His Beauty, (Glory to Him). And sometimes it may even be restricted to mere words and gestures.

The faithful, eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (God has sanctified his soul) spared no effort in encouraging his followers to attain this level of communication with God, and urged them to reach this basic stage of true prayer whereby the spirit of a prayer would leave its body and travel to the holy Ka’ba where it would be able to communicate with God through the scholar’s companionship. For the scholar was their leader who guided them to God, the Almighty, and so whoever loved him and held a bond of reverence for him would soon enter God’s Presence during their true, heartfelt prayers, and soar up from the foundation of ascension which is the holy Ka’ba.

Scholar Sheikho invited people to worship God alone, and because of his distinguished teaching and logical and effective interpretation of the Holy Qur’an, the flower of the youth of our country, Syria, and of many other countries, joined his circle to drink from the spring of his heavenly sciences of realities and certainty.

Dr. Badr al-Din Atfah, husband of a granddaughter of the eminent scholar, was a young man distinguished by his good heart and admirable personal qualities. He never missed any of the lectures of truth given by our noble guide, which in reality were sessions of the great Envoy (cpth). For he (cpth) said, “Still I will manifest myself in the noblest man among you.” Indeed, the scholar’s assemblies were like holy, heavenly Gardens during which all his students spent happy, sacred times whilst gaining sublime knowledge.

Dr. Atfah was one of the scholar’s murids, his committed followers, who reaped precious fruits from these inspiring lectures. The words of the eminent guide refined his nature and embraced him with his sanctified spirit until the doctor’s own spirit became totally clear and transparent, and adorned with Godly Lights. In this way he was able to attain a high level of true communication with God, just as this noble master wished all his murids to do.

But unfortunately, this enviable situation did not last with Dr. Atfah; something happened to upset the serenity of his life and cause him great dismay. One day he came to his teacher to talk to him about his problem in words full of sorrow, ‘Oh sir, by God, I used to be able to flow spiritually to al-Ka’ba and perform true heart communication with God through your companion, but now I feel that my condition has changed and so my communication with God has ceased.’ Indeed, by virtue of his association with this truthful, august guide, the disciple, Dr. Atfah, had reached a high state of closeness to God and attained real communication with Him during his prayers. His spirit was able to soar to the Godly Presence after he bound himself to his imam’s spirit in the holy Ka’ba.

So, what was the matter with him that caused his condition to deteriorate so that he was no longer able to ascend to that lofty Presence to be in true communication with God? In fact, the underlying reason for this regression was his practice of the medical profession through which he was obliged to meet women, the young and not so young, to examine them, talk to them about their illness, and give them advice and prescribe medication. This caused his spirit to be distracted from its previous truthful direction towards his noble guide and weakened its link with the Provider, thus it had become once again confined to its physical body, unable to soar towards its Creator during prayer. The goodhearted doctor had lost his true communication with God which our virtuous master explained to him, and which the Envoy (cpth) spoke of in his noble sayings. His spirit had lost its clarity because of his communication with the gentle sex, for any source of evil which the eye catches reaches the heart and harms it. This is always true even if there is no evil intention. So, this was what now prevented the spirit of the faithful murid from reaching al-Ka’ba and praying there.

He had studied medicine, not out of his love for the profession, but simply to please his father who was a majorgeneral in the Syrian Army and a minister of defence at that time. The father had the highest aspirations that his son would follow a dignified career, so he forced his own will onto his son and ordered him to study medicine. And so, he fulfilled his father’s wishes, and as he had also entered the military college he graduated as an officer and as a physician. Dr. Atfah held in his heart a deep love for his guide, Scholar Sheikho (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) so his strong attachment to him enabled the young man to attain true communication with God during his prayers. His spirit’s close association with the noble spirit of his mentor helped it to flow to the venerable Ka’ba: the base from which every truthful, obedient believer soars up to God, the Almighty. This is the positive fruit that every spirit reaps from keeping company with a true mentor.

The Envoy of God (cpth) said, “Man adopts the faith of his close friend; you should therefore be careful when choosing an intimate friend.” ﴿235﴾

Yet when this doctor engaged in his profession and treated any woman, his elevated state went into decline, and sometimes it even vanished completely; and with this, his true communication with God was lost. The new condition of this murid did not go unnoticed by his guide, who became more watchful of him and asked God every day to forgive the sins of his follower. This invocation does not consist of mere words and prayers: rather it has a reality known only to those believers who are endowed with heart insight.

The noble mentor was directing his own spirit, which was wholly immersed in God’s Light, towards the spirit of his murid in order to overwhelm it with this same Light; thus every piece of filthy evil that had become ensconced in it because of his professional experience and his unwillingness to treat women would be eradicated, and thus his spirit would be cleansed and cured.

This was the course of action of this merciful guide with all of his followers; he kept his eye on them, embracing them with his lofty state, seeking God’s Pardon for their sins and helped them to draw close to Him by virtue of his own great closeness to Him. Like an eagle which enfolds its chicks under its wings, looks after them and protects them from danger, so was our revered master with his followers. He fought the devils which approached them and deflected them from his followers.

Now we shall return to the good doctor, the subject of our story, and the difficult situations he experienced.

Poor doctor! Whenever he left his clinic in the evening to go home, waves of severe pain and distress began to attack him, causing him to feel overcome with exhaustion. One evening, while he was on his way, he suffered severe pains in his head causing him to groan out loud,

‘Oh my head… Oh what’s this persistent headache? Oh my bones… I feel as if they’re broken… not just my bones… every atom of my body is causing me terrible pain… oh… I feel that I have lost all my strength.’

He was so exhausted that the moment he reached the house of our noble guide and entered the large hall he threw his huge, weakened body to the sofa. The noble guide was already fully aware of the debilitated state of his disciple, the physician. How could he not be so when his heart’s eye was constantly observing him and looking after him. For to be a true guide, first you must possess the insight illuminated by God’s Light that allows you to witness realities and attain certainty. Only then can you be of benefit to your disciples, for you will constantly follow them with the heart’s eye and with certainty, observing their condition and cleansing their spirits with the luminous Light of God.

A few minutes passed before the noble guide called for his exhausted, stressed murid, ‘Dr. Badr, my son, would you kindly give me an injection in the muscle? Come on, son, take this solution and inject it into my body.’ The good-natured doctor could hardly summon the strength to stand up on his feet, but with slow, heavy steps he walked towards his medical bag and brought out a clean, sterilised syringe. He took the solution from his master’s hand and drew it through the needle, then, having sterilised the tip, he inserted it into his guide’s noble body.

‘Good health, sir,’ the doctor said to his guide, with his customary politeness.

How wonderful! As soon as the doctor finished his work with the noble guide, his own condition changed completely; his weakness turned to strength, his suffering vanished and his usual levels of activity and vitality were instantly restored. An overwhelming feeling of happiness flew into his heart and a light spread throughout his limbs and body to crown his spirit so that it shone with renewed contentment and joy. How strange! What was the secret of this needle? For its effects were amazing, not on the tender-hearted master to whom it was administered, but rather on the doctor who had administered it! Indeed he seemed like a lion that had been freed from a severe, debilitating cramp.

A close follower of the eminent scholar was also present at that time and witnessed Dr. Atfah’s reaction after rendering this simple service to his guide. He noticed that the good doctor improved instantly to become bursting with vitality, his face glittering with radiance. The noble guide saw this follower looking with astonishment at Dr. Atfah so he said to him, ‘Oh my son, he cures my body and I cure his heart.’ ﴿236﴾

Oh God! Who was this noble man? What was his reality? His firmly established faith in God had produced a power that could, by God’s Leave, turn weakness into strength, and a feeling of complete exhaustion into renewed youthful vigour and determination! Indeed, Scholar Sheikho offered everything he possessed in order to save humanity from darkness, by following in the steps of his role model, the Envoy Mohammad (cpth), who had declared in one of his noble sayings, “I have sacrificed my body and soul for the sake of my whole nation.”

Driven by this lofty intention, he decided to have a daily injection at the hands of his good-hearted physician follower. He had no need for it at all, but he took it only to help his follower regain his spiritual clarity and physical activity. He was the ideal example of self-sacrifice and all the deeds were of a humanitarian nature, with the purpose of helping his brothers in humanity to experience happiness in their lives.

Truly, the level of his sacrifice knew no bounds and here we shall tell of another incident.

Once, our noble scholar was suffering a piercing pain that had affected his noble head and caused him to suffer the terrible pain of an intense headache. The physicians were puzzled at his suffering and could not reach a diagnosis to explain the cause of it. However, having discussed the problem at great length some of them came to the conclusion that the cause of the pain lay in his teeth and advised him to have all of his teeth extracted as a solution to his problem. But the scholar understood perfectly well the source of his painful headache, so when they gave him their advice he replied, ‘It is my nerves and not my teeth which cause me this pain. For my teeth are all in good condition and there is no damage in them.’ Nevertheless, he accepted their advice, subjected himself to general odontectomy and had all of his teeth removed. And exactly as he had told them, every one of the teeth was healthy, with no sign whatsoever of dental bacteria or decay.

We ask God to grant him the reward he is worthy of, for the great sacrifices and deeds he rendered on behalf of humanity.

chapters.title: Charity Brings its Own Reward
chapters.html:
Al’lah the Almighty, through His Benevolence towards humanity grants mankind benefits and then ascribes those benefits to them so that the inner self of every man will be displayed and thereby establish which of them is best in deed.

In fact, the Almighty legislated about alms-giving and spending in the fields of benevolence. He imposed it on mankind through the obligation of almsgiving and decreed that it should be an act of charity thereby helping humanity draw nearer to Al’lah, the Almighty. Both of them aim at the purification of the human spirit through the spirit’s approach towards its Almighty Creator in this world and to gain Paradises for this benevolent deed in the Hereafter.

Since all money belongs to Al’lah, He apportioned a share of it to the pauper within the money of the affluent so that the latter may disburse some of it as appropriate and gain goodness through this deed and charity, and draw near to his Provider. And so is it with the pauper who will praise God and get closer to Him by thanking the Almighty Who has granted him this favour. Through that, he will love the wealthy donor who, in turn, will also love the poor for being a means through which he approaches Al’lah, the Almighty.

By such sympathy and reaching out both of them achieve benefits here and in the Hereafter; society, overall, becomes virtuous and happy, and mankind will have greater sympathy and care for one another.

And yet, the true believer has a sense of honour for he will never ask for such benefits, and even without his begging Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth) recognises him and discerns his need. The Almighty says, “You know them by their unfailing mark: they do not beg importunately from all and sundry.” ﴿237﴾

Similarly, the one who follows Al’lah’s Envoy will know them well through his link with him (cpth), so he allots an income from the Islamic treasury for them as did the Orthodox Caliphs.

Once the disciple, Abdul-Kadir Yahya al-Dayrani, was out with his eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, and while they were strolling the scholar was uttering sublime words which brought to mind the Supreme Attributes of Al’lah the Sacrosanct. As he spoke his face shone with light and brilliance, and his words might be compared to a fountain of precious jewels addressing the perceptions which lead to the indisputable reality in his spirit.

As they walked along the street leading to the Parliament a man sat on the ground in front of it; he appeared to be desperately poor, and hid his miserable face under a large round hat, similar to the caps of the Armenians. Seemingly his neediness, penury, and his embarrassment at the lack of work and income obliged him to hold a small glass box in which he had put some cheap candies and sweet bars aiming to earn his daily bread by selling them, since his self-esteem would not permit him to beg from others and ask them for alms. People were passing by but they failed to see him for they were wrapped in their own thoughts and intent on their own life gains, and they paid no attention to him. It had not come to their minds that he had been overcome by difficulty and dire need, which drove him to sit there: perhaps their behaviour was normal and instinctive since they did not possess the light whereby they could realise the truth… so, they failed to recognise the man in his need.

This man was desperately poor!

Oh my God! Where are those who see by Al’lah’s Light and witness the truth with their hearts? In fact, whether people inadvertently failed to see him or simply ignored him, is all the same, since they were not willing to give him even a few coins or relieve him of his embarrassment; that is why they shunned his goods and failed to buy any of the candies he offered for sale. Even so, he would never ask for alms, but he sat in silence without begging or asking for anything, except inwardly from his Provider.

By God, this is a deserving person on whom a gift would never be wasted, but on the contrary it would secure Paradises for its giver. So, who was the one who, through his insight, recognised and understood him? Surely, he was the only humane person among all those who sought their own worldly benefit: those whose eyes see but whose hearts are blind!

After walking a little ahead of the beggar the merciful master stood and called out, ‘Abdul-Kadir, my son!’

‘Yes, sir…?’ in a questioning tone.

The scholar said, ‘Oh, Abdul-Kadir, do you have a quarter of a lira?’ ﴿238﴾

With no hesitation the disciple said, ‘Yes, sir! I do.’

‘Well… hurry back and give it to that poor man.’

Being mindful of his desire to apply his supreme purpose, Abdul-Kadir went immediately towards the destitute man and put the coin in his hand. Then he returned to his beloved guide. As soon as he arrived, the scholar addressed him again, saying, ‘Abdul-Kadir! Do you have another quarter of a lira, my son?’

‘Yes sir, I do.’

‘Go then, and give it to him, Abdul-Kadir.’

‘I hear you, sir, and will do so!’

He promptly went back to the poor man and laid another coin in his hand, then he rejoined his dear guide who cheerfully said, ‘Abdul-Kadir! Have you seen how great is the reward you have gained for this act of charity?’

Commenting later on the request of our dear guide, the eminent scholar, the disciple Abdul-Kadir, said, ‘In fact I did not realise what I had gained and achieved at that time, as my own insight had not yet been opened, but, my willing obedience for all the orders of that grand master relied on his great sublime insight about which I was certain.

‘My son, Abdul-Kadir! Do you have another quarter of a lira?’

‘Yes sir, I do.’ ‘Go then, and give it to him.’

He handed the man the third coin and so Professor Abdul-Kadir felt that the pauper was overjoyed as he was temporarily relieved of his misfortune. And how would it not be so since he had known that his Provider would respond to him by sending the one who was distinguished by His Light, and knew about his need, and so he helped him. The Almighty says to His beloved Envoy (cpth), “You know them by their unfailing mark: they do not beg importunately from all and sundry.” ﴿239﴾

Only you, Prophet, and those who see by Al’lah’s Light are able to recognise such impoverished men.

chapters.title: A Loveable Human Being
chapters.html:
His heart was overflowing with the greatest love for all of God’s creation in general and for mankind in particular. Whoever sat with him and listened to his words sensed the pure love he carried in his heart for every one of them. Such was the character of the venerable scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho. It was because Al’lah loves everyone that he loved them too.

And so, if those who gathered with this noble master were good-hearted and inclined to recognise what is right and true, they would surely love his personality and yearn to meet him because they would feel something of the scholar’s mercy for his associates and his longing for them to receive guidance.

Mohammad al-Shaibani al-Taghlibi (may God have mercy upon him) was an example of such people who loved the humane scholar and had a heartfelt attachment to him at the deepest level. At that time, he was living with his family in the same neighbourhood as the scholar. Mohammad al- Taghlibi had served as an officer in the Faisali ﴿240﴾

Syrian army; he was from Damascus and was a kind-hearted and good natured man.

When the French army entered Syria in the year 1920 under the leadership of General Gouraud after the battle of Maysalun, the French governor gave orders that the Syrian army should be disbanded and its officers assigned as police officers after successfully completing a training course in Amber, the Royal Ottoman Faculty.

Mohammad al-Taghlibi joined this course and outdid all the other officers when he achieved the highest grade of them all. He then joined the same security corps in which our esteemed man, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, served as a police officer.

Al-Taghlibi had taken the revered master Amin Sheikho as his ideal and a role model for himself. He was able to understand an aspect of the secret of this pure human being as he witnessed some of his amazing deeds and successful actions in the field. Therefore he had great reverence for him and surrendered to him wholeheartedly just as the noble companions had done with the great Envoy of God (cpth). He was a faithful companion of the scholar and devoted himself entirely to his service.

Then, when the venerable master, Mohammad Amin, established his religious circle after the death of Sheikh Amin Kuftaro (may God have mercy upon him), al-Taghlibi became a loving, faithful disciple of the scholar. He stayed close to him constantly and never once missed the lectures of the scholar where he used to drink from the fountain of his knowledge and sip from his sublime state of being. The time that the two men spent together was not restricted to the periods of the scholar’s teaching, and in fact the venerable master frequently visited his friend and disciple in his home and sat with him in his orchard.

Master Ahmad al-Taghlibi, a son of Mohammad al- Taghlibi, was still a child when he asked his father one day, ‘Daddy… Daddy… who is older, you or our master Amin Bey?’ ﴿241﴾

It seemed as if the question deeply affected the father who answered his son with a look of consternation on his face, ‘Oh son, Amin Bey is more advanced, ﴿242﴾

not only than me, but more than everybody else. You should know, my son, that our master, Amin Bey, was born with the wisdom of a grown man.’ Then he explained to his child what he meant by these words. He related to him many incidents from the childhood ﴿243﴾

of the great scholar during which he, unlike any other child, acted as an enlightened adult. This was most evident after the death of his father when he was left alone at a tender age with his mother, as his elder brother Saleem had travelled away to pursue his studies.

‘At that time, my son,’ Mohammad al-Taghlibi continued his explanation to the young Ahmad, ‘our master, Amin Bey, was only seven years old. He was accustomed to receiving a considerable amount of pocket money from his father. However, after the death of his father he felt that the family’s former level of financial ease had changed considerably and therefore he told his mother that he no longer needed pocket money. From that time on he did not take even the smallest amount of money from his mother. And when she asked him what he would like to eat each day, he chose the cheapest kind of food in order not to burden her with increased household expenditure. As for meat, it was expensive, so he gave it up altogether until he became a young man and began to work and receive wages.’

It is clear that Mohammad al-Taghlibi had great reverence and love for his grand guide and therefore he kept company with him throughout his life. Out of his love for Mohammad Amin and his awareness of the benefits one would derive when listening to his Godly guidance, Mohammad al- Taghlibi’s great wish was that all people should attend the lessons of this great mentor or, at least, have a chance of sitting with him and listening to his words.

For this reason, when the venerable guide came to visit him at his farm, al-Taghlibi soon set about inviting all the workers on his land to come to sit in his presence and listen to some of the jewels and pearls of his revered teaching and wisdom. During one of these visits, Mohammad Amin was sitting on the ground when a large number of the workers gathered around him in response to the invitation of Mohammad al-Taghlibi who had called them to put aside everything they were doing and to come quickly! ‘It’s our master, the great guide,’ he said, ‘he’s come here to bless us.’

Truly, everybody loved this great teacher and guiding light and yearned to listen to his wise, healing words. Therefore the workers soon hurried to see him and so did a nephew of Mohammad al-Taghlibi and other relatives who had a farm next to his.

They all sat around the revered master with hearts filled with joy. Then one of the workers asked the great guide, ‘Oh sir, we all know that Lucifer, the first devil, was created from fire, but I wonder, how will the Almighty punish him with it? I mean, since he is a fiery creature, how will the fire affect him and burn him and cause him to suffer?’

Mohammad Amin always chose his words wisely when addressing people. He would talk to everybody according to that person’s ability to understand, and always quoted an example that would flow straight to his heart and make an impression on it. So, when the man finished asking his question, the venerable master picked up a clod ﴿244﴾

of earth and pelted him with it.

‘Oh… oh…’ the worker cried in pain.

‘What? Did it hurt you?’ the great scholar asked him.

‘Yes sir, it did.’

Then the wise scholar said to him, ‘So… it is the same for you as it is for the Devil. You were created from clods of earth such as this; however, when I pelted you with one of them, it caused you pain, didn’t it?’

At this, the worker nodded his head in agreement, ‘That’s right, sir. Now I understand.’

Such was the wonderful approach that the venerable master used when he answered questions. He knew well how to use his innate wisdom so therefore his answers were convincing and comforting.

Let us turn back to the son of Mohammad al-Taghlibi whose father had guided him to love the venerable master just as much as he himself loved him.
