The young Ahmad used to be with the two friends during most of the time they spent together, whether taking a walk or sitting in quiet companionship. The venerable scholar always treated the little boy with extreme kindness and sympathy. He never upset the boy at all, and always allowed him to accompany them whenever he wanted to do so.

Therefore, Ahmad was often seen in the home of the esteemed scholar and close to him from the age of five until he became a youth, when the noble scholar departed this world to live in the Presence of his Lord. Thus, because of his father’s love for the great scholar, because of the education which he received at his hands, and due to the mercy and tenderness he sensed in his heart, Ahmad was deeply attached to the venerable master, Mohammad Amin.

On a particular bitterly cold winter’s day it happened that the scholar was at home speaking to some guests with his usual words of great illumination and guidance. Then when he finished and the guests stood up to say goodbye to their host, the imposing master accompanied them to the street door demonstrating his customary kindness and hospitality as it was the first time they had visited him. As he stood at the door, the compassionate master felt the cold air penetrate to the very core of his noble body and before long it was clear that he was suffering from a common cold.

When young Ahmad entered the room of the great guide he saw the symptoms of illness on the face of this man who was so beloved of him and his father. Without delay, and unnoticed by anyone present, the little boy rushed out of the house and ran towards the clinic ﴿245﴾

of Dr. Qarcozian, a famous physician at that time. Ahmad rushed into the clinic and accosted the physician saying, ‘Oh doctor… please come with me. It is our master, Amin Bey… he’s ill. Will you please come with me right now and treat him?’

The physician also had a great love for the august master. He had sensed the kind and merciful manner he had when dealing with people and, at the same time, he was aware of his sound, superior logic. So, he immediately answered the little boy’s request and put on his outdoor clothes, while his son quickly prepared the medical bag. Then the physician, accompanied by the little boy Ahmad, hurried towards Mohammad Amin’s house in order to examine him.

When they reached there and entered the house, the physician was surprised to see the greatly revered master enjoying good health. He realised that the renowned scholar had simply caught a chill and there was nothing else to fear or cause concern. Mohammad Amin received the physician warmly and invited him to come in. They entered the sitting room and then the noble master began to speak with his customary gentle, sweet, and enlightening words which were full of logic and conviction, while the physician became fully absorbed in listening to the scholar’s words and understanding their meaning. He was elated to be in the presence of this noble master.

Whenever the physician met him he felt himself flying to the seventh heaven as long as he remained in his presence. He yearned constantly for such meetings where illumination and wholehearted rapture prevailed, and true wisdom and knowledge poured forth from the mouth of the noble guide.

The physician never concealed his belief in the humane master, in fact he expressed it at every opportunity saying, ‘If all of the Muslim sheikhs and scholars had been like the venerable master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, I would have declared publicly that I am a Muslim.’

chapters.title: Attempted Assassination
chapters.html:
It is true that the dreadful event we are about to relate really did take place. This heinous crime was perpetrated one evening against the honest, compassionate scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, though his heart held nothing but pure love for all of God’s creation without exception, and even for those who were his enemies.

But, thank God, the attempt failed! For who could possibly succeed in harming any man who faithfully worships God, and only God?

For forty years, the noble officer, Mohammad Amin, worked ceaselessly to establish the truth and overcome deception. He never failed to lend a helping hand to any needy or oppressed person, to spread peace and justice among the people by arresting criminals, seeking faithfully to root out all crime and wrongdoing, and efface every misdemeanour in the county where he was responsible for security as a police officer. This is how he spent the years of his youth: striving constantly in God’s Name as every single human being should do. Therefore, it was no wonder that his Provider chose him and sent His Illumination down to this man’s pure and immaculate heart, thereby revealing to him extensive realms of Godly Knowledge as a reward for his many sacrifices and miraculous deeds.

During this latter stage of his life he adopted a different path; rather than tracking down criminals in his quest to bring about the truth on earth, he set about guiding people in the way to believe in God and become illuminated by His Light, thus leading them to the Godly Presence through his own wise words and his elevated state. The Almighty revealed to him heavenly sciences and granted him great heart life; in turn the scholar delivered this gift to all those who followed his guidance, wishing only to help them enjoy happiness in this life and the life to come.

A great number of young disciples had been drawn to the humane scholar and attended his weekly lessons which he gave in his own house, so that they too might drink from this cup of transcendent knowledge and become aware of the Godly Wisdom behind His Actions.

During these lessons, the noble guide would relate a lofty interpretation of the verses of the Holy Qur’an, explaining God’s high Purposes from His Legislations and the sublime significance of His great Words. His teaching, therefore, was excellent in its expression, perfect in the interpretations it gave, and convincing in its reality and reasoning.

What is more, it flowed gently to the hearts of the listeners, bringing them spiritual life, filled with immeasurable joy and sacrosanct bliss. This is no wonder, for the Envoy of God (cpth) said, “Court of knowledge (about God) is a garden of Paradise.”

And the fruits of these blessed meetings were that the hearts of those present were refined and enriched with noble qualities such as mercy, tenderness kindness, generosity, justice, bravery, benefaction, wisdom and many others.

This was the course of the venerable guide’s life until, with the passing of the years, he was sixty years old and one evening he was faced, most unexpectedly, with a shocking incident.

During the winter the great guide began his lectures after the sunset prayer and they were concluded by performing the evening prayer at ten o’clock. On that day, as usual, before starting the lesson, the august teacher stood up to perform the communication with God, and all the disciples present stood with him, their submissive hearts fully directed towards the Grand God in the company of their guide. One of the disciples called for the prayer and another, introduced by the venerable guide, stood as an imam to lead the congregation. The lines were perfectly arranged and by uttering the statement ‘Al’lah is Greater’ they began the prayer.

However, within moments of beginning the prayer there was a knock at the door. According to the instructions previously given by the august teacher, if such a thing should occur, the last disciple to arrive at the prayer session would open the door for the new arrival and then return to continue his prayers.

And that was exactly what happened. But unfortunately, the last disciple to arrive that evening, was a new member who had only recently joined the circle of our guide and unfortunately did not yet know all his brothers in the group.

So, when he opened the door he saw a stranger but did not give it much thought because he assumed that the new arrival was one of the disciples whom he had not yet met. He allowed the newcomer to come in and then closed the door and hurried back to his prayers, leaving the stranger to follow him.

But all was not right!

The newcomer advanced slowly towards the congregation until he came to a halt right behind the great scholar. And there he sat on a chair, seemingly waiting in silence for the end of the prayer.…

Such behaviour would have appeared quite normal if anybody had given it any thought, for they would think that he had already performed his prayer at home, and surely someone who had performed the prayer would not perform it again.

The new arrival sat calmly, gazing at the great master who was praying: standing, then bowing and then preparing to prostrate himself on the floor.

Everything continued as normal until the moment when all those present, including the noble guide, prostrated themselves, when suddenly, the stranger leapt from his seat, unsheathing a dagger as he did so, and swooped down towards the virtuous guide. With great force he tried to stab him in the back, seemingly determined to make it pierce his noble heart!

But what a miracle!

Before the criminal’s treacherous hand could hit its target, the scholar flipped over to face his attacker and in a trice, with a sudden powerful movement, he grasped the hand holding the dagger, and then exerted such pressure that he might have broken it.

This skilful art of self defence was one of many outstanding disciplines that the eminent guide had acquired and practised during his service as an officer in the security forces when he struggled with the toughest criminals and lawbreakers.

And so, the precarious situation had been reversed in an instant: the treacherous brute was now lying on his back at the mercy of Mohammad Amin, who had pinned him to the ground, his knee on the assailant’s chest as he calmly picked up the dagger and held it to the man’s throat.

The criminal was taken completely by surprise at the instant reversal in his position; for he could never have imagined such an outcome. He had come to the meeting to kill a man and make a quick escape; but there he was, on his back, petrified and facing death! How had this happened? Neither he nor any of those present could possibly know!

In a trice the assailant had become the victim and was now crying and begging for his life, ‘Oh sir… for God’s Sake forgive me… I beg you sir, forgive me… please…’

His entire body was racked with fear as he believed himself face to face with his own impending death.

The noise caused by the awful struggle had disrupted the disciples’ prayers and they all turned towards the source of the sound where they saw a rather strange and dramatic sight. A young man, crying and begging forgiveness, was pinned to the ground by their awesome guide, his knee placed firmly on the man’s chest, as he held a long, sharp dagger to the interloper’s neck. It was truly an astonishing sight to behold!

How had all this happened seemingly in the blink of an eye? Until the moment when they were all prostrate in prayer there had been no sign of anything untoward for the entire incident had occurred within mere seconds!

On looking carefully at the face of the young man they soon realised that he was a stranger to their group and was, in fact, the latecomer to their prayer session, which only served to confirm his premeditated decision to kill their beloved guide.

Oh… what treachery!

Their hearts suddenly overcome with rage they rushed towards the assailant, intent on tearing him to pieces. But before they managed to reach him the voice of their noble master, Mohammad Amin, boomed out, ‘Leave him to me!’

They stopped in their tracks, in obedience to the command, with all of them endeavouring to suppress their anger. They stood aside, motionless, watching their revered master, with every last man wondering what was to become of the criminal and what punishment he would certainly receive.

As for our just and merciful man, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, he pondered the matter and said, ‘I wonder… I don’t recognise him… there is no previous problem between him and me. I clearly remember all the criminals that I caught in the act and punished in the past, when I was a security officer. He isn’t one of them, and he isn’t one of those I used to chase to prevent them committing crimes… so, as far as I know, he has no reason to want to kill me or even bear a grudge against me!

‘So, why did he attack me? I can see that he must have been motivated and misled by somebody else who must be an enemy of religion and truth.’

To be sure of his conclusion, the pious master asked the criminal, ‘You… tell me… what made you do this?’ In a quivering voice, the man told the master his story which was exactly as Mohammad Amin expected.

This criminal was in thrall to another man who falsely pretended to be a religious guide.

That loathsome, fraudulent teacher had used the criminal to carry out his appalling plan and enticed him by offering a large sum of money; worse still, he promised to protect him from any judgement that might made against him if he carried out the crime of killing the noble guide Mohammad Amin. Then to facilitate the task, he gave him a detailed description of the place where the guide was accustomed to meet with his disciples and the exact time that they would start the sunset prayer; thus he had formulated what he thought of as the perfect for this terrible crime to be committed.

Having heard the details of the conspiracy, the tolerant guide lifted the dagger from the neck of the would-be assassin and said to him in a commanding tone, ‘Stand up and get out!’ The man could not believe his ears; but he scrambled to his feet as quickly as he could and ran away, unable to believe that he would really escape what had seemed to be his inevitable death.

Yes indeed. This was how the merciful, pure-hearted guide turned evil back towards its perpetrators! Mohammad Amin allowed his assailant to leave peacefully even though he was fully capable of killing him with the very dagger the criminal had tried to use to stab him through the heart!

However, if the noble guide had killed the interloper he would not have been punished, for neither Godly Law nor human law would have condemned him as his act would have been considered a case of self-defence. He could even have given the felon a sound beating at the very least, and then taken him to the police station where he would have received his due penalty. But even this our merciful guide did not do! Not only did he forgive the man and set him free, and not only did he prevent his zealous followers from causing him any harm, but he also turned towards them declaring his intention, ‘Brothers, I do not want you to mention the name of this man nor of the one behind his actions to anyone at all: for Al’lah is the Coverer of faults and I have forgiven them… both of them. So, I do not want you to go against them or do harm to either of them. Understood?’

Some of the disciples could not hide their astonishment at the unusual reaction of their guide, and they replied in amazement, ‘But, sir, how do you pardon a person that willfully tried to kill you? And furthermore, you want us not to discuss this incident with others!’

The venerable master answered them, saying, ‘Listen my sons, I know the person who pushed this cowardly criminal to kill me, but I also remember that his father once did a favour for me and I always return a favour. So, for his father’s sake I have forgiven him and overlooked his sin, and I want you, too, to forget about it and not stand in their way. Okay?’

Truly, there are no words to express the wonderful picture of Godly Perfection that coloured the heart of this merciful human being; a picture that makes us bow our heads, and confess the sublimity and nobleness of its owner.

This story also takes us back 1400 years to the time when the people of Mecca plotted against the truth brought to them by the noble Envoy Mohammad (cpth) and made many attempts to kill him. Nevertheless, when the Envoy (cpth) returned to them at the head of a powerful army after his migration to al-Medina and they fell at his powerful, merciful hands, he stood before them and addressed them in a voice that calmed their hearts and planted renewed life in their spirits, ‘People of Quraysh, how shall I deal with you in your belief?’ They replied, ‘You are a noble brother and a son of a noble brother!’

There and then, the man (cpth) who was sent as a mercy for all the worlds said to them, ‘You may go… you are free!’

By such wise and merciful conduct, the Envoy of God (cpth) captivated his people’s hearts, which led them all to true belief and to follow the mission of truth.

chapters.title: Inspiration or Evaluation?
chapters.html:
Faith, in reality, is the sure knowledge and certainty attained and realised by the believing human spirit itself; thus, it becomes a fact settled within the spirit, where the two intermix so that they become as one.

Faith is a moral truth, sensible and tangible to the faithful spirit itself. When a spirit comes towards faith, faith will flow within it just as the light generated by electricity flows through wires, and water flows through the branches of a tree, bringing life to its leaves and flowers so as to help it bear fruits.

Faith penetrates the spirit just like the life force penetrates the body, and then it will be manifested through noble merits, exemplary behaviour and good deeds through which a believer seeks only to see the noble Face of the Grand God and gain His Satisfaction. Neither lowly desires nor personal benefits will be the reason or purpose for such a believer when practising his deeds; he will completely abstain from all that is forbidden and naturally embrace sublime compassionate intentions towards all his brothers and sisters in humanity.

Faith rises in the spirit when recognising the Source of every moment of bliss, light and delight, and the Origin of existence, movement and life. But one will not attain such true faith unless one possesses the firm will to do so; this is the will that stems from the fear of inevitable death. Once the human spirit fears its destination after death it will truthfully seek an escape, and thus will give thought to that which will drive it towards the Creator through the contemplation of His Creation.

Faith is based on the realisation of God’s Existence and the witnessing of His Light with the heart’s eye. When a spirit attains faith it will feel gratitude and give praise to the Benefactor for His countless Graces: this is a feeling completely free from any trace of malice, ingratitude or denial of the truth that may stain one’s behaviour, and behind which one may seek to gratify his own lowly desires.

Through faith, humanity will retrieve their previous connection with God after a foolish separation from Him (Glory to Him), and thus they will return to the Home of their origin after a long trance-like period filled with terrible visions.

They will return to the true glory and honour, to happiness and sublime love, to the heavenly ways of ascension, and to their fascination with the most beloved One Who is above all men and all things. Through faith, mankind will be able to live a life of theopathy after a long period of loneliness; and besides this, they will enjoy lawful pleasures and become enhanced with every desirable and wonderful attribute of perfection.

They will move out from the darkness towards the Godly Light which flows throughout the whole of existence, and thus view worlds of realities and attain observational knowledge that make them relish the Gardens of eternity while still in this mortal world, and before moving on to the Afterworld.

The realms and ranks of high ascent and illumination that the believer enters and ascends are not to be compared with all that the sources of physical light in this life produce or the exquisite beauty that roses and other flowers display. Life, indeed, should be lived as the believers live it, for only the believers perceive the grave purpose behind this life and the precious opportunity it offers humanity to attain high ranks of sublimity and felicity.

As for those who have not yet recognised their Provider and His Supreme Attributes, those who are distracted by their own base desires, infatuated by whatever is transitory and does not belong to them, their life is senseless and fruitless; worse still, it is filled with misery and distress. They have forgotten that sooner or later they will be presented with a long-term prison sentence through the one indisputable fact: death will certainly come to all. They have not thought of their situation after death when they will suffer the terrible flames of grief and sorrow, and much weeping and groaning. Such a destination is the consequence of their own foolish choices and their preference for worldly desires rather than the rewards of the Afterworld; then the only relief available to them on the Day of Resurrection will be the blazing Fire.

They will throw themselves into this Fire even though they are fully aware of the intense pain it will cause them; nevertheless, they will seek it out so that it may help them forget their unbearable spiritual fire, the fire of shame and regret which burns them from inside.

A miserable substitute relief indeed!

Al’lah, the Almighty, provides you, oh Mankind, with food and drink and all that is necessary to sustain life. This provision is for your body, but along with all these material blessings He also provided you with sublime guidance to help you return to Him and enjoy a happy life. If you consider His boundless Favour upon you, you will surrender to Him and gain all that you wish and more, but if you have an elevated sense of self pride you will lose everything.

This universe is like an open book for all people; everybody can read the signs that indicate the Presence and Existence of God, the Almighty, and those signs that show His Supreme Attributes.

If mankind has the inward motivation to study this book willingly, seeking to be guided to the Almighty God, and contemplates the words it contains until he feels love for Him, belief will flow to his heart and grow ever greater as he advances along this path and supports it wholeheartedly against his sick whims and rendering of good deeds.

This is the type of belief that the grand scholar, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, invited people to adopt and emphasized that they should attain. Since the years of his youth he shone with vitality and vigour, unwavering in doing favours and sparing no effort in offering a helping hand to the needy, sacrificing everything, whether cheap or precious, in the Cause of Al’lah. He did not waste a moment by day or by night, and in fact, he was used to spending most of the night hours struggling against criminals and criminality, seeking to curb the corruption and destruction they planted within people’s hearts and in their countries.

Nevertheless, despite all his remarkable feats he never felt for a single day that he was achieving great work, rather he saw all his deeds as insignificant and unpretentious, and only the simple means which would help him to draw closer to God. Had he once allowed himself to admire one of his own deeds he would have lost the accumulated rewards of all his deeds, but this never happened.

Because of his unparalleled truthfulness and excellent capacity, the Almighty Al’lah burnished him and prepared him to ascend to a high grade after He tested him and let him pass through sessions of training in the high Mohammadan school until he graduated as a teacher for all humanity, supported with divine illuminating knowledge.

This took place after he performed a true communication with God in the company of the master of the Envoys, Mohammad (cpth), during which he received a great revelation from God: a donation that qualified him to become a guide to lead people to the Supreme Being. However, he always declared to his followers and reminded them, ‘You will not derive benefit from me, that is to say, from the Godly Sciences which God sent into my heart and then on my tongue unless you truthfully and earnestly follow the path leading to belief in Him.’

Because of his mercy for all creation and his intense desire to lead humanity to God, the Almighty chose this noble man and assigned him to the position of guidance due to the perfection his spirit derived from God that made him surpass all other guides.

When the great scholar witnessed worlds of Beauty and Grandeur of God and acquired high transcendental knowledge about Him (Glory to Him), he looked around and found his brothers in humanity immersed in poor, inferior trappings, away from the essence and realities. No wisdom behind the Godly Edicts was known to them nor were they aware of the way leading to belief.

Others, scientists and researchers, had become immersed in studying the world of molecules and atoms and were wholly infatuated by them, to the extent that they devoted themselves entirely to discovering their laws. They were totally preoccupied by their research, completely forgetting the Grand Creator and Wise Maker, and withdrawing far from the Omnipotent Director and Provider. They did not consider the end towards which they were descending and that one day they would leave everything behind and depart from this world. They occupied themselves with their creature comforts instead of the Creator Who perfectly and singularly created the earth and the heavens. Had they turned themselves to Him and resorted to Him, He would have endowed them with sciences and knowledge incomparable to any of the human sciences.

The eminent scholar always repeated that belief is the only way which allows humans to obtain God’s Favour and unprecedented Rewards. For no human is able to observe the Commands of God and advance in this life within His Bounds, no human is able to follow the Law which leads eventually to happiness in both this world and the world to come and enjoy the Godly Gifts unless they think about the way which makes them truly believe in God and witness His Presence (Glory to Him). The Holy Qur’an stated that miracles avail a human of nothing in this respect if they have no motivation for recognising the Creator of this universe and then moving from the stage of mental belief to the stage of realisation and certainty of God’s Existence that a spirit perceives inside itself; and this is achieved only by following the path of heart belief that was followed by our master Abraham (pth).

Time and again the noble master, Mohammad Amin, emphasised, ‘The Almighty Al’lah created the heavens and the earth, the oceans, and all other beings for one sole purpose: to help man believe that there is no god except Al’lah.’

The revelation and facts presented to mankind by this humane scholar indeed worked as miracles for all people who became aware of them, and indeed no other scholar of religion could present the like of them.

The Almighty corroborated him with the wide knowledge of realities so as to help him in guiding His servants towards the straight path, bringing them back to the right direction and teaching of the Envoy of God (cpth) after they had lost the way of happiness and shunned their Provider.

Beside the lofty revelations with which God provided the noble guide, He also caused him to be the instigator of many extraordinary incidents so as to manifest his high rank with God and his true guidance.

As an example of these incidents, here are two stories that took place with the scholar before some of his disciples.

In the town of Duma in the east of the Damascus region, there was a fertile oasis, provided with fresh spring water called Ain al-Sukhnah. This spot is rich with water and fish and distinguished by its pleasant, gentle breeze.

On one outing, the venerable guide, accompanied by a few of his followers, visited this natural spring where tranquility prevailed and a refreshing breeze was gently blowing. The birds delighted the ears with their sweet song and the ripple of the glistening, abundant water created a wonderful feeling of joy in the spirit.

When the group reached their destination, the venerable guide stepped towards the edge of the spring and stood there looking towards the water with eyes that shone with brightness and vivacity.

Life seemed to gush forth from him like the abundant waters from the sparkling spring, quenching the thirst of the hearts of everyone that joined him seeking to recognise God and wanting to know how to attain His Satisfaction.

The disciples stood around their teacher, some on his right and others on his left, and observed every movement of their master as he bared his arm and stretched his hand into the water in order to scoop up water to drink. But how strange! It is commonly known that fish usually swim away as soon as they sense a strange body entering the water. They either swim away from the spot or take to their hideout, for like all creatures of the sea, they are considered wild animals and their existence differs from the life of all other creatures. It is impossible for them to become tame in the presence of mankind, rather their natural disposition is to avoid people whenever possible.

This phenomenon is known to everybody. But what happened with the noble master on that day bewildered all those who were around him and left them amazed. For the moment that our guide put his hand into the water, they saw great numbers of fish coming in shoals from every direction vying to touch the hand of this honest guide and then they went away pleased and enraptured even if they had achieved only one kiss! This phenomenon brought to mind the sight of the pilgrims when flocking to touch the Black Stone, or kiss it from a distance, ﴿246﴾

and then continuing their circumambulation of al-Ka’ba as though they had had their greatest hope fulfilled.

But what the fish had done with the noble guide did not come from traditions, in fact their behaviour was motivated by their own desire and love, for it is known that animals can receive inspiration. This was exactly what the unusual behaviour of the fish showed! All the disciples who were there stood astounded, unable to believe what they saw with their own eyes. Their astonishment grew even more when the noble master drew his hand from the water and then some of their brothers turned up their sleeves and put their hands into the water to emulate him; however, every last fish turned and swam away to avoid the hands! To confirm what they had seen the first time, the brothers in religion asked their beloved guide to put his hand into the water once again, and at their insistence the noble master complied. Again, multitudes of fish swam from every direction to have the honour of touching the hand of this pure man!

They caressed the merciful hand and then swam away for others to take their place. But who knows! Perhaps there were some fish which were not satisfied with just one touch and so they kept contact with the blessed hand as long as it remained in the water! How odd! Why did this happen with him, in particular? Why not with anyone else?

The great teacher drew his hand from the water and then sat close to the spring while his disciples gathered in a circle around him. Then he began to speak to them about belief and the necessity of man’s attaining a true connection with God. He explained to them that if a human wants to be safe from affliction in this world and avoid disgrace and torment in the world to come, they should not rely on merely performing the formal appearances of worship, rather they should seek to attain true heart belief associated with entering into God’s Presence and witnessing His Supreme Attributes. Only then will they enjoy the bliss and honour that God has prepared for them.

He continued his calm, even-toned speech which bestowed heart life into the hearts of those who were listening to him, and through which he mentioned some stories clarifying the way of true belief. He asserted to them that a human would not reach this level of belief except by repentance, honesty, thought and persistence in his pursuit to attain belief.

This kind of belief is not obtained by accepting it from other previous authorities or traditional sciences, but it depends on one’s own process of thought and daily contemplation of the signs of the universe, all of which are produced and made by the Grand God, until one realises the true Godly Existence and has this fact settled firmly in one’s mind.

A human being should ponder on the creation around them and before this, on their own creation; how they started as a sperm in their father’s loins, and then turned into an embryo in their mother’s womb; how they were born as an infant child and then grew day by day until they attained full maturity.

After this field of contemplation, this thinking person can move to wider fields that help them know more about their Creator. They may think of heaven and what it contains, the day and night, the four seasons, the earth and all that it includes of seas, rivers, mountains… and other great signs. While a person is deeply contemplating and earnestly seeking to know the truth, their spirit, abreast with their thought, directly reaps the fruit of their efforts and becomes fully interested in knowing the reality of this existence, yearning to recognise the Creator and Provider to Whom its destination and return will be.

This is what this grand guide addressed himself to; so, it is likely that God showed this event with him to his followers so that they might truthfully and seriously think about his wise and true teaching which would eventually lead them to achieve happiness in this life and in the life to come.

And here is another odd incident that also took place with the noble master and not with any other of his brothers in religion.

He enjoyed walking, which was possibly due to the nature of his previous work when he was a police officer and he used to walk through flat, grassy land and dry, sandy desert, mountains and valleys, covering large distances on foot. And so, later on, when he retired he adopted the habit of walking daily for many kilometers; he usually did this throughout the year except during the cold months of winter. The great guide appeared to spread light like the shining full moon surrounded with its gorgeous nimbus when he walked with his group from the al-Muhajireen area where he lived towards the mountain of Qasiyun.

They used to go there to escape the noise and bustle of the city where they would breathe the soft, fresh air and enjoy clement weather. They used to sit in a circle around their master at the top of the mountain with spirits having been cleared by the clarity and serenity of their teacher’s noble spirit.

Overwhelmed with a sublime Godly dignity and splendour that came to them through their guide, and with their hearts wholly focused on their teacher, they would listen to his high interpretation of the noble Qur’anic verses which captivated their minds and helped them derive great benefits from the oceans of Benefaction and Donation of the Merciful, Great God. From time to time he would narrate to them stories of great lessons and other examples so as to imbue them with the love of bravery, fortitude, magnanimity, devotion, and noble human sacrifices.

After this heavenly journey, they would start on the return journey having quenched the thirst of their hearts by the outpouring of bliss and revelation that came to them from Al’lah, the One Who knows all that is unseen. He reveals whatever He chooses of this to true believers by virtue of their company with this noble master.

This was no wonder, for the great guide was always with his Provider; so, by such lofty direction and his inspired instruction he could direct the spirits of his followers to his beloved God, and thus enable them to drink from his own great love and passion for his high Lord.

With the end of such a blessed session, all the disciples would have forgotten their earthly existence in order that their spirits should soar upwards to high, heavenly oceans whence they returned with their spirits coloured with the seeds of God’s Supreme Attributes and immersed in bliss, the like of which all the combined pleasures of this world failed to offer.

This explains to us why our great Prophet (cpth) said, “Court of knowledge (about God) is a garden of Paradise.” On the way back home, and not far from their path, it happened that one of the stray dogs, which had fled from man’s harm and preferred to wander in the mountains, used to follow the guide and his disciples after lying near the place where they sat. Every one of the disciples noticed how the dog ran close to them all during their way back; and whenever their noble guide stopped to speak to them with his affable, pleasant words which delighted the ear, the dog would also stop with them and would then continue to follow them as they went on their way.

Whenever one of them approached the district where he lived or his own house, he would leave the group after taking his leave of his guide; the dog, however, would not follow him.

Instead, it would continue to chase around the procession which, as light as the gentle breezes, would continue on its way through al-Muhajireen where their master lived.

And so, the chasing continued until the merciful guide headed alone towards his home, followed by this dog. Then when he opened the door of his house he would see that the dog had stopped about ten meters away, looking at him intently. So, in a kind and merciful way, the venerable guide would stretch out his hand as a gesture, saying to the dog, ‘Welcome… come in.’

There and then, the dog would bow its head, shake it right and left and wag its tail, and then as quick as lightning it would run away and back up the mountain until it was out of sight. This behaviour with the dog was always repeated whenever the venerable guide took his disciples for an outing up the mountain.

And even though we are subjected to oblivion by nature we shall never forget the deeply moving statement of this great human guide when he sorrowfully commented on this event saying,

‘Alas! The dogs could recognise our dignity but humanity could not!’

These true events are but two of the many that the Almighty effected through this humane guide in the company of various groups of his disciples, so as to turn their attention to his high rank. For, in reality, he was like a shining beacon for them, without which they would have proceeded through this life in absolute darkness.

Indeed, he was like a flower surrounded with beauty and a moon encircled with glory.

chapters.title: The Honest Man
chapters.html:
Fifty years ago, simplicity was a general characteristic of our forefathers, and the era was distinguished by its good, kind-hearted people. Rain fell abundantly over all the lands of Greater Syria, causing the earth to generously produce its blessings and bear fruit. Until that time the unpolluted air was still clean and refreshing, and carried with it the pleasant scents of roses and jasmine which grew in abundance. The prolific trees offered up their abundant fruits and helped to spread fine weather all over Damascus, the aromatic city. The abundant waters of the rivers coursed throughout the land to offer a welcome sight for the eye and to bring joy to the heart: A truly idyllic scenario!

As for the mothers of those times, they were accustomed to staying at home, dedicating themselves to taking care of their children and educating them in the many aspects of an upright way of life. They did not leave the house unless it was necessary to do so, and they were content to be in their homes where they were concerned only with the happiness and well-being of their families. Their houses were usually large Arabian-style buildings, at the heart of which was a spacious sunny courtyard surrounded by beds of fragrant greenery, exquisite, softly hued roses and other charming colourful flowers, which all grew abundantly. And in the centre of every courtyard there would be found a fountain overflowing with sparkling, pure water that breathed life into both the spirit and the soul.

While the interiors of the houses were spacious and comfortable, the roads outside were narrow, earthen lanes, along which hawkers would frequently pass, some carrying their wares and others drawing them on carts, and all calling out what they had for sale.

One day, beneath the gentle drops of light rainfall, a poor hawker sat on the ground, in the middle of a lane, shedding copious heart-rending tears that stirred the feelings of all who saw him. All around him, there were broken pieces of glassware scattered here and there.

A crowd of people had gathered around the distressed man, trying to comfort him in his misfortune. Some of them said, ‘Don’t be sad, brother, Al’lah is Generous.’ And others said, ‘Take it easy, man. There’s no reason for all this crying. Al’lah will not leave you without provision.’ One of the passers-by added, attempting to console the distraught hawker, ‘Thank God, the evil has been destroyed.’

As for the desolate man, with every consolatory statement that reached his ears, he either shed more tears or snapped back reprovingly, ‘What! What are you saying? You don’t know how great my problem is. I’ve lost all of my goods and I’m now heavily in debt… I borrowed money to buy most of this merchandise.’

And he shouted out, ‘Leave me alone, please, go away… go away!’

The poor peddler was accustomed to roaming the old quarter in Damascus, carrying on his head a large glass box containing many glass plates, cups and other such things.

On that particular rainy day, as he was walking through the muddy street, calling out his wares, trying to earn money to provide his daily needs, he suddenly lost his footing on the soaked, slippery earth, causing him to lose his balance and fall flat on the ground along with all the heavy weight he was carrying on his head. And so, in one unexpected moment the glassware was smashed and he had lost all of his wares.

As the glassware had dropped to the ground, he felt his heart drop into his boots, and with this he slumped to the mud, gazing at the broken pieces with tears in his eyes, and overcome by the awful shock. He remained silent for a while in an attempt to cover the bitter feelings and distress that overwhelmed his spirit, but he could no longer bear it. He burst into tears and began to wring his hands with grief and then slap his cheeks whilst all the time crying and groaning.

At this pathetic sight, people began to gather around the miserable man and to express their sympathy for him; but because of his deep distress, the peddler said to them, ‘Please… please leave me alone… by God, a few years ago, I lost three hundred golden Ottoman liras and I didn’t feel annoyed or even care about it. But today, by God, I feel my heart burning with grief and pain for every broken glass that costs only one golden lira.’

These words reached the ears of the benevolent master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, who was passing along the same road, accompanied by one of his intimate friends and faithful disciples, and the friend’s little son. When the virtuous master heard the statement about the loss of the three hundred golden Ottoman liras he stopped in his tracks, approached the poor man and said to him, ‘Stand up, my brother… come on, stand up and come with me.’

The poor, distressed man wiped his eyes and looked upward to see where these kind words had come from. He found before him a handsome, dignified and honourable man with a bright, radiant face, looking at him tenderly and urging him to go with him.

So, he did as he was asked and stood up. The revered master took the glass seller’s hand and led him away from the crowd, as he whispered in his ear, ‘Come with me, brother, for I have something to say to you.’

Thereupon, the loving friend who was accompanying the noble master approached his teacher and asked politely, ‘May I take my leave, sir? Or perhaps I can come with you, if you do not mind.’

‘With pleasure… come with us. Let’s go together.’

The three men walked away, followed by the little boy, and the crowd was left behind to wonder what the outcome would be. They watched until Mohammad Amin, his friend, his friend’s son and the distressed hawker disappeared into the distance, and then they all lost interest and eventually went off to pursue their own affairs.

The august master took the man home with him. When they reached there, he knocked at the door as a caution for the women inside that strangers were about to enter, and that they should go to their own quarters. Then he opened the door and called out, ‘I have some guests with me; make way for us,’ and waited a few minutes before inviting his guests to enter.

They went in to the reception room and sat down. Then the honourable master looked at the miserable peddler and said, ‘Now, I want you to tell me the story of the three hundred Ottoman golden liras which you lost. Would you please tell me how this happened? Where and when?’

The poor hawker sighed deeply before beginning his story, ‘Ah, sir… ah! This happened almost three years ago. I don’t know how I lost them. I was walking along the street holding them tightly in my hand when suddenly they were no longer there.’

‘But, at that time…’ the august man asked, ‘Didn’t you look for them and ask the shops around about them?’

‘No sir, on that particular day I did not give much thought to the golden coins for at that time I had inherited many thousands of Ottoman golden liras, and so the three hundred liras was a negligible sum for me. But, alas, I wasted all of that inheritance for the sake of gratifying my base desires, and eventually I became penniless and all those who had pretended to be my faithful friends then deserted me, and refused to have anything to do with me. Ah, sir, in fact, I paid dearly for my frivolity. I underwent hard and bitter times and experienced all sorts of hardship. I am full of remorse for what I have done! I was immersed in debauchery. I failed to repent for my irresponsible conduct until I was reduced to poverty.’

On hearing this, the august master rose from his seat and left the room for a little while, then when he came back, he had his hand in his pocket. He stood before the peddler and asked, ‘Can you give me a description of the purse that contained your three hundred golden liras?’

‘Yes… yes sir, of course I can, for I still remember it very well. I had put them into a small red bag and tied it with brown cord.’

There and then, the virtuous master pulled his hand from his pocket to disclose a bag which was exactly as the hawker had described.

‘Is this your bag of money?’

Taken by surprise, the poor man opened his mouth and stared at the noble master’s hand, and then he stammered, ‘Oh, sir, yes… yes… yes, it is my bag! By God, it’s the same bag into which I had put my money.’

His happiness was beyond description. He was like a withered plant that had been revived by pure water and restored once again to life and vigour.

In the gentlest way, the venerable master dropped the bag of money into the hands of its owner, the miserable peddler, who received it, but still with a look of disbelief written across his face: could this be true? Or merely a dream? His money had been returned to him after a lapse of three full years! Here it was, three hundred golden liras, the exact amount he had lost! God sent them back to him after he had lost hope, all hope of their return and was in desperate straits besides. And so, with this, the joy of life returned to him. With eyes full of tears, he began to praise and give thanks to God for what He had graciously arranged for him.

With the accident that occurred on that day, God (Glory to Him) took from the hawker only a small sum of money but then He compensated him with a great amount. He replaced his dire straits with affluence and his gloominess with well-being. The loss he suffered when the glassware was broken brought him an abundance of good, and his misfortune turned into a great benefit for him.

But how could our honest and faithful man, Mohammad Amin, keep the gold safe and untouched all during that period of time? How noble were his morals! How hightoned was his character that ensured that he abstained from using that gold to obtain for himself the pleasures of this world! For three years, he kept in trust the great fortune he had found and did not spend even one lira of it for any purpose whatsoever!

When he had first found the gold coins, he informed all the shopkeepers in the quarter and also left a written notification at every shop, stating, ‘I have found a sum of money; so, if anyone inquires about it, tell him to visit me and give me a full description of it and then I would gladly hand it over to him.’

But nobody was able to describe the bag and its contents correctly so he hid the bag, with the valuable gold coins in a safe place in his room until God willed that they should be returned to their rightful owner, through this wise, Godly decreed accident.

From this we learn that although we may suffer grave misfortune, eventually it may turn to our benefit. And this was what happened with the peddler who is the subject of our story.

As we have learnt, the relatively minor loss of his glassware ultimately produced a great blessing for him; and on the other hand, the attributes of virtue and honesty of our humane master, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, were openly displayed. For the entire three years that this supremely honest man had the bag in his possession he did not open it except just once when he counted the coins in order to verify their owner. He kept them in trust, waiting for the day when the owner would rightfully come to redeem his trust.

In the Qur’an the Almighty says, “We offered the Trust to the heavens, earth and mountains and they refused to bear it for they feared it; Man bore it. Man was unjust to himself and ignorant of its results!” ﴿247﴾

In fact, the great, eminent guide Mohammad Amin recounted this story to the disciples in his large circle many times, in order to give them an example of the good Guidance of God, the Almighty. He clarified how God, in His Mercy, had deprived the hawker of a portion of his money when he was living a life of frivolity and carelessness and entrusted it to an honest man to keep on behalf of the hawker ﴿248﴾

until the time came when he turned back to follow the path of virtue and justice. At that time, the Almighty decided to return money to the peddler after the gold had increased in value so that he might praise Him wholeheartedly and believe in His Wise Disposal and Merciful Handling with His creation.

chapters.title: Words from the Heart
chapters.html:
Officer Mohammad Amin first met Sheikh Amin when he was in his youth, and thereafter was never apart from him until the day he left this earth.

‘Take this thousand-bead rosary, my son.’ Sheikh Amin Kuftaro, the rector of the Naqshbandi school (may God have mercy upon him) said to his new disciple, Mohammad Amin Sheikho. ‘If you want to join our religious brotherhood, you have to glorify God over each of its beads, one by one, until you finish; and then repeat this five times. This must be done in one sitting.’

This was the way of belief which mankind should follow in the view of the traditional scholars of religion. If one hopes to be a member of a particular creed, one has to achieve the glorification of God as already mentioned, which in reality is simply the repetition of the Name ‘Al’lah’ while fingering each bead of a rosary: a simple verbal exercise which is not associated with witnessing or realisation!

‘Yes sir, I will do it with pleasure.’ the young officer replied.

He took the rosary and headed straight home. He entered the house and went immediately to his room where he sat on a wooden chair with a tightly woven rush seat. He had brought some stones from outside and placed them in a pile on the floor beside him; each time that he completed a round of the rosary in glorification of God he would move one stone to the other side of the chair. He held the rosary between his fingers and began his veneration of God, ‘Al’lah… Al’lah… Al’lah…’ He murmured this continuously until he completed one cycle of the rosary and bent down to move a stone to the other side; then he eagerly turned back to his absorption in repeating the Name of Al’lah, his most beloved One.

What an amazing act of reverence it was! Truly it was beyond comparison with any similar action carried out by others. It was as though a flame of the greatest esteem and veneration for the Grand God flew from his noble and pure mind to the lofty and supreme Side of God, the Source of all might and power, the Creator of all beauty, and the Lord of all goodness and perfection.

What a wonderful opportunity it was for this pure and virtuous spirit to practise its soaring and sublime love, to turn wholeheartedly to its most beloved One, celebrating and basking in His Supreme Attributes. Indeed, there was not a single atom of his heart that was not fully immersed in boundless love and yearning for His Excellency, the Almighty God.

A considerable time elapsed but the noble master did not move in the slightest from his original position. He was wallowing in his love for the Supreme Being of God, sinking deeper and deeper, with no feeling of boredom or weariness.

How could he feel bored or weary when he was living in a high state of recognition of his most beloved One.

This is how human beings should glorify God. It was the unmatched and irreproachable love he had for his Lord which made him truly glorify and exalt Him.

Many hours had passed before he focused again on the present moment and paid attention to the rosary and the stones. He remembered the obligation he was fulfilling and so he counted the stones which he had moved unconsciously from one side to the other and found a total of twenty five!

‘Oh… oh… what have I done?’ the venerable master said to himself, ‘How have I moved all of the rosary beads twenty five times? Sheikh Amin told me to glorify God for only five rounds of the rosary!’ He felt as though only a few minutes had passed, although in fact it was many hours. If he had not been conscious of abiding by the words of his sheikh, he would have continued in his glorification of God… but for how long would he have done this?

He had been sitting on the chair for so long without making the tiniest movement, that when he stood up the chair was attached to his clothes. In fact, he had been so absorbed in the glorification of God that his body had become numb. It was as if he had shed his body and left it motionless on the chair and then taken flight with his spirit, his heart filled with longing and passion for his Grand God, as he swam in worlds of sanctity and realms of majesty, beauty and perfection. What great love for the Almighty God was enclosed within his heart! Indeed, it was beyond compare and totally irreproachable.

Once, after undertaking this dignified guidance to Al’lah he expressed his great love for God when addressing his disciples, ‘Oh, sons, a question has struck my mind: in the world of the first creation when we were still abstract spirits before the creation of our physical bodies, I wonder, did I love God before He loved me, or was it He Who loved me first?’

He appeared engrossed in profound thought that denoted his immeasurable faithfulness and boundless passion for God, and then answered the question himself, saying, ‘It is Al’lah Who loved me before I loved Him. The truth is that Al’lah loved all creatures before they loved Him.’

Indeed, through his illustrious and honourable behaviour the venerable scholar set the pattern for the way that all humans should follow to love God, and take as an example for their own success in order to rise to high spiritual levels. Out of his great love for God and his devotion to Him, whenever he engaged in a discussion with inquirers he was careful not to quote Qur’anic verses as proof to confirm his explanations and thoughts which were all inspired by the wisdom of Godly Guidance. Rather, he would use eternal, logical and irrefutable proofs depending on the varying implications of the noble Qur’anic verses, and always refrained from quoting any text from the Holy Qur’an.

This was because he was concerned in case the inquirer did not understand the Godly Purpose and might, therefore, shun Almighty Al’lah within his heart, think badly about Him, or even deny His Words, glory to Him. Therefore, it was customary for Mohammad Amin to offer his explanation, set out his argument and give his proof which were all revealed to him by the Grand God and derived from His Holy Book. If he found that the inquirer was convinced by the answer and showed satisfaction with the reply, he would then quote the noble verses which confirmed his Qur’anic thoughts and explanations. But when his answer was not accepted by the inquirer and the explanation he gave about the Godly Wisdom behind His Words and Acts did not appeal to them because it was not in line with their illusory notions, then the merciful scholar would refrain from mentioning any Qur’anic verse. He preferred to make himself an object of criticism and to be wrongfully accused by the people than to let them utter one untrue word about his beloved Lord and cause their hearts to turn away from their Creator. Truly, he sacrificed himself entirely in order to avoid such reactions.

What arouses one’s amazement is the strange and deep effect and impression that his words had on those who heard them, the like of which had never been observed in any other human being. The chain of words flowed constantly from his heart to theirs, for everything he said was issued forth from a deep well of realities that he had witnessed with his own heart’s eye; therefore these words could touch the hearts of those who listened as they spoke to their inner core, and they would then move towards the actual truth.

As regards those who are taken up with embellishing their manner of speaking, composing elegant style and interspersing the meanings with complex statements, their words will leave no impression on the hearts of those who listen to them nor will they lead them to a greater understanding than they already have. The following account serves to illustrate this.

There was a certain respectable professor who lectured in universities. This professor had attended some lectures given by the eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho and admired them greatly. So, he decided to speak with the scholar’s wisdom: he learnt some of the lectures by heart and used his distinguished explanations when addressing people. Indeed, he began to speak about these sciences, using his customary embellished manner of speaking and well-formed statements, and quoted proofs so as to confirm these thoughts. However, despite all his efforts and attempts to mix the philosophy he had studied with the divine sciences he had learnt from the scholar, and despite his eloquent way of addressing people, he failed to leave any impression on the hearts of those who listened to him. He admitted this situation once and declared in amazement, ‘How strange! I speak classical Arabic and use rhetoric in the best way, and I offer appropriate proof and quotes, however, I am unable to convince those who listen to me, or even touch their hearts; whereas the scholar speaks in the simple vernacular, and still he impresses people with his words and captivates their hearts and minds until they become completely convinced of his thoughts!’

This is the simple truth; for guiding people to Al’lah is not accomplished by giving lectures about memorised sciences or repeating knowledge derived from text books, nor by using fluent phrases or elegant style. Spiritual guidance is an invitation to Al’lah depending on the clear insight of the guide. The heart of a real guide should be vibrant and engrossed in the state of witnessing the Presence of Almighty Al’lah and His Supreme Names, and of observing the realities of the noble verses of the Holy Qur’an. Such being the case, the tongue of the true guide will transform the state of his own enlightened heart into words which will flow directly to the hearts of those who listen to him, transmitting the high state in which he lives and will lead them, if they truly seek to recognise the truth, to the same witnessing of the lofty realities to which he is witness.

This is why the personality of this great scholar made a deep and unmatched impression on everyone who listened attentively and yearned to know all that is right and true. His words expressed the Qur’anic realities he had witnessed. Therefore, people became entirely absorbed in his noble speech which flooded from the ocean of God’s Peerless Words, and was filled with wonders and marvels. Yet, beside the effect of his words on people’s hearts he also embraced them with his lofty spirit in which the illuminating Manifestation of Al’lah descended upon him and the lights of His Supreme Attributes brightened his spirit. These were the divine realms to which his heart led them, realms by which his own heart was captivated and which he constantly yearned for.

How many times had he incidentally come across hardhearted people, people whom, nevertheless, he had been able to impress through his unparalleled illumination of truth and rectitude. The eminent scholar spoke about one of these meetings with such people that had come about through God’s Will for He arranged this meeting out of His Mercy for these kinds of people.

Once, when the great scholar was in Aleppo, he came across one such person in a public park, so he seized the opportunity and began to talk to him about God, revealing His kind Treatment with people and His great Love for them. Despite spending a long time talking to the man, he noticed that he was not in the least bit touched by his words. His pure heart looked into the man’s heart and found it to be as hard as stone, containing no hunger for his Creator, the Almighty, and totally unaffected by the lofty words he spoke in his endeavour to offer him guidance.

What a strange character! Indeed, the venerable scholar had never met a man with such a callous heart, so unaccepting of the description of God’s Tenderness, Mercy and great Favour upon His creation; in fact, this was a man who showed no appreciation of His deep Wisdom behind His Commands. It seemed as if his heart was impervious and therefore he failed to draw even a hair’s breadth closer to God.

This man reminded the august scholar of the episode with the great Envoy Mohammad (cpth): he (cpth) suffered so much with the people of Mecca whose spirits were as hard as the rocks of Mecca Mountain where they lived. When this thought struck his mind, pure tears filled his eyes and began to pour forth. He remembered the great efforts that the Envoy (cpth) had expended to bring those people out of the darkness and turn them towards the light, and to turn them from their errant ways and in the direction of guidance, until finally their hearts were in the right place. Thus, by mentioning God they, in turn, became messengers and set about enlightening people about God’s Mercy, Tenderness, and other high Supreme Attributes.

That night, the merciful scholar could not sleep. He spent the whole night weeping out of his tenderness for that man who was living totally estranged from God and whose heart was as black as the darkest night.

The next morning, the revered master, showing renewed energy and vitality, went to the same park so as to inhale clean, fresh air. He had to wait there for some legal business to be completed and it was God’s Will that he should again come across the same person he had met the day before. He approached him immediately and sat beside him on a bench where he began to talk to him with gentle words filled with deep significance about Godly Compassion.

Mohammad Amin talked and talked, trying to implant in him even the smallest particle of his immeasurable love for God until, eventually, the man was touched by his words and his heart began to respond and relent. With this, the man cried and cried. Oh… thanks be to God! At last, this callous man tasted the sweetness of being close to God by virtue of the company of the one who was talking to him and instructing him.

At last, his spiritual state changed from one of indifference to one of awareness and he began to mount the ladders of transcendence.

Another incident took place in the year 1963, when the ambassador of Yemen in Beirut visited the august scholar, Mohammad Amin, in a house belonging to one of his disciples in the city.

The Yemeni ambassador was fully engrossed in the scholar’s words and listened attentively to the holy explanation: his heart was totally enthralled and submissive to the point that he became wholly captivated by the character of the noble scholar.

Then, at the end of this meeting, which lasted for three and a half hours, the ambassador asked permission to take his leave having quenched his heart’s desire and enjoyed sweetness and delight such as he had never experienced before. It was the sweet taste of being close to the Almighty Al’lah, the like of which he would not find in any worldly pleasure or entertainment. He sensed that his heart had been nourished, his spirit relaxed, his knowledge and wisdom developed, and even that it had attained a high and sublime quality.

When he left this glorious meeting he bade goodbye to the venerable guide after expressing his gratitude towards him and his hope that he would kindly allow him to visit him once again in the same house.

Since the compassionate scholar had received a favourable and positive response from the Yemeni ambassador and he noticed the advantages he had attained from hearing the truth and the proper guidance, he welcomed the ambassador’s request for a second visit. Because he was so eager and sincere in his request, the ambassador came to meet the great guide the next day and was so happy to be allowed to attend another lecture of his precious lectures.

The venerable master again received the Yemeni ambassador with great warmth and welcomed him with pleasant words. And again, a sublime and divine revelation flew from the noble mouth of the great guide and as on the previous day, this meeting also lasted for three and a half hours, until the Yemeni ambassador felt that he had satisfied his heart and mind by unprecedented, lofty words, the like of which he had never heard before.

He left the great guide while experiencing an intense state of deep and heartfelt affection, mixed with an overwhelming feeling of appreciation for the new devout thoughts that had never come to him in the past.

Let us now return to our beautiful, ancient city of Damascus, and particularly to the house of our great scholar where he sat talking to his family, his wife and daughters, giving them enlightening advice that would be helpful and advantageous for their life to come. As they sat together, the great guide quoted some of the ideas and examples he had brought up in his conversation with the Yemeni ambassador.

When the family heard about his meeting with the ambassador, Mohammad Amin’s wife, wanting to have some idea about Yemenite fashion, asked her husband to describe the ambassador’s clothing to her.

The noble master remained silent for a short time while he tried to recall the ambassador’s apparel, but how strange! He could not remember a single detail of the ambassador’s appearance to relate to his wife! What an odd reaction from the great master! It was evident that he had been totally consumed with his words of guidance. He had sat face to face with the ambassador during two long meetings, each lasting at least three and a half hours, but he had no recollection of the ambassador’s apparel or even of his features! How strange!

Truly, the revered master was concerned only with the heart of a human and not with the outer body and its accoutrements. It was man’s heart which he looked for. He knew well that guidance flows to the hearts of people and takes its place therein, for it is there where the essence and core of humanity exists.

Then, as we shall see, it was God’s Will to release the venerable master from the tight corner he found himself in because of his wife’s request. At that moment, Al’lah directed the scholar’s son-in-law to the house; so when the august master saw his son-in-law coming, he quickly called him, ‘Come here, my son!’

The son-in-law approached his father-in-law saying, ‘Yes sir… I’m here.’

‘Come and describe to your mother-in-law the clothes of the Yemeni ambassador whom we met in Beirut. Help her to picture the style of Yemenite fashion.’

Thereupon, the son-in-law embarked on a formal description of the outer man.

Such was the distinguished character of the great scholar. He did not care one iota for external shapes or appearances. The heart of humanity was his chief concern.

The following is another incident which confirms what we say:

One day, a disciple belonging to the circle of the great scholar accompanied one of his friends to a lecture. He was hoping that his friend might be guided to the straight path when attending and hearing the teaching of his revered master. They sat together listening to the devout words of the venerable scholar, and then when the lecture finished, the two friends were given permission to leave the hall. In the street, the disciple asked his friend, ‘What’s your opinion about the lesson, my friend?’

The friend replied, ‘The Godly chants were wonderful and the lesson was momentous. Indeed, it captivated the hearts and minds of all present. But I wonder, why does the scholar let that Bedouin recite the Qur’an when his voice is not beautiful and there are many followers with melodic voices in his circle?’

Before mentioning the great scholar’s startling reply to such a question, we want to introduce the Bedouin mentioned above to our noble reader.

The man reciting the noble verses of the Qur’an was, in fact, a commanding officer in the Iraqi army. He sacrificed his high dignity and sold his house in Iraq and then came to Syria, leaving behind all his relatives and friends, seeking only to be near to God and acquaint himself with all that is right and true. He lived in the neighbourhood of the great faithful guide. He was truthful in seeking God and he sacrificed all he had that was precious to him in order to be closer to Him, the Great God (Glory to Him). Therefore, the compassionate guide chose him to be one of those who recite the Holy Qur’an in his circle although there were many of his disciples who had dulcet voices, which delighted the ear and captivated the heart, whereas the Iraqi did not.

One of these disciples asked his guide time and again to let him recite the Qur’an instead of the Iraqi man, but every time this request was met with an absolute and decisive refusal.

Now, let us go back once again to our great scholar who, a few days later, learnt of the conversation that took place between the two friends about the recitation of the Holy Qur’an in his chamber. When he was told of the question which the new-comer asked his friend, the humane scholar uttered his famous statement, ‘Look, my son! I do not want sheer sound intoning the Qur’an… no, I want a human being with a sensitive heart to recite it.’

That Iraqi man had a living heart which enjoyed closeness to God by virtue of his company with the humane guide and his reverence to him. Such a human can touch the hearts of people, for when words come from the heart they will reach the heart. The one who has a living, sensitive heart impresses other hearts, while the one who has a beautiful voice will leave an impression only on the ears. They can enrapture people and amuse them but they cannot touch their hearts and lead them to God.

The secret of guidance flows into the heart and therefore it is always the main focus for every true guide. And it was said, ‘It is good to vocalise the verses, but to put them into practise is better.’

chapters.title: Al - Fara Palace
chapters.html:
Al-Fara Palace

What is al-Fara Palace? Surely there is no one living today who had the good fortune to behold the beauty of this magnificent house and its exquisite gardens. In fact, this palace was already of a considerable age by the end of the nineteenth century. So, what could its story be?

On the slopes of Mount Qasiyun, close to the mosque of Sheikh Muhyiddin Ibn Arabi, there once stood an Arabianstyle house with a spacious courtyard. It was an awe-inspiring sight with its splendid architecture and classical style and structure. And making it appear even more wonderful and pleasing to the eye, was the Yazeed River, a branch of the Barada River, which flowed through the grounds of the house. This natural wonder gave the courtyards the appearance of an earthly paradise where the fresh, luxuriant foliage drew life from the abundant waters and the exquisite hues of the multitude of plants and espaliers, Damascene roses and other fragrant flowers were interspersed with the artistic architectural pieces created by man.

One day, as the venerable master, the scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho was strolling in the company of Sheikh Ali al- Tikriti (may God have mercy upon him), he happened to glance through the open door of a substantial house and noticed the airy spaciousness of its interior and a hint of its unique and splendid beauty.

He promptly turned his eyes back to Sheikh Ali saying, ‘May Al’lah grant happiness to its owners.’ Sheikh Ali heard the words of the esteemed master, but made no comment and they resumed their walk.

Time passed, and some days later, when the honourable master was at home, there came a knock at the door, and on opening it he found a man standing there. The man was holding a bag from which he drew out an envelope containing some official papers. He asked the scholar ‘Oh sir! Is this the house of Mr. Mohammad Amin Sheikho?’

The honourable master replied, ‘Yes, it is, and I’m Abu Fathi (Mohammad Amin Sheikho)… can I help you?’

The man said, ‘Congratulations Bey… on your new house… may it be blessed!’

The man introduced himself as a bailiff from the Damascus land registry, whereupon he took a paper from the envelope and asked the venerable master to sign, asserting that he had received official notification. Then, he said, ‘Allow me to offer my congratulations again! The entire house now belongs to you, master.’

With a look of astonishment clearly etched on his face, the noble master replied, ‘Which house do you mean, brother? I think you have mistaken both the person and the address!’

‘No, no master! Aren’t you Mr. Mohammad Amin Sheikho?’

‘Yes… yes… that’s me.’

‘Is there anyone else who has the same name as you in this quarter?’

‘No, brother, there isn’t.’

‘So, I haven’t made a mistake… you’re the man I’m looking for and this paper issued by the Damascus land registry office affirms that you bought this property, in its entirety, and therefore it all belongs to you personally. So, would you please sign this paper to confirm that you have received these documents?’

Still taken aback, the honourable master said, ‘Oh, brother! I don’t own anything like that nor have I bought this house from anyone; what’s more, I don’t know anything about this house or even where it is located. Evidently, there must be a mistake!’

The bailiff found the words of the honourable master most odd… then he replied, ‘Oh, distinguished sir… my job is restricted… all I’m required to do is to confirm that you are the person in question, hand you this envelope and get your signature to prove that you have received it; so I’m unable to correct any possible mistake. You’d better go to see the manager of the land office and repeat to him what you have just said to me.’

Early the following morning, the honourable master took all the relevant papers and went to the land office where he met the manager and explained the matter to him in detail. Then, he said, ‘Surely there is something wrong and it must be put right as this house has been transferred into my name, even though it has never belonged to me, nor have I bought it recently.’

There and then, the manager called the employee and asked him to bring the necessary records. He opened them at the page detailing the property under discussion and scrutinised it carefully. Then he said, ‘Oh, Bey! There’s no mistake… you bought this house from a man called Ali al- Tikriti!’

As soon as the noble master heard the name of Sheikh Ali al-Tikriti, he understood fully what was causing so much confusion. He then said goodbye to the manager of the land office and went immediately to Sheikh Ali with the title deeds in his hand.

As he was accustomed to do, Sheikh Ali welcomed him wholeheartedly and was extremely happy at the unexpected arrival of his friend. Having exchanged customary greetings, the two men sat down together.

The august master wasted no time in asking, ‘Why did you do that Sheikh Ali?’

Sheikh Ali replied, ‘Oh, sir! It’s merely a simple present. I hope it is befitting to your elevated rank… I believe that it is suitable for you, sir, and would like you to accept it from me! Please do so!’ Sheikh Ali pressed the honourable master and urged him to accept this house, until finally he even swore by God that Mohammad Amin had no option but to do so.

At this point, the noble master interrupted him saying, ‘I’ll accept it, Sheikh, but only if you allow me to reimburse you. That’s my one condition for accepting it.’

Eventually, through the persistence of the honourable master, Sheikh Ali yielded saying ‘As you wish master. I’m at your command!’

‘What does this house cost then?’ asked Mohammad Amin.

Sheikh Ali said, ‘It’s nine thousand, five hundred majeedi, ﴿249﴾

sir.’

‘But, Sheikh Ali, such a house would not be sold for less than eleven thousand, five hundred majeedi!’

Sheikh Ali said, ‘Oh please, sir! I had already decided to sell this house for the price I mentioned. It is something that I said to my spirit; I never lie to my spirit and always keep my word. So, I’m telling you that this is the price I had decided on and I will not change my mind.’

The honourable master refused to settle for that and the discussion continued back and forth until finally the notable men of the quarter were brought in as mediators to resolve the case. Eventually, their binding decision was to divide the difference between the two sums equally, and so it was agreed unanimously that they should settle on ten thousand, five hundred majeedi as the price for the house.

Once Sheikh Ali had agreed to abide by this decision the venerable master said, ‘Oh Sheikh Ali! I don’t have the whole amount now, therefore, I’ll pay you half now and the rest will be paid in instalments… by Al’lah’s Will.’ Sheikh Ali replied, ‘That’s fine… as you like, sir!’

As time passed, Sheikh Ali received one payment directly after another, until he had received the entire amount and then he came to the noble master and said, ‘Oh master! I’ve received the full price of the house, in fact, even more, so you’ve fulfilled your responsibility towards me.’

This house remained the property of the honourable master until, from the kindness of his heart, he saw fit to give it to the blind and disabled people amongst whom he specified a caretaker and allocated to him a monthly salary from his own money.
